trends.headline: 今週は、KV キャッシュ（過去の計算結果をためておく記憶）を小さくする研究と投機的デコードの研究が大量に出ました。強化学習の後処理ではオンポリシー蒸留（生徒が自分で書いた答えに先生が点をつける学び方）が一気に増え、Muon 系の最適化手法の分析も続きました。

week.title: MoE の All-to-All 通信を、ふつうのネットワークや安い GPU でも速くする
week.title_en: Making MoE All-to-All work on imperfect networks and cheap GPUs
week.body: どちらも、エキスパート並列（専門家ごとに GPU を分けるやり方）で起きる All-to-All（全員が全員に送る通信）の詰まりを扱います。RailWave は DeepEP の上で、送る量を複数のレール（並列のネット回線）に均し、毎回作り直さない固定の送信順を使います。GLM-4.5-Air の通信で、Native 比で H800 では最大 5.84 倍、H20 では最大 4.36 倍速くなりました。CoMoE は P2P（GPU どうしの直結）がない RTX 5090 で、ホスト CPU を中継役にします。スループットは最大 1.46 倍で、ハード代 23.4% のまま NVLink 付き A800 に近づいたと報告しています。
week.body_en: Both target the All-to-All bottleneck of expert parallelism. RailWave sits on DeepEP: it rebalances traffic across rails using only source-local information and reuses a topology-derived schedule, reaching up to 5.84x (H800) and 4.36x (H20) over Native on GLM-4.5-Air traces. CoMoE assumes PCIe consumer GPUs without P2P and turns the host into a routing hub. It reports up to 1.46x throughput on RTX 5090, approaching NVLink A800 performance at 23.4% of the hardware cost.

week.title: 強化学習で、学習側から生成側へ重みを速く運ぶ
week.title_en: Moving weights from trainer to rollout faster in RL
week.body: どちらも、学習用と生成用で重みの持ち方が違う RL（強化学習）で、重みの同期が一歩ごとの時間を食う問題を扱います。NCCL M2N は、送り元と送り先の配置から転送の計画を自動で作ります。256 GPU の DeepSeek-V3 では同期時間が 5.78 秒から 2.77 秒になり、一歩の時間は 12.7% 減りました。NeMo-DCR は、一歩で変わる重みが BF16 で約 1% しかない点に目をつけ、変わった分だけをビット単位で正確に送ります。1T モデルを 3% の変化率で送る場合、87.5 分かかっていたのが 150 秒になりました。
week.body_en: Both address weight sync when training and rollout use different layouts or clusters. NCCL M2N derives a global transfer schedule from source and destination meshes. On 256-GPU DeepSeek-V3 it cuts weight sync from 5.78 s to 2.77 s and step time by 12.7%. NeMo-DCR exploits that only about 1% of BF16 weights change per step and ships bit-exact deltas, bringing a 1T relay-tree refit at a 3% change rate from 87.5 minutes down to 150 seconds.

week.title: 経路の偏りを、送り先を見て直す
week.title_en: Destination- and rail-aware load balancing
week.body: Ofan はファットツリー型のネットワークで、上りの経路を選ぶと下りの経路が一つに決まってしまう点を指摘します。そのため、送り先を見ない負荷分散では偏りを後から直せません。そこで送り先を見て振り分けるスイッチ側の方式を P4 で作り、Llama-3 405B の FSDP2 学習で、通信完了時間の膨らみを既存方式の 16〜39 分の 1 にしました。RailWave も、GPU 側でレールの偏りを均すという同じ問題を扱っています。
week.body_en: Ofan argues that on a fat tree, destination-oblivious balancing cannot undo the imbalance it creates, and proposes a switch-based, destination-aware scheme in P4. It cuts CCT inflation 16-39x versus existing algorithms in FSDP2 training of Llama-3 405B. RailWave tackles the same rail-imbalance problem from the GPU side.

week.title: MoE の「人気エキスパート」への集中をどう抑えるか
week.title_en: Taming hotspot experts in MoE
week.body: CIPHER-MoE は、ルーターの Top-K 選び（各トークンが上位 K 個の専門家を選ぶこと）はそのままにします。そのうえで専門家側からトークンを絞り込み、DeepSeek-V4-Pro などで Top-1 エキスパートの負荷を最大 64.9 ポイント下げ、学習を 1.10〜1.94 倍速くしました。推論側の AFORE は、次に来るマイクロバッチの割り振りを先に見て、エキスパートを NVLink で移し替えます。110B MoE で、最も強い比較相手よりスループットが 10.1〜17.6% 上がりました。
week.body_en: CIPHER-MoE keeps token-side Top-K intact but filters from the expert side with explicit capacity. It cuts Top-1 expert load by up to 64.9 points and speeds training 1.10-1.94x on models including DeepSeek-V4-Pro. On the serving side, AFORE uses the visibility of upcoming microbatches in attention-FFN disaggregation to migrate experts over NVLink. It reports 10.1-17.6% higher throughput than the strongest baseline on a 110B MoE.

week.title: GPU の外にある記憶装置を学習に使う
week.title_en: Using memory and storage beyond the GPU
week.body: TRANSIT は、アプリにもドライバにも手を入れずに、CPU の DRAM を GPU メモリの延長として使います。64 台の H100 で、1 GPU あたりのスループットが TorchTitan より最大 68%、ZeRO-Infinity より最大 42% 高くなりました。また、GPU を半分にしても元の 90% 超の速さを保ちます。RetainZ は、チェックポイント（学習途中の保存）を Zoned SSD（区画ごとにまとめて消す SSD）に置くとき、いつ消すかの予定に合わせて置き場所を分けます。ZenFS と比べて p99 遅延が 47.5% 減り、書き込みの増幅も 1.165 から 1.003 に下がりました。
week.body_en: TRANSIT transparently extends GPU memory with CPU DRAM via a user-space interposition layer. On up to 64 H100s it beats TorchTitan by up to 68% and ZeRO-Infinity by up to 42% in per-GPU throughput, and keeps over 90% of baseline throughput with half the GPUs. RetainZ places checkpoints on ZNS SSDs by planned reclaim epoch. Versus ZenFS's allocator it cuts p99 latency by 47.5% and write amplification from 1.165 to 1.003, though evaluation is on FEMU with manifests up to Pythia-1B.

week.title: 連合学習で、通信量と鍵の消費を減らす
week.title_en: Federated learning: less drift, fewer keys
week.body: 連合学習（データを手元に置いたまま各所で学ぶ方式）の論文が 2 本ありました。1 本は、隠れ層の出力を少しだけ共有して client drift（各所のデータの違いで学習がずれること）を抑えます。決められた回数の中で、FedProx や SCAFFOLD より高い精度を出しました。もう 1 本は、物理的な鍵配送の生成速度が遅いことに注目します。固定したバックボーン・蒸留・量子化を組み合わせ、胸部 X 線の分類で鍵の消費を約 35 分の 1 にしました。
week.body_en: Two federated-learning papers. One shares a small amount of hidden-layer activations to counter client drift, reporting higher accuracy than FedProx, SCAFFOLD and others under a fixed round budget. The other targets the low generation rate of physics-based ITS keys and combines frozen backbones, distillation and quantization. It reports roughly 35x less key usage on chest X-ray classification while keeping accuracy.

week.title: KV キャッシュ圧縮: 「どのトークンを捨てるか」から、別の圧縮の軸へ
week.title_en: KV-cache compression moves beyond which-token-to-evict
week.body: 多くの論文が、注意の重み（attention）だけで捨てるトークンを決める方法には限界があると見ています。LORE-KV は、答えの続きを試しに作って後で使われる度合いを見積もり、Qwen2.5-14B の LongBench を 45.49 から 48.24 に上げました。ただし予算が大きくなると効果は小さくなります。BreadthKV は、捨てる代わりに精度を下げて本数を残し、18 条件のうち 17 で「捨てるだけ」の方法に勝ちました。特徴の軸で圧縮する AttSVD はメモリ 50% で元と同等の性能を保ち、学習で圧縮する AbridgeKV は vLLM でキャッシュを 3.5 分の 1 にしました。
week.body_en: Several papers question attention-mass heuristics. LORE-KV samples short continuations to estimate future utility, lifting Qwen2.5-14B LongBench from 45.49 to 48.24 at B=128, with gains shrinking at larger budgets. BreadthKV spends bytes on more tokens at lower precision and beats eviction alone in 17 of 18 settings. AttSVD compresses along the feature axis and stays on par with the dense cache at up to 50% memory. AbridgeKV learns pause tokens that shrink the cache 3.5x in vLLM.

week.title: 投機的デコード: 下書きの作り方と長さを状況に合わせる
week.title_en: Speculative decoding: adapt the drafter and the draft length
week.body: 投機的デコード（小さな下書きを大きなモデルがまとめて確かめる方法）で、固定の下書き長をやめる流れが目立ちます。APEX は EAGLE-3・n-gram・下書きモデルを学習で切り替え、Qwen3-8B で逐次生成の最大 5.24 倍になりました。AgSpec はコーディングエージェントの過去の文章から写して下書きを作り、最大 4.37 倍（バッチ 1）です。拡散モデルを下書きに使う DScout は、平均 3.84 倍と 4.14 倍を出し、最も強い比較相手を 9.1% と 7.1% 上回りました。また、凍結した Qwen3-8B に約 2.5B トークンで MTP ヘッド（複数トークン予測の部品）を後付けするだけで、同時に学習した MiMo-7B 並みの速さになるという報告もありました。
week.body_en: A shared move away from fixed draft lengths. APEX learns to pick among EAGLE-3, n-gram and draft-model speculation and adapts depth, reaching up to 5.24x over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3-8B. AgSpec retrieves from session and workspace text for coding agents, up to 4.37x at batch 1. DScout (diffusion drafter) reports 3.84x/4.14x mean speedups, 9.1%/7.1% over the prior best. Separately, post-training MTP heads on about 2.5B tokens on a frozen Qwen3-8B reportedly matches jointly trained MiMo-7B.

week.title: エージェントのための推論の受け入れ・記憶の扱い
week.title_en: Serving agents: admission, context and KV lifetime
week.body: エージェントの使い方（長いセッション、途中の中断、ツール呼び出し）を前提にした仕組みが増えています。Coda は、KV の状態に合わせて受け入れの順番を工夫し、vLLM などと比べて SLO（約束した応答時間）を守れたスループットを平均 70.5% 上げました。ReFold は、すでに見せた履歴を元に戻せる形で畳み、トークンを最大 2.5 分の 1 にしました。順番を変えて KV を再利用すると答えがぶれる問題では、文書単位で計算し直すことで、CacheBlend の 69.0% だったぶれを 26.1% に下げました。Lachesis は、寿命の短い KV を HBM に置くことでフラッシュの寿命を 1.19〜3.13 倍に延ばしました。
week.body_en: Systems increasingly assume agent sessions. Coda exploits admission-order flexibility for coding agents and reports 70.5% average gain in SLO-compliant throughput over state-of-the-art systems and vLLM. ReFold reversibly folds history and cuts tokens up to 2.5x without hurting task success. Document-aligned recomputation reduces answer variation across request orders from 69.0% (CacheBlend) to 26.1%. Lachesis keeps short-lived KV in HBM to extend high-bandwidth-flash lifetime 1.19-3.13x, in simulation.

week.title: KV キャッシュを 1〜2 bit まで落とす
week.title_en: Pushing KV caches to 1-2 bits
week.body: どれも KV キャッシュを極端に低いビット数にしつつ、精度の落ちを抑える工夫です。TaSQ は 1 bit のベクトル量子化で、BF16 と比べてバッチを最大 14 倍にし、ピークのスループットは 1.87 倍になりました。Dual-QK は、クエリとキーに別々の変換をかけて 2 bit と枝刈りを両立させ、SGLang で最大 3.75 倍です。ResidualQuant は、ループ型モデルの各ループの差だけを 2 bit で持ち、理論上の記憶量を 80.7% 減らしました。CanonQ は、重み・活性化・KV を同時に W2A4KV2 にする方法です。
week.body_en: All push KV caches to extreme low bit-widths. TaSQ reshapes the VQ space for 1-bit, supporting up to 14x larger batches and 1.87x peak throughput over BF16. Dual-QK pairs non-orthogonal query and key transforms for prunable 2-bit caches, up to 3.75x decode throughput in SGLang. ResidualQuant stores 2-bit residuals across loops of looped Transformers, cutting theoretical storage 80.7%. CanonQ goes further with joint W2A4KV2.

week.title: 見た目の指標ではわからない、低精度の壊れ方
week.title_en: Low-precision failures hidden by headline metrics
week.body: LatentQuant は、NVFP4 にした VAE で画質の指標がほぼ同じ（0.7403 対 0.7409）なのに、ロボット操作の成功率が 95.5% から 10.5% に落ちることを示しました。三値（-1, 0, 1）の LLM では、bf16 に書き出す手順だけで GSM8K の正答率が 58.79% から 0.78% に下がる例がありました。miniTE は、学習と生成でエンジンが違うと NVFP4 の計算結果がずれる点を合わせ込み、BF16 の 1.39 倍の速さを出しました。どれも、「形式を合わせれば同じ」とは言えないことを示しています。
week.body_en: LatentQuant shows NVFP4 VAEs can match FP32 on VBench (0.7403 vs 0.7409) while LIBERO success collapses from 95.5% to 10.5%. For ternary LLMs, the documented bf16 export can drop GSM8K strict accuracy from 58.79% to 0.78%. miniTE finds that matching formats across training and sampling engines is not enough, and its aligned NVFP4 learner reaches 1.39x BF16 throughput. Together they suggest format parity alone does not guarantee identical behavior.

week.title: カーネルを生成・移植・検証するコンパイラ
week.title_en: Compilers that generate, port and verify kernels
week.body: Cleave は、式の変形と実行順の決定を分けて探すことで、最も強い比較相手より平均 1.6 倍速いカーネルを作ります。本番の推論トレースでは、手書きの FlashInfer FA2/FA3 を幾何平均で 1.4 倍と 1.7 倍上回りました。RESOLVE は、AI が作った GPU カーネルを、タイミングを揺らすテスト・単純化・F* での証明で確かめ、これまで報告されていなかった問題を 4 件見つけました。MLIR を使った移植の例も 2 つあり、CUDA から Tenstorrent への移植で最大 4.2 倍、3D DRAM 内処理向けで最大 16.7 倍（未最適化の変換と比べて）でした。
week.body_en: Cleave decouples algebraic search from scheduling, generating kernels 1.6x faster on average than the best baseline and beating FlashInfer's handwritten FA2/FA3 by 1.4x/1.7x geomean on serving traces. RESOLVE validates AI-generated kernels via timing perturbation, reduction and F* proofs, finding four unreported issues. Two MLIR compilers port code to new hardware: up to 4.2x for CUDA-to-Tenstorrent over default realizations, and up to 16.7x for 3D-DRAM PIM over unoptimized lowering.

week.title: 疎な注意（一部だけ見る注意）と位置エンコーディングの手直し
week.title_en: Sparse attention and RoPE trimming
week.body: LatentIndex は、どのトークンを見るかを決めるためのキャッシュを層どうしで共有し、DeepSeek-V3.2 でその保存量を 61.1% 減らしました。SAGA は、キーの頭数をバリューより少なくし、長い文脈で全部を見る GQA の 2 倍超の速さを出しました。WavePrune は RoPE（回転による位置の埋め込み）を 1 周期分に限り、Qwen3-8B の HELMET を 35.7 から 40.0 に上げました。MC-Sparse は動画や 3D の拡散モデルで、学習なしに 1.80〜2.32 倍速くしました。
week.body_en: LatentIndex shares the sparse-attention indexer cache across layers, cutting it 61.1% on DeepSeek-V3.2. SAGA uses fewer key heads than value heads for over 2x decode speedup at long context versus full-attention GQA (models up to 1.5B). WavePrune limits each RoPE channel to one period, raising HELMET from 35.7 to 40.0 on Qwen3-8B. MC-Sparse gives 1.80-2.32x training-free speedups for video and 3D diffusion transformers.

week.title: MoE のルーターを「読む」・形を変える
week.title_en: Reading and reshaping MoE routers
week.body: ルーター（各トークンをどの専門家に送るか決める部品）を、振り分け以外の目的にも使う研究が並びました。ルーターの出力を言語どうしでそろえると多言語の性能が上がる、という報告があります。ルーターの値を読むだけで画像と文章の組み合わせの危険を見抜ける、という報告もあります。BRANCH-MoE は専門家を二分木に並べ、補助の損失なしで偏りを防ぎつつ、通信を近くに収めやすくします。
week.body_en: Routers are being used as signals, not just dispatchers. Aligning router outputs across languages improves multilingual transfer, and reading router logits during prefill detects unsafe multimodal inputs without touching parameters. BRANCH-MoE arranges experts on a binary tree, preventing routing collapse without an auxiliary loss and inducing a topology that can localize communication.

week.title: 再帰型・線形注意の記憶をうまく使う
week.title_en: Better use of recurrent and linear-attention memory
week.body: 大きさが決まった再帰の記憶をどう管理するかが共通の問いです。GSA2 は、キー側とバリュー側の両方から記憶を直して、線形注意の比較相手を上回りました。ハイブリッド型（注意と再帰を混ぜた型）は注意に頼りすぎている、と指摘する論文もあります。補助の損失で再帰側も使わせると、長い文脈での性能が上がりました。CMM は、短期と長期の記憶を分けることで、記憶付きネットワークの比較相手より一般化しやすくなりました。
week.body_en: Shared question: how to manage fixed-size recurrent memory. GSA2 corrects both key and value sides and improves over strong linear-attention baselines. Another paper finds hybrid LMs over-rely on attention and adds an auxiliary loss that pushes use of the recurrent state, helping long-context tasks. CMM splits short- and long-term matrix memories and reports stronger generalization than prior memory-augmented networks.

week.title: Muon は何が効いているのか、どう広げるか
week.title_en: Why Muon works and how to extend it
week.body: Muon（更新の行列を直交化する最適化手法）を分析したり、広げたりする論文がそろいました。Spectrally Targeted Muon は、Muon が効くのは小さすぎる方向を学べるようにするからだ、と結論づけています。TensorChain は層をまとめて正規化し、Muon と同じ損失に必要なトークンを平均 9.6% 減らしました。ORCA は学習の初めだけ直交化の制約をかけ、Muon が Adam に勝つのと同じかそれ以上の差で Muon に勝ちました。一方で、最良の最適化手法はバッチサイズで変わり、Muon に一貫して使えるスケーリング則はないという反論的な報告もあります。
week.body_en: A cluster of Muon analyses and extensions. Spectrally Targeted Muon concludes Muon wins mainly by making too-small directions trainable. TensorChain normalizes stacked cross-layer tensors and saves 9.6% of tokens over Muon at matched loss. ORCA's early-only orthogonality beats Muon by a margin matching or exceeding Muon's gain over Adam. Pushing back, another paper finds no principled Muon scaling rule works consistently and the best optimizer flips with batch size.

week.title: 2 次の情報を、メモリを増やさずに使う
week.title_en: Second-order curvature at low memory
week.body: Clean は、Nyström スケッチ（行列を小さく近似する方法）で SOAP の前処理を近似し、メモリを線形に抑えます。AdamW の最終性能に 26% 速く届き、13B を 80GB の GPU 1 枚で事前学習できました。SoftServe は、行列分解の代わりに GPU 向きの Newton-Schulz を使う準ニュートン法で、条件の悪い問題では Adam・Muon・SOAP より低い損失を出すことが多いと報告しています。Shampoo では、発散（ずれを測る関数）の選び方が近似の質を左右することが分析されました。
week.body_en: Clean approximates SOAP's preconditioners with Nyström sketching at linear memory, reaching AdamW's final performance 26% faster and enabling 13B pretraining on one 80GB GPU. SoftServe is a quasi-Newton method using Newton-Schulz iterations that often reaches lower losses than Adam, Muon and SOAP on ill-conditioned problems. A Bregman-divergence framework explains how divergence choice shapes Shampoo's Kronecker approximation.

week.title: LLM の外に広がるスケーリング則
week.title_en: Scaling laws beyond language models
week.body: 高エネルギー物理では、約 110 億ジェットのデータで、計算量に対してモデルとデータをほぼ同じ割合（√C）で増やすのが最適だと出ました。RoboJEPA は、ロボットの世界モデルの予測誤差が計算量のべき乗則に従うことを示し、8B まで伸ばしました。故障しやすいハードでも、モデルが大きいほど誤りに強くなるというスケーリング則もあります。RL の計算量については、log-sigmoid と log-linear の法則に理論の裏付けが与えられました。
week.body_en: On about 11B jets in HEP, compute-optimal scaling recovers a near-equal √C split between model and data. RoboJEPA finds robot world-model imagination error follows a power law in compute, up to 8B. Training on simulated faulty hardware suggests error resilience grows with scale. For RL compute, a two-stage policy model gives theoretical backing to log-sigmoid and log-linear scaling laws.

week.title: オンポリシー蒸留が急増: 速さ・偏り・安全の問題
week.title_en: On-policy distillation surges: speed, bias and safety
week.body: 今週もっとも多かった流れです。生徒が自分で書いた答えに先生が点をつける方式を、さまざまな角度から改良しています。Flash-OPD は、答えごとに途中で打ち切って 2.2〜7.5 倍速くしました。ResOPD は、上位 K 個だけを見るときの偏りを、残りの部分の扱い方で取り除きます。Δ-MOPD は、先生が学んだ差分だけを移し、Math で 4.11 ポイント上回りました。一方で、裏口を仕込んだ先生からは、汚染率 3% でも攻撃成功率が最大 70% になるという警告もありました。
week.body_en: The week's largest thread. Flash-OPD stops each rollout adaptively for 2.2-7.5x speedups over standard OPD. ResOPD removes Top-k bias with an exact tail gradient under the same sparse payload. Δ-MOPD transfers only teacher-minus-base shifts, beating endpoint composition by 4.11 Math points. A warning: a backdoored safety teacher can reach up to 70% attack success on the student at 3% poisoning.

week.title: 同期・非同期の溝を埋めるパイプライン
week.title_en: Closing the sync-async gap in RL pipelines
week.body: ThunderSyncRL は、入力が決まったところからすぐ勾配を計算し始めます。同期式とまったく同じ更新を出しながら最大 1.9 倍速く、同じ予算なら非同期式より 2.47 ポイント高くなりました。KLPO は、KL 正則化（方針の変わりすぎを抑える項）の基準を生成側に置くことで、重要度重み（古い方針とのずれの補正）をなくしました。進化戦略では、古い評価ばかりでも精度の落ちは小さいという結果が出ています。LoGRA は、勾配を低ランクの形で持ってメモリを最大 45.7% 減らし、27B を 8 GPU で動かしました。
week.body_en: ThunderSyncRL starts gradients as soon as inputs are fixed, provably matching synchronous updates while running up to 1.9x faster, and beats async by up to 2.47 points at fixed budget. KLPO anchors the KL at the sampler to drop importance weights. Async evolution strategies degrade only slightly even when all fitness is stale. LoGRA keeps low-rank gradient sketches, cutting memory up to 45.7% and fitting 27B on one 8-GPU node.

week.title: 4 bit で RL を回す
week.title_en: Running RL in 4-bit
week.body: TRACE は、生成側で量子化した結果を学習側の FP4 の丸めに反映させます。MoE 4 モデルで BF16 並みの RL 性能を保ち、生成は最大 5.4 倍速くなりました。miniTE は、エンジン間の数値のずれを合わせ、Qwen3-30B-A3B で長い RL を安定させました。複数の先生から学ぶ蒸留の分析では、BF16 の丸めのせいで、更新が反映されて初期値から変わった重みが 7〜11% しかない（FP32 では約 97%）ことも示されています。
week.body_en: TRACE uses rollout-side quantization outcomes to guide training-side FP4 rounding, keeping BF16-level RL quality on four MoE models with up to 5.4x rollout speedup. miniTE aligns cross-engine NVFP4 numerics for stable long-horizon RL on Qwen3-30B-A3B. A multi-teacher OPD study adds that BF16 rounding hides most updates: only 7-11% of BF16 weights move versus about 97% of FP32 masters.

week.title: KV キャッシュを精度・層・ヘッドの軸で削る
week.title_en: Shrinking KV caches by precision, layer and head
week.body: BreadthKV は、本数を残して精度を下げるほうが良いと示しました。最も厳しい予算では、上限の長さに届いてしまう AIME の実行が 91% から 40% に減りました。TaSQ（1 bit）と Dual-QK（2 bit・6.8 倍圧縮）は量子化の空間を工夫します。ResidualQuant はループ間の差を 2 bit で持ち、Coral-KV は動画生成で層をまたいだ予測の残りだけを量子化します。WakeKV は、読み方を途中で変えるヘッド（注意の頭）を CPU に退避させ、後で戻せるようにします。
week.body_en: BreadthKV argues for more tokens at lower precision, cutting AIME length-cap hits from 91% to 40% at the tightest budget on Qwen3-8B. TaSQ (1-bit) and Dual-QK (2-bit, 6.8x compression) reshape the quantization space. ResidualQuant stores 2-bit residuals across loops, and Coral-KV quantizes only cross-layer prediction residuals in video KV caches. WakeKV parks cooling heads in a recoverable CPU reservoir instead of evicting them.

week.title: 拡散言語モデルの高速化と学習
week.title_en: Diffusion language models: speed and training
week.body: 拡散言語モデル（文章を少しずつ書き直して作るモデル）の論文がそろいました。Clock Diffusion は、位置ごとにノイズの量を変えて半自己回帰型にし、KV キャッシュも使えるようにしました。SpecFold は、投機的デコードの枝どうしで重なる計算を使い回し、Spiffy の最大 1.64 倍になりました。Un-OPD は、ブロック境界のずれなどによる 2 つの偏りを直してオンポリシー蒸留を安定させ、学習時間をおよそ半分にしました。
week.body_en: Clock Diffusion uses position-dependent noise schedules to make continuous diffusion LMs semi-autoregressive with KV-cache support. SpecFold reuses parent computation across speculative branches, up to 1.64x over Spiffy. Un-OPD fixes boundary misalignment and support-dependent bias in block-diffusion OPD, stabilizing training and cutting wall-clock time by roughly half.

week.title: コーディングエージェントを速く・正しく扱う
week.title_en: Serving and understanding coding agents
week.body: AgSpec は、エージェントが同じコードやログを何度も書くことを利用した投機的デコードで、最大 4.76 倍（バッチ 16）になりました。Coda は、受け入れの順番を工夫して、SLO を守れたスループットを平均 70.5% 上げました。CABRA は、SWE-bench Verified では、編集した行数よりツールを呼んだ回数のほうがエージェントの正答率をよく予測すると報告しています。
week.body_en: AgSpec exploits code and log repetition for retrieval-based speculation, up to 4.76x at batch 16. Coda exploits admission flexibility for 70.5% average SLO-compliant throughput gains. CABRA reports that on SWE-bench Verified, tool-call counts predict agent accuracy better than lines edited.

week.title: 手書き CUDA から高水準の DSL へ: カーネル実装の置き換え
week.title_en: From hand-written CUDA to higher-level kernel DSLs
week.body: Meta は TLX（Triton の低レベル拡張）で Jagged Flash Attention を書き直しました。B200 上で、行数が FA4 の約 3 分の 1 のまま、順伝播で約 13%、逆伝播で約 50% 上回りました。Helion は 1 つの GEMM の実装から形状ごとの自動調整で、vLLM の量子化線形層で最大 10% 超の改善を出しました。FBTriton は推薦の埋め込み検索を CUDA から Triton に移し、元の CUDA カーネルを上回ったと報告しています。論文の Cleave も、コンパイラが手書きの FA2/FA3 を上回ったと報告しています。
week.body_en: Meta's TLX Jagged Flash Attention reportedly beats FA4 on B200 by about 13% forward and 50% backward with roughly a third of the code. Helion's single autotuned GEMM gives vLLM's quantized linear layers more than 10% throughput on some workloads over CUTLASS and DeepGEMM. FBTriton's TBE rewrite reportedly outperforms legacy CUDA. The Cleave paper similarly reports compiler-generated kernels beating handwritten FA2/FA3.

week.title: GPU クラスタを再現でき、検証でき、すぐ使えるものに
week.title_en: Reproducible, verifiable GPU clusters
week.body: NVIDIA は、Megatron Core でビット単位で同じ結果が出る（毎回まったく同じ結果になる）事前学習を大規模に回す方法を紹介しました。AICR v1.0 は、ドライバから各種フレームワークまでのバージョンの組み合わせを検証できる形にします。Modal Clusters は、最大 6.4 Tbps の InfiniBand で結ぶ複数ノードを一般提供しました。全ノードをまとめて確保するギャングスケジューリングのために、スケジューラを新しく作ったと述べています。
week.body_en: NVIDIA describes scaling bitwise-deterministic pretraining in Megatron Core for easier debugging and resumption. AICR v1.0 aims to make the version stack of GPU Kubernetes clusters verifiable. Modal made multi-node clusters with up to 6.4 Tbps InfiniBand generally available, saying it built a new observe-plan-act scheduler for gang scheduling.

week.title: 1 枚の GPU を分け合う、推論エンジンを詰める
week.title_en: Sharing one GPU and tuning a serving stack
week.body: Green Contexts は、1 つのプロセスの中の複数の処理に GPU の資源をどう配るかを決める仕組みとして紹介されました。論文の HALO も、SM（GPU の計算ユニット）を分けてベースと LoRA の計算を重ね、SLO を守ります。vLLM は DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash で、発表から 3 週間でエージェント向けのスループットを 5.3 倍にしました。そのうち SWA の再構築の工夫だけで、TTFT（最初のトークンまでの時間）を約 30% 縮めています。
week.body_en: NVIDIA presents Green Contexts for controlling how GPU resources are split among components in one process. The HALO paper similarly partitions SMs to overlap base and LoRA computation under SLOs. vLLM reports 5.3x agentic throughput on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash within three weeks, with SWA bounded replay alone cutting TTFT about 30%.

papers.title: Kinematic MeanFlow: One-Step Action Generation Policy for Robotic Foundation Models
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study how to achieve one-step action generation in Robotic Foundation Models (RFMs), aiming to overcome the high inference latency of multi-step flow matching. MeanFlow provides a promising framework for this goal, yet its direct application leads to performance collapse. We discover that this stems from two distinctive dynamics exhibited in the RFM velocity field: (1) the ``local acceleration" exhibits stability early on, but surges sharply towards the end of the denoising process, and (2) the spread of its magnitudes across samples widens as denoising progresses. To address these issues, we introduce Kinematic MeanFlow (K-MF), a novel one-step action policy tailored for RFMs. Specifically, grounded in a kinematic identity, K-MF decouples the time derivative term in the MeanFlow formulation into two sub-interval terms separated by an intermediate point. This decoupled formulation enables the two terms to capture early-stage and late-stage denoising dynamics, respectively, while mitigating the error amplification across the process. As a result, our K-MF empowers RFMs to achieve one-step action generation in both training from scratch and fine-tuning paradigms across diverse tasks, while outperforming multi-step flow matching in most settings. In terms of inference efficiency, K-MF reduces action-head latency of GR00T-N1.6 by 67.5%~74.4% across L40 and Jetson Orin in eager and compiled modes, yielding end-to-end latency reductions of 30.3%~54.9%. Code will be available at https://github.com/IntelChina-AI/K-MF.
papers.ja_title: ロボット基盤モデルの一手生成行動方針: カイネマティック・ミーンフロー
papers.summary: ロボット基盤モデル (RFM) は多段階のフローマッチングで行動を生成するため、推論に時間がかかるという問題がある。本研究は MeanFlow を単純に一手生成へ適用すると性能が崩壊する原因を、ノイズ除去終盤での加速度の急変とサンプル間のばらつきの拡大にあると発見し、時間微分項を中間点で2つに分割する K-MF を提案した。GR00T-N1.6 で行動ヘッドの遅延を L40 と Jetson Orin 上で 67.5~74.4% 削減し、全体の遅延も 30.3~54.9% 削減しつつ、多くの設定で多段階のフローマッチングを上回った。
papers.why: ロボット向け推論の低レイテンシ化を、単純な蒸留ではなく動力学的な分析に基づいて実現する手法で、低遅延な行動生成の推論設計に応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Robotic Foundation Models (RFMs) suffer from high inference latency due to multi-step flow matching for action generation. The authors found that directly applying MeanFlow for one-step generation causes performance collapse because the "local acceleration" in the RFM velocity field surges late in denoising and its spread across samples widens; they introduce Kinematic MeanFlow (K-MF), which decouples the time-derivative term at an intermediate point to capture early- and late-stage denoising dynamics separately. K-MF enables one-step action generation that outperforms multi-step flow matching in most settings, reducing GR00T-N1.6's action-head latency by 67.5%~74.4% on L40 and Jetson Orin and end-to-end latency by 30.3%~54.9%.
papers.why_en: It gives a kinematics-grounded fix for one-step action generation rather than naive distillation, directly useful for designing low-latency serving of robotic policies.

papers.title: Match the Distribution, Not the Compute: Post-Training Multi-Token Prediction Heads
papers.abstract: Multi-token prediction (MTP) improves the throughput of autoregressive generation by enabling the language model to draft multiple next tokens per forward pass, while a verification step over draft tokens ensures that token distribution of the backbone is preserved. Every open MTP-family release (MiMo-7B, DeepSeek-V3, Qwen3) trains its heads jointly with the backbone over the full pretraining run of tens of trillions of tokens, thus setting the drafter quality at pretraining time. We ask whether a lightweight post-training pass on target-generated chain-of-thought is enough to reach the same expected throughput speedup on a frozen reasoning model, and study how a serving-time system built on such a checkpoint can be optimized. We present three findings. 1) On a frozen Qwen3-8B with $K{=}3$ chained MTP heads, we show that a post-training recipe with plain cross-entropy on $\approx\!2.5$B tokens reaches or exceeds the expected speedup of jointly trained MiMo-7B on math, coding and knowledge benchmarks. Our post-training recipe utilizes $10^3$-$10^4\times$ less MTP-training tokens as compared with joint pre-training of MiMO-7B MTP baseline. 2) We propose a chain-aware relaxation of draft token verification rule that allows a bounded drift from backbone language model token distribution. We show that this relaxation lifts expected speedups by $+12$ to $+16\%$ per benchmark while preserving task accuracy. 3) We propose an adaptive controller that dynamically chooses the number of MTP heads to be engaged at inference time and demonstrate recovery of upto $11$--$14\%$ loss in speedup using fixed maximum MTP draft length.
papers.ja_title: 蒸留ではなく分布合わせ: 後付けで学習する複数トークン予測ヘッド
papers.summary: 既存の複数トークン予測 (MTP, 一度に複数の次トークンを下書きして生成を速くする仕組み) はすべて事前学習全体 (数十兆トークン) でヘッドを同時学習しており、学習コストが高い。本研究は凍結した推論モデルに対し約 25 億トークンのみの軽量な事後学習を行うことで、同等以上の速度向上を達成できることを示した。検証規則を緩めることでベンチマークごとに速度向上を 12~16 ポイント上乗せし、動的にヘッド数を切り替える制御器で固定長使用時に生じる速度損失の 11~14% を回復した。
papers.why: MTP ヘッドの学習コストを 1000~10000 倍削減しつつ同等の推論高速化を得る方法で、サービング時のドラフトモデル運用に直結する知見を与える。
papers.summary_en: Every open multi-token prediction (MTP) release trains its draft heads jointly with the backbone over the full pretraining run (tens of trillions of tokens), fixing drafter quality at pretraining time. The authors show that a lightweight post-training pass with plain cross-entropy on ~2.5B tokens on a frozen Qwen3-8B reaches or exceeds the expected speedup of jointly trained MiMo-7B, using 10^3-10^4x fewer MTP-training tokens; a chain-aware relaxation of verification lifts speedups by +12 to +16% per benchmark while preserving accuracy, and an adaptive controller recovers up to 11-14% of the speedup lost under a fixed maximum draft length.
papers.why_en: It shows MTP drafter quality can be decoupled from costly joint pretraining, giving serving-system builders a cheap recipe plus verification and controller tricks for draft-based decoding.

papers.title: Clock Diffusion: Efficient Semi-Autoregressive Continuous Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Recent works on continuous diffusion for discrete data have demonstrated performance on par with comparable discrete diffusion models. However, these continuous counterparts lack key features that are essential to practical use as language models, namely variable-length generation and support for a key-value cache, and they still lag behind the frontier of autoregressive and discrete diffusion quality. In this work, we address these limitations. We do so by introducing a model parameterization that uses position-dependent noise schedules to define semi-autoregressive (SAR) continuous diffusion language models (DLMs). Together with efficient training and sampling algorithms, we call this framework Clock Diffusion, and we present two special cases of our method: block and sliding window generation. We then define ClockDLMs, a family of Gaussian DLMs based on sliding window Clock Diffusion that attain state-of-the-art diffusion likelihood bounds on OpenWebText, even beating the performant block SAR discrete diffusion models. ClockDLMs trained on TinyGSM also substantially outperform continuous baselines on the GSM8K benchmark and match and exceed comparable SAR discrete diffusion models. Finally, building on our parameterization, we propose more efficient samplers that we dub Cache Grab, which adapt techniques from accelerated inference in discrete diffusion, such as committing tokens whose probabilities exceed a confidence threshold and self-speculative decoding, further improving our models' quality and efficiency.
papers.ja_title: クロック拡散: 半自己回帰的な連続拡散言語モデルの効率化
papers.summary: 離散データ向けの連続拡散モデルは性能は良いが、可変長生成や KV キャッシュ (生成の高速化に使う計算の再利用機構) に対応できず実用上の弱点があった。本研究は位置に応じて異なるノイズスケジュールを使い、ブロック単位やスライディングウィンドウで生成する半自己回帰的な連続拡散言語モデル Clock Diffusion (ClockDLMs) を提案した。OpenWebText では既存のブロック型離散拡散モデルを上回る最先端の尤度を達成し、TinyGSM で学習した GSM8K では連続拡散のベースラインを大きく上回り、離散拡散と同等以上の性能を得た。
papers.why: 連続拡散言語モデルに KV キャッシュと可変長生成を持ち込む設計で、拡散言語モデルのサービング実装に使える具体的な高速化手法 (Cache Grab サンプラー含む) を示す。
papers.summary_en: Continuous diffusion models for discrete data lack variable-length generation and KV-cache support, and still lag the quality frontier of autoregressive and discrete diffusion models. The authors introduce Clock Diffusion, which uses position-dependent noise schedules to define semi-autoregressive (block or sliding-window) continuous diffusion language models (ClockDLMs), achieving state-of-the-art diffusion likelihood bounds on OpenWebText that even beat performant block SAR discrete diffusion models, and substantially outperforming continuous baselines on GSM8K while matching or exceeding comparable discrete diffusion models. They also propose Cache Grab samplers that adapt confidence-based token committing and self-speculative decoding to further improve quality and efficiency.
papers.why_en: It brings KV-cache support and variable-length generation to continuous diffusion LMs via a concrete semi-autoregressive parameterization and sampler design, directly relevant to serving diffusion language models.

papers.title: RPTune: Learned Context Curation for LLM Catalog Search
papers.abstract: For small merchant businesses (SMBs) whose catalogs fit within a long-context LLM, full-catalog prompting offers a compelling alternative to multi-stage retrieval designed primarily for large marketplaces with millions of items. However, fitting the full catalog into the context window does not ensure that the model can use it effectively, since LLMs do not exploit long contexts uniformly. We therefore study in-context catalog search through two complementary questions: (1) how to curate and present catalogs to the LLM, and (2) how to adapt the LLM for product selection on curated contexts. We propose RPTune, an end-to-end framework that couples learned catalog curation with LLM post-training using automatically generated, catalog-grounded supervision. An encoder-reorganizer curator orders and prunes products guided by downstream LLM feedback, while the resulting curated catalogs in turn improve the effectiveness of LLM post-training with a context-relative reward. We evaluate RPTune on 7 real merchants spanning distinct retail verticals, using 100 complex conversational queries per merchant. RPTune consistently improves search accuracy across both proprietary and open-weight LLMs, with context curation yielding gains of up to 31.4 percentage points and post-training adding a further 10.3 points on average.

papers.title: Divide-and-Remember: Recursive Action-Relevant Memory for Long-Horizon VLA Policies
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models struggle on history-dependent manipulation tasks, where the current observation alone does not determine the action, and the policy needs a memory of the history. Existing memory methods decide what to remember by design, for example, keeping frames with large pixel changes, and show inconsistent gains across tasks. We view what to remember as an optimisation problem. From the POMDP formulation of imitation learning, we show that the optimal memory maximises the conditional mutual information $I(a_t; m_t \mid o_t)$ between the action and the memory given the current observation. Intuitively, this means preserving the action-relevant information in the history that is not already contained in the current observation. Based on our analysis, we propose Divide-and-Remember (D&R), a recursive memory method that learns a memory function $m_t = M(h_t)$ and scales to long contexts while staying compute-light. It involves two strategies: (1) the selection over the full history is divided recursively into subproblems of top-$K$ selection over $2K$ tokens, so that fixed-size, lightweight selectors learned end-to-end support an unbounded history; (2) all recursion blocks share one selector, which captures the selection rule common to every block and keeps the method efficient. On RoboMME, a benchmark of 16 long-horizon manipulation tasks that require remembering when, where, what, and how to act, D&R achieves a state-of-the-art average success rate with consistent gains across all four suites under a budget of only 64 tokens; real-robot experiments show the same gain. Code, checkpoints and more results are at https://dnr-memory.github.io/
papers.ja_title: 分割して記憶する: 長時間タスクのための行動関連メモリの再帰構造
papers.summary: 視覚言語行動 (VLA) モデルは、現在の観測だけでは行動が決まらない長時間タスクで履歴の記憶に失敗するという課題がある。本研究は何を覚えるべきかを「現在の観測を条件とした行動とメモリの条件付き相互情報量」を最大化する問題として定式化し、全履歴の選択を 2K トークンからの上位 K 選択という小問題に再帰的に分割する Divide-and-Remember (D&R) を提案した。16 個の長時間操作タスクからなる RoboMME ベンチマークで、わずか 64 トークンの予算のもとで4つのスイート全てに一貫した改善をもたらし最高水準の成功率を達成し、実機ロボット実験でも同様の効果を確認した。
papers.why: メモリに何を残すかを情報理論的に定式化し、固定サイズの軽量選択器を再帰的に共有することで無限長の履歴を扱えるようにした設計は、長時間タスク向け推論アーキテクチャの効率的な実装指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models struggle on history-dependent manipulation tasks where the current observation alone does not determine the action, and existing memory methods decide what to keep by hand-designed heuristics with inconsistent gains. The authors formulate optimal memory as maximizing the conditional mutual information between the action and memory given the current observation, and propose Divide-and-Remember (D&R), which recursively divides full-history selection into top-K selection over 2K tokens using a single shared, end-to-end learned selector that scales to unbounded history while staying compute-light. On RoboMME, a 16-task long-horizon manipulation benchmark, D&R achieves state-of-the-art average success rate with consistent gains across all four suites under a budget of only 64 tokens, and real-robot experiments show the same gain.
papers.why_en: It gives a principled, information-theoretic answer to "what to remember" and a recursive, compute-light selector architecture, offering a concrete efficient-memory design for long-horizon policy serving.

papers.title: The Devil Is in the Reconstruction Loss Scale: Rethinking Optimization in LLM Quantization
papers.abstract: Post-training quantization (PTQ) methods typically use sequential quantization that partitions a pre-trained LLM into a series of units (e.g., transformer blocks), with one unit quantized at each stage. State-of-the-art PTQ methods are predominantly learning-based, optimizing auxiliary quantization parameters (e.g., scaling factors, rotation matrices, clipping thresholds, and adapters) via gradient descent to minimize a reconstruction loss. A common practice is to use mean squared error (MSE) as the reconstruction loss function, yet its induced optimization behavior remains largely unexplored. In this work, we take a holistic view of sequential quantization and systematically investigate how optimization evolves from the first quantization stage to the last, aiming for a deep understanding of optimization in learning-based PTQ schemes. Through extensive empirical studies spanning representative learning-based PTQ methods, LLM families, model scales, architectures, quantization settings and various tasks, we consistently uncover Optimization Imbalance: reconstruction loss magnitudes vary dramatically across stages, accompanied by highly uneven gradient magnitudes and parameter updates under MSE. We term the cross-stage range of loss magnitudes the reconstruction loss scale, and reveal that MSE translates the unexpectedly large reconstruction loss scale into highly uneven gradient magnitudes, which in turn lead to uneven optimization strength across quantization stages. This finding suggests a general principle for improving learning-based PTQ: optimization strength across stages should be decoupled from the reconstruction loss scale. Theoretically, we show that root mean squared error (RMSE) variants defined at the sample, channel, token, and element levels naturally realize this principle through implicit gradient normalization, outperforming MSE significantly as a drop-in replacement.
papers.ja_title: 量子化の落とし穴は再構成損失のスケールにあった: LLM 量子化の最適化を見直す
papers.summary: 学習ベースの事後量子化 (PTQ) は Transformer ブロックを順に量子化していくが、よく使われる平均二乗誤差 (MSE) 損失がどう最適化に影響するかはこれまで調べられていなかった。本研究は複数の手法・モデル・規模・タスクで系統的に調査し、量子化の段階ごとに再構成損失の大きさが大きく異なり、それに応じて勾配や更新量も不均一になる「最適化の不均衡」を発見した。サンプル・チャネル・トークン・要素単位で定義した二乗平均平方根誤差 (RMSE) に置き換えることで、この不均衡を暗黙的な勾配正規化によって解消し、MSE を大きく上回る性能を示した。
papers.why: 量子化の損失関数選択が最適化バランスに与える影響を体系的に実証した研究で、PTQ 手法を実装・評価する際に損失関数設計を見直すべき具体的な根拠を与える。
papers.summary_en: Learning-based post-training quantization (PTQ) typically minimizes mean squared error (MSE) reconstruction loss stage-by-stage, but how this choice shapes optimization has been largely unexplored. Through extensive empirical studies spanning PTQ methods, model families, scales, architectures and tasks, the authors consistently find "Optimization Imbalance": reconstruction loss magnitudes vary dramatically across stages, driving highly uneven gradients and parameter updates under MSE. They show that RMSE variants defined at sample, channel, token, and element levels implicitly normalize gradients and significantly outperform MSE as a drop-in replacement.
papers.why_en: It uncovers a general, previously unexamined optimization pathology in learning-based PTQ and offers a simple loss-function fix, giving a concrete methodological lens for evaluating and designing quantization pipelines.

papers.title: Adapter Thickets: Splitting an RLVR Budget Beats Concentrating It
papers.abstract: Majority voting over sampled completions is the workhorse of test-time scaling, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) is the workhorse for making each completion better. The standard pipeline composes the two: train one policy with RLVR, then sample it many times and vote. We show that this composition is lossy. A vote can only overturn mistakes that its voters do not share, and RLVR sharpens a policy so that its samples increasingly make the same mistakes. With every method drawing exactly $160$ completions per problem, training a single LoRA adapter on the full RLVR budget raises single-sample accuracy on every model we test ($1.5$B-$8$B). Yet on three of four models it leaves the majority vote below that of the untrained base model, by up to $4.8$ points. The damage builds during training: voter errors grow steadily more correlated, and the majority vote accuracy peaks early before falling by up to $7.0$ points. The cause is concentration, not RLVR itself. We split the same data and training budget across $K$ LoRA adapters, each trained on its own random disjoint shard, and call the result an adapter thicket. Thickets out-vote the fully trained adapter in all $16$ (model, $K$) settings, and for $K{\geq}4$ they stay within $0.8$ points of the base model or above it. A single adapter stopped early, at a thicket member's step count, is a strong control that matches thickets for small $K$. For $K{\geq}8$, thickets keep more of RLVR's single-sample gain and out-vote this control in six of eight settings. The cost of concentration also grows with the number of votes: from $16$ to $160$ votes, the thicket's lead over the fully trained adapter widens from $1.3$ to $3.3$ points. When the plan is to sample and vote, an RLVR budget is better spent broad than deep.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: RLVR の予算は集中より分散が勝る: アダプター群による多数決
papers.summary: 検証可能報酬による強化学習 (RLVR) で方針を鍛えてから何度もサンプリングして多数決する手法はテスト時スケーリングの定番だが、本研究は RLVR が方針を鋭くしすぎてサンプル同士が同じ間違いを共有するようになり、多数決の効果を損なうことを示した。160 回サンプリングする設定で、単一の LoRA アダプターを全予算で学習すると単発精度は 1.5B~8B の全モデルで向上するが、4 モデル中 3 つで多数決の精度は訓練前のベースモデルより最大 4.8 ポイント低下した。同じデータと予算を K 個の LoRA アダプターに分割してそれぞれ別々に学習する「アダプター厚み」にすると、16 通りの (モデル, K) 設定すべてで単一アダプターの多数決を上回り、投票数が 16 から 160 に増えるほどその優位は 1.3 から 3.3 ポイントへ広がった。
papers.why: サンプリングと多数決を前提とするテスト時スケーリングでは、RLVR の学習予算を1つの方針に集中させず複数の独立な方針に分散させるべきという、学習計算資源の配分に関する実践的な知見を与える。
papers.summary_en: Majority voting over RLVR-trained policy samples is the standard test-time scaling pipeline, but the authors show this composition is lossy because RLVR sharpens a policy so its samples increasingly share the same mistakes. With exactly 160 completions per problem, training a single LoRA adapter on the full RLVR budget raises single-sample accuracy on every tested model (1.5B-8B), yet on three of four models the majority vote falls below the untrained base model by up to 4.8 points, and voter-error correlation grows during training. Splitting the same budget across K LoRA adapters trained on disjoint shards ("adapter thickets") out-votes the fully trained adapter in all 16 (model, K) settings, with the advantage widening from 1.3 to 3.3 points as votes increase from 16 to 160.
papers.why_en: It gives a concrete, empirically grounded recommendation that when sampling-and-voting is the deployment plan, an RLVR training budget should be spread across diverse policies rather than concentrated into one, a direct consideration for post-training resource allocation.

review.note: 多数決精度が単発精度の向上とは独立に悪化しうることを、投票数やアダプター数を変えて体系的に測定しており、テスト時スケーリング手法を評価する際に見落としがちな観点 (訓練中の誤り相関の増大) を示す。
review.note_en: It systematically measures how majority-vote accuracy can degrade independently of single-sample accuracy gains across varying vote counts and adapter counts, surfacing an easily overlooked evaluation pitfall (growing error correlation during training) for test-time scaling methods.

papers.title: AgSpec: Pushing the Limits of Retrieval-Based Speculative Decoding in Coding Agent Pipelines
papers.abstract: Retrieval-based speculative decoding (SD) drafts tokens by copying continuations from existing text, which suits coding agents that repeatedly reproduce code, logs, and earlier attempts. Yet existing methods fall short in agent pipelines: much of the reusable text is missing from their corpora or stored in a form that differs from what the agent emits, and their draft lengths ignore that accept length varies across agents and drifts over turns. We present AgSpec, a framework that supplies the corpus and draft-length policies that existing retrieval engines lack in coding-agent pipelines. AgSpec retrieves from session, workspace, and global corpora, retaining the ongoing session trajectory and indexing opened files in the agent's emission format. It bounds each agent's draft length with an offline-profiled cap and adapts the length online from verification feedback. On two repository-level multi-agent coding benchmarks, AgSpec outperforms five retrieval-based drafters and EAGLE-3 in most evaluated settings, raising generation throughput over autoregressive decoding up to 4.37$\times$ at batch size 1 and 4.76$\times$ at batch size 16. AgSpec also remains effective on benchmarks without a repository or a multi-agent pipeline, showing that its gains generalize to coding agents broadly.
papers.ja_title: AgSpec: コーディングエージェント向け検索ベース投機的デコーディングの限界を広げる
papers.summary: 検索ベースの投機的デコーディング (既存テキストから続きをコピーして下書きする高速化手法) はコードやログを繰り返し生成するコーディングエージェントに向いているが、既存手法は再利用できるテキストの多くをコーパスに持たず、下書きの長さもエージェントや会話の進行に応じて調整していない。AgSpec はセッション・ワークスペース・グローバルの3種のコーパスから検索し、エージェントの出力形式のままファイルを索引し、オフラインで計測した上限とオンラインの検証結果に応じて下書き長を適応させる。2つのリポジトリ規模マルチエージェントコーディングベンチマークで、5つの検索ベース手法と EAGLE-3 を上回り、自己回帰デコーディングに対しバッチサイズ1で最大 4.37 倍、バッチサイズ16で最大 4.76 倍のスループット向上を達成した。
papers.why: コーディングエージェント特有の再利用パターン (セッション履歴やファイル形式) に合わせたコーパス設計と適応的な下書き長制御という、投機的デコーディングの実運用上の具体的な改善点を示す。
papers.summary_en: Retrieval-based speculative decoding drafts tokens by copying continuations from existing text, fitting coding agents that repeatedly reproduce code and logs, but existing methods miss much reusable text and use fixed draft lengths despite accept length varying and drifting across agents and turns. AgSpec retrieves from session, workspace, and global corpora, indexes opened files in the agent's own emission format, and bounds/adapts draft length using offline profiling plus online verification feedback. On two repository-level multi-agent coding benchmarks, AgSpec outperforms five retrieval-based drafters and EAGLE-3 in most settings, raising throughput over autoregressive decoding up to 4.37x at batch size 1 and 4.76x at batch size 16.
papers.why_en: It targets the specific reuse patterns and length-drift issues of coding-agent pipelines, offering a concrete corpus-and-length-adaptation design for speculative decoding in agentic serving systems.

papers.title: Latent Information Sharing for Accelerating Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is a communication-efficient distributed learning paradigm. However, client drift remains one of the most critical challenges, hindering the efficient training of a global model. In this study, we propose a novel latent information sharing scheme that directly mitigates data heterogeneity across clients. Our theoretical and empirical results show that sharing a small amount of hidden-layer activations significantly improves training efficiency while preserving convergence guarantees and data privacy. Furthermore, we compare our method with existing FL approaches designed to address client drift, including FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedPVR, FedProto, and SplitFed, and demonstrate superior model accuracy under a fixed round budget without incurring excessive communication overhead. Overall, this work presents a promising new knowledge aggregation scheme and provides a comprehensive analysis of the impact of activation sharing on federated optimization.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 隠れ層の情報共有で連合学習の client drift を緩和
papers.summary: 連合学習 (複数端末が協力してモデルを学習する手法) では、端末ごとのデータの偏りによって学習がずれる client drift が問題になる。この研究は、各端末の隠れ層の活性化 (latent information) を少しだけ共有する方法を提案し、収束の保証とデータの秘匿性を保ったまま学習効率を上げた。FedProx、SCAFFOLD、FedPVR、FedProto、SplitFed といった既存手法と比べ、同じ通信ラウンド数のもとでより高い精度を達成し、通信量も過大には増えなかった。
papers.why: 通信コストを抑えつつ client drift を直接狙う新しい知識集約の方式として、連合学習基盤を作る人の設計の選択肢になる。
papers.summary_en: In federated learning, client drift caused by data heterogeneity across clients hinders efficient training of a global model. This work shares a small amount of hidden-layer activations (latent information) across clients, improving training efficiency while preserving convergence guarantees and data privacy. Compared with FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedPVR, FedProto, and SplitFed, it achieves superior model accuracy under a fixed round budget without excessive communication overhead.
papers.why_en: It offers distributed-training builders a new knowledge-aggregation scheme that targets client drift directly while keeping communication cost in check.

papers.title: Do Multilingual Encoders Produce Language-Consistent Semantic IDs?
papers.abstract: Semantic IDs (SIDs) compress item embeddings into discrete code sequences used in generative retrieval. We ask whether a multilingual encoder is sufficient for different-language renderings of the same product to receive language-consistent SIDs. Using Amazon ESCI listings rendered in English, Spanish, and Japanese, we test whether translations remain close to their English source, whether residual quantization is unusually sensitive to translation-induced movement, and whether multilingual or language-balanced quantizer fitting improves SID agreement. Multilingual E5 places translations measurably apart: under an English-heavy fit, a Japanese translation preserves the first SID code of its English counterpart in only 7.7% of cases, compared with 89.0% for an English rewording. Distance-matched product-directed controls produce nearly the same full-SID mismatch as translation, providing no evidence that the quantizer selectively amplifies language directions. Balancing the fitting mixture makes codebook use more uniform but further reduces cross-lingual prefix agreement: Spanish first-code consistency falls from 28.3% to 6.6%, while an English-only fit preserves it for 67.6% of Spanish translations. These results show that multilingual exposure and balanced codebook use alone do not guarantee language-consistent SIDs.

papers.title: Serving a Revisable World: Versioned Execution for Interruptible Agents
papers.abstract: LLM agents revise running tasks when users change instructions, tools fail, or new information changes a plan. Today's servers express a revision as aborting old requests and submitting replacements. Yet the old execution's buffered output and outstanding work must stop affecting the application, while completed KV state may still be useful to its replacement. Handling these obligations separately can leave obsolete effects publishable and force the successor to rebuild valid state. We present \retire, a serving control-plane redesign around \emph{versioned execution}. Requests own scheduling and memory resources; execution versions own \emph{authority}, the permission to publish output or install state for the current execution. \retire first revokes obsolete work, then bounds its remaining execution and certifies the completed prefix its successor can inherit. The successor runs from that state while isolated old resources are reclaimed asynchronously. This unifies fast invalidation and selective preservation in one version transition. We implement \retire in vLLM across output publication, GPU execution, KV handoff, tiered recovery, and distributed and multi-tenant serving. Correctness experiments verify current-version output and valid state inheritance across these paths. Combining invalidation with inheritance reduces revision-to-successor time-to-first-token by a median 17.1\% in controlled paired experiments. A replay of recorded coding-agent interruption arrivals emits no obsolete output and keeps every final version progressing through repeated revisions. \retire turns abort-and-restart into a coordinated handoff that stops obsolete work quickly and preserves useful work for its successor.
papers.ja_title: 版管理実行で LLM エージェントの中断・再実行を高速化
papers.summary: LLM エージェントは指示の変更やツール失敗で実行中のタスクを修正するが、既存のサーバーは古い要求を打ち切って新しい要求を出し直すだけなので、古い出力が残ったり、使えるはずの KV キャッシュの状態まで捨てて再構築する無駄が生じる。この研究は vLLM 上で「版管理実行 (versioned execution)」という仕組みを作り、古い実行の権限をすぐに取り消しつつ、有効な途中状態だけを次の実行に引き継がせる。制御実験では、切り替え後の最初トークンまでの時間が中央値で 17.1% 短縮され、実際のコーディングエージェントの中断記録を再現しても古い出力は一切出ず、すべての版が進行を続けた。
papers.why: 推論サービング基盤を作る人にとって、中断と再実行を場当たり的な打ち切りではなく一つの協調したハンドオフとして扱う制御プレーン設計の具体例になる。
papers.summary_en: LLM agents revise running tasks when instructions change or tools fail, but today's servers simply abort old requests and submit replacements, letting obsolete output leak out or forcing successors to rebuild valid KV state from scratch. This work introduces versioned execution in vLLM, which revokes authority from obsolete work while letting the successor inherit a certified valid prefix of state. In controlled paired experiments this reduces revision-to-successor time-to-first-token by a median of 17.1%, and a replay of recorded coding-agent interruptions emits no obsolete output while every final version keeps progressing.
papers.why_en: It gives serving-infrastructure builders a concrete control-plane design that turns abort-and-restart into a coordinated handoff instead of ad hoc cancellation.

papers.title: Science Utopia? Closed-Loop LLM Simulation of Academic Research Ecosystems
papers.abstract: Scientific progress emerges from a longitudinal ecosystem in which researchers, institutions, funding agencies, collaboration networks, and the scientific literature co-evolve. As AI becomes increasingly involved throughout the scientific research cycle, understanding these interconnected and evolving processes becomes increasingly important. We introduce SciUtopia, a persistent, closed-loop LLM-agent simulation framework for studying academic research ecosystems. SciUtopia models interconnected scientific processes such as research-direction choice, collaboration, submission, peer review, resubmission, citation, funding, and researcher attrition, while maintaining evolving states across simulated years. Its configurable institutional mechanisms and information channels provide a controlled testbed for matched counterfactual experiments and targeted interventions. Across 61 simulation worlds, SciUtopia simulates over 40,000 researchers from 8,000 institutions, producing around 400,000 publication decisions and 1.2 million LLM-generated peer reviews. Using these longitudinal simulations, we find that rejection-driven resubmission substantially amplifies reviewer burden beyond population growth alone, cautious exploration balances citation impact with career success and long-term topic diversity, and resource inequality can emerge even without detectable cumulative advantage from narrowly winning early funding. Code is available at https://github.com/Ahren09/ScienceUtopia.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク

papers.title: RapidMoE: Exploiting Cross-Asymmetry via Adaptive Residual Offloading for Large-Scale MoE Inference
papers.abstract: The widespread adoption of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) has created a growing need for deployment on heterogeneous platforms. However, it exposes a fundamental mismatch between the algorithmic demands of large-scale MoE and the disparate characteristics of hardware.Existing CPU-GPU hybrid inference systems fail to resolve this as they either encounter PCIe bandwidth bottlenecks when loading experts to GPUs, or rely heavily on CPU computation. Consequently, this leads to low resource utilization and inevitable violations of fixed latency budgets as parameters scale. In this paper, we identify and exploit Cross-Asymmetry--a structural alignment between the algorithmic workload skew of MoE routing and the physical disparity of heterogeneous hardware. To this end, we introduce RapidMoE, a residual offloading system for efficient large-scale MoE inference. We propose how RapidMoE leverages a residual-split framework to enable offloading paradigm shift from expert-level to bit-level, which unfolds across three key dimensions: (1) data representation, enabling compact and decoupled storage; (2) routing strategy, partitioning computation into dual paths aligned with hardware capabilities; (3) execution parallelism, scheduling a balanced storage-compute workload across devices. We further employ a novel Unified Multi-Level Importance Arbitration to adaptively adjust the critical expert set at runtime, ensuring the accuracy-latency Pareto frontier. These innovations exploit inherent cross-asymmetry, fundamentally breaking the algorithm-hardware misalignment. Experimental results show that RapidMoE achieves up to 3.5x speedup in decoding and 2.1x speedup in prefill compared to state-of-the-art (SOTA) offloading systems.
papers.ja_title: 異種ハードウェアの非対称性を利用した大規模 MoE 推論オフロード
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (複数の専門家モデルを切り替えて使う構造) をヘテロな CPU-GPU 環境で動かすとき、既存のオフロード手法はエキスパートを GPU に読み込む際の PCIe 帯域制限に詰まるか、CPU 計算に頼りすぎて資源利用率が低く遅延の目標を守れない。この研究は、MoE のルーティングが持つ偏りとハードウェアの違いが構造的に一致する「Cross-Asymmetry」を見つけ、ビット単位でのオフロードとデュアルパスのルーティング、ストレージと計算のバランス調整を行う RapidMoE を提案した。既存の最先端オフロードシステムと比べ、デコード時に最大 3.5 倍、プレフィル時に最大 2.1 倍の速度向上を達成した。
papers.why: 大規模 MoE を異種ハードウェアでサービングする人に、アルゴリズムとハードウェアの構造的な非対称性を直接利用する新しいオフロード設計を提供する。
papers.summary_en: Serving large-scale Mixture-of-Experts on heterogeneous CPU-GPU platforms suffers from either PCIe bandwidth bottlenecks when loading experts to GPUs or heavy reliance on CPU computation, causing low utilization and latency-budget violations. This work identifies Cross-Asymmetry, a structural alignment between MoE routing's workload skew and heterogeneous hardware, and builds RapidMoE, which shifts offloading from expert-level to bit-level via compact data representation, dual-path routing, and balanced storage-compute scheduling. It achieves up to 3.5x speedup in decoding and 2.1x speedup in prefill compared to state-of-the-art offloading systems.
papers.why_en: It gives builders of large-scale MoE serving systems a new offloading design that directly exploits the structural asymmetry between algorithm and heterogeneous hardware.

papers.title: ProtoFlow: Prototype-Guided Flow Matching for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Generative modeling has shown strong promise for multivariate time mseries (MTS) forecasting, especially scale to high-dimensional settings. Diffusion-based methods achieve competitive performance but typically require many sampling steps at inference. VAE-based non-iterative forecasting frameworks have therefore emerged as an efficient alternative. Within this line of work, vector quantization (VQ) enables controllable latent space modeling by mapping multivariate series into compact discrete representations. Existing VQ-based forecasting methods, however, typically rely on autoregressive (AR) token generation, which suffers from exposure bias and training-inference mismatch. Flow matching provides an efficient non-autoregressive alternative for latent forecasting, but existing formulations usually initialize transport from a generic Gaussian prior. We instead observe that the trained VQ codebook already captures representative latent prototypes and can thus serve as a more informative prior for flow matching. Based on this insight, we propose ProtoFlow, a forecasting framework that combines vector-quantized autoencoding with Prototype-prior Flow matching. Our method first maps multivariate sequences into a discrete latent space, then constructs a structured prior from the learned codebook, and finally learns a DiT-based rectified flow to transport samples from this prior to future latent representations conditioned on historical observations. By replacing generic noise initialization with a learned prototype prior, ProtoFlow avoids the rollout mismatch of AR token prediction and promotes faster training convergence. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets show that it consistently achieves superior forecasting performance with efficient inference.

papers.title: AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models
papers.abstract: Muon improves large-scale training by applying a spectral-norm steepest-descent update to matrix parameters, but practical models also contain parameter blocks that do not fit dense-matrix geometry. One important case is the tied vocabulary table, which appears in language models and other token generators and can receive multiple structurally different gradient sources, from sparse input lookups to dense output-classifier updates. In the reference recipe these blocks are handed to an auxiliary AdamW optimizer, which restores second-moment state and updates the aliased table as a generic tensor. We propose AF-Muon, an AdamW-free extension of Muon that keeps the Muon matrix update for hidden weight matrices while using a support-aware finite-cap linear minimization oracle for tied vocabulary tables and an RMS-normalized update for one-dimensional auxiliary parameters. AF-Muon therefore trains every parameter class with a single first-moment buffer and no second-moment state, saving around 20% optimizer-state memory relative to Hybrid Muon in our benchmark. Across nine tied-token settings - decoder-only language models from 124M to 1B parameters, a fully shared T5-style encoder-decoder, and ImageGPT-style image-token, protein, and sparse-MoE variants, spanning text, image, and protein-sequence data - AF-Muon improves mean validation loss and perplexity over both Hybrid Muon and a SCION-style Sign endpoint. Long-horizon runs and hyperparameter sensitivity studies confirm the gain is robust, and identical-momentum diagnostics attribute it to the finite cap, which preserves more within-row magnitude than Sign while bounding the coordinate concentration of row-RMS. These results identify tied vocabulary tables as a distinct optimizer geometry and yield a robust AdamW-free Muon variant across models, modalities, and architectures, with about 1% step-time overhead in matched training.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 共有語彙テーブルのための AdamW 不要な Muon 最適化手法
papers.summary: Muon は行列パラメータに合わせた更新方式で大規模学習を効率化するが、言語モデルで入力埋め込みと出力分類器を共有する「tied vocabulary table」のような密行列に合わないブロックは、従来は別の AdamW に任せて二次モーメント状態を余分に保持していた。この研究は、隠れ層の行列には Muon の更新を保ちつつ、共有語彙テーブルには有限キャップ付きの線形最小化方式、1 次元の補助パラメータには RMS 正規化更新を使う AF-Muon を提案し、すべてのパラメータを一次モーメントだけで学習できるようにした。124M〜1B パラメータの言語モデルから画像・タンパク質トークンモデル、スパース MoE まで 9 設定で、Hybrid Muon や SCION 式 Sign より検証損失とパープレキシティが改善し、オプティマイザの状態メモリは約 20% 削減、ステップ時間の増加は約 1% に留まった。
papers.why: 大規模モデルの学習を効率化する人に、tied vocabulary table という特有の最適化幾何を見つけ、メモリを節約しつつ性能を落とさない AdamW 不要な Muon 拡張を提供する。
papers.summary_en: Muon speeds up large-scale training with a spectral-norm steepest-descent update for matrix parameters, but tied vocabulary tables -- shared between input embeddings and output classifiers -- don't fit this dense-matrix geometry and are usually handed to an auxiliary AdamW optimizer with extra second-moment state. This work proposes AF-Muon, which keeps Muon's matrix update for hidden weights while using a support-aware finite-cap linear minimization oracle for tied vocabulary tables and an RMS-normalized update for 1D parameters, training every parameter class with only a first-moment buffer. Across nine tied-token settings spanning 124M-1B language models, a T5-style encoder-decoder, and image/protein/MoE variants, AF-Muon improves mean validation loss and perplexity over Hybrid Muon and a SCION-style Sign baseline while saving around 20% optimizer-state memory with only about 1% step-time overhead.
papers.why_en: It gives large-model training-efficiency engineers a distinct optimizer geometry for tied vocabulary tables and a memory-saving, AdamW-free Muon variant that keeps performance intact.

papers.title: Rethinking Probability-Based Reinforcement Learning From Posterior Concentration
papers.abstract: Verifier-free reinforcement learning with probability-based rewards offers a promising way to train LLMs on general reasoning tasks where external verifiers are unavailable. Yet the reliability of these rewards, especially in long-horizon reasoning, remains underexplored. This work identifies a length-dependent failure mode of probability rewards, which we call the Posterior Concentration Phenomenon (PCP). We show that the probability of a reference answer conditioned on a reasoning trace often collapses to a low-variance interval as the trace becomes lengthy. This phenomenon results in nearly indistinguishable rewards, which, under GRPO-based settings, makes probability-based policy optimization unstable and inefficient. Motivated by this, we propose Reinforcement Learning with Concentration-aware Posterior Rewards (RLCPR), a verifier-free RL framework to explicitly account for PCP for better optimization stability and token efficiency. It has two components: uncertainty-aware data sampling, which reduces concentration-prone rollouts before generation, and concentration-aware regularization, which penalizes unnecessarily long traces when posterior rewards collapse. Extensive experiments show that, alongside higher token efficiency, RLCPR outperforms the state-of-the-art verifier-free RL baseline by up to 4.0% on six of seven benchmarks, including general-domain and mathematical reasoning challenges.
papers.ja_title: 長い推論で確率報酬が偏る問題 (PCP) を踏まえた検証器なし RL
papers.summary: 検証器を使わずに確率に基づく報酬で LLM を強化学習させる手法は、推論過程 (reasoning trace) が長くなるほど参照答えの事後確率がほとんど同じ狭い範囲に集まってしまう現象 (Posterior Concentration Phenomenon, PCP) を起こし、GRPO のような学習で報酬の差がなくなって不安定・非効率になることが分かった。この研究は、集中しやすいロールアウトを生成前に減らすサンプリングと、報酬が収束したときに不必要に長い推論を罰する正則化を組み合わせた RLCPR を提案した。7 つのベンチマークのうち 6 つで、既存の検証器なし RL の最良手法より最大 4.0% 性能が向上し、トークン効率も改善した。
papers.why: 検証器が使えない一般的な推論タスクで LLM を RL 後学習する人に、報酬の信頼性が崩れる具体的な失敗モード (PCP) とその回避策を示す。
papers.summary_en: Verifier-free RL with probability-based rewards is attractive for training LLMs on general reasoning, but this work shows a length-dependent failure mode called the Posterior Concentration Phenomenon (PCP): the reference-answer probability conditioned on a reasoning trace collapses to a low-variance interval as traces lengthen, making rewards nearly indistinguishable and destabilizing GRPO-based optimization. The proposed RLCPR combines uncertainty-aware data sampling that reduces concentration-prone rollouts before generation with concentration-aware regularization that penalizes unnecessarily long traces when posterior rewards collapse. It outperforms the state-of-the-art verifier-free RL baseline by up to 4.0% on six of seven benchmarks while improving token efficiency.
papers.why_en: It gives post-training RL practitioners working without verifiers a concrete failure mode of reward reliability (PCP) and a mitigation.

papers.title: Open-Source Live-Reconfigurable Multi-Mode Wearable Ultrasound
papers.abstract: Wearable ultrasound enables continuous deep-tissue monitoring, and a single programmable probe can operate in multiple complementary modes, such as structural A-mode and Doppler flow measurement. However, each operating mode requires dedicated measurement parameters and peripheral states, with no single configuration serving all modes on resource-constrained devices. Time multiplexing of operating modes introduces reconfiguration latency that lowers the effective mode repetition rate. To address this limitation, we present an open-source, transition-aware control stack for low-latency, in-session reconfiguration of the 32-channel TinyProbe wearable platform. Operating modes are described as hardware configurations, and host-side shadow registers track the peripheral states, enabling transition-specific register updates. Transition sequences are executed either by the host (over Wi-Fi 6) or by a firmware loop on the probe MCU. We validate the stack on a pulsatile-flow phantom by interleaving blocks of 25 to 100 pulsed-wave Doppler shots at 1.43 kHz PRF with single 16-channel A-mode acquisitions, changing channel configurations at every transition. Compared to full reconfiguration, the overhead per transition decreases from 30.2 ms to 11.6 ms (host-scheduled) and 3.1 ms (MCU-scheduled). For 75-shot Doppler blocks, the multi-mode repetition rate reaches 16.0 Hz (MCU-scheduled), 90.1% of the theoretical maximum of 17.7 Hz. Concurrent reconstruction of a Doppler spectrogram and a lumen-diameter trace demonstrates the functionality of time-multiplexed flow and structural monitoring.
papers.ja_title: 装着型超音波プローブのモード切替を高速化する制御スタック

papers.title: In-context Learning of Single-index Targets: Comparing Kernel and Feature Learners
papers.abstract: In-context learning (ICL) enables a pretrained model to infer a task from demonstrations without updating its parameters. While much of the existing theory focuses on linear target functions, in this paper we study nonlinear cases by comparing two one-layer attention architectures on the same family of single-index tasks. A kernel learner first maps inputs through a fixed nonlinear feature map and then applies linear attention, whereas a feature learner applies attention to the original input, followed by a learned nonlinear readout. We derive predictions for their memorization and generalization errors using the replica method, retaining the effects of pretraining size, task-pool diversity, and training and inference context lengths. The resulting predictions closely match numerical experiments across a broad range of regimes. Our analysis yields phase diagrams that characterize when each architecture is advantageous as the amount of pretraining data, task diversity, and context lengths vary. We further identify qualitatively different context-length scalings for the two learners. Together, these results clarify how architectural choices interact with the dataset and govern nonlinear in-context learning.
papers.ja_title: 文脈内学習の理論:カーネル学習者と特徴学習者の比較
papers.summary: 文脈内学習 (ICL, 事前学習済みモデルが例示だけからタスクを推論する手法) の理論は線形タスクが中心で、非線形な場合の分析が不足していた。本研究は、固定の非線形特徴写像の後に線形注意を使う「カーネル学習者」と、入力そのものに注意を適用し非線形な読み出しを学習する「特徴学習者」を、単一指数関数タスクという共通の問題設定で比較した。レプリカ法で記憶誤差と一般化誤差を理論的に導き、事前学習データ量・タスクの多様性・文脈長に応じてどちらが有利かを示す相図を数値実験と良く一致する形で得た。
papers.why: 文脈内学習を担う注意機構のアーキテクチャ選択が、データ量やタスク多様性とどう相互作用するかを定量化しており、モデル構造の設計指針として使える。
papers.summary_en: In-context learning (ICL) theory has mostly addressed linear targets, leaving nonlinear cases underexplored. This paper compares two one-layer attention architectures on the same family of single-index tasks: a kernel learner (fixed nonlinear feature map plus linear attention) and a feature learner (attention on raw input plus a learned nonlinear readout). Using the replica method, the authors derive memorization and generalization error predictions that closely match numerical experiments, yielding phase diagrams of when each architecture is favored as pretraining size, task diversity, and context length vary.
papers.why_en: Quantifies how architectural choices in attention-based ICL interact with pretraining data and task diversity, offering theoretical guidance relevant to designing nonlinear in-context learners.

papers.title: ePACT: Energy-Performance-Aware Commitment Tracking for LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Reducing LLM serving energy does not by itself guarantee lower deployment cost when electricity procurement exposes operators to unfavorable deviations from preset commitments. We study hourly commitments with positive, potentially asymmetric costs for overuse and underuse, and formulate energy-Performance-Aware Commitment Tracking: minimize deviation costs subject to request-level service requirements. We implement ePACT, a two-level controller that adjusts serving capacity and GPU clocks as requests arrive. A global planner updates interval energy targets from measured consumption and the remaining hourly commitment. A local decision maker predicts candidate configurations' energy and completion times, checks predicted deadline misses, and selects among admitted configurations by asymmetric target-deviation cost, with a service-first fallback. Coarse-to-fine action search runs asynchronously with serving. We evaluate ePACT through single-hour comparisons, controller ablations, and full-day trace simulations for H20 and H200 GPU pools. In the 24-hour simulations, ePACT reduces the asymmetric deviation cost by $73.8\%$ and $75.7\%$ relative to vLLM while retaining near-vLLM SLO attainment. Mean absolute hourly deviations are $2.16\%$ and $2.31\%$, respectively.
papers.ja_title: 電力契約の逸脱コストを抑える LLM 推論サービングコントローラ ePACT
papers.summary: LLM 推論サービスは電力消費を減らすだけでは、時間単位の電力契約 (超過・不足にそれぞれ非対称なコストがかかる契約) 違反によるコスト増を防げない。本研究は、サービス品質 (SLO) を保ちながら契約逸脱コストを最小化する二段階コントローラ ePACT を提案し、全体計画器が時間ごとのエネルギー目標を更新し、局所判断器がサービス能力と GPU クロックをリクエストごとに調整する。H20・H200 の GPU プールでの 24 時間トレースシミュレーションでは、vLLM と比べて非対称な契約逸脱コストを 73.8% と 75.7% 削減しつつ、SLO 達成率はほぼ同等だった。
papers.why: 電力契約という実運用コストの制約を推論サービングのスケジューリングに直接組み込む設計を示し、データセンター運用者に実務的な指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: Reducing LLM serving energy alone doesn't guarantee lower cost when hourly electricity commitments impose asymmetric penalties for overuse and underuse. The authors propose ePACT, a two-level controller that adjusts serving capacity and GPU clocks per request to minimize commitment-deviation costs while meeting per-request SLOs, with a global planner updating energy targets and a local decision maker selecting configurations. In 24-hour trace simulations on H20 and H200 GPU pools, ePACT reduces asymmetric deviation cost by 73.8% and 75.7% relative to vLLM while retaining near-vLLM SLO attainment, with mean absolute hourly deviations of 2.16% and 2.31%.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates a concrete scheduling design that folds real electricity-commitment costs into LLM serving control, directly useful for data center operators balancing energy procurement against SLOs.

papers.title: SkillEvoLean: Mutation-enhanced skill evolution for Lean provers
papers.abstract: Skill evolution offers a promising way to improve large language model agents without updating their parameters, but its use in formal theorem proving remains underexplored. Existing methods mainly target natural-language reasoning, improving skills by analyzing successful and failed trajectories and incrementally revising solving strategies. Although the Lean verifier provides reliable execution feedback, when all sampled trajectories fail, existing skill evolution methods lack successful trajectories from which to infer effective update directions. Furthermore, these methods also focus mainly on the root instruction file, thus underexploring the evolution of reference knowledge including mathematical concepts and proving techniques. To address these limitations, we propose a mutation-enhanced skill self-evolution framework for building skill-augmented Lean provers. The framework jointly evolves a high-level solving policy and its reference knowledge through progressive and mutation-based updates. Progressive evolution derives local improvements from successful and failed trajectories, while mutation is triggered when no complete proof can be generated, sampling mathematical concepts to produce and select new skill candidates under verifier feedback. We evaluate our method on MiniF2F, PutnamBench, the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO 2025), and the 2026 USA Mathematical Olympiad (USAMO 2026). Under the same backbone model, trajectorysampling budget, and test-time compute, our method achieves proof success rates of 100.0%, 90.6%, 4/6, and 4/6, respectively, with GPT-5.5, outperforming the baseline methods. Further analysis shows that concept-guided mutation outperforms random-text-guided mutation by 6.9 and 8.2 percentage points on MiniF2F and PutnamBench, respectively, while solving one additional problem on both IMO 2025 and USAMO 2026.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 突然変異を使った Lean 証明器のスキル自己進化フレームワーク SkillEvoLean

papers.title: Cross-Lingual Alignment for Decoder-Only Models using MoE Routers
papers.abstract: Cross-lingual contrastive learning has been a core component of multilingual encoder training, but the ability to explicitly align representations is not possible in decoder-only LLMs because of varying multilingual tokenization. However, a growing amount of research suggests that even in LLMs, higher cross-lingual representational alignment leads to improved cross-lingual transfer. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to reimagine cross-lingual contrastive learning given the architectural constraints of modern LLMs. Rather than applying an auxiliary alignment loss on hidden states, we propose using the outputs of the mixture-of-experts (MoE) routers as the target for alignment. Router outputs lend themselves better to pooling over many tokens, enabling more reliable cross-lingual comparisons at the sequence-level. Controlled continual pre-training experiments on four open-source MoEs show that incorporating this routing loss also aligns the underlying hidden representations across languages. Most importantly, this loss improves multilingual performance on our diverse evaluation suite, demonstrating the potential of cross-lingual MoE router alignment.
papers.ja_title: MoE ルーター出力を揃えて多言語転移を改善する
papers.summary: デコーダー専用 LLM はトークン化が言語ごとに異なるため、従来の対照学習のように隠れ状態を直接揃える多言語アライメントが難しかった。本研究は、Mixture-of-Experts (MoE, 複数の専門家ネットワークを切り替える構造) のルーター出力をアライメントの対象とすることを提案し、トークン単位でなく系列単位でプーリングできる利点を活かした。4 つの公開 MoE モデルでの継続事前学習実験で、このルーティング損失が隠れ表現自体の言語間整合も改善し、多言語評価スイートの性能を向上させた。
papers.why: MoE のルーター出力という新しいアライメント対象を使うことで、トークン化の不一致というデコーダー専用モデル特有の制約を回避しつつ多言語アライメントを実現する発想が、モデル構造設計者に役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Decoder-only LLMs can't easily align hidden states across languages via contrastive learning because tokenization differs by language. The authors propose instead aligning mixture-of-experts (MoE) router outputs, which pool more reliably over many tokens for sequence-level cross-lingual comparison. Controlled continual pre-training on four open-source MoEs shows this routing loss also aligns underlying hidden representations and improves multilingual performance on a diverse evaluation suite.
papers.why_en: Offers a new alignment target—MoE router outputs—that sidesteps the tokenization mismatch blocking cross-lingual contrastive learning in decoder-only models, useful for designing multilingual MoE architectures.

papers.title: Learning to Predict Distributions over Weight Updates for Test-Time Adaptation
papers.abstract: Hypernetworks have recently shown success in dynamically adapting the parameters of Large Language Models (LLMs) at runtime based on signals such as task descriptions or additional demostrations. Here we ask: how much adaptation signal can be obtained using only the input query to an LLM?. To answer this, we study query-conditioned Hypernetworks for LoRA estimation. Further, we introduce distributional Hypernetworks, able to produce not only point estimates of parameter adaptors, but also a distribution over possible LoRAs. For this we propose a simple end-to-end loss using a differentiable Monte Carlo approximation and explore multiple distribution parametrizations including regression and convex combination variants. Results show that even using the mean of the learned distribution can outperform deterministic hypernetworks. Crucially, the learned distribution enables a different form of test-time scaling: instead of spending additional compute only by sampling more token sequences from a fixed model, we sample weight updates, yielding multiple adapted models for the same query. Performance improves as more weight samples are considered and remains stronger than corresponding token-sampling adaptation baselines. Finally, we find that generated updates can transfer across queries, suggesting that the hypernetwork learns reusable structure in how the model should adapt. Together, these results show that query-conditioned distributions over weight updates can support both adaptation and test-time scaling.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 重み更新の分布を予測するハイパーネットワークでテスト時適応を拡張する
