papers.summary: ハイパーネットワーク (入力から別のネットワークの重みを生成する仕組み) は、タスク説明や例示から LLM の LoRA パラメータを動的に生成できるが、本研究は入力クエリだけからどれだけ適応信号が得られるかを調べた。点推定だけでなく LoRA の分布を出力する「分布型ハイパーネットワーク」を、微分可能なモンテカルロ近似による損失で学習する方法を提案した。学習した分布の平均を使うだけでも決定論的なハイパーネットワークを上回り、テスト時に複数の重みサンプルを使うほど性能が向上し、トークンサンプリングによる適応よりも強い結果を示した。
papers.why: トークン生成を増やす従来のテスト時スケーリングに代えて「重み更新のサンプリング」という新しい軸を示し、LLM の推論時適応・計算配分の設計に新しい選択肢を与える。
papers.summary_en: Hypernetworks can dynamically adapt LLM parameters at runtime, but this paper asks how much adaptation signal comes from the input query alone, studying query-conditioned hypernetworks for LoRA estimation. The authors introduce distributional hypernetworks that output a distribution over possible LoRAs via a differentiable Monte Carlo loss; even the distribution's mean outperforms deterministic hypernetworks, and sampling multiple weight updates at test time—rather than more token sequences—yields further gains over token-sampling baselines, with generated updates even transferring across queries.
papers.why_en: Introduces a new axis for test-time compute scaling—sampling weight updates instead of token sequences—giving infrastructure designers another lever for inference-time adaptation and compute allocation.

papers.title: MoE-CORE: Coordinated Expert Offloading and Residency for Memory-Constrained MoE Inference
papers.abstract: Sparse expert activation reduces MoE models' computation, yet expert weights can exceed limited device memory. Offloading makes inference feasible on a compact AI appliance but exposes host-to-device transfers to the inference path. We present MoE-CORE, a system that coordinates expert offloading and residency for memory-constrained MoE inference. It stages complete expert layers in alternating buffers during prefill. During decode, it combines nonuniform layer-wise cache capacity, domain-informed initialization, routing-history-aware replacement, and cross-layer prefetching. The main configuration executes router-selected experts exactly; an optional score-based substitution path handles eligible low-score misses. The main comparison uses 1K- and 128-token output caps for MoE-CORE and vLLM Prefetch, respectively. Across five workloads per model, MoE-CORE records a mean time per output token (TPOT) of 38.0-44.8 ms versus 1268.9-1269.1 ms for the evaluated vLLM Prefetch configuration on DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A8; the corresponding values on GLM-5.2-W4A8C8 are 206.6-220.5 and 5941.5-5941.8 ms. Under an 84-GB NPU-memory cap, the best measured DeepSeek GSM8K configuration achieves a TPOT of 21.5 ms with approximate expert substitution and multi-token prediction (MTP) at depth 2. These results support coordinated expert residency and transfer scheduling under a device-memory constraint. The code is here.
papers.ja_title: メモリ制約下の MoE 推論を高速化するエキスパートオフロード協調システム MoE-CORE
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) モデルは計算量を抑えられるが、専門家 (エキスパート) の重みがデバイスメモリに収まらず、オフロード (ホストとデバイス間の重み転送) が推論経路の速度を落としてしまう。MoE-CORE は prefill 時にエキスパート層を交互バッファに事前配置し、decode 時には層ごとの不均一なキャッシュ容量・領域情報に基づく初期化・ルーティング履歴を使った入れ替え・層をまたぐ先読みを組み合わせる。DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A8 では平均トークン出力時間 (TPOT) が vLLM Prefetch の 1268.9〜1269.1 ms から 38.0〜44.8 ms に短縮され、GLM-5.2-W4A8C8 でも 5941.5〜5941.8 ms から 206.6〜220.5 ms に改善した。
papers.why: メモリに乗らない MoE モデルのエキスパート転送をどう先読み・キャッシュして遅延を減らすか、という推論サービングの実装レベルの具体策を示す。
papers.summary_en: Sparse MoE models cut compute but their expert weights often exceed device memory, so offloading exposes host-to-device transfers on the inference critical path. MoE-CORE stages complete expert layers in alternating buffers during prefill and, during decode, combines nonuniform layer-wise cache capacity, domain-informed initialization, routing-history-aware replacement, and cross-layer prefetching. On DeepSeek-V4-Flash-W4A8, mean TPOT drops from 1268.9-1269.1 ms (vLLM Prefetch) to 38.0-44.8 ms, and on GLM-5.2-W4A8C8 from 5941.5-5941.8 ms to 206.6-220.5 ms; under an 84-GB NPU memory cap, the best DeepSeek GSM8K configuration reaches 21.5 ms TPOT with approximate expert substitution and depth-2 multi-token prediction.
papers.why_en: Provides concrete implementation-level techniques—prefetching, caching, and substitution policies—for reducing latency from expert weight transfers in memory-constrained MoE inference.

papers.title: Controllable Multi-label Video Safety Detection via Adaptive Tversky Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of video-based social media has increased users' exposure to harmful content, creating a need for reliable automated video safety detection. Although recent Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show strong video understanding capabilities, existing harmful video detection systems face two key limitations: they typically reduce safety detection to binary classification, overlooking the inherently multi-label nature of unsafe videos, and they rely on static training objectives that do not support controllable precision-recall trade-offs, though the desired operating point may vary across moderation pipelines and unsafe categories. To address these gaps, we propose Adaptive Tversky Policy Optimization (ATPO), a reinforcement learning framework for Multi-label Video Safety Detection (Multi-VSD). ATPO introduces the Adaptive Tversky Reward (ATR), which dynamically adjusts false-positive and false-negative penalties during training to enable controllable precision-recall trade-offs. Experiments on SafeWatch-Bench and XD-Violence show that ATPO substantially improves multi-label performance, increasing the Jaccard Index from 40.66 to 75.44 on SafeWatch-Bench-Real. Moreover, ATR enables reliable steering of the precision-recall operating point, supporting deployment scenarios with heterogeneous policy requirements. Code and checkpoints are provided at https://bruceyg.github.io/ATPO-project-page/ .
papers.ja_title: 多様な運用基準に対応できる動画有害コンテンツ検知の強化学習手法 ATPO

papers.title: From Gradients to Capabilities: Understanding Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) aims to combine the strengths of RL-trained teachers in a single student, but how teacher signals affect parameter changes remains underexplored. We study Qwen3-1.7B with four domain teachers trained with RL from the same initialization as the student, comparing gradients, optimizer updates, and task learning curves, with additional SmolLM3-3B diagnostics. We find that several factors influence teacher signals. First, loss averaging implicitly weights responses: token averaging favors longer responses, and equalizing domain contributions retains this weighting within domains. Second, Adam's first moment reduces differences in parameter updates: the cosine similarity is 0.83 between teachers and 0.96 between averaging rules, despite differences in raw gradients. Third, BF16 rounding hides small changes: about 97\% of FP32 master weights differ from initialization, but only 7--11\% of BF16 weights do. Finally, the top-64 intersection KL gradient closely matches Qwen's full-vocabulary gradient, but the effect on task performance depends on averaging: mathematics accuracy is 2.6 points higher than with sampled-token policy-gradient (PG) under response averaging and 2.1 points lower under global token averaging.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 複数教師オンポリシー蒸留:勾配から能力まで何が起きているか
papers.summary: マルチティーチャー・オンポリシー蒸留 (複数の専門教師モデルから 1 つの生徒モデルに知識を移す手法) では、教師の信号がどのようにパラメータ変化に反映されるかが分かっていなかった。本研究は Qwen3-1.7B を生徒に、同じ初期化から RL で学習した 4 つの専門教師を使い、勾配・オプティマイザの更新量・学習曲線を比較した。損失の平均化方法が暗黙的に長い応答を重視すること、Adam の一次モーメントが教師間の更新方向の違い (コサイン類似度 0.83) を平均化規則間の類似度 0.96 まで縮めること、BF16 (16 ビット浮動小数点) への丸めにより FP32 (32 ビット) では 97% のパラメータが初期値と異なる一方 BF16 では 7〜11% しか変化が見えないことが分かった。さらに語彙の一部だけを見る KL 勾度の近似では、応答単位の平均化で数学の正解率が通常のポリシー勾度より 2.6 ポイント高くなるが、トークン単位の平均化では 2.1 ポイント低くなるなど、平均化の選び方が結果を左右した。
papers.why: マルチティーチャー蒸留のパラメータ更新を精密に解剖し、損失平均化・オプティマイザ・数値精度のどれが生徒の能力獲得を左右するかを示した点が、RL 後学習パイプラインを作る人に実務的な指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) combines RL-trained teacher signals into a single student, but how these signals translate into parameter changes was unclear. The authors study Qwen3-1.7B distilled from four domain teachers (plus SmolLM3-3B diagnostics), finding that loss averaging implicitly weights longer responses, Adam's first moment shrinks raw gradient differences between teachers (cosine similarity 0.83) down to differences between averaging rules (0.96), and BF16 rounding hides most updates: ~97% of FP32 master weights differ from initialization versus only 7-11% of BF16 weights. A top-64 vocabulary KL-gradient approximation closely matches the full-vocabulary gradient, but its effect on task performance flips sign depending on averaging: math accuracy is 2.6 points higher than sampled-token PG under response averaging, but 2.1 points lower under global token averaging.
papers.why_en: By dissecting exactly how loss averaging, optimizer moments, and numeric precision shape parameter updates in multi-teacher distillation, this gives practitioners building RL post-training pipelines concrete guidance on which design choices actually matter.

review.note: 損失の平均化方法や BF16 丸めが見かけ上の更新量を大きく変えることを示しており、学習ログやパラメータ差分を見るときは精度形式と平均化規則を揃えて比較する、という測定上の注意点になる。
review.note_en: Shows how loss-averaging choices and BF16 rounding can drastically change the apparent magnitude of parameter updates, a reminder to control for numeric precision and averaging rules when comparing training logs or weight diffs.

papers.title: SoftServe: A Scalable Quasi-Newton Method for Deep Learning
papers.abstract: Quasi-Newton (QN) methods have long been among the most effective methods for large-scale unconstrained convex optimization. Two obstacles have limited their use in deep learning: non-convexity and enormous parameter sizes. We introduce SoftServe, a family of QN methods designed to overcome these obstacles without line searches or ad hoc curvature corrections. SoftServe derives positivedefinite curvature estimates from the variational objective of Berglund et al. (2025), even in the presence of negative curvature. We develop diagonal and Kroneckerfactored variants that preserve positive definiteness by construction and scale to massive neural networks. Finally, SoftServe relies on the stable coupled Newton-Schulz iteration for the required matrix operations, replacing costly matrix decompositions with GPU-friendly matrix multiplications. SoftServe excels on problems that are severely ill-conditioned, including tasks such as recurrent networks, deep autoencoders, physics-informed neural networks, and a 136M-parameter physics-informed diffusion model, often achieving lower losses than established baselines including Adam, Muon, and SOAP.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: SoftServe: 深層学習のための拡張性ある準ニュートン法
papers.summary: 準ニュートン法 (勾配の 2 次情報を使う最適化手法) はこれまで非凸性と巨大なパラメータ数のため深層学習にほとんど使われてこなかった。本研究は Berglund らの変分目的関数から正定値な曲率推定を導き、ラインサーチや場当たり的な補正なしに動く SoftServe を提案し、対角版とクロネッカー分解版により巨大なネットワークにも拡張できるようにした。行列演算には分解でなく GPU に向いた行列積ベースの Newton-Schulz 反復を使い、再帰ネットワーク・深層オートエンコーダ・物理情報ニューラルネットや 1.36 億パラメータの拡散モデルなど条件の悪い問題で、Adam・Muon・SOAP より低い損失をしばしば達成した。
papers.why: Adam 系とは異なる曲率情報を使う最適化手法が巨大モデルでも GPU フレンドリーに動く設計を示しており、学習効率を高める最適化アルゴリズムの選択肢を広げる。
papers.summary_en: Quasi-Newton (QN) methods have long excelled at convex optimization but have been largely unusable for deep learning due to non-convexity and huge parameter counts. SoftServe derives positive-definite curvature estimates from the variational objective of Berglund et al. (2025) without line searches or ad hoc curvature fixes, offering diagonal and Kronecker-factored variants that scale to massive networks, and replaces costly matrix decompositions with GPU-friendly Newton-Schulz matrix multiplications. On severely ill-conditioned problems—recurrent networks, deep autoencoders, physics-informed neural networks, and a 136M-parameter physics-informed diffusion model—SoftServe often achieves lower losses than Adam, Muon, and SOAP baselines.
papers.why_en: It offers a curvature-aware optimizer that stays GPU-friendly and scales to large models, widening the toolbox for training-efficiency work beyond Adam-family optimizers.

papers.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
papers.abstract: What makes great scientists great? Even as AI systems start to make progress on open problems, scientists remain far ahead of them at sensing which prior idea, buried in an ever-growing archive of research, a new problem needs. To study this skill, we draw on researchers who know firsthand which earlier work advanced their completed projects, with papers serving as pointers to the ideas within. Using our automated pipeline that makes author annotation scalable, we build ScholarCatalyst by having 184 lead authors of 207 recent computer science papers label which candidates did or could have advanced their project, each with a detailed rationale. We introduce a retrieval task with author-provided judgments: given an initial research question, retrieve these papers from only the literature available when the project began. Agentic search does no better than embedding retrieval (0.42 vs. 0.48 Recall@20) despite calling that same retriever as a tool. Even an agent built on Claude Fable 5.1, which may have seen the completed papers during training, reaches only 0.51 R@20. These results highlight the need for new training recipes that equip models with expert intuition for searching broad corpora. We envision ScholarCatalyst as a step toward scientific agents that can take a half-formed idea and point to the prior research it needs.

papers.title: Lexicographic Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) usually optimizes answer correctness, yet useful language-model behavior also requires high-quality reasoning and concise responses. Existing multi-reward post-training methods typically scalarize rewards or combine specialists without explicitly protecting a reward priority order. This is problematic when trade-offs are asymmetric: conciseness, for example, should not improve at the cost of correctness. We introduce Lexicographic Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation (LMOPD), a multi-teacher method for integrating reward-specialized policies under explicit priorities. For each student rollout, LMOPD selects the specialist for the first objective whose gate detects a deficiency, then locally projects its centered log-policy correction to remove components that oppose higher-priority specialists. We evaluate 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts transformer models in two- and four-expert settings on three math benchmarks, measuring retained specialist gains. With two experts, LMOPD's point estimates fully retain the accuracy and reasoning-quality gains while acquiring $46.9\%$ of the conciseness gain. With four experts, it retains $\approx90\%$ of both the accuracy gain and reasoning-correctness gain, compared to only $\approx57\%$ by the next best evaluated baseline. Matched four-expertablations show that lexicographic routing outperforms random routing and that projection further strengthens both top-priority capabilities. Across both scales, LMOPD preserves the highest-priority capabilities more effectively than the existing baselines we evaluate, demonstrating the value of explicit priorities for specialist integration.
papers.ja_title: 優先順位付き複数目的のオンポリシー蒸留 (LMOPD)
papers.summary: RLVR (検証可能な報酬を使う強化学習) では正解率だけを最適化しがちだが、推論の質や簡潔さも大事で、これらの間にはトレードオフがある。本研究は LMOPD という手法を提案し、生徒モデルの出力ごとに優先順位の高い目的から順に専門教師を選び、下位目的の修正が上位目的に逆行する成分を局所的に取り除く。300 億パラメータ級 (活性化 30 億) の Mixture-of-Experts モデルで、2 専門家構成では正解率と推論質の向上を完全に保ちながら簡潔さの向上を 46.9% 獲得し、4 専門家構成では正解率と推論正確性の向上を約 90% 保持した (次善のベースラインは約 57% しか保持できなかった)。
papers.why: 複数の報酬特化モデルを「優先順位を明示的に守りながら」1 つの生徒に統合する手法で、RL 後学習で複数目的を組み合わせる際の設計指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) usually optimizes answer correctness alone, but good LLM behavior also needs high-quality reasoning and conciseness, which trade off asymmetrically with correctness. The authors propose Lexicographic Multi-Objective On-Policy Distillation (LMOPD), which for each student rollout selects the specialist teacher for the highest-priority deficient objective and projects away correction components that would hurt higher-priority specialists. On 30B-A3B mixture-of-experts models, LMOPD with two experts fully retains accuracy and reasoning-quality gains while capturing 46.9% of the conciseness gain, and with four experts retains ≈90% of both accuracy and reasoning-correctness gains versus only ≈57% for the best baseline evaluated.
papers.why_en: It gives a way to merge multiple reward-specialized teachers into one student while explicitly enforcing a priority order, offering a concrete design pattern for combining multi-objective RL post-training signals.

papers.title: Coco: An Agentic Copilot for the Hardware--Software Co-Design Lifecycle
papers.abstract: Co-designing ML models and the accelerators that run them is an unusual reasoning task: architects must draw confident, high-stakes conclusions about systems that do not yet exist, and the pace of both model evolution and hardware cadence means the analysis burden grows every quarter. The evidence behind each decision--hundreds of gigabytes of fresh simulation sweeps over novel design points--is by construction absent from any LLM's pretraining corpus, and there is no external literature to retrieve; naive "chat-with-your-data" approaches hallucinate exactly where correctness matters most. We present Coco (Copilot for Codesign), an agentic platform deployed with TPU architects that accelerates the co-design lifecycle of setting up experiments, sweeping simulators, and deriving insights. Coco is built as four layers: (i) a datastore that automatically registers every simulation sweep into a normalized relational schema, so agents ground every number in a SQL query rather than scraping heterogeneous files; (ii) a library of tools with typed APIs that agents compose without human orchestration; (iii) agents that encode recurring analysis workflows--most notably iso-execution analysis, which compares systems at matched execution configurations, including swept-but-dominated points off the Pareto frontier; and (iv) a platform UX whose navigation state doubles as agent context. We report early deployment experience toward a reduction in time-to-simulation and time-to-insight, and argue that co-design is a distinct agentic domain: its data must be retrieved rather than memorized, its workflows are recurring but context-dependent, and expert adoption hinges on UX that balances IDE-style control with interactive exploration.

papers.title: FlashSinkhorn 2: Block-Sparse Entropic Optimal Transport
papers.abstract: Streaming GPU solvers for entropic optimal transport (EOT), such as FlashSinkhorn, avoid storing the dense kernel but still evaluate all $n\times m$ point pairs in every Sinkhorn iteration. We present \textbf{FlashSinkhorn~2} (FS2), a solver for squared-Euclidean cost on low-dimensional point clouds that solves large discrete EOT problems to a prescribed marginal residual on a single GPU by coupling two stages. A coarse stage solves on cell centroids, lifts the potentials to every point and, when a sampled marginal check rejects the lift, continues on the centroids, replacing most point-level updates. A block-sparse fine stage then removes the centroid error that coarse updates cannot. Its Morton-ordered blocks support screening and fused tensor-core execution, and a threshold set by the block masses bounds each omitted tile's contribution to every row and column. On synthetic benchmarks, FS2 reaches the target residual on all 32 problems and GeomLoss multiscale on 10. On one A100, FS2 solves discrete EOT between two $1.34\times10^8$-particle measures from a cosmological $N$-body simulation, at an entropic blur equal to the mean interparticle distance, to an all-particle marginal residual below 0.01 in under 2.5 hours. To our knowledge, it is the largest discrete EOT problem solved to this accuracy within hours. For reproducibility, we release an open-source implementation at https://github.com/ot-triton-lab/flash-sinkhorn
papers.ja_title: FlashSinkhorn 2: ブロック疎なエントロピー最適輸送の高速 GPU 解法
papers.summary: エントロピー正則化付き最適輸送 (OT) を GPU 上で解く既存手法 FlashSinkhorn は、密な行列を保存しない代わりに毎回全ての点対 (n×m 通り) を計算する必要があり大規模問題で遅かった。本研究の FlashSinkhorn 2 (FS2) は、まず粗いセル中心上で解いてポテンシャルを持ち上げ、サンプリングした周辺分布の誤差検査で不十分と判定された部分だけを Morton 順序のブロック疎な細かい段階で計算し直す 2 段構成にした。これにより 1 枚の A100 上で、宇宙論的 N 体シミュレーションから得た 1.34×10^8 粒子同士の離散 OT 問題を、全粒子の周辺分布誤差 0.01 未満まで 2.5 時間以内で解くことに成功し、著者らの知る限りこの精度でこの規模を解いた最大の例としている。合成ベンチマーク 32 問題全てで目標精度に達した一方、比較対象の GeomLoss マルチスケール法は 10 問題のみ到達した。
papers.why: テンソルコアを使うブロック疎カーネルと階層的な粗密 2 段アルゴリズムの組み合わせにより、大規模最適輸送を低精度・疎性を活かして高速化する実例であり、カーネル設計の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Streaming GPU solvers for entropic optimal transport (EOT) such as FlashSinkhorn avoid storing the dense kernel but still evaluate all n×m point pairs every Sinkhorn iteration, which is costly at scale. FlashSinkhorn 2 (FS2) couples a coarse stage that solves on cell centroids and lifts potentials to points with a block-sparse, Morton-ordered, tensor-core fine stage that only recomputes points flagged by a sampled marginal check. On a single A100, FS2 solves a discrete EOT problem between two 1.34×10^8-particle measures from a cosmological N-body simulation to an all-particle marginal residual below 0.01 in under 2.5 hours—to the authors' knowledge the largest such problem solved to this accuracy within hours—and reaches the target residual on all 32 synthetic benchmarks versus only 10 for GeomLoss multiscale.
papers.why_en: It demonstrates a tensor-core-friendly, block-sparse, coarse-to-fine kernel design that scales entropic optimal transport to huge point clouds, a useful pattern for kernel engineers working on large structured computations.

papers.title: Bandits via Additive Quantized Representations
papers.abstract: Contextual bandits require balancing nonlinear reward modeling with online efficiency. Tree ensembles and neural methods capture nonlinearities but require periodic retraining and large replay buffers. Linear models update efficiently per observation with O(1) memory, but are fundamentally restricted to linear reward structures. We propose Residual Quantization (RQ) as a representation layer to bridge this gap. An offline-trained RQ codebook maps continuous contexts into discrete centroid assignments across multiple levels, set dynamically through a shadow mechanism. This enables a spectrum of additive bandit algorithms that achieve nonlinear expressivity with strictly bounded memory. Across 13 datasets, RQ variants beat their non-RQ counterparts on 11 of 13 datasets, often by wide margins, while matching doubling-retrain XGBoost and neural baselines using up to 1000 times less memory.

papers.title: What Does a Token Cost? A Mixture-of-Agents Measurement of Sufficient Per-Token Compute
papers.abstract: Large language models spend the same amount of computation on every token they generate, regardless of how difficult each token is to produce. Methods such as speculative decoding and model routing are built on the premise that much of this computation is unnecessary, yet the computation an individual token actually requires has not been measured. We measure it through a Mixture-of-Agents (MoA) lens: a panel of fifteen language models of increasing capacity, drawn from three families, in which every agent attempts to reproduce a reference sequence token by token, conditioned on the correct preceding tokens. We define the inference cost of the smallest agent that succeeds as the token's sufficient compute, which upper-bounds what the token requires. On three core benchmarks, a 0.5B agent reproduces 92--95\% of reference tokens. Across Qwen, OLMo, and R1-distilled panels, the most expensive 10\% account for 64--80\% of estimated FLOPs. On all 500 MATH-500 problems, the MoA-derived map helps model routing reduce projected latency from 7.59 to 5.12 seconds while slightly improving accuracy, relative to the best confidence-routing baseline. The MoA-map helps drafting use 32.6\% fewer draft tokens and approximately 20\% lower projected latency than fixed-window drafting at similar accuracy. These comparisons reveal remaining allocation headroom, motivating controllers that exploit sufficient-compute structure.
papers.ja_title: 1 トークンにどれだけの計算が必要か:Mixture-of-Agents で測る
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルは生成する全てのトークンに同じ計算量をかけるが、本当に必要な計算量はトークンごとに違うはずなのにこれまで測られていなかった。本研究は能力の異なる 15 個のモデル (3 系列) を並べた Mixture-of-Agents で、正解の前文脈を与えた上で各モデルがそのトークンを再現できるかを調べ、再現に成功した最小モデルの計算量を「十分な計算量」と定義した。3 つの主要ベンチマークでは 0.5B パラメータのモデルだけで参照トークンの 92〜95% を再現でき、上位 10% の高コストなトークンが推定 FLOPs の 64〜80% を占めることが分かった。この知見を使うと MATH-500 の全 500 問でモデルルーティングの想定レイテンシを最良の信頼度ベースのベースラインの 7.59 秒から 5.12 秒に短縮しつつ正解率もわずかに改善し、投機的デコーディングの下書きトークン数も固定窓方式より 32.6% 削減して想定レイテンシを約 20% 下げられた。
papers.why: トークンごとに必要な計算量を実測で定量化しており、モデルルーティングや投機的デコーディングの設計を最適化する際の裏付けデータになる。
papers.summary_en: LLMs spend the same compute on every generated token regardless of difficulty, but how much compute a given token actually needs had not been measured directly. The authors measure this via a Mixture-of-Agents panel of fifteen models across three families, each trying to reproduce a reference token given the correct preceding context, defining the smallest successful agent's inference cost as the token's "sufficient compute." On three core benchmarks, a 0.5B agent alone reproduces 92-95% of reference tokens, and across Qwen, OLMo, and R1-distilled panels the most expensive 10% of tokens account for 64-80% of estimated FLOPs. Using this map, model routing on all 500 MATH-500 problems reduces projected latency from 7.59 to 5.12 seconds versus the best confidence-routing baseline while slightly improving accuracy, and speculative-decoding drafting uses 32.6% fewer draft tokens with about 20% lower projected latency than fixed-window drafting at similar accuracy.
papers.why_en: It provides a measured, empirical map of per-token compute sufficiency that directly backs the design of model-routing and speculative-decoding controllers in serving systems.

papers.title: World Action Modeling with Progressive Visual Planning
papers.abstract: World action models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic control by jointly predicting future visual dynamics and actions from an initial observation and instruction. However, existing WAMs struggle with long-horizon prediction, as generating dense video rollouts is highly inefficient. Some recent WAMs address this by predicting a single future frame without generating the full video, but this approach neglects how to progress toward the goal. We present ProWAM, a progressive world action model that jointly predicts actions and an ordered sequence of sparse visual sub-goals, providing explicit visual guidance to anchor action generation throughout task execution. This design scales naturally, as sub-goal prediction can be learned from large-scale action-free videos, allowing the video backbone to offload complex visual planning from the action policy. For efficient action generation, ProWAM executes a single video-backbone forward pass to cache sparse sub-goal features, eliminating iterative full-video generation and requiring only lightweight action denoising during replanning. Across extensive evaluations, ProWAM achieves superior out-of-distribution robustness. On simulation benchmarks, it sets new state-of-the-art results on LIBERO-Plus (85.8%) and randomized RoboTwin (75.7%), outperforming the strongest baseline with relative gains of up to +35.9%. On RoboCasa365, ProWAM achieves a 48.1% success rate and 18.2% on the challenging Composite-Unseen split, ranking 4th overall. Crucially, in zero-shot real-world experiments, ProWAM achieves 70.0% success, outperforming the strongest baseline by +15.0 (from 55.0% to 70.0%, a +27.3% relative gain) in novel scenes. These results demonstrate the value of progress-indexed visual foresight for closed-loop control. Our program is in https://sii-ferenas.github.io/ProWAM-page.

papers.title: Activation Sparsity with Weight Approximation for Faster LLM Decoding on Offloaded Weights
papers.abstract: Deploying LLMs on consumer-grade GPUs with insufficient memory to hold their weights can result in prohibitively slow inference, because decoding repeatedly transfers offloaded weights from system RAM or flash storage into GPU at much lower bandwidth than local GPU-memory access. Activation sparsity reduces these transfers by skipping weights associated with zero or near-zero activations. However, as more activation contributions are omitted, model quality eventually degrades rapidly, indicating that weights associated with small-magnitude activations collectively influence model quality sharply. In this work, we improve the trade-off between model quality and decoding performance when exploiting activation sparsity. Our key idea is to replace the binary choice of whether or not to read a weight with three options: fully retain it, approximate it using a compressed weight representation, or omit it entirely. SpAx skips weights associated with activations closest to zero, reads approximate weights for smaller-magnitude activations, and reads original weights for the largest-magnitude activations. Smaller-magnitude activations attenuate the errors introduced by approximate weights, while compressed weight representations require fewer bytes to be transferred. With weights offloaded to CPU memory, SpAx speeds up decoding by 3.86X on average (up to 5.57X) with 16-bit weights and 2.06X (up to 2.74X) with 4-bit weights, at a WikiText-2 perplexity increase of at most 10%. With weights offloaded to flash storage, the speedups are 3.31X on average (up to 4.81X) and 1.54X (up to 2.03X).
papers.ja_title: 重みオフロード環境での活性スパース性に3択の読み方を導入して LLM デコードを高速化
papers.summary: メモリ不足の消費者向け GPU で LLM を動かすと、重みを CPU や flash から都度転送するため推論 (デコード) が非常に遅くなる。既存の活性スパース性 (ほぼゼロの活性に対応する重みを読まない工夫) は省く量を増やすと品質が急に落ちる問題があった。SpAx は重みを「そのまま読む・圧縮して近似する・完全に省く」の 3 択にし、CPU オフロード時に 16 ビット重みで平均 3.86 倍 (最大 5.57 倍)、4 ビット重みで平均 2.06 倍 (最大 2.74 倍) 高速化しつつ、WikiText-2 のパープレキシティ上昇を最大 10% に抑えた。flash オフロードでも平均 3.31 倍、1.54 倍の高速化を確認した。
papers.why: 量子化と活性スパース性を組み合わせた 3 択方式で、重みオフロード環境の帯域制約を緩和する実用的な手法として、推論基盤の高速化に直接応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Deploying LLMs on consumer GPUs with insufficient memory makes decoding slow because offloaded weights must be transferred from RAM or flash at low bandwidth each step. Prior activation-sparsity methods degrade model quality sharply once too many small-magnitude-activation weights are skipped. SpAx replaces the binary skip/read choice with three options—fully retain, approximate with a compressed representation, or omit—speeding up decoding by 3.86X on average (up to 5.57X) with 16-bit weights and 2.06X (up to 2.74X) with 4-bit weights under CPU offloading, at a WikiText-2 perplexity increase of at most 10%, with 3.31X and 1.54X average speedups under flash offloading.
papers.why_en: A practical three-way read policy combining quantization and activation sparsity directly addresses the bandwidth bottleneck of offloaded-weight inference, making it useful for serving infrastructure under memory constraints.

papers.title: What Is Lost in Post-Training? Default Collapse and the Loss of In-Context Steerability Across Diverse Perspectives
papers.abstract: AI models serving a heterogeneous population must act on the principles appropriate to each user and context. While post-training has been shown to narrow the views large language models express, prior work has focused on default behavior rather than the ability to adapt to in-context information. We show that post-training also degrades a model's ability to be steered in-context toward perspectives it was not trained to favor. In controlled experiments, we fine-tune models toward one side of cultural-value disagreements and evaluate checkpoints throughout training. The trained side becomes increasingly dominant in ordinary use, while the ability to recognize and faithfully enact the opposing view declines. These findings point to a tension between prioritizing a single set of values and preserving the technical capacity needed to serve diverse stakeholders. Finally, we propose and analyze an alternative objective that maximizes reward subject to a prescribed distribution over expressed perspectives, and present stance-distribution matching as a practical implementation.

papers.title: Annotation-Driven Migration of CUDA Programs to Tenstorrent Blackhole
papers.abstract: Tenstorrent Blackhole combines distributed local memories, explicit inter-core communication, and Tensix cores decoupling data movement from computation. CUDA offers a substantial HPC software base but leaves physical data placement and scheduling largely implicit. Migrating CUDA HPC kernels to Blackhole requires spatial mapping across cores and per-core coordination of compute and data-movement kernels. We present an MLIR-based compiler deriving data placement, inter-core communication, and tile computation from a statically shaped affine CUDA subset. Declarative annotations express choices not fixed by the source, including compute/DM operation placement and streaming granularity. We evaluate it on Gaussian elimination, five-point stencil, and symmetric rank-k update. Relative to our compiler's default realizations, the best measured configurations achieve a 4.2x speedup for BF16 Gaussian and 2.1-2.2x for FP32 Gaussian and Jacobi. A choice's performance impact can reverse with surrounding policies, precision, and loop schedule, motivating comparison of alternative per-core realizations rather than independent policy selection.
papers.ja_title: 注釈付きコンパイラで CUDA カーネルを Tenstorrent Blackhole に移植
papers.summary: Tenstorrent Blackhole は分散ローカルメモリとコア間の明示的通信を持つため、CUDA の HPC カーネルを移植するにはデータ配置とコアごとの計算・データ移動の調整を自分で決める必要があった。本研究は、形が静的に決まる CUDA の一部分からデータ配置・コア間通信・タイル計算を自動で導く MLIR ベースのコンパイラを作り、ソースだけでは決まらない選択 (計算/データ移動の配置、ストリーミング粒度) を宣言的な注釈で指定できるようにした。ガウス消去法・5 点ステンシル・対称ランク k 更新で評価し、デフォルト実装に対して BF16 ガウス消去で 4.2 倍、FP32 ガウス消去とヤコビ法で 2.1〜2.2 倍の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: CUDA から Tenstorrent のようなタイル型 AI アクセラレータへ HPC カーネルを移植する際の自動データ配置・スケジューリング手法として、カーネル開発者の作業を大きく減らせる。
papers.summary_en: Tenstorrent Blackhole combines distributed local memories with explicit inter-core communication, so migrating CUDA HPC kernels requires spatial mapping across cores and per-core coordination of compute and data movement. The authors build an MLIR-based compiler that derives data placement, inter-core communication, and tile computation from a statically shaped affine CUDA subset, exposing choices not fixed by the source (compute/DM placement, streaming granularity) via declarative annotations. On Gaussian elimination, five-point stencil, and symmetric rank-k update, the best configurations achieve a 4.2x speedup for BF16 Gaussian and 2.1-2.2x for FP32 Gaussian and Jacobi relative to the compiler's default realizations.
papers.why_en: An automated data-placement and scheduling approach for porting CUDA HPC kernels to tile-based AI accelerators like Tenstorrent, reducing manual effort for kernel developers.

papers.title: LEAP: Learning Efficient Action Proposals For LLM Agents
papers.abstract: LLM agents are known to be slow in rollouts. An agent completes a task one step at a time. At each step, it reasons and then chooses an action to execute. The next step and action cannot start until the previous one has finished. Speculative decoding accelerates the rollouts at the reason phase by drafting and verifying the inference tokens. Recent works have also started to apply similar ideas at the action phase. These works use off-the-shelf models, usually large, to draft action proposals for target model to verify. Large drafters match the target more often but take longer to propose, while small off-the-shelf models are fast but rarely make the same decision as the target. We ask a more general question: what determines the end-to-end speedup of action speculation? To answer it, we develop a latency framework for the speculative round. The framework compares what a round gains with what it costs. The gain depends on how well the drafter predicts the target and on how many steps the task can take before it ends. The cost comes from drafting, from waiting for target verification and from executing tools. Guided by the framework, we introduce LEAP (Learning Efficient Action Proposals) which keeps the drafter small and makes it accurate by training it on the target actions sequences. With a small 0.6B model, LEAP agrees with the target on most decisions and makes agents up to 60% faster in end-to-end wall clock time, with no systematic change in task success. Across various datasets, target models and draft models, the framework accounts for most of the measured speedups. We also show the draft model can be online trained with no prior trace collection and match the performance of offline training, making LEAP practical to deploy in the real world.
papers.ja_title: 小型ドラフトモデルを目標と同じ行動で訓練し LLM エージェントの行動選択を投機的に高速化
papers.summary: LLM エージェントはステップごとに推論して行動を選び、前のステップが終わるまで次に進めないため全体として遅い。既存の投機的デコードを行動選択にも使う研究は既製の大きなモデルを下書き役 (ドラフター) にするため、目標モデルとの一致率と速さのトレードオフが悪かった。本研究は投機的ラウンドの利得とコストを定式化する遅延フレームワークを示し、それに基づき 0.6B の小さなドラフターを目標の行動列で学習させる LEAP を提案した。その結果、LEAP は目標モデルの判断にほとんど一致しつつ、エンドツーエンドの実時間を最大 60% 短縮し、タスク成功率は体系的に悪化しなかった。
papers.why: ツール呼び出しを含む LLM エージェントの逐次実行を、学習済みの小型ドラフターと利得・コストの定式化によって高速化する実用手法で、エージェント基盤の推論最適化に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: LLM agents are slow because each step's reasoning and action must finish before the next can start, and prior action-speculation work uses off-the-shelf large drafters with a poor match-rate/speed trade-off. The authors develop a latency framework comparing the gain and cost of a speculative round and introduce LEAP, which keeps the drafter small (0.6B) but trains it on target action sequences, making it agree with the target on most decisions and speeding up agents by up to 60% in end-to-end wall clock time with no systematic change in task success.
papers.why_en: A practical speculative-decoding extension for the action phase of LLM agents, paired with a latency framework that attributes most of the measured speedup, directly usable for optimizing agent-serving pipelines involving tool calls.

papers.title: FDP: The Data Placement Promise of Modern NVMe SSDs
papers.abstract: NVMe SSDs are now widely deployed as the storage tier in data centers. As SSDs have evolved over the past decade, the commu- nity has continued to debate the interfaces they expose and how operating systems and storage systems should exploit them. The NVMe Flexible Data Placement (FDP) proposal is the latest point in this design space. FDP introduces an interface based on Reclaim Units that enables explicit data placement to reduce device write amplification without the software engineering costs of sequential- write constraints and host garbage collection. FDP-enabled SSDs are emerging in commercial products and early data center de- ployments. Their compatibility with conventional block I/O allows existing applications to run unchanged, allowing a frictionless adop- tion in industry. This paper presents an experimental evaluation of FDP SSDs to characterize their data placement guarantees over the raw device interface. We then revisit two widely deployed and distinct open- source storage systems, MySQL and RocksDB, and examine whether lifetime-based data separation and distinct write patterns built into their architectures can be mapped onto FDP SSDs without inva- sive changes. Our evaluation shows end-to-end WAF reductions at higher device utilization, along with QoS and throughput improve- ments under synthetic and real-world workloads. These results demonstrate that FDP provides a practical and deployable cross- layer mechanism for data placement with open-source ecosystem support on Linux. They also highlight why FDP SSDs are gaining traction in industry.

papers.title: Decoupling Memory from Context: Structured Memory for Token-Efficient Test-Time Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in enterprise, scientific, and medical applications, where agents must incorporate domain-specific knowledge and adapt from experience. Context engineering offers a practical alternative to weight updates by improving model behavior through instructions, strategies, and evidence supplied at inference time. However, adapting context online typically requires a costly trial-and-error process, while queries are often processed independently, preventing useful experience from carrying forward. Memory systems address this limitation by retaining information across interactions, but approaches that continually append information to a shared context face increasing token costs, context-window limits, and performance degradation as the context expands. We introduce a unified formulation of context optimization and show that an agent memory system update can be interpreted as an optimization update procedure over the model's context. This perspective attempts to provide a principled framework for studying memory design and its efficiency. We then propose GraphMemory, a lightweight graph-based memory that accumulates, refines, organizes, and connects reusable strategies. For each query, GraphMemory retrieves only the relevant subgraph, enabling online context adaptation without exposing the model to the entire memory. Under bounded retrieval, the amount of retrieved memory remains constant as the number of processed examples grows. Experiments show that GraphMemory achieves competitive downstream performance while using approximately 81-85% fewer memory-construction tokens than our baselines.
papers.ja_title: グラフ型メモリで LLM エージェントのテスト時学習を省トークン化
papers.summary: LLM エージェントに経験を蓄積させる既存手法は、共有コンテキストに情報を追記し続けるためトークンコストが増え、コンテキスト長の上限や性能低下を招いていた。本研究はコンテキスト最適化を統一的に定式化し、メモリ更新をコンテキストに対する最適化手順とみなす枠組みを示し、再利用可能な戦略を蓄積・整理・接続する軽量なグラフ型メモリ GraphMemory を提案した。クエリごとに関連する部分グラフだけを取り出すことで、取得メモリ量は処理例数が増えても一定に保たれ、ベースラインに比べてメモリ構築トークンを約 81〜85% 削減しつつ、下流タスク性能は同程度を達成した。
papers.why: 推論時 (テスト時) に LLM エージェントが経験を貯めて再利用する際のトークンコストを抑える構造化メモリ設計として、エージェント基盤のコンテキスト管理に直接活用できる。
papers.summary_en: Existing memory systems for LLM agents keep appending information to a shared context, causing growing token costs, context-window limits, and performance degradation. The authors formulate context optimization as an optimization-update procedure and propose GraphMemory, a lightweight graph-based memory that accumulates, refines, organizes, and connects reusable strategies, retrieving only the relevant subgraph per query so retrieved memory stays bounded as processed examples grow; this achieves competitive downstream performance while using approximately 81-85% fewer memory-construction tokens than baselines.
papers.why_en: A structured, bounded-retrieval memory design for test-time continual learning in LLM agents that keeps token costs flat as experience accumulates, directly applicable to context-management in agent-serving infrastructure.

papers.title: Conditional Capacity and Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Particle Transformers
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models can increase parameter capacity without proportionally increasing active computation, but it is unclear how this trade-off behaves in particle-physics transformers. We study dense and MoE Particle Transformers on 188-class JetClass-II, varying expert count, routing capacity, top-K, and auxiliary loss. We find that, when token dropping is avoided, top-1 MoE models improve over the dense baseline at nearly unchanged nominal forward compute, while further increasing the number of stored experts produces little additional accuracy gain. Activating multiple experts per token yields additional predictive improvements at higher computational cost. Routing analyses show that expert assignments become more strongly associated with particle identity and kinematics in some configurations, but this structure does not increase monotonically with classification performance. These results highlight the need to distinguish stored parameter capacity, active computation, routing capacity, and routing organization when evaluating sparse expert models for jet classification. Code and experiment configurations are available at https://github.com/kpendiyala/MPT.
papers.ja_title: 粒子物理 Transformer での MoE の容量とルーティングの効果を分解評価
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE、専門家混合) は計算量をあまり増やさずにパラメータ容量を増やせるが、粒子物理学用の Particle Transformer でこのトレードオフがどう働くか分かっていなかった。本研究は 188 クラスの JetClass-II で専門家数・ルーティング容量・top-K・補助損失を変えて dense と MoE の Particle Transformer を比較した。トークンの取りこぼしを避けると top-1 の MoE は計算量をほぼ変えずに dense より性能が上がるが、保存する専門家数を増やしても追加の精度向上はわずかで、複数専門家を使う top-K を増やすと計算コストは増えるがさらに精度が上がった。
papers.why: 保存パラメータ容量・実計算量・ルーティング容量・ルーティング構造を区別して評価する必要性を示し、スパース専門家モデルの設計・評価方法に一般的な示唆を与える。
papers.summary_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) can increase parameter capacity without proportionally increasing active computation, but how this trade-off behaves in particle-physics transformers was unclear. The authors study dense and MoE Particle Transformers on 188-class JetClass-II, varying expert count, routing capacity, top-K, and auxiliary loss, finding that when token dropping is avoided, top-1 MoE improves over dense at nearly unchanged nominal forward compute, further increasing stored experts yields little additional accuracy gain, and activating multiple experts per token yields additional improvements at higher computational cost.
papers.why_en: The results highlight the need to distinguish stored parameter capacity, active computation, routing capacity, and routing organization when evaluating sparse expert models, offering general guidance for MoE design and evaluation.

papers.title: Learning to Revise Reasoning with Segment-wise On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) improves large language model reasoning by training students on their own rollouts with dense token-wise supervision from the teacher. However, token-wise OPD does not explicitly provide a coherent alternative reasoning step showing how the student's step could be revised to improve subsequent reasoning. Furthermore, this paradigm can become less effective when the student produces a degenerate reasoning prefix, as subsequent teacher supervision remains conditioned on that prefix and may reinforce poor reasoning patterns. In this work, we focus on learning reasoning revision with segment-wise OPD to rework intermediate reasoning steps and better support subsequent reasoning. Through controlled reasoning interventions, we find that replacing student segments with teacher redrafts improves subsequent reasoning accuracy. Therefore, we address the problem of turning teacher redrafts into explicit supervision for learning to revise reasoning. We propose Segment-wise On-Policy Distillation (Seg-OPD), which selects student segments based on an uncertainty metric and obtains corresponding teacher redrafts. Seg-OPD trains the student to prefer teacher redrafts over their paired student segments while retaining dense token-wise OPD supervision. Extensive experiments on mathematical reasoning and competitive programming tasks show that Seg-OPD-trained students achieve higher revision success rates than baselines. Seg-OPD consistently outperforms the compared state-of-the-art baselines in reasoning accuracy with an average relative improvement of 5.22% across diverse models and tasks. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/Seg-OPD.
papers.ja_title: 教師の書き直しで推論ステップを直す蒸留手法 Seg-OPD
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデル(LLM)の推論を生徒モデルが自分の出力(ロールアウト)で学ぶ蒸留(オンポリシー蒸留)は、生徒が途中で変な推論を書くとそれに引きずられて教師の指導も効きにくくなるという困りごとがある。Seg-OPD は不確かさの高い推論の区切り(セグメント)を選び、教師にそこだけ書き直させて、生徒がその書き直しを好むように学習させる。数学推論や競技プログラミングで、既存の最先端手法に比べ平均 5.22% の相対的な正解率向上を達成した。
papers.why: 推論の途中経路を直接直す教師ありの蒸留設計は、RL 後学習やモデル蒸留の基盤づくりに使える新しい視点。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student LLM on its own rollouts with teacher supervision, but when the student's reasoning prefix degenerates, subsequent teacher supervision can reinforce poor patterns. Seg-OPD selects uncertain student reasoning segments, obtains teacher redrafts for them, and trains the student to prefer these redrafts while keeping dense token-wise OPD supervision. Across mathematical reasoning and competitive programming tasks, Seg-OPD outperforms state-of-the-art baselines with an average relative improvement of 5.22% in reasoning accuracy.
papers.why_en: Provides a concrete way to supervise and correct intermediate reasoning steps rather than only final tokens, useful for anyone building reasoning-distillation or RL post-training pipelines.

papers.title: WakeKV: Reactive, Reversible KV Residency for Heads That Change Their Minds
papers.abstract: Most KV-cache compression methods classify attention heads once, either offline or during prefill, and keep this classification fixed throughout generation. Across three models (1.5B-8B) and three regimes (needle retrieval, long chain-of-thought, and multi-turn recall), we measure head behavior on four model-regime combinations and find that most heads change their reading behavior at least once during generation. We introduce WakeKV, a reactive residency policy that moves cooling heads to a recoverable CPU reservoir rather than freezing or permanently evicting their state. At matched memory or budget, WakeKV consistently improves miss rate over frozen classification and destructive eviction, evaluated across five model-regime combinations and over three cited baselines (SnapKV, uniform R-KV, and ReasonAlloc) across four eligible combinations. A FlexiCache/vLLM implementation on Mistral-7B confirms the benefit on real hardware, improving throughput while retaining LongBench quality.
papers.ja_title: 考えを変える注意ヘッドに対応する KV キャッシュの出し入れ WakeKV
papers.summary: KV キャッシュ(推論中に使う過去の情報の保存領域)を減らす既存手法は、各注意ヘッド(入力のどこを見るか決める部品)の役割を生成の最初に一度決めて固定してしまう。しかし 1.5B から 8B のモデルを調べると、多くのヘッドが生成中に読み方を少なくとも 1 回変えることが分かった。WakeKV は冷えたヘッドの状態を捨てずに CPU の予備領域に移して戻せるようにする方式で、同じメモリ量でも固定分類や破壊的な追い出しより一貫してキャッシュのミス率を改善し、vLLM 上の実装でも Mistral-7B でスループットを上げつつ LongBench の品質を保てた。
papers.why: ヘッドの役割が動的に変わるという観測と、それに対応する可逆な KV 管理方式は、推論サービングの KV キャッシュ最適化の設計に直結する。
papers.summary_en: Most KV-cache compression methods classify attention heads once and keep this fixed, but across models from 1.5B to 8B, the authors find most heads change their reading behavior at least once during generation. WakeKV is a reactive residency policy that moves 'cooling' heads to a recoverable CPU reservoir instead of freezing or evicting them, consistently improving miss rate over frozen classification and destructive eviction at matched memory across five model-regime combinations, and a vLLM-compatible implementation on Mistral-7B improves throughput while retaining LongBench quality.
papers.why_en: The dynamic-head-behavior observation and the reversible CPU-reservoir mechanism give serving-system builders a new lever for KV-cache management beyond static head classification.

papers.title: Ego2World: Compiling Egocentric Cooking Videos into Executable Worlds for Belief-State Planning
papers.abstract: Egocentric videos capture how people carry out everyday activities, yet testing an agent requires evaluating the consequences of actions it chooses itself. We introduce Ego2World, a benchmark that turns annotated cooking activities into executable planning environments under partial observation. Its compiler links source steps and objects to symbolic action rules, persistent world states, and explicit task conditions, so researchers can execute an agent's proposed actions and check their outcomes. World state and agent belief are maintained separately, enabling controlled studies of planning and information reuse across continuing tasks. Evaluating six planners on 105 tasks shows that accepted operations often leave task goals unmet. Execution traces and condition checks distinguish interrupted runs, partial attainment, and completed execution without goal attainment. In a separate paired Qwen-Plus study, persistent belief improves action validity by 4.15 percentage points and reduces visual-query attempts by 90.27%, with higher token use and no detected completion gain. Ego2World provides a reusable testbed for tracing how planning and memory choices affect execution, observation demand, and task attainment, connecting recorded human activity to the development and evaluation of interactive agents.

papers.title: ServeTwin: A Benchmark-Validated Simulator for Distributed LLM Architecture Exploration
papers.abstract: Evaluating distributed LLM serving designs on physical clusters is costly. Yet existing simulators provide only subsets of the capabilities needed for realistic design exploration: stateful closed-loop execution, timing prediction without profiling target hardware, and direct execution of unmodified serving benchmarks. We present ServeTwin, a closed-loop simulator that couples specification-driven analytical timing with a stateful serving loop. This coupling captures feedback among request completion, scheduling, queue state, and KV-cache evolution, including prefill-decode disaggregation and multi-turn agent workloads. ServeTwin avoids target-hardware operator profiling through iSTAGE, an analytical trace generator that derives per-iteration traces from model and engine specifications while representing ragged batches and discrete engine mechanisms such as CUDA-graph batch padding. It further decomposes execution time into component-owned throughput, scheduler, and runtime costs. This ownership lets unaffected parameters transfer across platforms and confines recalibration to changed hardware or software components. ServeTwin implements a vLLM-compatible interface and runs unmodified serving benchmarks. Against real deployments, it reproduces InferenceX's steady-state throughput-interactivity frontier with a 3.6% mean error and predicts LMBenchmark's multi-turn performance with a 9.9% error while tracking KV-cache evolution. Pre-silicon sweeps reveal that the preferred HBM bandwidth-capacity tradeoff reverses across workload states and that increasing concurrency shifts the bottleneck from memory bandwidth to scheduler and runtime overheads. Together, these capabilities enable practical exploration of distributed LLM serving systems before target hardware is available.
papers.ja_title: 本物のクラスタなしで LLM サービング設計を試せるシミュレータ ServeTwin
papers.summary: 分散 LLM サービング(複数の GPU にまたがる推論提供)の設計を実機クラスタで試すのはコストが高いという困りごとがある。ServeTwin は、対象ハードウェアを事前に計測(プロファイル)せずに解析的にタイミングを予測する iSTAGE と、リクエスト完了やスケジューリング、KV キャッシュの状態変化を追う状態付きのループを組み合わせたシミュレータで、vLLM 互換のインターフェースで改造なしのベンチマークをそのまま動かせる。実機と比べ、InferenceX のスループット対応答性能の限界線を平均誤差 3.6% で再現し、LMBenchmark の複数ターン性能を誤差 9.9% で予測できた。
papers.why: 量産前のハードウェアでも分散推論サービングの設計(HBM 帯域幅と容量のトレードオフなど)を事前検討できる道具立てを示しており、サービング基盤設計のレビューや意思決定に使える。
papers.summary_en: Evaluating distributed LLM serving designs on physical clusters is costly, and existing simulators lack realistic, stateful, hardware-profiling-free capabilities. ServeTwin couples an analytical trace generator (iSTAGE), which derives per-iteration timing from model and engine specifications without profiling target hardware, with a stateful closed-loop serving simulator, and runs unmodified serving benchmarks through a vLLM-compatible interface. Against real deployments, it reproduces InferenceX's throughput-interactivity frontier with 3.6% mean error and predicts LMBenchmark's multi-turn performance with 9.9% error.
papers.why_en: Lets teams explore distributed LLM serving trade-offs (e.g., HBM bandwidth vs. capacity) before target hardware exists, offering a validated tool for pre-silicon serving-architecture decisions.

papers.title: Inner Momentum for Differentially Private Muon
papers.abstract: Differentially private training clips each per-example gradient before adding noise. This clipping is radial for each example, yet unequal clipping factors can distort the relative singular-vector geometry of their average. Muon is particularly exposed to this effect, since its update is an approximate polar factor UV^T that depends only on the singular vectors that clipping can shift. To curb this degradation, we propose averaging each sampled example's Muon gradient over the current model and a short history of recent models before clipping. The clipped batch matrix then separates into a common rescaling and a covariance residual R between sampled gradients and clipping values, with ||R||_F <= sigma_lambda sigma_G, bounding the clipping-induced distortion directly. We further show that a finite Newton-Schulz iteration preserves the polar factor of its input under these spectral conditions, confirming that our correction survives orthogonalization. In private GPT-2 fine-tuning on E2E and DART at epsilon in {1, 2, 4, 8}, DP-Muon-IM improves BLEU and ROUGE-L over DP-Muon in every seed-matched comparison, and non-private diagnostics show 2-4% lower pre-noise polar error.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 差分プライバシー付き Muon 最適化を内部モーメンタムで改善
papers.summary: 差分プライバシー学習(個人情報を漏らさないよう各サンプルの勾配を切り詰めてノイズを混ぜる手法)では、サンプルごとに違う切り詰め具合が、Muon という最適化手法が使う特異ベクトル(行列の向きを表す成分)の形を歪めてしまう困りごとがある。提案手法 DP-Muon-IM は、切り詰める前に現在と直近のモデルの Muon 勾配を平均することで歪みを抑え、理論的にも歪みの大きさに上限を与えた。GPT-2 を使った E2E と DART のプライベート微調整で、プライバシー予算 ε が 1, 2, 4, 8 のすべての設定で DP-Muon より BLEU と ROUGE-L が改善し、ノイズを加える前の特異ベクトルのずれ(極因子誤差)も 2〜4% 小さくなった。
papers.why: 差分プライバシー学習で Muon のような構造を持つ最適化手法を安全に使うための補正手法で、プライバシー配慮が必要な学習効率化の基盤として使える。
papers.summary_en: In differentially private training, clipping each per-example gradient before adding noise can distort the singular-vector geometry that Muon's update depends on. DP-Muon-IM averages each example's Muon gradient over the current and recent models before clipping, bounding the clipping-induced distortion, and in private GPT-2 fine-tuning on E2E and DART at epsilon in {1,2,4,8}, it improves BLEU and ROUGE-L over DP-Muon in every seed-matched comparison, with 2-4% lower pre-noise polar error.
papers.why_en: Offers a principled correction for using structure-aware optimizers like Muon safely under differential privacy, relevant to anyone building efficient, privacy-preserving training pipelines.

papers.title: OPD Before RL: Warm-Starting Rubric-Based RL with On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Many useful language-model tasks cannot be evaluated by exact outcome verification. Rubric-based reinforcement learning (RL) addresses this issue by scoring open-ended responses against explicit criteria. However, because the reward is assigned after the complete response, the training signal does not directly identify which individual decisions contributed to the final score. We propose a two-stage training framework that uses rubrics first as privileged teacher context for dense token-level supervision, then as rewards for further RL. In the first stage, rubric-privileged on-policy distillation (RP-OPD), a student without access to the rubric matches a rubric-aware teacher's next-token distributions at student-generated prefixes. In the second stage, RL directly optimizes the rubric reward and improves beyond the observed distillation plateau. We evaluate the framework on health and science tasks using open-weight models. Across HealthBench, ResearchQA, and RubricHub Science, we compare post-training methods and vary the amount of SFT or RP-OPD training before RL, finding that our two-stage framework achieves the highest scores among the methods evaluated. RP-OPD + RL shows limited signs of reward hacking on RubricHub Science, whereas the SFT + RL baseline increasingly receives high rewards for claims of rubric compliance without providing the required content. These findings support using rubrics to guide on-policy distillation before applying rubric-based RL.
papers.ja_title: 採点基準(ルーブリック)を使った強化学習の前に蒸留で下地を作る
papers.summary: 健康相談や科学の質問のように正解が一つに決まらない課題では、採点基準(ルーブリック)で採点する強化学習(RL)が使われるが、最終的な点数しか分からず、どの発言が良かったか分からないという困りごとがある。提案手法は、まず採点基準を知る教師モデルの出力を使ってトークン単位で生徒を蒸留し(RP-OPD)、その後に採点基準に基づく RL を続ける二段構成で、HealthBench・ResearchQA・RubricHub Science で比較した手法の中で最も高い点数を達成した。さらに、SFT から RL に進めた比較手法は採点基準を満たしたと主張するだけで内容を伴わない「報酬ハッキング」の兆候が増えるのに対し、RP-OPD + RL ではその兆候が少なかった。
papers.why: ルーブリック型 RL の前段に密な蒸留を挟むという設計は、報酬ハッキングを抑えつつ RL 後学習の効果を伸ばす具体策として基盤づくりに役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Rubric-based RL scores open-ended responses against criteria but only assigns reward after the full response, leaving which decisions contributed unclear. The proposed two-stage framework first uses rubric-privileged on-policy distillation (RP-OPD), where a student matches a rubric-aware teacher's next-token distributions at student-generated prefixes, then applies rubric-based RL; across HealthBench, ResearchQA, and RubricHub Science, this framework achieves the highest scores among evaluated methods, and RP-OPD + RL shows limited signs of reward hacking on RubricHub Science compared to an SFT + RL baseline that increasingly claims rubric compliance without providing required content.
papers.why_en: Shows a concrete recipe—dense distillation before rubric-based RL—that both improves scores and curbs reward hacking, useful for building RL post-training pipelines on non-verifiable tasks.

papers.title: Gated Slot Attention-2: Two-Sided Associative Memory Correction in Linear Attention
papers.abstract: Linear attention models have emerged as efficient alternatives to standard attention, but effectively managing their fixed-size recurrent memory remains challenging. To improve memory, recent work has explored two distinct directions: delta-rule variants for precise correction of values associated with keys, and slot-based architectures such as Gated Slot Attention for modeling key and value memories in two stages. We observe that these directions are complementary--the delta rule provides effective memory correction, while the two-stage structure provides a natural way to operate on both sides of an association. Building on this insight, we introduce a new Gated Oja Rule for key-side correction and extend it with decoupled erase and write control to obtain Gated Oja Rule-2. We then introduce Gated Slot Attention-2 (GSA2), which combines Gated Oja Rule-2 for key-side correction with Gated Delta Rule-2 for value-side correction through shared latent slots. We further derive a hardware-efficient chunkwise algorithm for parallel training. Experiments demonstrate that GSA2 consistently improves over strong linear-attention baselines across benchmarks while retaining linear-time sequence modeling and constant-memory recurrent decoding.
papers.ja_title: 線形注意の記憶を両側から訂正する Gated Slot Attention-2
papers.summary: 線形注意(計算量を抑えた注意機構)は固定サイズの記憶(メモリ)をうまく管理するのが難しいという困りごとがある。本研究はキー側を正確に訂正するデルタルールと、キーと値を2段階で扱うスロット方式を組み合わせられると気づき、新しい Gated Oja Rule によるキー側訂正と Gated Delta Rule-2 による値側訂正を共有スロットでつなぐ Gated Slot Attention-2 (GSA2) を提案した。実験では、線形時間と一定メモリでの逐次生成を保ったまま、既存の強い線形注意の手法を一貫して上回った。
papers.why: キーと値の両方を訂正する記憶設計は、効率的な長文処理モデルの構造を考える上での新しい選択肢になる。
papers.summary_en: Linear attention models offer efficiency but managing their fixed-size recurrent memory well remains hard. The authors combine delta-rule-style key correction with two-stage slot-based key/value memory, introducing a Gated Oja Rule for key-side correction and pairing it with Gated Delta Rule-2 for value-side correction through shared latent slots to form Gated Slot Attention-2 (GSA2), along with a hardware-efficient chunkwise training algorithm. Experiments show GSA2 consistently improves over strong linear-attention baselines while retaining linear-time sequence modeling and constant-memory recurrent decoding.
papers.why_en: Offers a new two-sided memory-correction mechanism for linear attention architectures, relevant to anyone designing efficient long-context model structures.

papers.title: FastOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Lightweight VLA Deployment
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models have scaled rapidly to enhance manipulation performance and generalizability, but this scaling incurs high computational costs that render real-world deployment increasingly challenging. Existing approaches typically mitigate this issue by designing smaller architectures or reducing the iterative denoising steps in flow-based policies. In this work, we propose FastOPD, a foundation-to-lightweight VLA framework that enables the practical deployment of large-scale VLAs through efficient on-policy distillation. Specifically, FastOPD adapts a flow map for single-state teacher supervision and combines it with a self-consistency objective to construct a compact student that learns the teacher dynamics. Furthermore, we theoretically demonstrate that minimizing this objective allows the distilled student to recover a distribution on par with that induced by an ideal few-step teacher model. We evaluate FastOPD across diverse foundation policies in simulation and real-world experiments. On LIBERO, FastOPD retains 84% of the performance of $π_{0.5}$ with only two inference steps, reducing inference latency by 78.1% while outperforming existing few-step distillation baselines in average success rate. With LingBot-VLA as the teacher, FastOPD improves the single-step success rate over the base student by 15.9 percentage points on RoboTwin 2.0. We further demonstrate its applicability to a World Action Model (WAM) and deploy a compact student distilled from MolmoAct2 on a real robot.
papers.ja_title: 視覚言語行動モデルを軽くする蒸留 FastOPD
papers.summary: ロボット操作向けの視覚言語行動モデル(VLA、画像と言葉から動作を出すモデル)は性能を上げるほど計算コストが増え、実機での利用が難しいという困りごとがある。FastOPD は教師モデルの出力をもとにオンポリシー蒸留し、少ない推論ステップで動く軽い生徒モデルを作る手法で、LIBERO では π_{0.5} の性能の 84% を推論ステップ 2 回だけで保ちながら推論の待ち時間を 78.1% 減らし、RoboTwin 2.0 では LingBot-VLA を教師にした場合に 1 ステップでの成功率を元の生徒モデルより 15.9 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: 大規模な VLA 基盤モデルを実機で速く動かすための蒸留レシピで、推論サービングの効率化を考える人に使える。
papers.summary_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) foundation models scale to improve manipulation performance but incur high computational costs that hinder real-world deployment. FastOPD distills a compact student via on-policy distillation with a flow-map-based single-state teacher objective and a self-consistency loss; on LIBERO it retains 84% of π_{0.5}'s performance with only two inference steps, reducing inference latency by 78.1%, and with LingBot-VLA as teacher it improves single-step success rate over the base student by 15.9 percentage points on RoboTwin 2.0.
papers.why_en: Provides a distillation recipe for deploying large VLA foundation models at low latency on real robots, relevant to those optimizing inference serving for embodied foundation models.

papers.title: Harness-Aware Distillation for Small Language Model Agents
papers.abstract: Language model agents are deployed with a harness, the software around the model that manages its context, tools, and feedback. When such an agent is distilled into a smaller one, the harness stays in place, so the student mainly needs the teacher-specific abilities that the harness cannot provide, such as acting correctly on harness information. Standard distillation, however, imitates the teacher's full outputs and treats the harness as part of the input. We propose Harness-Aware Distillation (HAD), which focuses distillation on what the teacher adds beyond the harness. HAD complements on-policy distillation with two components: an action preference that contrasts the same teacher's actions with and without the harness information, scored after the student's own reasoning, and a validity check that drops preference pairs whose preferred action contradicts the harness records. We show that the contrast gives the student information that imitating the teacher alone cannot provide, and HAD needs no task rewards, success labels, or future information. Across multiple long-horizon agent benchmarks and models, HAD outperforms on-policy distillation baselines with the same fixed harness. Our analysis shows that HAD enters fewer unproductive loops and recovers from errors more often than the baselines, and suggests that it adaptively keeps learnable feedback in its weights while reading state information from the harness.
papers.ja_title: ハーネスを考慮した小型 LLM エージェントの蒸留手法 HAD
papers.summary: LLM エージェントは周辺ソフトウェア (ハーネス) 付きで動くため、通常の蒸留は教師の出力をそのまま真似て非効率になる問題がある。この研究は、ハーネス情報がある時とない時で同じ教師の行動を比較し、ハーネスの記録と矛盾する選好ペアを除く手法 (HAD) を提案した。複数の長時間タスクのベンチマークで、同じハーネスを使った通常のオンポリシー蒸留より性能が上回り、無駄なループに陥る回数が減り、誤りからの回復もより多く見られた。
papers.why: タスク報酬や成功ラベルを使わずに教師と生徒の差分だけを学習に使う発想は、分散エージェントシステムの後学習パイプラインを軽くする設計の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: LLM agents run with a harness that manages context, tools, and feedback, but standard distillation imitates the teacher's full outputs including harness-derivable behavior, wasting capacity. Harness-Aware Distillation (HAD) instead contrasts the same teacher's actions with and without harness information, scored after the student's own reasoning, and filters out preference pairs that contradict harness records, needing no task rewards or success labels. Across multiple long-horizon agent benchmarks, HAD outperforms on-policy distillation baselines with the same fixed harness, entering fewer unproductive loops and recovering from errors more often.
papers.why_en: The idea of distilling only the teacher-specific delta beyond what the harness already provides, without task rewards or success labels, offers a lighter post-training recipe for agent systems built on a fixed harness.

papers.title: Dynamic Expert Pruning for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures scale language models efficiently by activating only a few experts per token, but the saving is confined to computation: every expert must stay resident on the accelerator, so memory bounds where these models can be deployed. Expert pruning reduces this footprint, yet existing methods are static --- a single mask, calibrated offline, is applied to the model for every subsequent request. This assumption can fail when the workload is heterogeneous, most prominently in multi-agent systems, where one backbone serves many tasks and roles at once: our analysis shows that different tasks and roles recruit different experts, while static methods assign one fixed subset to all of them. We therefore propose Dynamic Expert Pruning (DEP), which rests on a finding we establish here: an agent's system and task prompts are by themselves sufficient to identify the experts that agent and its task require, since that text already describes what the agent will do. A lightweight predictor, trained once on workflow transcripts, turns those prompts into a specialized per-request mask in a single forward pass, with no per-configuration calibration. Across diverse tasks and roles, model scales, and MoE architectures, DEP achieves better overall accuracy than static pruning and merging baselines, and generalizes to workflows unseen in training without retraining. Its margin over those baselines is largest when few experts are retained, suggesting that the role specialization inherent to multi-agent systems permits sparser serving than static pruning allows.
papers.ja_title: マルチエージェント向け動的エキスパート枝刈り DEP
papers.summary: MoE (専門家混合) モデルは計算は省けても全ての専門家をメモリに置く必要があり、複数のタスクや役割を同時に処理するマルチエージェントシステムではメモリが課題になる。この研究は、エージェントのシステムプロンプトとタスクプロンプトだけから必要な専門家を予測する軽量モデルを一度だけ学習し、リクエストごとに専用の枝刈りマスクを 1 回の順伝播で作る DEP を提案した。多様なタスク・役割・モデル規模・MoE 構造で、固定マスクを使う既存の静的枝刈りやマージ手法より精度が高く、残す専門家が少ないほど差が大きかった。
papers.why: リクエストごとに動的に専門家を選ぶことで、オフラインで固定した枝刈りより疎なサービングが可能になる点は、マルチエージェント基盤の推論メモリ最適化に直結する知見。
papers.summary_en: MoE architectures save compute but every expert must stay resident in memory, which becomes a bottleneck in multi-agent systems where one backbone serves many tasks and roles with different expert needs. The paper proposes Dynamic Expert Pruning (DEP), training a lightweight predictor once on workflow transcripts that turns an agent's system and task prompts into a specialized per-request pruning mask in a single forward pass, with no per-configuration calibration. Across diverse tasks, roles, model scales, and MoE architectures, DEP achieves better overall accuracy than static pruning and merging baselines, with the largest margin when few experts are retained.
papers.why_en: Selecting experts per-request from prompt text alone, rather than via one static offline mask, enables sparser serving than static pruning allows, directly relevant to memory-constrained multi-agent inference infrastructure.

papers.title: SlimKV: Joint Token-Feature KV Cache Compression with Reconstruction-Free Beacon Attention
papers.abstract: Long-context LLM serving is increasingly bottlenecked by KV-cache memory, especially in resource-constrained scenarios. Among existing KV-cache compression strategies, token-wise methods reduce cached states but risk information loss through eviction or condensation, while feature-wise methods reduce per-token KV dimensions but can require full-dimensional reconstruction to apply positional embedding, limiting decoding speedups. We introduce SlimKV, a question-agnostic joint token-feature KV-cache compression method. SlimKV uses low-rank-aware training to compress long contexts into beacon memory states with latent KV representations, together with layer-adaptive rank allocation. We further uncover a positional asymmetry: removing key-side RoPE affects beacon and raw tokens differently, with much smaller degradation for beacon tokens. Exploiting this asymmetry, SlimKV trains beacon KV projections under a K-RoPE-free constraint and enables latent-space attention during decoding, mitigating reconstruction latency. On LongBench, SlimKV outperforms baselines at 16x/32x compression and remains leading at 4x/8x, where it retains over 96% of the uncompressed model's score. Needle-in-a-Haystack confirms robustness across evidence positions, and efficiency evaluation shows up to 7.34x attention speedup and 3.38x end-to-end decoding speedup over the uncompressed model at 128K length.
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュのトークンと特徴を同時圧縮する SlimKV
papers.summary: 長い文脈を扱う LLM のサービングは KV キャッシュ (注意機構の中間データ) のメモリが足かせになるが、既存の圧縮手法はトークンを削ると情報が失われ、特徴次元を削ると位置情報の再計算で速度が落ちる問題がある。この研究は、長い文脈を低ランクの潜在表現 (ビーコン) に圧縮し、鍵側の位置エンコーディング (RoPE) を外しても劣化が少ないという非対称性を利用して、復元なしで潜在空間のまま注意計算できる SlimKV を提案した。LongBench で 16 倍・32 倍圧縮時に既存手法を上回り、4 倍・8 倍圧縮では無圧縮モデルの 96% 以上の性能を保ち、12.8 万トークン長で注意計算が最大 7.34 倍、末端から末端の復号が最大 3.38 倍速くなった。
papers.why: 位置エンコーディングの非対称性を使って再構成を省く設計は、長文脈サービングのメモリと速度のトレードオフを改善する具体的なカーネル・システム設計の手がかりになる。
papers.summary_en: Long-context LLM serving is increasingly bottlenecked by KV-cache memory, where token-wise compression risks information loss and feature-wise compression often needs full-dimensional reconstruction for positional embedding, limiting decoding speedups. SlimKV compresses long contexts into low-rank beacon memory states with layer-adaptive rank allocation, exploiting a discovered positional asymmetry where removing key-side RoPE degrades beacon tokens much less than raw tokens, enabling reconstruction-free latent-space attention during decoding. On LongBench, SlimKV outperforms baselines at 16x/32x compression and retains over 96% of the uncompressed model's score at 4x/8x, with up to 7.34x attention speedup and 3.38x end-to-end decoding speedup at 128K length.
papers.why_en: Exploiting a positional-encoding asymmetry to avoid reconstruction latency is a concrete kernel/system technique for improving the memory-speed tradeoff in long-context serving.

papers.title: Dirac-Interconnected Neural Elements: Discovering Modularity in Physical Systems Without Reduction
papers.abstract: Deep learning has shown remarkable success in the data-driven modeling of dynamical systems. Much of its success is attributed not to the flexibility of neural networks but to inductive biases based on physical prior knowledge, such as energy conservation and symplecticity. However, existing methods do not fully exploit the fact that real-world physical systems are interconnections of components. Some methods require the interconnection to be known a priori, while others assume the system to be reducible to an ordinary differential equation (ODE) and learn only the reduced ODE, discarding the algebraic constraints imposed by the interconnection. Here, we propose Dirac-interconnected neural elements (DINEs), a neural network model that represents a physical system as a differential-algebraic equation (DAE), whose algebraic constraints are given by a Dirac structure in kernel representation. With DINEs, we simultaneously identify from data the interconnection among the components as a Dirac structure and learn the characteristics of the components as neural networks. This allows us to keep the learned subsystems in unreduced form and isolate or compose them to make a new system without retraining. Moreover, DINEs can handle partially observable systems. Experimental results demonstrate these capabilities on physical systems beyond the reach of existing methods.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク

papers.title: Tailoring the Quantization Space for 1-Bit KV Cache Compression
papers.abstract: The key-value (KV) cache becomes a major memory bottleneck in long-context LLM inference, placing substantial pressure on memory capacity and bandwidth. To mitigate this bottleneck, vector quantization (VQ) has emerged as a promising approach for aggressive KV cache compression. However, existing VQ methods degrade substantially in the 1-bit regime. At such extreme compression, each codebook must represent a larger group of channels with a limited set of centroids, making effective use of its capacity increasingly challenging. To address this, we introduce $\textbf{TaSQ}$, which tailors the VQ target space by combining query-guided channel weighting, cross-head normalization, and covariance-aware channel grouping to better reflect the error sensitivity and statistical structure of cached activations. Since these transforms are RoPE-compatible and can be easily merged into projection weights and codebooks, TaSQ preserves the conventional VQ lookup structure and adds negligible serving overhead. Across general, long-chain-of-thought reasoning, and long-context retrieval benchmarks, TaSQ consistently outperforms existing low-bit KV cache VQ baselines while preserving reasoning stability. On a single RTX 6000 Ada GPU, its SGLang implementation supports up to $14\times$ larger batch sizes and achieves $1.87\times$ higher peak throughput compared to the BF16 baseline.
papers.ja_title: 1ビットKVキャッシュ量子化のための量子化空間の最適化手法 TaSQ
papers.summary: 長い文脈を扱う LLM(大規模言語モデル) の推論では、KVキャッシュ(過去の計算結果を保存する領域)がメモリの大きな負担になる。TaSQ は、クエリに応じたチャンネルの重み付け、ヘッド間の正規化、共分散を考慮したチャンネルのグループ化を組み合わせ、1ビットという極端な量子化(値を少ないビットで表すこと)でも精度を保てるようにした。RTX 6000 Ada 1 枚の SGLang 実装で、BF16(16ビット浮動小数点)基準と比べて最大 14 倍大きいバッチサイズ、1.87 倍高いピークスループットを達成した。
papers.why: 1ビットという極端な圧縮域で既存ベクトル量子化の劣化を抑え、既存の量子化パイプラインにほぼそのまま組み込める点が、長文脈サービングのメモリ最適化に直接応用できる。
papers.summary_en: KV cache is a major memory bottleneck for long-context LLM inference, and existing vector quantization (VQ) methods degrade substantially at 1-bit compression. TaSQ tailors the VQ target space via query-guided channel weighting, cross-head normalization, and covariance-aware channel grouping, preserving the conventional VQ lookup structure with negligible serving overhead. Its SGLang implementation on a single RTX 6000 Ada supports up to 14x larger batch sizes and achieves 1.87x higher peak throughput compared to the BF16 baseline.
papers.why_en: It offers a drop-in improvement to existing low-bit VQ pipelines for KV cache, directly useful for memory-constrained long-context serving.

papers.title: HyperThink: Text-to-Parameter Hypernetworks for Efficient Reasoning
