papers.abstract: Long-form thinking traces can substantially improve the multi-step reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs), but they introduce high inference-time overhead, with latency dominated by sequential decoding. We propose HyperThink, a text-to-parameter approach that amortizes this reasoning computation into a single query-conditioned parameter update: a lightweight hypernetwork reads the question and predicts updates to a small subset of the base LLM's parameters, while a vector-quantized decoder constrains them to a finite set of reusable patterns to improve robustness and transfer. Trained end-to-end on outputs from the base model itself, HyperThink eliminates long thinking traces at test time: after one hypernetwork forward pass, the adapted model generates a concise step-by-step solution and final answer without an intermediate trace, using far fewer tokens while retaining strong reasoning performance. Empirically, HyperThink improves the low-latency region of the accuracy-latency trade-off on mathematical and general reasoning tasks, with its strongest gains in the near-non-thinking regime.
papers.ja_title: 長い思考過程をパラメータ更新に圧縮する HyperThink
papers.summary: LLM は長い思考過程(途中の推論ステップ)を出すと多段推論の正解率が上がるが、逐次デコードのせいで推論時間が大きくかかる。HyperThink は、質問文を読んで軽量なハイパーネットワーク(別のネットワークを作るネットワーク)が元の LLM の一部パラメータの更新量を予測し、ベクトル量子化デコーダで有限のパターン集合に制約することで、推論時に長い思考過程を出さずに 1 回のフォワードパスだけで簡潔な解答を生成できるようにした。数学・一般推論タスクで、精度と遅延のトレードオフの低遅延領域を改善し、特に思考なしに近い条件で効果が大きいと報告している。
papers.why: 思考トレースの生成をパラメータ更新に置き換えるという発想は、推論時の逐次デコードコストを削減する新しい方向性として、低遅延サービングの設計に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Long-form thinking traces improve multi-step reasoning in LLMs but introduce high inference latency dominated by sequential decoding. HyperThink uses a lightweight hypernetwork that reads the question and predicts updates to a small subset of the base LLM's parameters, constrained by a vector-quantized decoder to a finite set of reusable patterns, eliminating long thinking traces at test time after a single forward pass. It improves the low-latency region of the accuracy-latency trade-off on math and general reasoning tasks, with its strongest gains reported in the near-non-thinking regime.
papers.why_en: Replacing explicit thinking-trace generation with a single parameter update is a new direction for cutting sequential-decoding latency, relevant to low-latency serving design.

papers.title: HARPO: Hallucination-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Faithful and Creative Language Generation
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are prone to generating hallucinated content, which compromises their reliability in knowledge-intensive tasks. To address this challenge without sacrificing creativity, we propose HARPO, a reinforcement learning framework designed to jointly optimize faithfulness and creativity. HARPO incorporates a Hallucination-Aware Generative Reward Model (HA-GRM), trained via verifiable feedback, to assess both faithfulness and writing quality. A Selective Activation Mechanism (SAM) activates writing rewards only for outputs judged hallucination-free by HA-GRM, while a data curriculum progressively shifts training from creative writing to hallucination-centric tasks. On RAGTruth, our Qwen3-4B-based HA-GRM achieves a response-level F1 score of 78.08%, compared with 66.37% for the supervised fine-tuning baseline. Experiments on Qwen2.5 and Qwen3 models from 1.7B to 8B parameters show improvements in both faithful generation and writing quality. On Qwen3-4B, HARPO reduces the HA-GRM-judged hallucination rate on MultiHopRAG from 3.29% to 1.02%, while increasing the Arena-Hard-v2.0 creative-writing score from 16.95% to 27.54%.
papers.ja_title: 幻覚を抑えつつ創造性も保つ強化学習 HARPO
papers.summary: LLM は事実と異なる内容(幻覚)を生成しやすく、信頼性が課題になる。HARPO は、検証可能なフィードバックで学習した幻覚検知用の報酬モデル(HA-GRM)を使い、幻覚がないと判定された出力だけに創作の報酬を与える選択的活性化機構と、創作タスクから幻覚対策タスクへ徐々に重点を移すカリキュラム学習を組み合わせた。RAGTruth での HA-GRM の F1 スコアは教師あり微調整の 66.37% から 78.08% に向上し、Qwen3-4B では MultiHopRAG での幻覚率を 3.29% から 1.02% に下げつつ、Arena-Hard-v2.0 の創作スコアを 16.95% から 27.54% に高めた。
papers.why: 忠実性と創造性という相反しがちな目標を 1 つの報酬設計とカリキュラムで同時に最適化する手法で、RL 後学習の報酬モデル構築に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: LLMs are prone to generating hallucinated content, compromising reliability. HARPO combines a Hallucination-Aware Generative Reward Model (HA-GRM) trained via verifiable feedback with a Selective Activation Mechanism that activates writing rewards only for hallucination-free outputs, plus a curriculum shifting from creative writing to hallucination-centric tasks. On RAGTruth, their Qwen3-4B-based HA-GRM achieves a response-level F1 of 78.08% versus 66.37% for the SFT baseline, and on Qwen3-4B, HARPO reduces the HA-GRM-judged hallucination rate on MultiHopRAG from 3.29% to 1.02% while raising the Arena-Hard-v2.0 creative-writing score from 16.95% to 27.54%.
papers.why_en: Jointly optimizing faithfulness and creativity via a single reward design and curriculum is a useful reference for reward-model construction in RL post-training.

papers.title: Coda: Exploiting Admission Flexibility for Coding-Agent Serving
papers.abstract: Coding agents powered by large language models (LLMs) repeatedly alternate between model inference and tool calls, creating long-lived sessions with reusable key-value (KV) states and asynchronous request resumptions. Logical readiness, however, does not ensure efficient admission in a shared serving system. Through direct trace analysis and trace-driven replay, we identify two mismatches: reusable KV states reside across storage tiers and incur unequal computational costs for state preparation, while requests with heterogeneous context lengths can decode inefficiently together. Our central insight is that exploiting admission flexibility can improve serving performance while preserving request progress. We present Coda, a coding-agent serving system that realizes this insight through a readiness-informed admission layer incorporating two mechanisms. Tiered-Aging state admission exploits bounded flexibility in admission order to improve admission efficiency and preserve request progress. Compatibility-Aware execution admission exploits flexibility in attention grouping within each model iteration to reduce mixed-context interference and improve shared decoding efficiency. For multi-worker configurations, Coda introduces a separate routing layer that considers KV-state residency, worker load, and request-to-worker context-length compatibility to guide efficient request placement. We evaluate Coda across different models and workloads against state-of-the-art coding-agent serving systems and vLLM. Across the single-worker and multi-worker experiments, Coda improves output-token and SLO-compliant throughput by 20.3% and 70.5% on average, with peak gains of 29.3% and 140.2%.
papers.ja_title: コーディングエージェント向けサービングの受け入れ制御 Coda
papers.summary: コーディングエージェントは LLM 推論とツール呼び出しを繰り返し、再利用可能な KV 状態(過去の計算結果)を持つ長命なセッションを作るが、既存の共有サービングシステムはこれを効率よく受け入れられていない。Coda は、KV 状態の保存階層ごとの準備コストの違いを利用する Tiered-Aging 受け入れと、文脈長が異なるリクエストをまとめる際の相性を考慮する Compatibility-Aware 受け入れという 2 つの仕組みを導入し、複数ワーカー構成では状態の配置や負荷も考慮するルーティング層を加えた。既存のコーディングエージェント向けサービングシステムや vLLM との比較で、出力トークンおよび SLO 準拠スループットを単一・複数ワーカーでそれぞれ平均 20.3%・70.5% 改善し、最大で 29.3%・140.2% の向上を確認した。
papers.why: 長命セッション・再利用 KV・混在する文脈長というコーディングエージェント特有の負荷特性に着目した受け入れ制御とルーティングの設計は、実運用の推論サービング基盤を作る人に直接参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Coding agents alternate between LLM inference and tool calls, creating long-lived sessions with reusable KV states, but logical readiness does not ensure efficient admission in shared serving systems. Coda introduces Tiered-Aging state admission, which exploits bounded flexibility in admission order across storage tiers, and Compatibility-Aware execution admission, which reduces mixed-context interference during attention grouping, plus a routing layer for multi-worker setups that considers KV-state residency, load, and context-length compatibility. Against state-of-the-art coding-agent serving systems and vLLM, Coda improves output-token and SLO-compliant throughput by 20.3% and 70.5% on average in single- and multi-worker experiments, with peak gains of 29.3% and 140.2%.
papers.why_en: The admission-control and routing design tailored to coding agents' long-lived sessions, reusable KV states, and heterogeneous context lengths is directly useful for building production inference serving systems.

papers.title: ULTRADISCOVERY: Abductive Exploration in an Interconnected, Epistemically Open Universe
papers.abstract: Scientific discovery often begins when scattered clues call for a new way of describing the world. Such abductive exploration can require constructing the representation in which an explanation is stated, when the world is epistemically open, and composing evidence scattered across contexts, when it is structurally interconnected. Existing benchmarks rarely separate these two demands or control them independently. We introduce ULTRADISCOVERY, an interactive world of five domains in which an agent revises an initially successful theory and predicts the outcome of an unseen cross-domain intervention. A $2 \times 2$ design leaves the representation open or discloses it, and leaves the evidence distributed or aligns it, with the latent dynamics fixed. With the representation open, agents across eleven models often retract the axiom they were taught, and none introduces the unobserved entity or rewrites the variables that a replacement requires. Disclosure triples intervention requests and adds about one of the eighteen findings the world affords, and alignment adds less. Two vendor-harness systems carry discovery into more domains, and one of them rewrites the variables in Open episodes. No system makes the exact prediction within 200 paid actions. At larger budgets one exact prediction appears with both aids, while every Open episode remains inexact. The results locate the difficulty in the step from accumulating evidence to composing it into a representation that transfers.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク

papers.title: Contextual Flow Matching: Adaptive Step Selection in Flow Models for Efficient Visual Generation
papers.abstract: Flow Matching enables high-quality visual generation via continuous-time dynamics, but inference remains costly due to multiple sequential function evaluations. Existing acceleration methods reduce the number of function evaluations but often introduce additional training overhead, degrade quality, or fail to account for input-dependent variability. We propose COFLOW, an inference-time method that adaptively selects the step counts each generation based on the prompt features. Our context-aware COFLOW is trained online with an unsupervised reward that balances inference efficiency and generation fidelity. Our method is plug-and-play, requiring no retraining of the underlying generative model. It generalizes to image and video generation, achieving over 2.5x speedup while preserving perceptual and semantic quality. We further provide a theoretical analysis establishing an O(1/K) forward-Euler discretization error bound under standard regularity conditions.
papers.ja_title: 入力ごとにステップ数を変えるフローマッチング高速化手法 COFLOW
papers.summary: フローマッチング (連続時間で画像や動画を作る生成モデル) は推論時に何度も計算を繰り返す必要があり、コストが高いことが課題だった。COFLOW はプロンプトの特徴に応じて生成ごとに必要なステップ数を自動で決め、追加学習なしで既存モデルに後付けできる方法を提案し、効率と品質のバランスを取る教師なし報酬でオンライン学習する。画像・動画生成の両方で 2.5 倍以上の高速化を達成しつつ知覚・意味的な品質を保ち、離散化誤差が O(1/K) で抑えられることも理論的に示した。
papers.why: 拡散・フロー系生成モデルの推論サービングを作る人にとって、ベースモデルを変更せずに入力適応的な計算量削減を導入できる実用的な手法として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Flow Matching generation requires many sequential function evaluations at inference, making it costly, and existing speedups either need retraining or ignore input-dependent variability. COFLOW adaptively selects the number of inference steps per generation based on prompt features, trained online with an unsupervised reward balancing efficiency and fidelity, and is plug-and-play without retraining the base model. It achieves over 2.5x speedup on image and video generation while preserving perceptual and semantic quality, with a theoretical O(1/K) forward-Euler discretization error bound.
papers.why_en: Offers a practical, retraining-free way to add input-adaptive step reduction to flow/diffusion serving systems, which is directly useful for those building inference pipelines for generative models.

papers.title: AFORE: Attention-FFN Disaggregation with Overlapped Reconfiguration of Experts
papers.abstract: Efficient serving of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models is challenging due to large expert parameters, input-dependent expert activation, and dynamic workloads. Expert parallelism distributes expert computation across GPUs, while attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) separates attention and feed-forward computation into independent worker pools. However, we observe that a naive AFD implementation could make expert load imbalance more harmful: once FFN computation becomes an independent pipeline stage, overloaded experts directly slow the FFN stage and degrade end-to-end serving performance. To solve this problem, we present AFORE, a timely expert reconfiguration system for AFD-based MoE serving. AFORE exploits two architectural properties of AFD. First, AFD exposes the expert-token distribution of upcoming microbatches before they reach FFN execution, enabling placement decisions based on near-future demand instead of stale historical profiles. Second, AFD creates a pipeline window in which expert migration for a target microbatch can be overlapped with the computation of preceding in-flight microbatches. AFORE formulates expert reconfiguration as a microbatch-aware scheduling problem and uses a migration-aware scheduler to decide when and which experts to migrate. AFORE further implements lightweight demand prefetching and NVLink-based GPU-GPU expert migration to reduce reconfiguration overhead. Evaluation on a 110B-parameter MoE model across four dynamic workloads shows that AFORE improves output throughput by 10.1-17.6% and reduces P95 inter-token latency by 7.1-9.5% compared with the strongest competing baseline. Compared with static placement, AFORE improves throughput by 29.8% on average and reduces P95 inter-token latency by 18.2% on average. Migration profiling further shows that AFD pipeline overlap can fully hide expert-migration latency.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: Attention と FFN を分離した MoE 推論で専家負荷を先読みして再配置する AFORE
papers.summary: MoE (専家混合) モデルの Attention と FFN (順伝播層) を別々のワーカー群に分離するサービング方式 (AFD) では、専家 (expert) の負荷が偏ると FFN 段全体が遅くなる問題が悪化することが分かった。AFORE は FFN 実行前に次のマイクロバッチの専家利用分布が見えるという AFD の特性と、移行処理を直前の計算と重ねられるパイプラインの余地を利用し、専家の再配置をスケジューリング問題として解いて移行のタイミングと対象を決める。110B パラメータの MoE モデルで評価したところ、最良の既存手法に比べ処理量が 10.1〜17.6% 向上し P95 レイテンシが 7.1〜9.5% 短縮し、静的配置に比べると平均で処理量 29.8%、レイテンシ 18.2% の改善を達成した。
papers.why: Attention-FFN 分離構成の MoE サービングを構築する人にとって、負荷の先読みとパイプライン重畳を利用した専家再配置の具体的な設計指針になる。
papers.summary_en: In attention-FFN disaggregated (AFD) MoE serving, naive implementations make expert load imbalance more harmful because overloaded experts directly slow the independent FFN pipeline stage. AFORE exploits two AFD properties — visibility of upcoming microbatches' expert-token distribution before FFN execution, and a pipeline window where migration can overlap with in-flight computation — to formulate expert reconfiguration as a microbatch-aware scheduling problem with lightweight prefetching and NVLink-based migration. On a 110B-parameter MoE model across four dynamic workloads, AFORE improves output throughput by 10.1-17.6% and reduces P95 inter-token latency by 7.1-9.5% over the strongest baseline, and by 29.8% throughput and 18.2% latency on average over static placement, with migration latency fully hidden by pipeline overlap.
papers.why_en: Gives concrete design guidance for anyone building AFD-based MoE serving systems on how to predictively reconfigure experts using near-future demand and overlap migration with pipeline computation.

papers.title: Collective Bias Mitigation via Model Routing and Collaboration
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in public health, finance, and governance, requiring both accuracy and societal value alignment. Despite recent advances, LLMs often perpetuate or amplify bias embedded in their training data, posing challenges to fairness. While self-debiasing encourages an LLM to identify and correct its own biases, relying on a single model's intrinsic knowledge may be insufficient to address deeply ingrained stereotypes. To address this limitation, we introduce Collective Bias Mitigation (CBM), a framework that alleviates bias by learning fine-grained model behavior and fostering knowledge sharing among diverse LLMs. This work is the first to systematically explore the effective selection and organization of distinct LLMs to cultivate fairer LLM responses. Experiments show CBM substantially outperforms standalone baselines (e.g., in the top-7 setting, Committee lowers the age bias score from 0.25 to 0.10). Our Debating and Committee topologies achieve substantial bias reduction, with the latter balancing mitigation effectiveness and inference cost, highlighting the potential of CBM for fairer LLMs.

papers.title: SCAD: Structured Credit Assignment and Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Training long-horizon agents to solve complex tasks requires effective supervision over extended interaction sequences. However, sparse terminal rewards obscure intermediate contributions, while on-policy distillation can lose informative teacher guidance as student-generated histories grow. To address this problem, we introduce SCAD, which organizes interactions into planning and bounded subtask execution, distills execution in local contexts, and refines planning credit through cross-rollout subtask prefix trees, with planning receiving full terminal credit and execution receiving positive terminal credit and teacher guidance. Across all evaluated benchmarks, SCAD improves macro-average accuracy over the strongest training baseline by 4.48 percentage points for text tasks and 4.19 points for multimodal tasks. SCAD effectively combines outcome-based credit assignment with teacher-guided distillation to improve planning and execution in long-horizon agents.
papers.ja_title: 計画と実行を分けて信用割り当てと蒸留を組み合わせる長期タスク向け学習法 SCAD
papers.summary: 長い手順を要するエージェントの学習では、最終結果だけに報酬が付くと途中の判断の良し悪しが分からず、生成履歴が長くなるほど教師モデルからの蒸留 (知識の受け渡し) が効きにくくなる問題があった。SCAD はやり取りを「計画」と「範囲の決まったサブタスク実行」に分け、実行部分は局所的な文脈で蒸留し、計画部分は複数のロールアウトを比較したサブタスク木を使って信用割り当てを精緻化する。すべての評価ベンチマークで、最も強い既存手法と比べてテキストタスクで平均正解率が 4.48 ポイント、マルチモーダルタスクで 4.19 ポイント向上した。
papers.why: 長期タスクを行う LLM エージェントの RL 後学習基盤を作る人にとって、結果ベースの信用割り当てと教師蒸留を組み合わせる具体的な設計を提供する。
papers.summary_en: Training long-horizon agents suffers because sparse terminal rewards obscure intermediate contributions, and on-policy distillation loses informative teacher guidance as student-generated histories grow. SCAD organizes interactions into planning and bounded subtask execution, distills execution in local contexts, and refines planning credit via cross-rollout subtask prefix trees, giving planning full terminal credit and execution positive terminal credit plus teacher guidance. Across all evaluated benchmarks, SCAD improves macro-average accuracy over the strongest training baseline by 4.48 percentage points on text tasks and 4.19 points on multimodal tasks.
papers.why_en: Provides a concrete design for combining outcome-based credit assignment with teacher-guided distillation, useful for anyone building RL post-training infrastructure for long-horizon LLM agents.

papers.title: RailWave: Adaptive Spatial and Temporal Scheduling for Expert-Parallel Communication
papers.abstract: Irregular All-to-All communication is a major bottleneck in expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models. Even with fixed expert routing and placement, uneven utilization of parallel network Rails and incast can limit communication performance. We present RailWave, a phase-adaptive communication layer built on DeepEP that addresses these bottlenecks below the routing layer through spatial and temporal traffic shaping. RailBalance redistributes source traffic across eligible Rails using source-local information, while a reusable, topology-derived permutation schedule limits concurrent senders per receiver without rebuilding demand-dependent schedules for each communication phase. A lightweight calibrated selector chooses an execution path according to each phase's traffic characteristics and offline profiling results. On training-derived communication workloads from the 106B GLM-4.5-Air model, RailWave delivers up to 5.84x speedup on H800 and 4.36x on H20 over Native. Code is available at https://github.com/CyberSecurityErial/RailWave-EP.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: MoE の All-to-All 通信をレール単位で均す RailWave
papers.summary: 専家並列 (expert parallelism) の MoE モデルでは、専家の割り当てや配置を固定しても、並列ネットワークの「レール」の使い方が偏ったり、受信が一点に集中する incast が起きて通信性能を落とすことが課題だった。RailWave は DeepEP 上に構築した通信層で、送信元の情報だけで利用可能なレールに通信を再分配する RailBalance と、通信フェーズごとに作り直さない再利用可能な順列スケジュール、フェーズの特性に応じて実行経路を選ぶ軽量な選択器を組み合わせる。106B パラメータの GLM-4.5-Air モデルの学習由来の通信負荷で評価した結果、H800 で最大 5.84 倍、H20 で最大 4.36 倍、既存手法 (Native) に比べて高速化した。
papers.why: MoE 学習・推論の通信基盤を作る人にとって、ルーティング層の下でレール単位・フェーズ単位に通信を整形するという新しい具体策を示している。
papers.summary_en: Irregular All-to-All communication is a major bottleneck in expert-parallel MoE models, where uneven utilization of parallel network rails and incast can limit performance even with fixed expert routing and placement. RailWave is a phase-adaptive communication layer built on DeepEP that redistributes source traffic across eligible rails using source-local information (RailBalance), uses a reusable topology-derived permutation schedule instead of rebuilding demand-dependent schedules per phase, and picks an execution path with a lightweight calibrated selector based on offline profiling. On training-derived communication workloads from the 106B GLM-4.5-Air model, RailWave delivers up to 5.84x speedup on H800 and 4.36x on H20 over Native.
papers.why_en: Offers a concrete technique below the routing layer for shaping All-to-All traffic spatially (across rails) and temporally (across phases), directly relevant to those building communication infrastructure for MoE training and inference.

papers.title: Jumping the Line: Exploiting Length Predictions in LLM Scheduling
papers.abstract: Efficient request scheduling is increasingly important for reducing completion time in large language model (LLM) serving. Size-based policies such as Shortest Job First prioritize shorter requests, but output lengths are unknown before generation, so practical schedulers rely on predicted lengths. We introduce JIL, an attack on prediction-based LLM schedulers that manipulates the scheduling signal to obtain higher priority and reduce completion time. Using TRAIL as a case study, JIL optimizes an adversarial suffix that causes a lightweight output-length probe to underestimate a request's length. We evaluate JIL on two datasets and four LLMs across varied request profiles and deployment configurations. JIL reduces predicted output lengths by up to 83.4 percent, and adversarial requests complete up to 1.53 times faster on average in end-to-end serving experiments. The reduction in predicted length is substantially larger than the change in actual output length, revealing a mismatch between the scheduler's estimate and the request's realized size. Response utility varies across models and tasks, exposing a trade-off between scheduling advantage and response quality. We also evaluate scheduler-side defenses and find that grouping length predictions into coarse intervals reduces JIL's scheduling advantage and mitigates delays to benign requests.
papers.ja_title: 出力長の予測を欺いて LLM スケジューラの優先度を奪う攻撃 JIL
papers.summary: LLM サービングでは完了時間を短くするため、生成前に出力長を予測して短い要求を優先するスケジューラが使われるが、その予測器自体が攻撃対象になりうることが示された。JIL は、軽量な出力長予測器に実際より短い長さを推定させる敵対的な接尾辞 (サフィックス) を最適化し、TRAIL スケジューラを例に 2 つのデータセットと 4 つの LLM で検証した。予測長を最大 83.4% 減らすことに成功し、攻撃した要求は実運用のサービング実験で平均最大 1.53 倍速く完了し、粗い区間に分けて予測するという対策でこの優位性を弱められることも分かった。
papers.why: 予測長に基づく LLM スケジューラを運用する人にとって、予測器が操作可能であるという脆弱性と、区間化による簡便な防御策の有効性を示す実例になる。
papers.summary_en: LLM serving systems increasingly rely on predicted output lengths (e.g., Shortest Job First) to reduce completion time, but this prediction signal can itself be attacked. JIL optimizes an adversarial suffix that causes a lightweight output-length probe to underestimate a request's length, evaluated on TRAIL as a case study across two datasets and four LLMs. JIL reduces predicted output lengths by up to 83.4 percent, and adversarial requests complete up to 1.53 times faster on average in end-to-end serving experiments, while grouping length predictions into coarse intervals is shown to mitigate JIL's scheduling advantage.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates that prediction-based LLM schedulers are vulnerable to adversarial manipulation and shows that coarse-grained interval defenses can mitigate this, relevant for anyone operating length-prediction-based scheduling in production.

review.note: 予測ベースのスケジューラを評価する際、通常の入力だけでなく敵対的な入力で予測が操作されないかを確かめる検証の観点、および粗い区間化などの防御策の効果まで測定する手法が示されている。
review.note_en: Shows a verification angle for evaluating prediction-based schedulers: testing whether predictions can be adversarially manipulated, not just how accurate they are on normal inputs, and measuring the effectiveness of defenses like coarse interval grouping.

papers.title: OptiSelect: How does the Optimizer Shape Data Curriculum?
papers.abstract: Online data selection has demonstrated substantial efficiency gains for LLM pretraining by training on the most valuable candidates within each batch. Since a candidate's value is realized through its effective model update, principled selection should account for the optimizer step, which reshapes the raw gradient before it updates model parameters. We formalize this optimizer-aware selection paradigm as OptiSelect and present the first systematic study of how the optimizer shapes data selection. Our theory establishes a selection gain principle in which the advantage of online selection is governed by the discriminability of the optimizer-induced utility scores. We prove that sign-based and polar-tangential preconditioners of Lion and Muon would suffer from a discriminability collapse which caps attainable gains from OptiSelect, whereas diagonal-adaptive optimizers such as AdamW and Sophia admit strictly better upper bounds. The proposed principle also yields a quantitative derivation of the optimal candidate oversampling ratio. Pretraining experiments on 124M and 720M models are consistent with our theoretical analysis and show that AdamW's diagonal-adaptive scoring geometry remains the strongest scoring geometry even with Muon as optimizer. We further demonstrate that OptiSelect retains its benefits under data rephrasing, a technique used in modern data processing pipelines. Our findings provide theoretical foundations and practical guidance for co-designing optimizers and data selection in LLM pretraining.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: オプティマイザの種類がデータ選択の効果を左右することを示す OptiSelect
papers.summary: LLM の事前学習ではバッチ内で価値の高いデータを選ぶオンラインデータ選択が効率化に有効だが、選ぶ際の価値判断は勾配を変形する最適化手法 (オプティマイザ) の影響を考慮していなかった。OptiSelect はこの最適化手法を考慮したデータ選択を理論的に整理し、Lion や Muon のような符号・方向ベースの最適化手法ではスコアの識別力が崩れて選択の効果に上限ができる一方、AdamW や Sophia のような対角適応型の手法ではより高い上限を持つことを証明し、最適な過剰サンプリング比も導いた。124M と 720M パラメータのモデルでの事前学習実験でこの理論が確認され、Muon を最適化手法に使っても AdamW 的なスコア計算が最も強いことが分かり、データのリフレーズ処理を加えても効果が保たれることも示された。
papers.why: 事前学習の効率化を担う人にとって、データ選択とオプティマイザの組み合わせを個別に選ぶのではなく一緒に設計すべきだという理論的根拠と具体的な指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: Online data selection improves LLM pretraining efficiency by choosing the most valuable candidates per batch, but principled selection should account for how the optimizer step reshapes the raw gradient, which prior work ignores. OptiSelect formalizes this optimizer-aware selection paradigm, proving that sign-based and polar-tangential preconditioners (Lion, Muon) suffer a discriminability collapse that caps attainable selection gains, while diagonal-adaptive optimizers (AdamW, Sophia) admit strictly better upper bounds, and derives the optimal candidate oversampling ratio. Pretraining experiments on 124M and 720M models are consistent with the theory, showing AdamW's diagonal-adaptive scoring geometry remains strongest even when Muon is the training optimizer, and that OptiSelect's benefits persist under data rephrasing.
papers.why_en: Provides theoretical grounding and practical guidance for co-designing optimizers and online data selection in LLM pretraining, rather than treating them as independent choices, which is directly relevant to training efficiency practitioners.

papers.title: Learning from Repaired Reasoning: Root-Cause-Guided On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) uses reference solutions as privileged hindsight to supervise student-generated reasoning trajectories. However, reference-based guidance may explain a correct solution without addressing why the student's own reasoning fails. This reasoning mismatch between the guidance provided and the correction needed can encourage the student to borrow correct conclusions while leaving its reasoning errors unresolved. Moreover, applying the same hindsight throughout the trajectory risks a distillation trap, where unnecessary constraints on valid reasoning compete with correction of substantive errors. To address these issues, we propose Root-Cause-Guided On-Policy Distillation (RC-OPD), which uses repairs of the student's own reasoning to provide guidance that addresses its specific errors while building on valid progress. For each failed attempt, RC-OPD locates the earliest substantive error, develops a local correction, and uses the corrected intermediate result as an anchor for the valid prefix. An iterative diagnosis--repair--continuation process tests the repairs through student continuation, identifying further errors within a fixed repair budget. For repair chains that reach a correct answer, root--cause--guided distillation uses failure diagnoses and corrective goals to supervise the erroneous segments, while anchor-guided distillation supports the corresponding valid prefixes with reasoning chains leading to the repaired intermediate results. We evaluate RC-OPD across multiple datasets and model scales. Extensive experiments and analyses show that it mitigates reasoning mismatch and the distillation trap, yielding substantial performance gains.
papers.ja_title: 根本原因に基づくオンポリシー蒸留で学生モデルの推論誤りを修復
papers.summary: 従来のオンポリシー蒸留は正解の手本をそのまま学生モデルに与えるため、学生が自分の誤りを直さずに正しい結論だけを借用してしまう「推論の食い違い」や、正しい部分にも余計な制約をかけてしまう「蒸留トラップ」が起きていた。本研究の RC-OPD は、学生の失敗した推論の中で最初に起きた重大な誤りを見つけてそこだけをローカルに修正し、その修正点を足場として学生に続きを生成させる診断・修復・継続のループを繰り返す。複数のデータセットとモデル規模で評価し、性能が大きく向上したと報告されている。
papers.why: 学生モデル固有の誤りだけに狙いを絞って修正信号を与える点が新しく、LLM の後学習・自己蒸留の効率化に使える知見を提供する。
papers.summary_en: Standard on-policy self-distillation gives reference solutions as hindsight, letting students borrow correct conclusions without fixing their own reasoning errors (reasoning mismatch), and uniform hindsight over a trajectory can over-constrain already-valid steps (distillation trap). RC-OPD instead locates the earliest substantive error in a failed student trajectory, repairs it locally, and uses the corrected intermediate result as an anchor through an iterative diagnose-repair-continue loop. Extensive experiments across datasets and model scales show substantial performance gains from mitigating both issues.
papers.why_en: The approach targets correction signals precisely at the student's own failure points rather than the whole trajectory, offering a useful idea for improving self-distillation and RL-style post-training efficiency.

papers.title: Divergence controls entropy in distillation
papers.abstract: Distillation has become a core primitive of large language model training, but its properties are not yet well understood. We take an entropic perspective, studying how the entropy of the student depends on the data and the divergence that define the distillation objective. We prove that forward KL inflates the entropy of the student above that of the teacher. Since cross-entropy training is a special case, this yields an identity that we verify quantitatively in pretraining and supervised finetuning. Other divergences come with no such guarantee: reverse KL deflates entropy until the gap between student and teacher gets too large, and interpolating between the two changes entropy smoothly early in training but abruptly at convergence. The lower entropy of on-policy distillation comes from token-level reverse KL, not from on-policy sampling. The divergence therefore acts as an implicit entropy regularizer, whose role is clearest in self-distillation: as conditioning on privileged information deflates entropy, the divergence hyperparameters that work best are those that compensate for it.
papers.ja_title: 蒸留で使う発散(ダイバージェンス)の種類が学生モデルのエントロピーを左右する
papers.summary: 大きな教師モデルの出力を小さな学生モデルに学ばせる「蒸留」は LLM 訓練の基本手法だが、その性質はまだよく分かっていない。本研究は、学生の出力の「ばらつき」(エントロピー)が、学習目的に使う発散(ダイバージェンス)の種類によってどう変わるかを数学的に示し、前向き KL 発散では学生のエントロピーが必ず教師より高くなることを証明し、事前学習とファインチューニングで数値的に確認した。逆向き KL 発散はエントロピーを下げる一方、学生と教師の差が大きすぎると効果が崩れることも分かった。
papers.why: 発散の選び方が暗黙のエントロピー正則化として働くことを示し、自己蒸留でのハイパーパラメータ選びに直接使える理論的な根拠を与える。
papers.summary_en: Distillation is a core primitive of LLM training but its properties remain poorly understood. The paper proves that forward KL always inflates student entropy above the teacher's, verifying this identity quantitatively in pretraining and SFT, while reverse KL deflates entropy until the student-teacher gap grows too large, and interpolating between the two changes entropy smoothly early in training but abruptly at convergence.
papers.why_en: The divergence choice acts as an implicit entropy regularizer, giving a principled basis for picking divergence hyperparameters in self-distillation settings.

papers.title: Credit Where It Matters: Dependency-Aware Policy Optimization for Terminal Agents
papers.abstract: Terminal-using agents benefit from reinforcement learning (RL) in coding, debugging, and other multi-step terminal tasks. In these tasks, later commands often depend on information or intermediate results produced by earlier commands. However, existing trajectory-level and step-level credit assignment methods do not explicitly trace the read-write dependencies through which commands affect the final outcome. Consequently, training signals could still be assigned to irrelevant operations, weakening learning from relevant steps. In this paper, we propose Dependency-Aware Group Policy Optimization (DepGPO), which uses execution dependencies between commands to guide credit assignment for terminal agents. Specifically, we construct a command dependency graph from execution traces and trace backward from the resources inspected by the task verifier. We then assign credit to relevant writes and their supporting reads along these paths, and use it to redistribute trajectory advantages across steps. Extensive comparative experiments and ablation studies demonstrate that DepGPO improves task performance and training stability on complex terminal tasks.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 依存関係グラフでターミナル操作エージェントの強化学習の功績分配を改善
papers.summary: コーディングやデバッグなどターミナル(コマンドライン)を操作するエージェントの強化学習では、後のコマンドが前のコマンドの結果に依存することが多いが、既存の軌跡単位・ステップ単位の功績分配(クレジット割り当て)はこの読み書きの依存関係を追跡しておらず、関係のない操作にも学習信号が割り当たってしまっていた。本研究の DepGPO は実行履歴からコマンド依存グラフを作り、タスク検証器が調べる資源から逆方向にたどって関係する書き込み・読み込みだけに功績を割り当て、軌跡内の各ステップへ利得を再配分する。比較実験とアブレーションにより、複雑なターミナルタスクで性能と学習の安定性が改善したと報告されている。
papers.why: マルチステップのツール使用エージェントで学習信号が無関係な操作に薄まる問題を、実行依存関係グラフで解決するアイデアであり、他のエージェント強化学習にも応用しやすい。
papers.summary_en: In multi-step terminal-using RL tasks, later commands often depend on earlier ones, but existing trajectory- or step-level credit assignment does not trace these read-write dependencies, so training signal can leak to irrelevant operations. DepGPO builds a command dependency graph from execution traces, traces backward from the resources inspected by the task verifier, assigns credit to relevant writes and supporting reads, and redistributes trajectory advantages accordingly. Extensive experiments and ablations show improved task performance and training stability on complex terminal tasks.
papers.why_en: The dependency-tracing idea addresses credit dilution in multi-step agentic RL and could generalize to other tool-using agent training setups.

papers.title: Retrieval-Centric Deep Learning in Growing Nonparametric Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We investigate a general-purpose layer for deep learning that, instead of compressing arbitrary-size training data into fixed-size weight matrices, stores a new pair of key-value representations for every data point during training, and retrieves and recombines these representations through an attention mechanism at inference time - resulting in a growing neural net (NN). While Irie et al. (arXiv:2202.05798) have put forward this perspective from the classic duality expressing any linear layer in a deep NN trained by gradient descent as linear attention (LA) over the training data points, replacing LA by more powerful attention functions, as they suggest, turns out to be non-trivial: we show that naively applying learning rules from the LA case to advanced kernels does not lead to principled optimization. Here we fill this gap and develop functional gradient-based learning rules for kernelized attention layers, based on radial basis function (RBF) and softmax-like kernels - establishing the principled "retrieval-centric deep learning" (RCDL) paradigm. Empirically, we demonstrate the promising performance and learning-efficiency of RCDL on image classification and synthetic teacher-student learning tasks. Moreover, we show that replacing LA in the dual form of NNs by advanced LA variants, namely MesaNet/DeltaNet, yields a formal connection to recently proposed optimizers for conventional fixed-size NNs, offering a novel perspective on deep learning optimization.
papers.ja_title: 検索(リトリーバル)中心の深層学習で「成長するニューラルネット」を作る
papers.summary: 通常の層は訓練データを固定サイズの重み行列に圧縮してしまうが、本研究はデータ点ごとにキーと値のペアを保存し続け、推論時に注意機構(アテンション)で検索・組み合わせる「成長するニューラルネット」を提案した。線形注意を高性能なカーネル(RBF やソフトマックス型)に単純に置き換えるとうまく最適化できないことを示し、これらカーネル化注意層のための新しい勾関数的学習則を導いた。画像分類や人工的な教師-学生タスクで有望な性能と学習効率を実証したと報告されている。
papers.why: 線形注意の双対性をより強力なカーネルに理論的に拡張し、既存の線形注意系最適化手法(MesaNet/DeltaNet など)とのつながりを示す点が、モデル構造・最適化手法の設計に新しい視点を与える。
papers.summary_en: Instead of compressing arbitrary-size training data into fixed-size weight matrices, the paper stores a new key-value pair for every data point during training and retrieves/recombines them via attention at inference, forming a growing neural net. The authors show that naively swapping linear attention for more powerful kernels (RBF, softmax-like) does not lead to principled optimization, and derive new functional gradient-based learning rules for kernelized attention layers, demonstrating promising performance and learning efficiency on image classification and synthetic teacher-student tasks.
papers.why_en: The work formally extends the linear-attention duality to stronger kernels and connects it to recent optimizers for conventional fixed-size networks (MesaNet/DeltaNet), offering a fresh theoretical angle on model architecture and optimization.

papers.title: Proxy Confidence: Auditing Black-Box LLM Agents with a Surrogate's Log-Probabilities
papers.abstract: A deployed LLM agent emits tool calls, queries, and code that can be silently wrong -- by the time the error surfaces, the action has run. Frontier chat APIs hide the model's token probabilities; the agent's stated confidence barely beats chance on the mistakes that matter; and resampling does not help, since frontier models are highly repetitive, reproducing the same call across samples. We recover the missing signal from a low-cost open-weight surrogate run in parallel. It reads the same context, schema, and proposed action as the agent, then scores the call from its own log-probabilities through a family of complementary readouts: teacher forcing and request-PMI weigh the likelihood of each argument value, a discriminative verdict judges the call as a whole, and tool-choice competition tests the function against its siblings. One principle says which to trust: a generative likelihood localizes wrong argument values, while the verdict catches holistically wrong calls. When the error type is unknown, an ensemble is the low-regret default. The readout is training-free, needs no access to the agent's internals, and costs one prefill pass alongside the tool call. On difficult coding tasks it reaches AUROC 0.825 where the actor's stated confidence is near chance (0.598), and the generative readouts beat it by +0.07 to +0.28 across three further actors. Against self-consistency it gains +0.14 to +0.19 on near-deterministic actors, at 1/K the cost. The signal drives two deployment modes: a real-time gate escalating the least-trustworthy calls for review (+0.05 to +0.30 accepted-action accuracy at 50% coverage), and confidence feedback, returning the tool result with the score so the agent adapts its next step -- lifting task success on live-execution benchmarks (+0.119 and +0.137, p <= 1e-4) and beating a random-value control where step errors are silent (+0.078, p = 0.003).
papers.ja_title: 代理モデルのログ確率でブラックボックス LLM エージェントの危険な行動を見張る
papers.summary: デプロイされた LLM エージェントが出すツール呼び出しやコードは静かに間違っていることがあり、エラーが表面化する頃には既に実行されてしまっている。本研究は、フロンティア API が隠すトークン確率の代わりに、低コストなオープンウェイトの代理モデルを並行実行し、そのログ確率から呼び出しの信頼度を複数の読み出し方法で評価する手法を提案した。難しいコーディングタスクでは、エージェント自身の信頼度がほぼ運任せの AUROC 0.598 なのに対し、提案手法は AUROC 0.825 に達し、自己一致性(self-consistency)よりも 1/K のコストで +0.14〜+0.19 の改善を得た。低信頼な呼び出しをレビューに回すゲートや、スコアをエージェントに返す仕組みにより、実行ベンチマークでのタスク成功率が +0.119〜+0.137 向上したと報告されている。
papers.why: ブラックボックス API でも低コストな代理モデルでエージェントの危険な行動を事前に検知できる実用的な監査手法で、エージェント運用・デプロイのリスク管理に直結する。
papers.summary_en: A deployed LLM agent's tool calls, queries, and code can be silently wrong, and frontier chat APIs hide token probabilities while the agent's stated confidence barely beats chance and resampling does not help due to high repetitiveness. The authors recover the missing signal from a low-cost open-weight surrogate run in parallel, scoring calls via teacher forcing, request-PMI, a discriminative verdict, and tool-choice competition. On difficult coding tasks the method reaches AUROC 0.825 versus the actor's near-chance 0.598, beats self-consistency by +0.14 to +0.19 at 1/K the cost, and lifts task success on live-execution benchmarks by +0.119 and +0.137 (p<=1e-4) via a confidence-gated review mode and confidence feedback.
papers.why_en: The training-free, surrogate-based auditing signal offers a practical way to detect risky agent actions even behind black-box APIs, directly relevant to safe agent deployment and monitoring.

papers.title: LatentQuant: Preserving the Policy-Facing Latent Contract under NVFP4 VAE Quantization
papers.abstract: Recent world action models (WAMs) reuse pretrained video VAEs whose encoder latents directly condition downstream action policies. Quantization must therefore preserve not only reconstruction fidelity but also the policy-facing latent contract expected by the frozen policy. Direct NVFP4 leaves W4A4 quantization error uncompensated, whereas joint quantization-aware training (QAT) can recover reconstruction by moving this representation. On Wan2.1, joint QAT nearly matches FP32 VBench-7 (0.7403 versus 0.7409), yet LIBERO success collapses from 95.5% to 10.5%. Controlled decoder-only experiments show that activation quantize-dequantize operations alter the reconstruction signal and decoder Jacobian, redirecting the gradient returned to the encoder and inducing persistent latent drift. Based on this mechanism, we introduce LatentQuant, a two-stage NVFP4 QAT framework that first aligns the quantized encoder with its high-precision counterpart, then freezes it while adapting the decoder. Across Wan2.1 and Wan2.2, LatentQuant preserves near-baseline control and high reconstruction quality, achieving 95.75% success on LIBERO and 68.8% on RoboTwin. On NVIDIA B300 GPUs, NVFP4 execution achieves 1.17x-1.26x end-to-end VAE speedups over BF16 cuDNN.
papers.ja_title: LatentQuant: 世界行動モデルの VAE 量子化で方針への入力契約を守る
papers.summary: 世界行動モデル(WAM)は事前学習済みの動画 VAE をそのまま使い、エンコーダの潜在表現がそのまま下流の行動方針(ポリシー)への入力になる。単純な NVFP4 量子化や従来の量子化対応学習(QAT)では再構成品質(VBench-7)は FP32 とほぼ同等(0.7403 対 0.7409)でも、LIBERO タスクの成功率が 95.5% から 10.5% に崩壊することが分かった。原因は量子化・逆量子化操作がデコーダの勾配を歪めて潜在表現を継続的にずらす「潜在ドリフト」であることを突き止め、まずエンコーダを高精度版に合わせ、その後デコーダだけを適応させる 2 段階 QAT 手法 LatentQuant を提案し、LIBERO で 95.75%、RoboTwin で 68.8% の成功率を保ちつつ、NVIDIA B300 上で BF16 比 1.17〜1.26 倍の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: 再構成誤差の指標だけでは量子化の実害を見逃すことを示し、下流ポリシーへの「契約」を守るための量子化診断・訓練手法を提供する点が、低精度カーネル開発者にとって重要な教訓になる。
papers.summary_en: World action models reuse pretrained video VAEs whose encoder latents directly condition a frozen downstream policy. Direct NVFP4 or naive joint QAT nearly matches FP32 VBench-7 (0.7403 vs 0.7409) yet LIBERO success collapses from 95.5% to 10.5%, traced to activation quantize-dequantize operations distorting the decoder Jacobian and inducing persistent latent drift. LatentQuant, a two-stage NVFP4 QAT that first aligns the quantized encoder then freezes it while adapting the decoder, preserves near-baseline control (95.75% LIBERO, 68.8% RoboTwin) with 1.17x-1.26x end-to-end VAE speedups over BF16 cuDNN on NVIDIA B300 GPUs.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates that reconstruction-quality metrics alone can mask severe downstream policy failures under quantization, and offers a diagnosis-and-training recipe to preserve the policy-facing latent contract, a key lesson for low-precision kernel developers.

review.note: 再構成指標(VBench)が良好でも下流タスク成功率が崩壊する例を示し、量子化の評価は下流タスクまで確認すべきという測定上の注意を与える。
review.note_en: Shows that good reconstruction metrics (VBench) can coexist with collapsed downstream task success, cautioning that quantization evaluation must check downstream task performance, not just reconstruction fidelity.

papers.title: LongSocialBench: Do Long-Context LLMs Understand Online Discussion Threads?
papers.abstract: Long-context LLMs can now ingest entire online discussion threads, but understanding their social discourse requires more than reading a long document: models must track parent-reply relations, turning points, scoped subtrees, cross-branch contrasts, and participant trajectories. To test this structure-aware social reasoning, we introduce LongSocialBench, a benchmark of 1,462 verified human-authored multiple-choice items drawn from 94 complete Hacker News, Stack Exchange, and Reddit r/ChangeMyView episodes, with a median length of approximately 73K tokens. Each item pairs a complete serialized discussion and reply structure with a four-option question, requiring models to recover structured social evidence. Released items are verified for answerability, option uniqueness, and evidence grounding. Across 18 models and 29 evaluation settings, current long-context workflows remain far below human performance. The best individual result comes from Claude-Opus-4.7, which reaches 63.0% when prompted to eliminate incorrect options before answering, compared with 72.4% for independent human readers. Averaged across all 18 models, the full-context Baseline scores 43.9%. Supplying the gold evidence scope raises this to 55.0%, showing that substantial errors remain even after the relevant thread region is identified. LongSocialBench shows that the missing capability is not context access or prompting alone, but social understanding over structured reply trees.

papers.title: How RL Reshapes LLM Reasoning: Transferability, Coverage, and Scaling Laws
papers.abstract: Recent studies on reinforcement learning (RL) report seemingly conflicting evidence about large language model (LLM) reasoning. Training on mathematics can improve performance in other domains, yet gains in Pass@1 can coincide with lower Pass@$N$ than the base model. This raises a fundamental question: does RL expand an LLM's reasoning boundary, or merely reweight its existing reasoning space? We revisit these phenomena across Qwen and Gemma model families, showing both cross-domain gains and forgetting, while coverage at large sampling budgets increases on some tasks and decreases on others. Detailed analysis of solution traces before and after RL indicates a shift in the reasoning strategies the model employs, motivating a two-stage autoregressive policy model that separates \emph{strategy selection} from problem-specific execution. Within this framework, we prove how RL's implicit bias reshapes strategy preferences, allowing gains on some tasks while suppressing strategies required by others. This mechanism can also broaden or narrow coverage at a given sampling budget even without expanding strategy support. We further provide theoretical justifications for log-sigmoid and log-linear scaling laws in RL compute, and evaluate their predictive power. Together, these results connect changes in strategy selection to cross-domain transfer, reasoning coverage, and compute scaling.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 強化学習は LLM の推論をどう変えるか:転移・カバレッジ・スケーリング則
papers.summary: 数学で強化学習(RL)を行うと他分野の性能が上がる一方、Pass@1 は上がっても大規模サンプリング時の正解率(Pass@N)はベースモデルより下がるという矛盾する報告がある。本研究は Qwen と Gemma の複数モデルで、分野を越えた性能向上と「忘却」が同時に起きること、大規模サンプリングでのカバレッジ(カバー範囲)がタスクによって増えたり減ったりすることを確認した。RL 前後の解答過程を分析し、推論戦略の選択と問題固有の実行を分離する二段階の方針モデルを提案し、RL の暗黙のバイアスが戦略の好みを変えることで一部タスクの向上と別タスクの戦略抑制が同時に起きる仕組みを理論的に示し、RL 計算量に対する log-sigmoid 型・log-linear 型のスケーリング則も理論的に正当化して予測力を評価した。
papers.why: RL が LLM の推論能力を「拡張」するのか「既存戦略の再重み付け」に過ぎないのかという論争に、戦略選択という統一的な説明とスケーリング則の理論的根拠を示す点が、RL 後学習の設計・計算量配分に直結する。
papers.summary_en: Recent RL studies report seemingly conflicting evidence: training on math can improve cross-domain performance, yet gains in Pass@1 can coincide with lower Pass@N than the base model. Revisiting this across Qwen and Gemma families, the authors show both cross-domain gains and forgetting, with coverage at large sampling budgets increasing on some tasks and decreasing on others; analysis of solution traces motivates a two-stage policy model separating strategy selection from execution, proving how RL's implicit bias reshapes strategy preferences and can broaden or narrow coverage even without expanding strategy support, while also theoretically justifying log-sigmoid and log-linear scaling laws in RL compute.
papers.why_en: The strategy-selection framework offers a unifying explanation for the debate over whether RL expands or merely reweights an LLM's reasoning space, with theoretical scaling laws directly useful for RL post-training design and compute allocation.

papers.title: Asynchrony Is Nearly Free for Evolution Strategies on Long-Horizon LLM Agentic Tasks
papers.abstract: Synchronous policy updates can limit the efficiency of post-training for long-horizon LLM agents. When trajectories span multiple interaction turns, completion times can vary substantially, and synchronous update barriers leave faster workers idling, wasting compute resources. Asynchronous reinforcement learning addresses this inefficiency but introduces policy lag and off-policy optimization. Evolution strategies (ES) are a backpropagation-free alternative to gradient-based training, yet require many perturbed-policy evaluations and have remained largely synchronous in current LLM post-training. We introduce bounded-staleness asynchronous ES and investigate its training behavior under stale fitness measurements. On WebShop, we systematically vary the lag and fraction of stale fitness measurements and additionally introduce two stress tests to probe extreme staleness cases. Natural asynchrony closely tracks synchronous ES, and degradation in evaluation accuracy remains small even under extreme staleness, including when all fitness measurements are stale. These findings suggest that ES can tolerate substantial policy staleness without explicit off-policy correction, supporting its use in asynchronous post-training for long-horizon LLM agents.
papers.ja_title: 進化戦略を使ったLLMエージェント学習、非同期化はほぼノーコスト
papers.summary: 複数ターンにわたる長い対話をするLLMエージェントの強化学習では、各試行(トラジェクトリ)の完了時間がばらつくため、全員が揃うまで待つ同期更新は計算を無駄にする。研究者らは勾配を使わない最適化手法である進化戦略(ES)に、古さの上限を決めて非同期に更新する手法を導入し、オンラインショッピングのエージェントタスク WebShop で検証した。評価値(フィットネス)が全て古い極端な場合でも精度の低下はわずかで、同期版とほぼ同じ性能を保てることが分かった。
papers.why: ES ベースの LLM 後学習(post-training) は明示的な補正をしなくても非同期化に強いことを示し、長時間エージェントタスクの強化学習を高速化する際の基盤となる知見を与える。
papers.summary_en: In long-horizon LLM agent training, synchronous policy updates leave fast workers idling while waiting for slow trajectories to finish. The authors introduce bounded-staleness asynchronous evolution strategies (ES) and test them on WebShop, varying the lag and fraction of stale fitness measurements, including extreme stress tests. They find that natural asynchrony closely tracks synchronous ES, with only small degradation in evaluation accuracy even when all fitness measurements are stale.
papers.why_en: This suggests ES-based LLM post-training can tolerate substantial policy staleness without explicit off-policy correction, supporting efficient asynchronous training infrastructure for long-horizon agentic RL.

papers.title: ALoDLM: Adaptively Looped Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) enable fast generation by predicting multiple tokens in parallel, but their practical adoption remains limited by a persistent quality gap relative to comparably sized autoregressive (AR) models. We attribute this gap to a computation-difficulty mismatch: within a partially observed sequence, some unknown tokens are easy to predict, while others require substantially more computation. Existing DLMs nevertheless apply uniform computational depth to all unknown positions at each denoising step. We introduce ALoDLM, which replaces uniform computation with token-adaptive latent recurrence. At each denoising step, ALoDLM iteratively refines latent representations and allocates computation according to token difficulty. Tokens ready to commit are fed back as discrete context, while unresolved tokens retain and further refine their latent states through additional recurrent passes. To learn token prediction and computation allocation jointly, we formulate token-wise computation schedules as latent variables and derive a conditional negative evidence lower bound (NELBO). We train ALoDLM at 1.7B and 8B parameter scales. Across eleven benchmarks, ALoDLM outperforms all evaluated DLMs and the corresponding AR baselines in average benchmark score at both scales. ALoDLM also retains fast parallel decoding, yielding a strong quality-efficiency trade-off among evaluated autoregressive and diffusion models under optimized inference engines.
papers.ja_title: 難しい単語だけ長く考える拡散言語モデル ALoDLM
papers.summary: 拡散言語モデル(DLM、複数トークンを並列に予測して高速に文章を作る仕組み)は、同じ規模の自己回帰(AR)モデルに比べて生成品質が劣るという課題がある。筆者らは、トークンごとに予測の難しさが違うのに今までのDLMは全ての未確定トークンに同じ計算量をかけていたことが原因だと考え、ALoDLM という手法で簡単なトークンはすぐ確定させ、難しいトークンには潜在表現の繰り返し精緻化(リカレント処理)で追加の計算を割り当てるようにした。1.7B と 8B のモデルで学習したところ、11 個のベンチマーク平均で、評価した全ての DLM と対応する AR ベースラインを上回り、高速な並列デコードも維持した。
papers.why: トークンごとに計算量を動的に配分する仕組みは、推論エンジンの効率化や DLM のデコード速度と品質のトレードオフを改善する実装の着眼点として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Diffusion language models (DLMs) enable fast parallel token generation but typically lag behind comparably sized autoregressive (AR) models in quality, which the authors attribute to applying uniform computation depth to all unknown tokens regardless of difficulty. ALoDLM instead allocates token-adaptive latent recurrence, committing easy tokens quickly while refining hard tokens through additional recurrent passes. Trained at 1.7B and 8B scales, ALoDLM outperforms all evaluated DLMs and corresponding AR baselines on average across eleven benchmarks while retaining fast parallel decoding.
papers.why_en: The token-adaptive computation allocation offers a concrete design pattern for improving the quality-efficiency trade-off of diffusion LM decoding under optimized inference engines.

papers.title: Clean: Second-order LLM Training at Linear Memory Cost via Nystr{ö}m Sketching
papers.abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) entails a fundamental trade-off: memory-efficient optimizers such as Adam discard cross-parameter curvature, whereas full-curvature methods such as SOAP can accelerate convergence at prohibitive memory costs. We introduce Clean, a memory-efficient and full-curvature optimizer designed to resolve this bottleneck. Clean leverages the randomized Nystrom method to accurately approximate the left and right preconditioners in SOAP, and to reduce the optimizer's memory complexity from quadratic to linear in terms of model dimensions. We subsequently reintegrate the off-subspace components to capture curvature information beyond the low-rank approximation, preserving rich curvature at minimal memory cost. We further propose Q-Clean, a low-precision variant that aggressively compresses optimizer states. Q-Clean reduces optimizer memory consumption by over 50% compared to Muon when pre-training a LLaMA-1.3B architecture, all while maintaining strong and competitive predictive performance. Notably, Clean operates with a smaller optimizer-state footprint than standard AdamW while reaching AdamW's final performance 26% faster in wall-clock time. Furthermore, our methods uniquely enable the pre-training of a 13B-parameter model on a single 80GB GPU, providing a scalable, efficient, and accessible approach to large-scale model optimization.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: Nyströmスケッチで2次最適化を線形メモリで実現する Clean
papers.summary: LLM の学習では、省メモリな Adam はパラメータ間の曲率情報を捨ててしまい、SOAP のような完全曲率の手法は高精度だがメモリを大量に使うという二択があった。筆者らは Nyström 法(行列を低ランクで近似する手法)を使って SOAP の前処理行列を近似する Clean を提案し、メモリ使用量をモデル次元に対して2次から線形に減らした。LLaMA-1.3B の事前学習で、低精度版 Q-Clean は Muon よりオプティマイザのメモリを 50% 以上削減しつつ競争力のある性能を保ち、Clean は AdamW よりオプティマイザの状態を小さく保ったまま、AdamW の最終性能に 26% 速く(壁時計時間で)到達した。さらに 80GB の GPU 1 枚で 13B パラメータモデルの事前学習も可能にした。
papers.why: 曲率情報を活かした最適化とメモリ効率を両立させる手法で、大規模モデルの事前学習を限られたGPU資源で行う際の実装選択肢として直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Training LLMs forces a trade-off between memory-efficient optimizers like Adam, which discard cross-parameter curvature, and full-curvature methods like SOAP, which are prohibitively memory-hungry. Clean uses randomized Nyström sketching to approximate SOAP's preconditioners, cutting optimizer memory from quadratic to linear in model dimension while reintegrating off-subspace curvature information. On LLaMA-1.3B pretraining, the low-precision variant Q-Clean cuts optimizer memory by over 50% versus Muon while remaining competitive, and Clean reaches AdamW's final performance 26% faster in wall-clock time with a smaller optimizer-state footprint, enabling pretraining of a 13B-parameter model on a single 80GB GPU.
papers.why_en: Combining curvature-aware optimization with linear memory cost gives a directly usable building block for pretraining large models under limited GPU memory.

papers.title: Language-Conditioned Token and Reasoning Efficiency in Large Language Models: A Paired Cross-Lingual Study Protocol
papers.abstract: Large language models incur language-dependent representation and inference costs, but existing comparisons often conflate input language, assigned observable-trace language, and answer realization. We specify a prospective paired study that separates these interfaces while holding the semantic item, checkpoint, and answer oracle fixed. The initial design instantiates 240 exactly scored items rendered from templates in English and seven non-English languages, three distinct-lineage open-weight checkpoints, three trace-token budgets, 22 input- and trace-language conditions, a fixed answer reserve, and a separately counted delimiter: 47,520 initial core runs before prospective sample-size selection. RQ1-RQ3 estimate input and trace effects by intention-to-treat with failure-inclusive terminal accounting and test answer realization by cloning a sealed prefix and runtime-native KV state into eight crossed branches. Pre-freeze independent language review, fixed-form ASCII selectors, and code/surface/solver agreement constrain the realization test. H1-H5 share one Holm family and a global simultaneous component band. A secondary randomized experiment compares one-long-attempt and complete K-short-attempt policies at equal trace allowance under frozen seeds and oracle-blind aggregation; it is a full-policy contrast because answer capacity differs. Outcomes include exact token spans, correctness, latency, runtime-exposed memory, and qualified same-host operating-system-reported energy over prespecified hardware rails. The protocol separates tokenizer expansion, observable-trace cost, and answer-realization cost without treating visible traces as internal cognition or operating-system estimates as physical cross-device energy. No confirmatory model outcome is reported; result fields remain disabled until the frozen evidence ledger passes independent verification.
papers.ja_title: 言語によるトークン数と推論コストの違いを厳密に測るための実験プロトコル
papers.summary: 多言語でLLMを比べる既存研究は、入力言語・途中の思考過程(トレース)の言語・最終回答の実現方法を混同しがちで、公平な比較になっていなかった。本研究はこれらを分離した前向き(prospective)な対応実験のプロトコルを設計し、英語と7つの非英語を使った240問、3つの異なる系統のオープンモデル、3つのトレーストークン予算、22通りの入出力言語条件などを組み合わせ、事前に47,520回の実行を計画した。正解・レイテンシ・メモリ・同一ホストでのエネルギー消費を測る指標を定め、トークナイザの展開、トレースのコスト、回答実現のコストを混ぜずに測ることを目指すが、今回のバージョンでは確証的な結果はまだ報告されていない。
papers.why: 多言語でのLLM推論コストを測るとき、何と何を混同してはいけないかを明示したプロトコルであり、ベンチマーク設計時に参照すべき落とし穴がまとめられている。
papers.summary_en: Existing cross-lingual LLM comparisons often conflate input language, the language of intermediate observable traces, and how the final answer is realized, confounding the measurements. This paper specifies a prospective paired-study protocol that separates these interfaces while holding the semantic item, checkpoint, and answer oracle fixed, instantiating 240 items across eight languages, three model lineages, three trace-token budgets, and 22 language conditions, planning 47,520 core runs before sample-size selection, with exact-match accuracy, latency, memory, and same-host energy as outcomes. The protocol explicitly avoids treating visible reasoning traces as internal cognition or OS-reported energy as true device energy, and reports no confirmatory model outcome in this version.
papers.why_en: It lays out concrete pitfalls to avoid when measuring per-language token and inference cost of LLMs, serving as a checklist for designing rigorous cross-lingual efficiency benchmarks.

papers.title: COSMOS: Soft Mechanism Mixtures with Verifiable Routing for Long-Horizon PDE Forecasting
papers.abstract: Neural operators offer an efficient alternative to classical PDE solvers, but most learn a monolithic map per equation family and discretization. Real systems are compositional: transport, diffusion, wave, and reaction processes can act simultaneously. Existing mixture-of-experts operators typically use sparse top-$K$ routing, although concurrent physics is naturally a blend rather than a discrete choice. We propose COSMOS (Cooperative Operator Specialists with Mechanism-level Operator Soft-routing), a soft mechanism-mixture neural operator. Four process-biased specialists remain active at every step and are continuously mixed by a learned gate, with their features fused by a small network. Specialists share a coarse latent grid, while a zero-initialized full-resolution residual restores detail lost through the bottleneck. We also introduce an operator-splitting compositional benchmark with known mixture weights $w^\star$ per trajectory. Against family-tuned FNO under 20-step rollouts, an initial 3-seed evaluation suggested gains on diffusion--reaction, parity on Navier--Stokes, and weaker shallow-water performance. An 11-seed audit showed that the diffusion--reaction gain was unstable, motivating caution in small-seed rollout comparisons and precluding a reliable accuracy-win claim on these families. Ablations show that uniform routing or removing the specialist mixture substantially degrades stable-regime rollouts. On the labeled benchmark, dense soft routing yields $2.2\times$ lower error than hard top-1 routing at identical fusion; using generator weights $w^\star$ at inference further lowers rollout error to $0.034$, diagnosing limitations of the learned gate. However, routing labels do not align with the specialists' intended mechanisms: COSMOS supports compositional accuracy, not mechanism identity.

papers.title: Trinity: Self-Evolving Vision-Language Models with a Self-Verifier
papers.abstract: Self-evolving vision-language models (VLMs), a form of self-improvement in which a model generates its own training data from unlabeled images, are a promising route toward agents that expand their reasoning capability in an unsupervised manner, without relying on ever-larger annotation budgets. Existing methods pair a Questioner that proposes problems with a Solver that answers them, but reward both roles mainly by agreement among sampled answers. Agreement is a weak proxy for truth: it cannot tell whether a question is grounded in the image, whether the proposed reference answer is right, or whether a confident majority is wrong in the same way. We present Trinity, in which one VLM plays three roles, Questioner, Solver, and Verifier, and the Verifier is a self-verifier: an exponential moving average (EMA) of the policy itself, requiring neither labels nor an external judge. The Verifier screens every generated question for image grounding and answer correctness before it becomes supervision, scores Solver reasoning against the image, and adjudicates disputes between the reference answer and a strong Solver consensus, correcting the reference and penalizing the Questioner when the consensus is right. Trained on images alone, Trinity improves Qwen3-VL-8B on mathematical visual reasoning and on science benchmarks with biology content, for example, +8.6 points on the biology split of SciVQR and +12.8 on MathVerse, and its reward dynamics behave as a healthy self-play curriculum should. These results suggest that a self-evolving multimodal agent can strengthen its scientific reasoning from unlabeled scientific images alone, with the model itself serving as the verifier.
papers.ja_title: 一人三役で自己検証するVLMの自己進化学習 Trinity
papers.summary: ラベル付きデータなしで視覚言語モデル(VLM)自身が問題を作り答えさせて自己改善する手法は、サンプル同士の多数決(一致度)だけを正しさの目安にしていたため、質問が画像に基づいているか、答えが本当に正しいかを判断できなかった。Trinity は1つのVLMに出題者・回答者・検証者の3役をさせ、検証者には方策自身の指数移動平均(EMA、過去のモデルの平均)モデルを使うことで、ラベルも外部の判定者も使わずに出題と回答の正しさを審査する。画像だけで学習させた結果、Qwen3-VL-8B の性能が、生物学分野の視覚質問応答(SciVQR)で +8.6 点、数学の視覚推論(MathVerse)で +12.8 点向上した。
papers.why: 外部ラベルなしで自己学習の報酬を健全に保つ仕組みとして、強化学習的な自己改善(self-play)の報酬設計に使える新しい検証者の作り方を示している。
papers.summary_en: Existing self-evolving VLM methods pair a Questioner and Solver but reward both mainly by agreement among sampled answers, which cannot verify whether a question is grounded in the image or whether a confident consensus is actually correct. Trinity has a single VLM play Questioner, Solver, and Verifier, with the Verifier being an exponential moving average (EMA) of the policy itself that screens questions and adjudicates answer disputes without labels or an external judge. Trained on images alone, Trinity improves Qwen3-VL-8B by +8.6 points on the biology split of SciVQR and +12.8 on MathVerse.
papers.why_en: It offers a label-free verifier design for keeping self-play reward signals healthy, which is directly useful for building RL-style self-improvement pipelines without external judges.

papers.title: InferOpt: Constrained Multi-Objective Search for LLM Inference Configurations
papers.abstract: Serving an LLM means setting dozens of inference-time knobs, from per-layer KV retention to per-layer expert counts. Practice sets them with mechanism-specific heuristics that return a single operating point and do not scale to layer-wise search spaces. We recast inference configuration as constrained multi-objective black-box optimization and build InferOpt, a reusable search framework that requires only variable bounds, a deterministic resource cost, and an evaluation hook. InferOpt searches on a frozen sampled proxy set, rejects over-budget candidates before any model call, tightens the budget adaptively, and re-validates Pareto representatives on full-scale dataset. One pipeline covers a 28-dimensional continuous KV space (Qwen2.5-7B) and a 26-dimensional discrete MoE space (DeepSeek-V2-Lite). On KV, post-prefill pruning cuts the 16K cache by 64.4% and TPOT by 22.9--48.5%, and the searched layer-wise budget by InferOpt beats a matched uniform budget by 7.3% and 14.0% of the Full KV reference points. On MoE, a searched top-k schedule by InferOpt removes 43.0% of routed token--expert pairs while staying within 0.59 points of the default, closer than the matched-budget baselines. Against Random Search, NSGA-II, and MOTPE, InferOpt leads on both spaces, taking the best proxy hypervolume and the lowest retention on KV and staying closest to the uncompressed reference at the lowest experts on MoE.
papers.ja_title: LLM推論の設定値を多目的で自動探索する InferOpt
papers.summary: LLM をサービングする際には、層ごとのKV(キー・バリュー)キャッシュの残し方や層ごとのエキスパート数など数十個のつまみを調整する必要があるが、既存のやり方は仕組みごとの経験則に頼り1つの設定しか出せず、層単位の広い探索空間に対応できない。InferOpt は、変数の範囲・決まった計算コスト・評価関数だけを渡せば動く制約付き多目的探索の枠組みで、サンプルを絞った代理集合で探索し予算超えの候補を事前に除外する。Qwen2.5-7B の28次元の連続KV空間では、プリフィル後の枝刈りで16Kキャッシュを 64.4% 削減しTPOT(1トークンあたりの時間)を 22.9〜48.5% 短縮し、層ごとの予算を探索した結果は均一な予算に比べてフルKV基準点の 7.3% と 14.0% 上回った。DeepSeek-V2-Lite の26次元の離散MoE空間では、ルーティングされるトークン・エキスパートの組を 43.0% 削除しつつ性能低下をデフォルトから0.59点に抑え、ランダム探索やNSGA-II、MOTPEより優れた結果を示した。
papers.why: 推論時の多数のハイパーパラメータを層単位で自動調整する再利用可能な探索フレームワークであり、サービング基盤のチューニングに直接応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Serving an LLM requires tuning dozens of inference-time knobs such as per-layer KV retention and per-layer expert counts, but current practice relies on mechanism-specific heuristics that return a single operating point and don't scale to layer-wise search spaces. InferOpt is a reusable constrained multi-objective black-box search framework that needs only variable bounds, a deterministic cost, and an evaluation hook, searching on a sampled proxy set and rejecting over-budget candidates early. On a 28-dimensional continuous KV space (Qwen2.5-7B), post-prefill pruning cuts the 16K cache by 64.4% and TPOT by 22.9-48.5%, and the searched layer-wise budget beats a matched uniform budget by 7.3% and 14.0% of the Full KV reference points; on a 26-dimensional discrete MoE space (DeepSeek-V2-Lite), a searched top-k schedule removes 43.0% of routed token-expert pairs while staying within 0.59 points of the default, outperforming Random Search, NSGA-II, and MOTPE.
papers.why_en: It provides a reusable, layer-wise automatic search framework for the many inference-time hyperparameters in LLM serving, directly applicable to tuning production serving stacks.

papers.title: PhaseGate: Phase-Aware CPU Retrieval Scheduling for On-Device LLMs on Unified Memory
papers.abstract: On-device assistants run GPU-based LLM inference alongside CPU retrieval on unified-memory systems. Under a saturated local-retrieval workload, four concurrent retrieval workers raise 95th-percentile (p95) decode latency by 60-61% on two M4 systems, whereas prefill latency rises by only 5.7-6.9%. We study LLM phase as an admission signal for independent CPU retrieval under controlled LLM workloads. PHASEGATE calibrates separate concurrency limits for prefill and decode, selecting four and one on our base-M4 configuration. Under a backlogged queue, it achieves 2.0 times the aggregate retrieval throughput of the best tested feasible fixed policy, with both p95 LLM latency metrics within 1.25 times their no-retrieval baselines in all seven held-out runs. A phase-blind control, TimeGate, uses the same two limits on a calibration-derived schedule without observing LLM phase. It achieves similar retrieval throughput but violates the output-token latency limit in every run. M2 and M2 Pro Mac minis reproduce the policy ordering, while output-length sweeps show that the advantage narrows as decode occupies more of each request.
papers.ja_title: LLMの処理段階を見てCPU検索の同時実行数を決める PhaseGate
papers.summary: オンデバイスのAIアシスタントは、GPUでのLLM推論とCPUでの検索(リトリーバル)を同時に動かすが、検索処理が混み合うと、4つの検索ワーカーが同時に動くだけで、M4搭載の2台のシステムでデコード(文章生成)のp95レイテンシが 60〜61% も悪化する一方、プリフィル(文章生成前の準備段階)への影響は 5.7〜6.9% にとどまることが分かった。PhaseGate は LLM の処理段階(プリフィルかデコードか)を見てCPU検索の同時実行数の上限を変える仕組みで、基本のM4構成ではプリフィル時4・デコード時1に制限する。待ち行列が溜まった状態で、試した固定方策の中で最良のものと比べて検索のスループットを2倍にしつつ、7回すべての評価でLLMのp95レイテンシを検索なしの場合の 1.25 倍以内に保てた。段階を見ない比較手法(TimeGate)は同程度のスループットを出せたが、全ての実行で出力トークンのレイテンシ制限を破った。
papers.why: GPUとCPUを共有するオンデバイス推論で、LLMの処理段階を信号として周辺処理のリソースを動的に制御する、サービング基盤のスケジューリング設計の具体例を示している。
papers.summary_en: On-device assistants run GPU-based LLM inference alongside CPU retrieval on unified-memory systems, and under saturated retrieval, four concurrent retrieval workers raise p95 decode latency by 60-61% on two M4 systems while prefill latency rises by only 5.7-6.9%. PhaseGate calibrates separate concurrency limits for prefill and decode (four and one on the base M4 configuration) using LLM phase as an admission signal, achieving 2.0x the aggregate retrieval throughput of the best fixed policy under a backlogged queue while keeping p95 LLM latency within 1.25x of the no-retrieval baseline in all seven held-out runs. A phase-blind control (TimeGate) achieves similar throughput but violates the latency limit in every run.
papers.why_en: It shows a concrete serving-infrastructure scheduling design that uses LLM execution phase as a real-time signal for controlling concurrent background resource usage on shared CPU/GPU on-device systems.

papers.title: From Probe Scores to Alarm Policies: Operational Validity of Activation Monitors for Language-Model Agents
papers.abstract: Activation probes can predict safety-relevant properties of language models with high area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC), but deployed agent monitors make thresholded alarm decisions under tight false-alarm budgets. These are different estimands. We introduce an Operational Validity Contract that fixes a monitor's target, observability, identity, timing, intervention unit, comparator, calibration, and cost. We formalize risk at the semantic request or trajectory level: when one task contains repeated alarm opportunities, row-level AUROC and false positive rate do not identify semantic-unit any-alarm risk. A confidence-certified threshold also requires enough independent negative units, a tie-safe rule, and transport to deployment. Across Models Under Pressure, LASR refusal prediction, immutable AgentDojo, and a prospectively protocol-frozen ST-WebAgentBench replication, joint activation-observable monitors reach AUROC 0.957 and 0.935 on the first two benchmarks, yet their locked 5%/10% detection rates are only .642/.742 and .719/.782, respectively. On AgentDojo, the secondary mean-activation rollout monitor reaches AUROC 0.922 but detects none of 38 positive semantic cases at the locked 5% operating point; thresholds intended for 10% false alarms realize 18.7-20.0% on test. Because the test misses its prospectively frozen 40-positive support gate, we label it support-insufficient. On ST-WebAgentBench, activation reaches AUROC .874, but 23 independent calibration negatives cannot identify even a 10% controller; the locked policy abstains rather than reporting its mechanical zero FPR as a success. An exploratory counterexample also lowers full AUROC while improving realized 10% utility. The fail-closed compiler caps MUP and LASR at restricted predictive value and AgentDojo and ST-Web at representation accessibility; no setting reaches alarm-policy validity.

papers.title: LatentIndex: Cross-Layer Sharing with Layer-Specific Selection for Sparse Attention
papers.abstract: Sparse attention reduces core-attention computation, but its indexers still incur repeated selection work and per-layer key-cache storage. Reusing selected indices across layers reduces this overhead but constrains multiple layers to the same token set. We introduce LatentIndex, which extends the latent-sharing principle of Multi-head Latent Attention across indexer layers. Each layer group constructs a shared latent cache from its first layer's hidden states, while layer-specific scoring enables independent token selection. Absorbing key decoders into queries enables direct scoring of the shared cache without reconstructing historical per-layer keys. We develop training-free calibration and investigate a training-aware instantiation of this principle. To balance quality and computation, a hierarchical selection (HS) variant lets followers independently refine a shared candidate set proposed by the anchor. With four-layer sharing, LatentIndex reduces logical indexer-cache storage by 61.1% on DeepSeek-V3.2. Across DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5, training-free LatentIndex improves head-wise attention-mass recall over IndexCache by up to 3.28 percentage points while maintaining RULER and LongBench performance close to native DSA. HS further achieves 2.30-2.72 times decode indexer speedups over DSA across 8K-128K contexts, retaining most of LatentIndex's recall. LatentIndex offers a new perspective on cross-layer indexing: sharing continuous representations rather than discrete selections enables efficient reuse while preserving layer-specific token selection.
papers.ja_title: 層をまたぐ潜在共有で疎注意のインデックス計算を減らす LatentIndex
papers.summary: 疎な注意機構(スパースアテンション)は計算量を削るが、層ごとにトークン選択をやり直すためインデックス計算とキャッシュのコストが積み重なる、という困りごとがある。LatentIndex は Multi-head Latent Attention の潜在共有の考え方を層の指標計算にも広げ、層グループの先頭層から作った共有潜在キャッシュに対し各層が独自のスコアリングで選択だけを個別に行う。DeepSeek-V3.2 で 4 層をまとめて共有すると、インデックス用キャッシュを 61.1% 削減しつつ IndexCache に比べ注意質量の再現率(recall)を最大 3.28 ポイント改善し、階層選択を使うと DSA 比で 2.30〜2.72 倍のデコード高速化を達成した。
papers.why: 層間でキー表現を共有しつつ層ごとの選択自由度を保つ発想は、長文脈 LLM 推論のキャッシュ設計に直接使える新しい視点を示す。
papers.summary_en: Sparse attention cuts attention compute, but redoing token selection and caching keys per layer still accumulates overhead. LatentIndex extends Multi-head Latent Attention's latent-sharing idea to indexing: layers in a group build a shared latent cache from the first layer's hidden states while each layer still scores tokens independently. With four-layer sharing on DeepSeek-V3.2 this cuts logical indexer-cache storage by 61.1%, improves head-wise attention-mass recall over IndexCache by up to 3.28 percentage points, and the hierarchical-selection variant gives 2.30-2.72x decode indexer speedups over DSA.
papers.why_en: Sharing continuous latent representations across layers while keeping per-layer token selection offers a new, directly usable perspective for cache design in long-context LLM inference.

papers.title: A Tropical Geometry View of Forgetting: A Per-Unit Projector for Knowledge-Preserving Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning a language model on new text degrades what it already does. Replay-free projectors such as Adam-NSCL and GPM forbid one shared subspace of a layer's inputs in every row of the update. The tropical geometry of a ReLU layer shows why this is too coarse. In data space, the units' walls are tropical hypersurfaces whose cells are dual to the upper vertices of a zonotope; in weight space, each old token is a hyperplane, and the tokens cut out a polyhedron, the closure of the weights that keep every token on its side. An exact identity joins the two pictures: the squared change of the layer's output under any weight change splits into in-cell, open-to-closed and closed-to-open terms, and the first two live on the tokens each unit fires on.
