The identity names a gate-aware per-unit projector, and a budget-separation theorem prices exact protection: it costs a unit the rank of its own open tokens, while a shared subspace pays at least the rank of their union in every row. On OPT-1.3b, where 96% of (token, unit) pairs are closed, the projector forgets less than Adam-NSCL at all six matched budgets from 9 to 60 constrained directions per row, the gap widening from $1.1\times$ to $4.3\times$; with 1/5.5 of the directions it halves the forgetting of Adam-NSCL at GPM's energy threshold. On OPT-6.7b, it matches Adam-NSCL's forgetting at matched budget while learning more. As the theory predicts, the open/closed partition is the operative variable: open tokens beat random, sign-blind and anti-gate token sets on 18 of 18 seed-pairs. In pruning repair, every derivative-based local model of the output error at the dense weights is blind to pairs that open: the minimisers of the gate-weighted objective can leave the polyhedron, the objective's closed-form solution is 1.94 nats worse than no repair on OPT-1.3b, and a convex one-sided penalty bounds the escape.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: トロピカル幾何で見るファインチューニングの忘却:ユニット単位の保護法
papers.summary: 言語モデルを新しいデータで追加学習(ファインチューニング)すると元々できていたことを忘れてしまう、という困りごとがある。既存の Adam-NSCL や GPM は層全体で 1 つの共有部分空間を禁止する粗い方法だが、本研究は ReLU 層をトロピカル幾何で分析し、各ユニット(ニューロン)が実際に発火しているトークンだけを守るユニット単位の射影法を導いた。OPT-1.3B では制約方向数 9〜60 の全 6 設定で Adam-NSCL より忘却が少なく、差は 1.1 倍から 4.3 倍に広がり、同じ保護強度なら必要な方向数を 1/5.5 に減らせた。
papers.why: 層全体でなくユニットごとに「忘れてはいけない方向」を理論的に絞り込む発想は、追加学習での知識保持コストを削る学習パイプライン設計に新しい視点を与える。
papers.summary_en: Fine-tuning a language model on new text degrades what it already does. Prior replay-free projectors like Adam-NSCL and GPM forbid one shared subspace per layer, but this work uses tropical geometry of ReLU layers to derive a gate-aware, per-unit projector that protects only the tokens each unit actually fires on. On OPT-1.3B it forgets less than Adam-NSCL at all six matched budgets (9-60 constrained directions per row), with the gap widening from 1.1x to 4.3x, and needs only 1/5.5 of the directions to halve Adam-NSCL's forgetting at GPM's energy threshold.
papers.why_en: Narrowing the protected subspace from the whole layer down to each unit's own firing tokens gives a theoretically grounded way to cut the cost of preserving prior knowledge during fine-tuning.

papers.title: Learning to Clarify Underspecified Intents Under Limited Interaction
papers.abstract: AI assistants receive requests that leave out information needed for a good outcome, for example about users' preferences or goals. They must then either speculate or ask for more information before proceeding. We reconceptualize this as a value-of-information problem: the assistant should acquire information whose absence causes the greatest avoidable loss in user utility. This is rarely known ex ante; rather, assistants must predict it in order to optimally allocate limited user interactions. We instantiate this problem in image generation and derive a reinforcement learning framework using multi-turn simulated users to maximize utility recovery under uncertainty. In a preregistered study with 456 interactive sessions across 76 human participants, this helped users significantly better match reference images with significantly fewer questions, less total interaction time, and lower cost. This points toward a simple and scalable framework for training language model assistants to better disambiguate user intent by asking more informative questions.

papers.title: More Value per Key: Asymmetric Sparse Attention for Faster LLM Decoding
papers.abstract: Autoregressive generation in Large Language Models (LLMs) is constrained by the memory and computational demands of attention mechanisms. Sparse attention methods mitigate this cost by selecting only high-probability entries of the attention matrix. We observe that in many such methods, this renders the probability-value multiplication negligible, shifting the bottleneck to the query-key step. Key heads can therefore be reduced to accelerate inference, while retaining more value heads preserves capacity with limited additional decoding cost. We introduce Sparse Asymmetric Group-Query Attention (SAGA), which decouples key and value head counts to exploit this principle, and pair it with approximate top-N (Atop-N) attention, a simple sparse attention method designed to study the interaction between sparsity and head-count asymmetry. We formalize the benefits of this asymmetry theoretically and validate them empirically through latency measurements and quality evaluations on models up to 1.5B parameters. Together, SAGA and Atop-N achieve end-to-end decoding speedups exceeding $2\times$ over our full-attention GQA baseline at long contexts. Models trained from scratch with SAGA nearly match the quality of comparable GQA variants on the evaluated benchmarks. To facilitate adoption, we introduce an efficient fine-tuning method that converts pretrained models to the SAGA architecture, enabling practitioners to benefit from our approach without costly retraining.
papers.ja_title: キーとバリューの頭数を非対称にして LLM のデコードを高速化する SAGA
papers.summary: 疎な注意機構では選ばれたキーに対する確率と値(バリュー)の掛け算はほぼ無視できるほど軽く、実際のボトルネックはクエリとキーの計算に移る、という観察がある。そこで SAGA(Sparse Asymmetric Group-Query Attention)はキーのヘッド数を減らしつつバリューのヘッド数は多めに残す非対称な設計を導入し、簡易な近似 top-N 注意 Atop-N と組み合わせた。最大 1.5B パラメータのモデルで検証したところ、長い文脈では通常の GQA 全注意に比べてエンドツーエンドで 2 倍を超えるデコード高速化を達成し、品質はほぼ同等の GQA 変種と変わらなかった。
papers.why: キーとバリューのヘッド数を分離する非対称設計は推論のメモリ・計算コストを削る新しい選択肢で、既存モデルを再学習なしで変換する方法も示されており採用コストを下げる。
papers.summary_en: In many sparse attention methods, the probability-value multiplication becomes negligible once only high-probability entries are selected, shifting the real bottleneck to the query-key step. SAGA (Sparse Asymmetric Group-Query Attention) decouples key and value head counts, shrinking key heads while keeping more value heads, paired with a simple approximate top-N attention. On models up to 1.5B parameters, SAGA and Atop-N together give end-to-end decoding speedups exceeding 2x over a full-attention GQA baseline at long contexts, with models trained from scratch nearly matching comparable GQA quality.
papers.why_en: Decoupling key and value head counts is a new, practical lever for inference memory/compute cost, and the paper also gives a fine-tuning recipe to convert existing pretrained models without costly retraining, lowering adoption cost.

papers.title: Scalable Distortion-Aware Clustering for Fronthaul-Limited Cell-Free MIMO Networks
papers.abstract: This paper studies distortion-aware clustering for uplink fronthaul-limited cell-free MIMO networks employing maximum ratio combining (MRC). While MRC is appealing for its low-complexity, its performance is limited by interference, fronthaul distortions, and channel imperfections. This motivates clustering strategies that compensate for these impairments through coordination of access points. Since instantaneous small-scale fading-based optimization is not scalable in large systems, and is impractical due to frequent channel variations, we instead optimize an objective depending only on large-scale fading coefficients. To this end, asymptotic analysis is used to derive deterministic equivalent expressions for the average network sum rate, with focus on quantization distortion, leading to a quadratic-over-linear objective. Although maximizing such an objective under binary constraints is non-convex, we exploit its structure to develop a polynomial time scheme that attains the global optimum. Numerical results show that the proposed clustering method provides performance gains over improved variants of existing literature, and remains competitive with the small-scale fading-based global optimum obtained via exhaustive search.

papers.title: Enhancing Long-Video VLM Embeddings with Query-Aware Streaming Latent Reasoning
papers.abstract: Long-video embedding requires capturing sparse query-relevant evidence under a limited visual-token budget. Uniform sampling can miss brief events in videos spanning minutes or hours, whereas encoding more frames in a single context increases memory and computation. We introduce \textbf{Query-Aware Streaming Latent Reasoning} (QASLR), a post-training framework that accumulates evidence across clips while keeping the embedding size fixed. QASLR selects a bounded set of frames, restores their temporal order, and processes them clip by clip with a vision-language backbone. A compact set of persistent think tokens cross-attends to each clip's features, while an embed token reads out a normalized representation after every update. This design integrates evidence across multiple backbone calls without requiring all selected frames to share a single context. Training combines final contrastive learning, step-wise contrastive supervision, and final-embedding self-distillation. Intermediate supervision trains partial-video readouts for retrieval, while self-distillation regularizes them toward the final representation. Query-aware selection produces query-conditioned representations for candidate-set scoring and reranking, whereas query-independent selection enables reusable corpus indexing. Under the full training recipe, HourVideo retrieval Hit@1 increases from 54.2 to 70.7 and from 57.4 to 72.8 for 2B and 8B Qwen3-VL-Embedding backbones, respectively. Gains extend to the evaluated moment-retrieval and video-QA tasks, and the streaming head transfers to a second Qwen-family embedding backbone. These results support streaming latent aggregation as an effective approach to integrating long-video evidence into fixed-dimensional representations.
papers.ja_title: クエリに応じて要点を蓄積するストリーミング型の長尺動画埋め込み QASLR
papers.summary: 数十分から数時間に及ぶ長い動画を埋め込み(embedding)にする際、均等にフレームを間引くと短い重要場面を見逃し、逆に多くのフレームを一度に読み込むとメモリと計算が爆発する、という困りごとがある。QASLR はクリップ単位で動画を処理し、常駐する「思考トークン」がクリップごとの特徴に注意を向けて情報を蓄積し、埋め込みトークンが毎回正規化された表現を読み出す後学習の仕組みを加える。HourVideo の検索タスクでは Hit@1 が Qwen3-VL-Embedding の 2B モデルで 54.2 から 70.7 に、8B モデルで 57.4 から 72.8 に向上した。
papers.why: 固定サイズの埋め込みを保ったまま長時間動画の証拠を段階的に積み上げる設計は、長文脈マルチモーダルモデルの推論メモリ管理に応用できる考え方を示す。
papers.summary_en: Long-video embedding needs to capture sparse, query-relevant evidence under a limited visual-token budget: uniform sampling can miss brief events, while encoding more frames in one context blows up memory and compute. QASLR processes a bounded set of frames clip by clip, with persistent 'think tokens' cross-attending to each clip's features and an embed token reading out a normalized representation after every update, trained with a post-training recipe. Under the full training recipe, HourVideo retrieval Hit@1 increases from 54.2 to 70.7 and from 57.4 to 72.8 for the 2B and 8B Qwen3-VL-Embedding backbones respectively.
papers.why_en: Accumulating evidence across clips while keeping the embedding size fixed offers an approach to long-context memory management that could transfer to other multimodal inference settings.

papers.title: SpecFold: Folding Multi-Branch Redundancy for Faster Speculative Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion large language models (DLLMs) generate text through iterative block denoising, and multi-branch speculative decoding accelerates this process by verifying a main branch together with multiple draft branches in a single forward pass. While prior DLLM acceleration methods primarily exploit temporal redundancy across denoising steps, we identify a complementary redundancy axis within each speculative verification step: multi-branch computational redundancy. During speculative verification, draft branches inherit most tokens from their parents while unmasking a small set of additional positions, causing large portions of hidden states to remain highly similar across branches. We propose SpecFold, an algorithm-system co-design that exploits this multi-branch redundancy to reduce the cost of multi-branch speculative verification. Algorithmically, SpecFold performs token-level residual gating and selectively reuses parent computation through folded attention and FFN while preserving residual hidden states. Systemically, a Triton kernel implementation translates this fine-grained reuse into end-to-end throughput gains through efficient sparse multi-branch execution. SpecFold is orthogonal to temporal caching and compatible with existing DLLM speculation strategies. Across two DLLM families, five models, and five standard benchmarks, SpecFold achieves up to 1.64x throughput over Spiffy and up to 1.99x over vanilla decoding, while maintaining comparable task performance.
papers.ja_title: 拡散言語モデルの投機的デコードで枝間の重複計算を畳み込んで高速化する SpecFold
papers.summary: 拡散型の大規模言語モデル(DLLM)はブロックごとのノイズ除去を繰り返して文章を生成し、複数の分岐(ドラフト枝)を一度に検証する投機的デコードで高速化できるが、各分岐の隠れ状態は親からほとんど変わらず似通っているのに同じ計算を繰り返してしまう、という困りごとがある。SpecFold はトークン単位で残差をゲートし、似た部分の計算を親から再利用する「折り込み注意・FFN」を提案し、Triton カーネルで実装してスループットの改善につなげた。2 系統・5 モデル・5 ベンチマークで、Spiffy 比で最大 1.64 倍、素のデコード比で最大 1.99 倍のスループットを、タスク性能を保ったまま達成した。
papers.why: 時間方向の再利用(キャッシュ)とは別の「分岐間の冗長性」という軸を見つけ、アルゴリズムとカーネル実装の両方で実測した点が、投機的デコード高速化の設計に実用的な示唆を与える。
papers.summary_en: Diffusion large language models (DLLMs) generate text via iterative block denoising, and multi-branch speculative decoding speeds this up by verifying a main branch with several draft branches in one forward pass, but draft branches inherit most of their parent's hidden states, leaving large portions highly similar and redundantly recomputed across branches. SpecFold performs token-level residual gating and selectively reuses parent computation through folded attention and FFN, implemented via a Triton kernel for end-to-end throughput gains, orthogonal to and compatible with existing temporal caching strategies. Across two DLLM families, five models, and five benchmarks, SpecFold achieves up to 1.64x throughput over Spiffy and up to 1.99x over vanilla decoding while maintaining comparable task performance.
papers.why_en: Identifying multi-branch computational redundancy as a complementary axis to temporal caching, and backing it with a real kernel implementation and measured speedups, gives a practically useful direction for speeding up speculative decoding.

papers.title: ResOPD: Tail Residualization for Sparse On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student model on self-generated trajectories, but transmitting dense teacher distributions across long reasoning traces creates prohibitive communication and memory bottlenecks. Practical systems therefore rely on sparse teacher interfaces, typically transmitting either the sampled-token score or a small Top-$k$ distribution. However, this sparse setting faces a fundamental dilemma: sampled-token estimators are unbiased but suffer from severe gradient variance, whereas directly optimizing Top-$k$ objectives introduces systematic bias. To improve this trade-off, we propose ResOPD (On-Policy Distillation with Tail Residualization), which provides unbiased full-vocabulary reverse KL gradient estimation under on-policy sampling, with substantial variance reduction under the same sparse payload in the evaluated settings. ResOPD aggregates the unobserved vocabulary into an observable coarse tail event, computes its exact aggregate gradient, and samples only the fine-grained within-tail residual, which requires no additional teacher queries or forward passes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ResOPD substantially reduces gradient variance, stabilizes online training dynamics, and improves downstream performance across the evaluated settings. These results establish ResOPD as an efficient, plug-and-play variance reduction primitive for sparse on-policy distillation.
papers.ja_title: 疎な教師信号でも偏りなく安定させるオンポリシー蒸留 ResOPD
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留(生徒モデルが自分で生成した軌跡で教師モデルから学ぶ手法)では、長い推論過程全体で教師の確率分布を送ると通信とメモリの負担が大きいため、実際のシステムではサンプルトークンのスコアだけ、または上位 k 個(Top-k)の確率だけを送る疎な方式を使う。しかしサンプルトークン方式は偏りがない一方で勾配のばらつきが大きく、Top-k 方式は逆に系統的な偏りが出るというジレンマがあった。ResOPD は観測されない語彙全体を 1 つの「尾部イベント」としてまとめて正確な勾配を計算し、尾部内の細かい部分だけを追加の教師呼び出しなしでサンプリングすることで、偏りのない勾配推定と大幅なばらつき低減を同じ通信量で両立させた。実験では学習が安定し、下流タスクの性能も向上したことが示された。
papers.why: 疎な教師信号で通信・メモリコストを抑えつつ Top-k 方式の系統的バイアスを避けられる差し替え可能な手法として、大規模な RL 後学習パイプラインにそのまま組み込める。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation trains a student on its own generated trajectories, but sending the teacher's dense distribution across long reasoning traces creates prohibitive communication and memory bottlenecks, so practical systems rely on sparse interfaces (sampled-token scores or Top-k). Sampled-token estimators are unbiased but suffer severe gradient variance, while Top-k objectives introduce systematic bias. ResOPD aggregates the unobserved vocabulary into an observable tail event, computes its exact aggregate gradient, and samples only the fine-grained within-tail residual with no additional teacher queries, giving unbiased full-vocabulary reverse-KL gradient estimation with substantial variance reduction under the same sparse payload. Experiments show ResOPD stabilizes online training dynamics and improves downstream performance across evaluated settings.
papers.why_en: It provides a plug-and-play variance-reduction primitive for sparse on-policy distillation, letting large-scale RL post-training pipelines keep low communication cost while avoiding the systematic bias of Top-k-only objectives.

papers.title: Billion-Scale Thumbnail Optimization for Uncurated Short-Form Videos via Multi-Armed Bandits
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a real-time thumbnail optimization system deployed at a global $O(B)$ scale on a major short-form video platform. Unlike traditional long-form content, where custom thumbnails are heavily curated by creators, a considerable fraction of short-form videos are published without human-selected artwork. To address this uncurated corpus, we present a fully automated, end-to-end framework that replaces static default frames with dynamic, data-driven selections across billions of videos. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first published work demonstrating an online Multi-Armed Bandit framework successfully deployed at an $O(B)$ scale for uncurated short-form video discovery. Our solution pairs a multi-stage candidate generation pipeline with a low-latency serving infrastructure. By initializing the exploration framework with image-specific priors derived from a deep visual quality model, the system minimizes exploration costs and dynamically serves optimal thumbnails at serving time. Global deployment demonstrates statistically significant improvements in core user discovery and engagement metrics.

papers.title: DiVeR: Decision-Critical Verifier Learning for VLA Test-Time Scaling
papers.abstract: Scaling robot data and model capacity has improved Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies, but further progress is constrained by the high cost of robotic data. Verifier-guided test-time scaling offers an efficient alternative by sampling multiple action candidates and selecting the one most likely to lead to task success at inference time. Existing classification-based verifiers learn from trajectory-level outcomes but treat all visited states equally, even though their value for candidate discrimination can vary across a trajectory. At many states, plausible actions are similar and provide limited discrimination signal, while only a sparse set of decision-critical states admits meaningfully different actions that can substantially affect downstream outcomes. To address this, we propose DiVeR, which estimates decision criticality from the dispersion of sampled action representations. DiVeR then uses this signal to reweight verifier learning toward states where action selection is most consequential, without requiring step-level annotations or additional environment interaction. Across LIBERO, RoboCasa, and real-world experiments on a Franka Research 3 robot, DiVeR consistently improves task success through more effective verifier-guided action selection, while adding negligible verifier inference overhead.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 重要な場面だけに重みを置いて学習効率を上げるVLA検証器 DiVeR
papers.summary: ロボット操作のビジョン・言語・行動(VLA)モデルでは、行動候補を複数サンプリングして成功しそうなものを選ぶ検証器(verifier)を使ったテスト時スケーリングが有効だが、既存の検証器は軌跡中の全状態を同じ重みで学習し、実際には行動選択がほとんど結果に差を生まない状態と、結果を大きく左右する「決定的な状態」が混在していることを無視していた。DiVeR はサンプリングした行動表現のばらつき(分散)から各状態の決定的重要度を推定し、その重要度に応じて検証器学習を重み付けすることで、追加のステップ注釈や環境との相互作用を増やさずに精度を高めた。LIBERO、RoboCasa、実機のFranka Research 3ロボットでの実験で、推論の計算コストをほとんど増やさずにタスク成功率が一貫して向上した。
papers.why: 検証器ガイド付きテスト時スケーリングを少ない追加計算でより効果的にする重み付け学習の工夫であり、推論時の候補選択の作り込みに直結する。
papers.summary_en: Verifier-guided test-time scaling for VLA policies samples multiple action candidates and selects the one most likely to succeed, but existing classification-based verifiers treat all visited trajectory states equally even though only a sparse set of "decision-critical" states meaningfully affects downstream outcomes. DiVeR estimates decision criticality from the dispersion of sampled action representations and reweights verifier learning toward these states, without step-level annotations or additional environment interaction. Across LIBERO, RoboCasa, and real-world Franka Research 3 experiments, DiVeR consistently improves task success through more effective verifier-guided action selection while adding negligible verifier inference overhead.
papers.why_en: It offers a lightweight reweighting technique to make verifier-guided test-time scaling more compute-efficient, directly relevant to designing inference-time candidate selection mechanisms.

papers.title: From Overloaded to Guaranteed: High-Throughput Multi-SLO Enforcement for LoRA-Assisted On-Premise LLM Deployment
papers.abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) become essential in privacy-sensitive sectors like hospitals and government agencies, the on-premise LLM servers offer a cost-effective and secure alternative to public cloud services. However, these resource-constrained servers struggle to guarantee heterogeneous Service Level Objectives (SLOs) when serving multiple LoRA-adapted services simultaneously. Existing serving frameworks suffer from severe SLO violations due to the computational overhead of LoRA layers and the rigid nature of batch scheduling. To address this, we propose HALO, a scheduling method tailored for LoRA-assisted on-premise LLM deployment. HALO introduces two key innovations: a spatial multiplexing strategy that overlaps Base and LoRA computations by partitioning GPU Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), and an SLO-aware scheduler that decouples request execution based on "request-level slack." By prioritizing urgent tasks and utilizing idle budget for traffic shaping, HALO significantly mitigates resource contention. Our evaluation demonstrates that HALO minimizes SLO violations while improving throughput compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
papers.ja_title: LoRA混在サービングでもSLOを守るGPUスケジューラ HALO
papers.summary: 病院や官公庁などオンプレミス(自社設置)サーバーで複数のLoRAアダプタ付きLLMサービスを同時に動かすと、LoRA層の計算負荷とバッチ処理の柔軟性の低さから、サービス品質目標(SLO)の違反が頻発していた。HALO は GPU のストリーミング・マルチプロセッサ(SM)を分割してベースモデルとLoRA計算を重ねて実行する空間多重化と、リクエストごとの「余裕時間」に基づいて緊急度の高いタスクを優先するSLO対応スケジューラを組み合わせた。評価では、既存の最先端手法と比べてSLO違反を大幅に減らしつつスループットも改善したことが示された。
papers.why: 複数テナントのLoRAサービングにおけるGPUリソース競合を減らす具体的なスケジューリング手法であり、オンプレミス推論基盤の設計にそのまま応用できる。
papers.summary_en: On-premise LLM servers in privacy-sensitive sectors struggle to guarantee heterogeneous SLOs when serving multiple LoRA-adapted services simultaneously, with existing frameworks suffering severe SLO violations due to LoRA layer overhead and rigid batch scheduling. HALO introduces spatial multiplexing that overlaps base and LoRA computation by partitioning GPU Streaming Multiprocessors, plus an SLO-aware scheduler that decouples request execution based on per-request slack, prioritizing urgent tasks and using idle budget for traffic shaping. Evaluation demonstrates HALO significantly mitigates resource contention, minimizing SLO violations while improving throughput compared to state-of-the-art baselines.
papers.why_en: It gives a concrete GPU-partitioning and slack-aware scheduling approach for multi-tenant LoRA serving, directly applicable to designing on-premise inference infrastructure.

papers.title: TrajLong: Co-Designing Agentic and Long-Context Supervision for Mid-Training
papers.abstract: LLM agents for coding, search, and workplace tasks increasingly rely on long-context capabilities to effectively aggregate and reason over extended interaction histories. Recent work has incorporated agent trajectories into mid-training stage, drawing on their naturally long and interaction-rich structure. Yet how to organize the information within these trajectories into effective mid-training supervision remains underexplored. In this work, we investigate the relationship between long-context and agent atomic capabilities and introduce TrajLong, a novel framework that compiles trajectories into long-context training tasks with dense supervision, targeting three representative atomic capabilities: evidence grounding, cross-evidence aggregation, and temporal state maintenance. We mid-train Qwen3-14B-Base and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base with data compiled by TrajLong, followed by supervised fine-tuning. Experiments on 6 long-context and 12 agent benchmarks demonstrate broad performance gains, with controlled ablations showing improvements over raw and masked trajectory baselines. Capability-level analyses further reveal task-dependent associations between long-context and agent atomic capabilities. These findings suggest that the shared capability demands of long-context reasoning and agent execution provide a principled basis for designing mid-training data to develop downstream agent capabilities.
papers.ja_title: エージェント軌跡から長文脈能力を育てる中間学習フレームワーク TrajLong
papers.summary: コーディングや検索などのLLMエージェントは長い対話履歴をうまく扱う長文脈能力に依存するが、エージェントの行動履歴(軌跡)をどう中間学習(mid-training)用の教師データに整理すればよいかはまだよく分かっていなかった。TrajLong は軌跡を「根拠の特定」「複数根拠の統合」「時間的な状態保持」という3つの基礎能力を狙った密な教師データに変換する手法で、Qwen3-14B-Base と Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base をこのデータで中間学習した後に指示学習(SFT)した。6 つの長文脈ベンチマークと 12 個のエージェントベンチマークで、未加工の軌跡やマスクした軌跡を使う方法より性能が向上したことが確認された。
papers.why: 長文脈推論とエージェント実行の能力を結びつけて中間学習データを設計する具体的な方法を示し、LLMの構造・学習効率を考える人に役立つ。
papers.summary_en: LLM agents for coding, search, and workplace tasks increasingly rely on long-context capabilities to reason over extended interaction histories, but how to organize agent trajectories into effective mid-training supervision remained underexplored. TrajLong compiles trajectories into long-context training tasks with dense supervision targeting three atomic capabilities—evidence grounding, cross-evidence aggregation, and temporal state maintenance—and mid-trains Qwen3-14B-Base and Qwen3-30B-A3B-Base on this data before SFT. Across 6 long-context and 12 agent benchmarks, TrajLong shows broad performance gains over raw and masked trajectory baselines in controlled ablations.
papers.why_en: It provides a concrete recipe for designing mid-training data that links long-context reasoning and agent execution capabilities, useful for anyone building training pipelines for agentic long-context behavior.

papers.title: Beyond LLM Serving: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Workloads for Embodied AI System Design
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate multimodal observations into low-level robot actions. During robot operation, each control period sets an inference deadline, and overruns leave the robot acting on stale observations, reducing task success. Meeting this deadline motivates on-device or nearby edge execution, where a single robot requires batch-1 inference outside the design point of LLM serving systems. Although VLA architectures combine familiar vision-language, autoregressive, and diffusion-style components, their runtime behavior in this batch-1 control setting remains uncharacterized. We characterize four representative VLA models on an edge GPU server and two onboard SoCs, using single-inference profiling and 43,200 closed-loop episodes. Action tensor dimensionality determines whether a stage is memory- or compute-bound, platform balance can shift that bottleneck, and GPU frequency scaling yields a platform-dependent energy-latency sweet spot. In closed-loop operation, overlapping inference with action execution creates an accuracy-speed-energy tradeoff, and no configuration is Pareto-dominant across deployment SLOs. These results guide joint design of VLA model architectures, hardware, and runtime policies.
papers.ja_title: ロボット用VLAモデルの推論特性を実機で測って明らかにする
papers.summary: ビジョン・言語・行動(VLA)モデルはロボットの各制御周期ごとに推論の締め切りがあり、遅れると古い観測で動いてしまいタスク成功率が下がるため、ロボット搭載機やエッジ機器でバッチサイズ1の推論が必要になる。本研究は4種類の代表的なVLAモデルを、エッジGPUサーバーと2種類の搭載SoC上で、単発推論の詳細測定と4万3200回のクローズドループ実験により特性を調べた。行動テンソルの次元がメモリ制約か計算制約かを決め、GPUの動作周波数調整によって速度・精度・消費電力のトレードオフに最適点があるが、どの設定もすべてのサービス品質目標(SLO)で同時に最良にはならないことが分かった。
papers.why: バッチ1でのVLA推論の実測プロファイリングは、LLMサービングの前提が通用しない組み込み・エッジ推論システムの設計指針として直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) models face a per-control-period inference deadline; overruns leave the robot acting on stale observations and reduce task success, motivating batch-1 on-device or edge inference outside the design point of LLM serving systems. The authors characterize four representative VLA models on an edge GPU server and two onboard SoCs using single-inference profiling and 43,200 closed-loop episodes, finding that action tensor dimensionality determines memory- vs compute-bound stages, platform balance can shift the bottleneck, and GPU frequency scaling yields a platform-dependent energy-latency sweet spot, with no configuration Pareto-dominant across deployment SLOs.
papers.why_en: This gives directly usable measured profiling of batch-1 VLA inference, informing hardware/runtime co-design for embodied edge systems where typical LLM serving assumptions do not hold.

papers.title: Advectra: Asymmetric Latent Transport for Non-Stationary Physics
papers.abstract: Many latent neural operators represent input and output fields in a stationary latent chart. In particular, common latent routing mechanisms use fixed or shared assignment weights for feature projection and reconstruction, limiting their ability to model transport-dominated systems where coherent structures move relative to fixed coordinate frames. We propose Advectra, a transport-aware latent operator that introduces a regularized kinematic coordinate map to decouple source and target coordinate systems. This yields an approximately co-moving latent reference frame and enables asymmetric feature aggregation and reconstruction. Combined with a geometry-aware ordering mechanism for state-space models, Advectra captures advective dynamics while maintaining stable global interactions. Advectra achieves the best performance among evaluated geometry-constrained and form-free baselines on advection-dominated benchmarks, including passive scalar transport in Navier--Stokes flows and Rayleigh--Taylor instability, while demonstrating strong generalization on real-world engineering tasks. These results highlight the benefit of explicit moving-frame structure in neural operators for non-stationary physics.

papers.title: METRO: Metric-Enhanced Token Routing Operator
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art neural operators scale to complex meshes via slice-and-process architectures, yet many rely on linear compatibility scores for latent tokenization. Under common feature normalization, such scores are equivalent to isotropic Euclidean clustering, while without normalization they induce unbounded linear decision regions. In both cases, they lack slice-specific anisotropic locality, which can lead to redundant and entangled latent slices. To address this, we propose Metric-Enhanced Token Routing Operator (METRO), a geometry-aware routing mechanism that replaces linear projection with a learnable Mahalanobis metric. By enabling each latent slice to learn a local anisotropic tensor, METRO shapes receptive fields into exponentially localized, oriented ellipsoids that naturally align with flow features like boundary layers and wakes. As a drop-in replacement, METRO yields consistent improvements across both Transformer and Mamba backbones. Empirically, our method achieves substantial performance gains on irregular domains, outperforming baselines on both standard PDE benchmarks and complex industrial design tasks. Finally, METRO exhibits enhanced robustness in out-of-distribution regimes across varying Reynolds numbers and geometric configurations.

papers.title: Verification Trap: Understanding Test-Time Selection Failures under False Premises in Code Generation
papers.abstract: Test-time compute has become a central way to improve code generation: systems sample multiple candidate programs and use verifier-visible evidence to select the final output. This paradigm implicitly assumes that the verifier provides a corrective signal independent from the generator. We challenge this assumption under misleading task premises. When the generator and verifier share a false premise, they become coupled through a mistaken belief: the generator produces premise-consistent shortcuts, while the verifier supplies evidence that fails to expose them. Consequently, the selector may choose a hidden-test-wrong candidate even when a hidden-test-correct program exists in the pool. We call this failure mode Verification Trap. Across three code-generation benchmarks and five code models, false premises consistently degrade first-sample correctness, reduce selector-chosen correctness after 64-sample test-time selection, and amplify recoverable mis-selection. Mechanistically, verifier-written tests inherit the premise-level blind spot, reshaping verifier-visible candidate space away from hidden-test correctness. These traces make Verification Trap predictable before hidden execution: a lightweight gold-free predictor using verifier-visible features reaches 0.846 AUROC. Our results identify decoupled evidence as a key mitigation axis: coupled scaling provides limited recovery, whereas premise-agnostic robustness auditors recover substantial oracle headroom.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 検証のワナ:誤った前提下でのコード生成テスト時選択の失敗
papers.summary: 生成した複数のコードから正しいものを選ぶ「検証」は、生成器(コードを作るモデル)と検証器(テストで確認するモデル)が同じ誤った前提を共有すると機能しなくなる、という問題を調べた。3 つのベンチマークと 5 つのコードモデルで、誤った前提があると 64 サンプルの候補から選んだコードの正解率が下がり、本来選べたはずの正解コードを選べない「回復可能な誤選択」が増えることを示した。さらに、検証器が見える特徴だけを使った軽量な予測器で、この失敗を実行前に AUROC 0.846 で予測できることも分かった。
papers.why: テスト時計算によるコード生成の信頼性を測る人にとって、生成器と検証器が結合して失敗する具体的な条件と、その事前検知の手がかりが分かる。
papers.summary_en: The paper studies "Verification Trap": when the generator and verifier of a test-time code-selection pipeline share the same false task premise, the verifier's test-based evidence fails to expose premise-consistent shortcuts, so the selector can pick a wrong candidate even though a hidden-test-correct one exists in the pool. Across three benchmarks and five code models, false premises consistently lower first-sample correctness and correctness after 64-sample selection, and increase recoverable mis-selection; a lightweight gold-free predictor using only verifier-visible features reaches 0.846 AUROC in anticipating this failure before hidden execution.
papers.why_en: Gives people relying on test-time selection for code generation a concrete account of when generator-verifier coupling breaks the assumed independence, plus an early-warning signal for it.

review.note: 検証器と生成器が同じ誤った前提を共有すると評価が崩れる、という評価設計の落とし穴を示す例。テスト時選択のベンチマークを作るときに前提の独立性を確認する観点になる。
review.note_en: Shows a pitfall in evaluation design: when generator and verifier share the same false premise, test-time selection benchmarks silently break the assumed independence between generation and verification.

papers.title: Robust Parameter-Efficient LLM Adaptation on Analog Hardware
papers.abstract: Analog in-memory computing is a promising platform for on-device execution of large language models because it performs matrix--vector multiplications (MVMs) in memory and in parallel, reducing data movement. However, limited digital-to-analog converter precision, input noise, and finite conductance states can degrade model accuracy, while full-model retraining to address these effects can be costly. We develop an optimizer-agnostic, parameter-efficient adaptation method based on Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), keeping the pretrained weights stored on analog arrays fixed while training the LoRA weights to adapt to downstream tasks and hardware non-idealities. Reliable adaptation requires handling errors in both forward and backward MVMs and physical weight updates. We use input reshaping to reduce input-induced MVM errors and update accumulation to retain small updates before programming them to finite-state analog devices. Across Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B with both Muon and AdamW, input reshaping improves analog LoRA fine-tuning under noisy MVM computation. Update accumulation separately preserves sub-threshold updates and substantially improves adaptation under finite-resolution programming, including configurations with as few as 20 conductance states. Additional experiments show consistent held-out negative log-likelihood improvements across noisy analog settings.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: アナログ計算ハードウェア上で頑健に LoRA 微調整する手法
papers.summary: アナログ・インメモリ計算(メモリの中で行列演算をしてデータ移動を減らす方式) で LLM を動かすと、AD/DA 変換の精度不足や雑音、有限の抵抗状態の数によって精度が落ちる。この研究は LoRA (少数パラメータだけを学習する手法) を使い、入力の整形と更新の蓄積という 2 つの工夫で、ノイズのある順伝播・逆伝播や離散的な重み更新(わずか 20 段階の抵抗状態でも) に対応できるようにした。Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct と Llama-3-8B で、Muon と AdamW 両方の最適化手法において、held-out の負対数尤度が一貫して改善することを確認した。
papers.why: アナログハードウェア上での省メモリな LLM 適応を考える人にとって、ハードウェアの不完全さを前提にした学習テクニックとして参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Analog in-memory computing can run LLM matrix-vector multiplications with reduced data movement, but limited DAC precision, input noise, and finite conductance states degrade accuracy, and retraining the full model to fix this is costly. The authors adapt LoRA with input reshaping (to cut input-induced MVM errors) and update accumulation (to preserve sub-threshold updates before programming them to finite-state devices), showing on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct and Llama-3-8B with both Muon and AdamW that these tricks improve LoRA fine-tuning under noisy MVM computation, including configurations with as few as 20 conductance states, with consistent held-out negative log-likelihood improvements.
papers.why_en: Offers hardware-aware training tricks for parameter-efficient LLM adaptation specifically tuned to analog in-memory computing's non-idealities, useful to anyone targeting such hardware for on-device LLMs.

papers.title: When Does Longer Reasoning Help? Predicting Mathematical Reasoning Through Discovery and Execution
papers.abstract: Test-time compute can improve mathematical reasoning, but can short-budget runs predict how mathematical reasoning scales with additional compute? We introduce a Discovery--Execution (DE) framework that predicts the aggregate held-out scaling curves through a convolution of strategy discovery and conditional execution. From independent short-budget attempts and oracle-sketch-conditioned runs, the framework estimates cumulative success along held-out reasoning trajectories under alternate compute allocations. We evaluate four models on 35 fresh Olympiad problems and non-geometry problems from IMO-ProofBench Advanced. Under the DE framework, near-saturated execution predicts geometric scaling, as observed for the GPT models. For Claude Opus 4.8, incorporating measured execution substantially improves held-out forecasts over geometric extrapolation across one- and two-arm allocations. As a secondary application, regularized DE (R-DE) decisions to continue or restart yield lower average regret than the best model-specific retrospective policy. Together, these results show that measuring conditional execution provides information about longer reasoning that short-budget success rates do not always capture.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 短い試行でどこまで長い推論の伸びを予測できるか
papers.summary: 数学の問題を解く LLM に計算時間(トークン数) を増やすと精度が上がるが、短い試行だけから長時間計算時の精度を予測できるかを調べた研究。発見(戦略を見つける) と実行(見つけた戦略を使い切る) を分けて測る Discovery-Execution 枠組みを作り、35 問の新作オリンピック問題などで、実行の測定を組み込むと Claude Opus 4.8 では単純な幾何級数的な予測より held-out での予測が大きく改善した。さらに続行するか打ち切るかを決める簡易版 (R-DE) は、モデルごとの最良の事後ルールより平均の後悔(regret) が小さくなった。
papers.why: テスト時計算のスケーリング予測や計算予算配分を扱う人にとって、短時間の試行から長時間の挙動を見積もる具体的な測り方の提案になる。
papers.summary_en: The paper asks whether short-budget test-time-compute runs can predict how mathematical reasoning scales with more compute, introducing a Discovery-Execution (DE) framework that separates strategy discovery from conditional execution. On 35 fresh Olympiad problems and IMO-ProofBench Advanced, near-saturated execution predicts geometric scaling for GPT models, while for Claude Opus 4.8 incorporating measured execution substantially improves held-out forecasts over geometric extrapolation; a regularized variant (R-DE) for continue/restart decisions achieves lower average regret than the best model-specific retrospective policy.
papers.why_en: Provides a concrete measurement method for estimating long-horizon test-time-compute scaling and budget-allocation decisions from short-budget trials, useful for anyone managing inference compute budgets.

papers.title: Towards Unbiased On-Policy Distillation for Block Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) has emerged as an effective post-training paradigm for language models, with recent efforts extending it to block diffusion language models (BDLMs). However, existing studies focus almost exclusively on small block sizes, leaving distillation into student models with larger blocks underexplored. In this work, we investigate this regime and reveal two critical optimization biases that induce severe training instability. First, mismatched block boundaries between teacher and student cause \textbf{\textit{context misalignment}}, providing distorted supervisory signals that misguide student decoding. Second, even under aligned contexts, an \textbf{\textit{intrinsic optimization bias}} in OPD, where the student tends to rapidly absorb high-support signals while lagging on low-support updates, drives a premature confidence surge that traps weaker students in catastrophic overconfidence collapse. To resolve these, we propose \mbox{\textbf{Un-OPD}}, an unbiased on-policy distillation framework with two novelties for stabilizing BDLM training. First, Un-OPD introduces a boundary-aware step filtering strategy that eliminates context-misaligned decoding steps. Second, Un-OPD proposes moderating optimization intensity at high-support positions via a support-rebalanced confidence calibration, thereby bypassing overconfidence collapse. Beyond stability, we also introduce a rollout reuse mechanism to reduce rollout generation overhead. Extensive experiments on math reasoning and code generation benchmarks show that Un-OPD consistently stabilizes training and delivers superior performance while reducing wall-clock training time by approximately half.
papers.ja_title: ブロック拡散言語モデルのための偏りのないオンポリシー蒸留
papers.summary: ブロック拡散言語モデル(文章を複数トークンのブロックごとに生成する拡散モデル) を、教師モデルの出力を使って蒸留(知識を移す) するオンポリシー蒸留は、ブロックが大きくなると学習が不安定になる。原因は教師と生徒でブロックの境界がずれる「文脈のずれ」と、確信度の高い部分だけを急いで吸収して過信に陥る「最適化の偏り」の 2 つだと分かった。境界のずれたステップを除く工夫と、確信度の高い位置での学習の強さを抑える工夫を組み合わせた Un-OPD を作り、数学推論とコード生成のベンチマークで学習を安定させつつ、学習時間を約半分に減らした。
papers.why: 拡散言語モデルの蒸留による後学習を安定・高速化したい人にとって、不安定化の原因の分解とその対処策が具体的に示されている。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) for block diffusion language models becomes severely unstable with larger block sizes, due to two biases: context misalignment from mismatched teacher-student block boundaries, and an intrinsic optimization bias where the student rapidly absorbs high-support signals while lagging on low-support ones, causing premature overconfidence collapse. The authors propose Un-OPD, which filters boundary-misaligned decoding steps and rebalances optimization intensity at high-support positions, plus a rollout reuse mechanism; on math reasoning and code generation benchmarks, Un-OPD stabilizes training, improves performance, and cuts wall-clock training time by roughly half.
papers.why_en: Offers a concrete diagnosis and fix for training instability in on-policy distillation of block diffusion LMs, relevant to anyone building RL/distillation post-training pipelines for diffusion-style LLMs.

papers.title: Task Vector Descent: Learning from Non-IID Batches
papers.abstract: A central challenge in continual learning is to acquire new knowledge without forgetting what the model has already learned. This challenge appears in language model training when training data comes from various domain-, user-, or task-specific distributions that are encountered unevenly over time. In such settings, successive minibatches are temporally clustered by distribution instead of being sampled i.i.d. from the overall data mixture. Training on temporally clustered data induces a stability-plasticity tradeoff. Adapting the model to the active distribution can improve the model on the active distribution but may lead to a performance degradation on data it previously trained on. We find that this tradeoff intensifies with longer exposure to the same distribution. We therefore ask if the parameter displacement produced by such a sequence (the task vector) should be fully retained or applied partially. We compare applying the full displacement ($λ=1$) with partial integration, which scales the task vector by $λ$ before applying it to the continuing model and scales the optimizer state by the same coefficient. Across continual pretraining, pretraining from random initialization, supervised post-training, and reinforcement post-training, we find that intermediate values of $λ$ often improve average continuing-model performance relative to full integration, particularly after longer same-distribution sequences. In continual-pretraining experiments with both controlled streams and naturally defined adaptation sequences, task-vector scaling outperforms full integration at the matched learning rate, showing that its benefits are not reproduced by learning-rate scaling alone.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 非 i.i.d. バッチからの継続学習:タスクベクトルを部分的にだけ適用する
papers.summary: LLM を異なる分野・ユーザー・タスクのデータで時間的にまとまったバッチ (i.i.d. でないデータ) で学習すると、今のデータに合わせるほど前に学んだことを忘れやすくなる、という安定性と柔軟性のトレードオフがある。この研究は、あるデータ列による重みの変化量 (タスクベクトル) をそのまま全部適用する (λ=1) のではなく、係数 λ で小さくスケールして適用する方法を比べた。継続事前学習・事後学習・強化学習後学習など複数の場面で、λ を中間の値にすると特に同じ分布への露出が長いときに平均性能が上がり、これは学習率を変えるだけでは再現できない効果だと分かった。
papers.why: 分布が偏ったデータ列で LLM を継続学習させる人にとって、忘却と適応のトレードオフを緩和する軽量な手段 (タスクベクトルのスケーリング) を提供する。
papers.summary_en: Continual training on temporally clustered (non-i.i.d.) batches from different domains, users, or tasks creates a stability-plasticity tradeoff that intensifies with longer exposure to one distribution. The authors compare applying the full parameter displacement from such a sequence (the task vector, λ=1) versus scaling it down by a coefficient λ before integrating it (along with optimizer state). Across continual pretraining, pretraining from scratch, supervised post-training, and RL post-training, intermediate λ values often improve average continuing-model performance versus full integration, especially after long same-distribution sequences, and this benefit is not reproduced by learning-rate scaling alone.
papers.why_en: Gives people continually training LLMs on skewed data streams a lightweight lever (task-vector scaling) to mitigate the forgetting-vs-adaptation tradeoff.

papers.title: FLEX-WAM: Flexible Block-Causal World-Action Models for Long-Horizon Imagination and Planning
papers.abstract: World--action models (WAMs) promise a unified model that predicts action-conditioned futures, generates feasible actions, and supports planning in imagination. However, existing joint video--action models often use computationally heavy, fixed-horizon backbones ill-suited to streaming inference and stable long-horizon open-loop rollouts. We introduce FLEX-WAM, a Flexible and Efficient Block-Causal World--Action Model for unified simulation and policy inference. FLEX-WAM supports variable-length contexts and non-causal prediction horizons, as well as infinite autoregressive generation frame by frame or block by block. Its block-causal, KV-cacheable architecture combines axial attention and blockwise diffusion forcing to enable efficient real-time rollout and deployment-time latency--throughput tradeoffs without retraining. Joint training can nevertheless produce plausible futures that weakly respond to commanded actions. We address this failure mode by balancing state and action flow-matching gradient contributions across the state--action diffusion-noise grid and regulating world-model sampling using Forward-Dynamics (FD) elasticity, an efficient training-time proxy for action responsiveness. Across simulated and real-world datasets, FLEX-WAM achieves superior multi-step prediction quality and latency while producing stable joint state--action rollouts for thousands of steps. As a joint action proposer and simulator within MCTS, it solves long-horizon PushT and all five OGBench Puzzle-4x4 tasks entirely in imagination. On a bimanual OpenArm-based robot, a single checkpoint jointly serves as a play policy and expected-outcome predictor, enabling real-time identification and collection of model--reality mismatches for future self-improvement.
papers.ja_title: ブロック因果な世界-行動モデルで長時間の想像と計画をする FLEX-WAM
papers.summary: 動画と行動を同時に予測する世界モデルは、固定長の重い構造のため、連続的な推論や長時間の自己回帰生成に向いていない、という問題がある。FLEX-WAM は、可変長の文脈と KV キャッシュが使えるブロック因果構造を使い、再学習なしで速度と精度のトレードオフを調整できるようにした。さらに、状態と行動それぞれの学習の勾配バランスを取り、行動への応答性を測る指標 (FD elasticity) で学習を調整することで、同時学習でも行動に反応しない「もっともらしいだけの未来予測」を防いだ。結果、PushT や OGBench Puzzle-4x4 の全 5 課題を想像内のプランニング (MCTS) だけで解き、実機の両腕ロボットでも方策と結果予測を一つのモデルで兼ねられた。
papers.why: ロボット向けの世界モデルを実時間で動かしたい人にとって、KV キャッシュ可能なブロック因果構造と、行動応答性を保つ学習工夫が参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Existing joint video-action world-action models often rely on computationally heavy, fixed-horizon backbones poorly suited to streaming inference and stable long-horizon rollouts. FLEX-WAM uses a block-causal, KV-cacheable architecture with axial attention and blockwise diffusion forcing to support variable-length contexts and tunable latency-throughput tradeoffs without retraining, and addresses the failure where jointly trained models produce plausible but action-unresponsive futures by balancing state/action flow-matching gradients and regulating sampling via a Forward-Dynamics elasticity proxy. It achieves superior multi-step prediction quality and latency, solves long-horizon PushT and all five OGBench Puzzle-4x4 tasks entirely in imagination via MCTS, and on a bimanual robot a single checkpoint serves jointly as policy and outcome predictor.
papers.why_en: Relevant to anyone deploying world models for real-time robotics, offering a KV-cacheable block-causal architecture and training tricks to keep predicted futures responsive to actions.

papers.title: RetainZ: Reclaim-Time-Aware Placement for AI Checkpoints on Zoned SSDs
papers.abstract: Solid State Drives (SSDs) are becoming the dominant medium for performance-critical storage. Zoned Namespace (ZNS) SSDs are getting more and more attractive because sequential writes and explicit zone resets reduce address-mapping, over-provisioning, and internal garbage-collection costs. However, reclaiming space requires resetting an entire zone, so deleting one file does not free its space while other files there must be kept. This erase-before-write constraint becomes a bottleneck for write-intensive workloads, particularly AI checkpointing during model training, where frequent saves of model and optimizer state compete for space with long-retained checkpoints. We observe that retention policies inherently encode when data can be retired, avoiding the need for a learned lifetime predictor. We present RetainZ, a storage backend that translates these policies into explicit reclaim epochs. Its allocator isolates long-retained data and groups objects with nearby reclaim epochs, balancing delayed space reclamation against unused space at zone ends. Evaluated on FEMU with multi-tenant streams and checkpoint manifests up to Pythia-1B, RetainZ reduces space occupied by deleted data and unused zone tails by 41.7% and mean per-input checkpoint p99 latency by 47.5% at 84% target load compared with the allocator of ZenFS, an established lifetime-aware ZNS backend, and lowers host write amplification from 1.165 to 1.003.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: Zoned SSD 向け、回収時刻を意識した AI チェックポイント配置 RetainZ
papers.summary: Zoned SSD (順次書き込みとゾーン単位の消去でゴミ集めの負荷を下げる SSD) は、1 つのファイルを消してもそのゾーンに残すべき他のファイルがあると空間を回収できない、という制約がある。モデル学習中の頻繁なチェックポイント保存は、短命なものと長期保持するものが混在するため、この制約がボトルネックになる。RetainZ は、保持期限の方針からいつ回収できるかを予測し、回収時刻が近いデータをまとめて配置するストレージ基盤で、既存の ZenFS と比べて削除済み・未使用領域を 41.7% 削減、p99 レイテンシを 47.5% 削減 (負荷 84% 時)、書き込み増幅を 1.165 から 1.003 まで下げた。
papers.why: 大規模学習基盤でチェックポイント保存の I/O を最適化したい人にとって、保持ポリシーをそのまま活用するストレージ配置の具体的な改善策になる。
papers.summary_en: Zoned Namespace (ZNS) SSDs require resetting an entire zone to reclaim space, so AI checkpointing workloads—where frequent model/optimizer saves compete for space with long-retained checkpoints—suffer from this erase-before-write constraint. RetainZ translates retention policies directly into explicit reclaim epochs, isolating long-retained data and grouping objects with nearby reclaim epochs; evaluated on FEMU with checkpoint manifests up to Pythia-1B, it reduces space occupied by deleted/unused data by 41.7%, cuts mean per-input checkpoint p99 latency by 47.5% at 84% target load versus ZenFS's allocator, and lowers host write amplification from 1.165 to 1.003.
papers.why_en: Gives people operating checkpoint-heavy training storage a concrete, policy-driven zoned-SSD placement scheme that cuts tail latency and write amplification compared to an established lifetime-aware baseline.

papers.title: Cut Binary Cross Entropy: Efficient Large-Vocabulary Loss and Gradient Kernels for Sequential Recommendation
papers.abstract: Industrial sequential recommender systems operate over massive item catalogs (e.g., 10^5--10^7 items). Multi-label recommendation models are trained with Binary Cross-Entropy (BCE) loss over the full vocabulary, but standard BCE materializes a dense [B, N, V] logits tensor in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), incurring prohibitive $O(BNV)$ memory and fatal Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors. While chunked loss optimizations exist for Softmax Cross-Entropy in LLMs, large-scale multi-label BCE optimization remains unexplored across deep learning ecosystems. We propose CutBCE, an exact, hardware-accelerated BCE loss and gradient operator implemented in JAX and Pallas for large-vocabulary workloads. CutBCE introduces (1) an exact fused reformulation evaluating dense background loss and sparse target corrections; (2) a custom Vector-Jacobian Product (VJP) with a dedicated Pallas TPU backward kernel computing logit tiles on-chip in both passes so logits and their gradients never reside in HBM; (3) dynamic VMEM budgeting and sharding-aware collective hoisting for distributed meshes; and (4) count-based zero-overhead training metrics. On single-chip TPU v5e/v6e mini-benchmarks, CutBCE eliminates OOM errors with up to 91.9% speedup. On 8-chip TPU slice training for multi-label SASRec with 876k items (Yambda-50M), CutBCE reduces peak HBM by 65.7% (>14 GiB saved per chip) and increases training speed by 225.9% with comparable accuracy. CutBCE is open-sourced at https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/RecML/blob/main/recml/core/ops/binary_cross_entropy_ops.py.
papers.ja_title: 大語彙推薦向けの BCE 損失を省メモリに計算する CutBCE カーネル
papers.summary: 10 万〜1000 万件規模の商品を扱う推薦システムでは、全語彙に対する Binary Cross-Entropy 損失を計算すると [バッチ, 系列長, 語彙] の巨大なロジット行列をメモリに展開してしまい、メモリ不足で学習が落ちる問題がある。CutBCE は JAX と Pallas で書いた専用カーネルで、疎な正解部分と密な背景部分を分けて計算し、ロジットとその勾配を一度もメモリに置かずに TPU の高速メモリ上だけで処理する。TPU 8 チップで 87 万6千件の商品を持つ SASRec を学習させると、ピークメモリを 65.7% (チップあたり 14 GiB 超) 削減し、学習速度を 225.9% 向上させつつ精度は同程度を保った。
papers.why: 大語彙を持つ推薦モデルや類似の分類ヘッドを学習する人にとって、メモリ不足を避けながら厳密な損失計算を速くする具体的なカーネル実装の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Industrial sequential recommenders with huge item catalogs (10^5-10^7 items) train with full-vocabulary Binary Cross-Entropy loss, but materializing the dense [B,N,V] logits tensor causes prohibitive O(BNV) memory use and fatal OOM errors. CutBCE is an exact, hardware-accelerated JAX/Pallas BCE kernel that fuses dense background loss with sparse target corrections and computes logit tiles on-chip during both forward and backward passes so logits and gradients never reside in HBM. On single-chip TPU v5e/v6e it eliminates OOM with up to 91.9% speedup, and on an 8-chip TPU slice training SASRec with 876k items it cuts peak HBM by 65.7% (>14 GiB per chip) and increases training speed by 225.9% with comparable accuracy.
papers.why_en: Offers a concrete kernel-engineering template for anyone training large-vocabulary classification/recommendation heads to avoid OOM while keeping exact loss computation fast.

papers.title: RESOLVE: Language-Agnostic Validation of GPU Kernels Through Testing, Reduction, and Proof
papers.abstract: AI systems can now write and optimize production GPU kernels, but validating them remains an important challenge. Evaluating the kernel on a few random inputs and checking that its outputs match a trusted reference kernel within numeric tolerances is not sufficient: races can cause nondeterministic behavior that fails to manifest in tests, and numeric tolerances can hide bugs and cause false positives even after extensive calibration. To address this challenge, we present RESOLVE, which combines testing and formal verification to build a comprehensive kernel validation pipeline. It operates in three steps: First, it tests for nondeterminism using binary instrumentation that perturbs execution timing to expose races. Second, an agent rewrites the candidate and reference kernels to obtain "reduced-concurrency" versions that are simpler to analyze but still produce bitwise-identical outputs in all tests. Third, the reduced kernels are formally analyzed in the F*/Pulse framework and prove that they perform the same computation on real numbers. This sidesteps the need for numeric tolerances. We show that RESOLVE can validate a broad selection of kernels using KernelBench, and prove equivalence across fused GEMMs in three state-of-the-art frameworks and languages: CUTLASS, Triton, and Gluon. It also analyzes mega-kernels, notoriously difficult to validate, and finds four previously unreported issues, including two clear bugs. We show that agents can use RESOLVE to repair the issues, with minimal performance impact, highlighting that agents can optimize aggressively when they can rigorously check their results.
papers.ja_title: GPU カーネルを言語に依存せず検証する手法 RESOLVE
papers.summary: AI が生成した GPU カーネルは、少数の入力で出力を照合するだけでは競合状態 (レース) による見逃しや数値誤差許容 (トレランス) によるバグの隠れが起きる。RESOLVE はまずバイナリ計装でタイミングを乱してレースを検出し、次にエージェントが並行度を落とした等価カーネルを作り、最後に F*/Pulse という形式検証の枠組みで実数上の計算が一致することを証明する。CUTLASS・Triton・Gluon の融合 GEMM で等価性を証明し、検証が難しいとされるメガカーネルから未報告の問題を 4 件 (バグ 2 件含む) 見つけた。
papers.why: カーネル生成を自動化するエージェントに、性能最適化と正しさ保証を両立させる検証基盤を与える点が新しい。
papers.summary_en: Evaluating AI-generated GPU kernels on a few test inputs with numeric tolerances can miss races and hide bugs. RESOLVE first uses binary instrumentation that perturbs timing to expose nondeterminism, then has an agent rewrite kernels into reduced-concurrency versions with bitwise-identical test outputs, and finally formally proves equivalence over real numbers in F*/Pulse, sidestepping numeric tolerances. It validates fused GEMMs across CUTLASS, Triton, and Gluon, and finds four previously unreported issues (including two clear bugs) in notoriously hard-to-validate mega-kernels.
papers.why_en: It gives kernel-generating agents a validation pipeline that lets them optimize aggressively while rigorously checking correctness, combining testing with formal proof rather than relying on numeric tolerances.

review.note: GPU カーネルは数値トレランス照合だけでなく、タイミング摂動でレースを暴いたり並行度を落として形式検証する、という正しさ検証の観点。
review.note_en: A correctness-checking perspective for GPU kernels: perturb timing to expose races and reduce concurrency for formal verification, rather than relying only on numeric-tolerance matching.

papers.title: Spend Bytes on Breadth: Precision-Count Trade-offs for Decode-Time KV Compression in Long Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
papers.abstract: Reasoning models write most of their KV cache while decoding long chains of thought (CoT), so the cache has to be compressed online under a fixed memory budget. Decode-time methods mostly decide which tokens to evict. We ask how a fixed byte budget should be split between the number of cached tokens and their precision. BreadthKV spends the bytes on more tokens at low precision, combining quantization with eviction, and picks the bit-width for each model and budget with a 60-problem end-to-end calibration, since offline attention error does not predict it reliably. On three reasoning models and four math and science benchmarks, it scores above eviction alone in 17 of 18 settings and produces shorter outputs. Much of what eviction loses comes from derailed runs, which keep reasoning until the length cap without reaching an answer. On Qwen3-8B at our tightest budget, eviction sends 91% of AIME samples to the cap and BreadthKV 40%. Under the same protocol, BreadthKV is statistically indistinguishable from a joint rate-distortion allocator (RDKV) that uses 27% more KV memory-time, and it outperforms our re-implementation of ThinKV.
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュ圧縮は「本数」より「精度」を削るべきか: BreadthKV
papers.summary: 長い思考の連鎖 (CoT) を生成する推論モデルは KV キャッシュがどんどん増えるため、決まったメモリ予算の中でトークンを捨てる (退避) だけの圧縮が使われてきた。BreadthKV はトークンを減らす代わりに低精度化 (量子化) と退避を組み合わせ、60 問での事前調整でモデルと予算ごとに最適なビット幅を選ぶ。3 つの推論モデルと 4 つの数学・科学ベンチマークで 18 設定中 17 で退避だけの手法を上回り、出力も短くなり、Qwen3-8B の最も厳しい予算では AIME で上限打ち切りになる割合が退避の 91% から 40% に減った。
papers.why: KV キャッシュの圧縮予算配分を「本数か精度か」という軸で初めて定量評価し、量子化と退避を組み合わせる実用的な指針を示した点が新しい。
papers.summary_en: Reasoning models write most of their KV cache while decoding long chains of thought, and decode-time compression under a fixed byte budget has mostly focused on which tokens to evict. BreadthKV instead spends bytes on more tokens at lower precision, combining quantization with eviction, choosing bit-width per model/budget via a 60-problem calibration since offline attention error doesn't predict it reliably. Across three reasoning models and four benchmarks it beats eviction alone in 17 of 18 settings with shorter outputs, and on Qwen3-8B at the tightest budget it cuts the fraction of AIME runs hitting the length cap from 91% (eviction) to 40%.
papers.why_en: It is the first to frame the KV-cache compression budget as a count-vs-precision trade-off and shows a practical recipe combining quantization with eviction that beats eviction-only and nearly matches a more memory-hungry joint allocator.

papers.title: CIPHER-MoE: Balancing Efficiency and Routing Fidelity in Trillion-Scale MoE Training
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) has been widely adopted in recent large language model (LLM) architectures. However, scaling up MoE in LLM training introduces system-level challenges on training, where non-uniform token routing can lead to highly imbalanced workloads across experts and devices, further destabilizing the training process. With trillion-scale LLMs, imbalanced expert workloads further amplify the resource cost of MoE training, resulting in degraded training efficiency and hardware utilization for underloaded experts, while hot experts require additional resources to accommodate excessive workloads. Recent studies address imbalanced MoE training through intricate parallelism strategies or resource reallocation. However, these system-level approaches often introduce additional resource requirements and considerable orchestration complexity, which become increasingly difficult to afford when training trillion-parameter LLMs under constrained computational resources. This work introduces CIPHER-MoE, which mitigates MoE workload imbalance while keeping the router's token-side Top-K selection unchanged. CIPHER-MoE applies affinity-aware Expert-to-Token filtering with explicit capacity control to reduce hotspot expert workloads without additional hardware resources or complex runtime design. The proposed method has been evaluated on large-scale MoE models, including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, showing up to 64.9 percentage points Top-1 expert workload reduction and 1.10$\times$-1.94$\times$ training acceleration, while preserving the training quality. The source code will be released soon.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: トップ K を変えずに MoE の負荷偏りを抑える CIPHER-MoE
papers.summary: 大規模な Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) モデルの学習では、トークンの振り分け先 (ルーティング) が偏ると一部の専門家 (エキスパート) だけ負荷が過大になり、学習効率が落ちる。CIPHER-MoE はルーターのトップ K 選択自体は変えず、相性を考慮したエキスパート側のフィルタリングと容量制限で過負荷を抑える。DeepSeek-V4-Pro 級のモデルで検証し、トップ 1 エキスパートの負荷を最大 64.9 ポイント減らし、学習速度を 1.10〜1.94 倍にしながら学習品質を保った。
papers.why: 複雑な並列化戦略や資源再配置をせずに MoE の負荷偏りを解消できる軽量な手法で、兆パラメータ級の学習にそのまま適用できる点が実用的。
papers.summary_en: In large Mixture-of-Experts training, non-uniform token routing creates hotspot experts whose imbalanced workload degrades training efficiency, and trillion-scale models amplify this cost. CIPHER-MoE keeps the router's token-side Top-K selection unchanged but applies affinity-aware expert-to-token filtering with explicit capacity control to curb hotspot load without extra hardware or complex runtime orchestration. Evaluated on large-scale models including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, it cuts Top-1 expert workload by up to 64.9 percentage points and accelerates training by 1.10x-1.94x while preserving training quality.
papers.why_en: It offers a lightweight fix for MoE load imbalance that avoids intricate parallelism redesign or resource reallocation, making it directly applicable to trillion-parameter-scale training.

papers.title: Request Order Matters: Cache-History Sensitivity in Selective KV-Cache Reuse for Rolling Agents
papers.abstract: Long-running agents repeatedly call an LLM while retaining most of their document window, evicting old documents, and appending new ones. These rolling updates break exact prefix caching and motivate non-prefix KV-cache reuse with selective recomputation. We show that persistent KV-cache reuse with selective recomputation can be history-dependent: in our rolling-agent workload, an unchanged prompt can produce different answers depending on the requests processed before it. At a matched 5% recomputation budget, document-aligned recomputation reduces answer variation across request orders from 69.0% with CacheBlend's token top-$k$ policy to 26.1%. When each prompt is evaluated after a different sequence of preceding requests, document-aligned recomputation improves fidelity to full prefill by 34.5-52.5 percentage points over token top-$k$, while both policies achieve approximately 5.7$\times$ median TTFT speedup. Our ablation study shows that, in our rolling-agent workload, contiguity is the main factor associated with robust selective recomputation.
papers.ja_title: リクエストの順番で答えが変わる? ローリングエージェントの KV キャッシュ再利用
papers.summary: 長時間動くエージェントは古い文書を捨てて新しい文書を追加しながら LLM を何度も呼ぶため、完全一致の前方キャッシュ (プレフィックスキャッシュ) が使えず、一部だけ再計算する選択的な KV キャッシュ再利用が使われる。本研究は、同じプロンプトでも直前にどんな処理をしたかで答えが変わってしまう「履歴依存」が起きることを示した。再計算予算を 5% に固定した場合、文書単位でまとめて再計算する方式は、既存の CacheBlend のトークン単位 top-k 方式に比べ、リクエスト順序による答えの揺れを 69.0% から 26.1% に減らし、完全再計算への忠実度も 34.5〜52.5 ポイント改善し、どちらの方式も初回応答時間 (TTFT) を約 5.7 倍高速化した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュ再利用の評価では通常の単発プロンプトテストだけでは不十分で、処理順序を変えた再現性テストが必要だという、ベンチマーク設計上の落とし穴を明らかにした。
papers.summary_en: Long-running agents call an LLM repeatedly while evicting old documents and appending new ones, breaking exact prefix caching and motivating selective, non-prefix KV-cache reuse with partial recomputation. This work shows such reuse can be history-dependent: an unchanged prompt can produce different answers depending on the requests processed before it. At a matched 5% recomputation budget, document-aligned recomputation reduces answer variation across request orders from 69.0% (CacheBlend's token top-k) to 26.1%, improves fidelity to full prefill by 34.5-52.5 percentage points, while both approaches give roughly 5.7x median TTFT speedup.
papers.why_en: It exposes a benchmarking pitfall for selective KV-cache reuse: single-prompt evaluations miss history-dependent errors, so order-varied reproducibility testing is needed to judge such systems fairly.

review.note: KV キャッシュ再利用の評価は単発プロンプトだけでは不十分で、処理順序を変えて再現性を確かめる必要がある、という評価設計の落とし穴の指摘。
review.note_en: A measurement pitfall: evaluating selective KV-cache reuse with single prompts misses history-dependent errors; order-varied reproducibility testing is needed.

papers.title: Off-Policy Merging Beats On-Policy Self-Distillation for Continual Learning
papers.abstract: A long-standing goal of AI is a model that can continually learn and improve itself. On post-trained models, supervised finetuning (SFT) on new data often causes poor generalization and catastrophic forgetting. As such, the conventional wisdom is that on-policy training is a prerequisite for continual learning. In practice, however, data containing new knowledge or capabilities are often off-policy. While methods such as on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) try to bridge this gap by converting off-policy data into on-policy signal, they have been shown to cause reasoning collapse. In this paper, we show that off-policy merging beats OPSD for continual learning. We first show that SFT learns a useful signal from new data, but naively applying its update interferes with existing capabilities. We reduce this interference with a simple recipe we term grafting, which changes where the update is learned and how it is applied: (1) learning the update on an earlier donor checkpoint, ideally even before the end of pretraining, and applying the weight update to the post-trained model; (2) scaling the weight update, equivalent to a form of model merging; and (3) optionally, masking the most sensitive update directions when the new data distribution is far from the post-trained model. Across continual learning settings including (1) distilling from expert traces, (2) self-improvement with STaR and Pedagogical RL, and (3) injecting knowledge after pretraining cutoff, grafting Pareto-dominates both SFT and OPSD in new-task and old-task performance, while avoiding expensive on-policy sampling. Therefore, our work challenges on-policy training as a necessity for continual learning on RL-trained models.
papers.ja_title: 継続学習には「オンポリシー」でなくモデル統合 (グラフティング) が効く
papers.summary: 事後学習済みモデルに新しい知識を教師あり微調整 (SFT) すると、既存の能力を忘れてしまう (破滅的忘却) ことが多く、オンポリシー学習が継続学習には必須だとされてきた。本研究は、オフポリシーなデータから学んだ更新を、事後学習前の初期チェックポイントに学習させてから強さを調整して重みに加える「グラフティング」という手法を示した。専門家の軌跡からの蒸留、自己改善 (STaR やペダゴジカル RL)、事前学習後の知識注入などの設定で、グラフティングは SFT やオンポリシー自己蒸留 (OPSD) よりも新旧タスクの両方で優れ、高コストなオンポリシーサンプリングも不要にした。
papers.why: 「継続学習にはオンポリシー学習が必要」という前提に反例を示し、安価なオフポリシー手法でも忘却を避けられることを実証した点が重要。
papers.summary_en: Supervised finetuning (SFT) on new data for post-trained models often causes catastrophic forgetting, leading to the conventional wisdom that on-policy training is a prerequisite for continual learning. This paper introduces "grafting": learning the update on an earlier (even pre-pretraining-cutoff) donor checkpoint, scaling the weight update like a form of model merging, and optionally masking sensitive directions. Across distillation from expert traces, self-improvement (STaR, Pedagogical RL), and post-cutoff knowledge injection, grafting Pareto-dominates both SFT and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) on new- and old-task performance while avoiding expensive on-policy sampling.
papers.why_en: It challenges the assumption that on-policy training is necessary for continual learning on RL-trained models, showing a cheap off-policy merging recipe avoids forgetting better than existing on-policy distillation.

papers.title: MiniCorp: The Last Mile to an AI Agent Corporation
papers.abstract: The last mile toward enterprise AGI is a company that runs itself. Training and adapting such agents require longitudinal enterprise data, which remain scarce, costly to acquire, and often restricted by privacy constraints. Historical archives are also frequently incomplete and record only what actually happened. They cannot show the outcomes of alternative decisions. We introduce MiniCorp, an office simulator for studying how agents can collectively run a company while generating enterprise data at scale. Using an e-commerce company as a demonstration, MiniCorp connects two interacting worlds. The external world models customers, dynamic competitors, and market mechanisms. The internal world consists of agents that observe events, discuss their options, and make strategic decisions. These decisions have lasting effects on the market, and the resulting feedback informs the firm's later decisions. As the firm and market interact, MiniCorp continuously records the agents' communications and decisions. These records preserve the information available at the time and the business results that followed. Checkpointing allows the same situation to be replayed under different decisions, providing comparisons unavailable in static archives. We evaluate end-to-end fidelity against patterns reported in empirical studies of real markets. These evaluations provide agents with realistic market feedback and reduce the risk that they learn to exploit flaws in the simulator. Our experiments show agents coordinating across roles and adapting their decisions to market feedback. With explicit long-term strategic guidance, they also sustain advertising exploration despite weak early returns. MiniCorp thus provides an environment for studying AI-run companies and a scalable source of longitudinal and counterfactual enterprise data for agent training and evaluation.

papers.title: The Arbitrary-Placement Problem in Entropy-Minimizing Selection, and a Residual-Entropy Formulation
papers.abstract: Entropy-based selection objectives suffer from a fundamental degeneracy: minimizing Shannon entropy $H(p_A)$ rewards confident selection regardless of whether the selected candidate is informative. We address this limitation with the residual entropy $D = H(p_A) - H(p_β)$, where $p_β$ is induced by candidate trust weights. We prove the exact identity $D = -\mathrm{KL}(p_A\Vert p_β) - Δ$, where $Δ$ measures whether the score-induced distribution and trust profile favor the same candidates. Boundary cases establish basic safety: under uniform trust, $D\leq0$ automatically, so an equal-trust, non-starving state is never penalized, while at any one-hot limit, $D\to0$ regardless of the selected candidate. For the intermediate regime where selection occurs, we prove that $D\leq0$ when candidate ordering by trust agrees pairwise with ordering by informativeness, and derive a tighter certificate based on the leading candidate's margin over its competitors. These results are independent of the candidate-scoring function and apply to both stationary and dynamically changing information. Experiments with a gradient-based mixture-of-experts router confirm that the ordering conditions can hold during real optimization and show that correct ordering improves downstream performance when candidates are non-interchangeable and selections are used directly rather than averaged. Beyond routing, margin-based reweighting matches or outperforms fixed-strength baselines in a class-imbalance task, while informative selection in a production video-prediction system reduces MSE by approximately 20$\%$ and transfers to a related species. Residual entropy, therefore, provides a safety criterion for selection and a usable signal for deciding when that selection is informative.
papers.ja_title: 「自信がある」だけでは不十分: 選択の情報量を測る残余エントロピー
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts のルーティングなどで使われる「エントロピー最小化」という選択基準は、選んだ候補が実際に有用かどうかに関係なく自信ありげな選択を褒めてしまう欠陥がある。本研究は、候補への信頼度から導く分布とのエントロピー差である「残余エントロピー」を提案し、これが選択の情報量を測る安全な指標になることを数学的に証明した。勾配ベースの MoE ルーター、クラス不均衡タスク、実運用の映像予測システムの実験で、情報量に基づく選択は映像予測の平均二乗誤差 (MSE) を約 20% 削減し、別の種にも転用できた。
papers.why: ルーティングや選択の目的関数設計において、単なる自信度ではなく情報量を測る理論的基盤を与え、実運用システムでの改善効果も確認した点が新しい。
papers.summary_en: Entropy-based selection objectives have a fundamental degeneracy: minimizing Shannon entropy rewards confident selection regardless of whether the chosen candidate is actually informative. The paper proposes residual entropy D = H(p_A) - H(p_β), proves it equals -KL(p_A||p_β) - Delta, and establishes boundary-case safety and ordering conditions under which D<=0. Experiments with a gradient-based MoE router, a class-imbalance task, and a production video-prediction system show informative selection reduces MSE by approximately 20% and transfers to a related species.
papers.why_en: It gives a theoretical, scoring-function-independent safety criterion for when a confident selection is actually informative, with a demonstrated ~20% MSE reduction in a production video-prediction system, relevant to MoE routing objective design.

papers.title: ThunderSyncRL: Lossless Acceleration of Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Language models are moving beyond generating answers to pursuing long-horizon goals in interactive environments. Post-training these agents requires long, heterogeneous trajectories, and synchronous systems leave learner engines idle until rollout and verification finish. To squeeze out these pipeline bubbles, asynchronous training overlaps rollout and learning across updates, but comes at the cost of policy staleness. We introduce ThunderSyncRL, which starts gradient computation as soon as all required inputs are fixed, without policy staleness. For group relative policy optimization (GRPO), ThunderSyncRL computes each trajectory's score gradient as soon as the reward for that trajectory arrives, without waiting for the group. For on-policy distillation (OPD), it computes gradients for each completed agentic turn's teacher-scored actions while tool calls run in the sandbox. We prove that gradient streaming produces the same GRPO and OPD updates as batch-synchronous training, without changing either objective. On SWE-bench Verified and Terminal Bench 4.0, we train models to the same performance up to $1.9 \times$ faster than synchronous training. With zero policy staleness, ThunderSyncRL also outperforms asynchronous training at a fixed budget by up to $2.47$ percentage points.
papers.ja_title: 停滞ゼロで非同期化する強化学習パイプライン ThunderSyncRL
papers.summary: 長期的な目標を追うエージェントの強化学習では、ロールアウトと検証が終わるまで学習エンジンが待たされる「パイプラインの泡 (バブル)」が発生し、非同期化すると方針の古さ (ステイルネス) という代償が生じる。ThunderSyncRL は GRPO では各軌跡の報酬が届いた時点でその勾配計算を始め、OPD ではツールがサンドボックスで動いている間にも完了したターンの勾配を計算することで、方針の古さを一切出さずに待ち時間をなくす。数学的に同期学習と同じ更新になることを証明し、SWE-bench Verified と Terminal Bench 4.0 で同期学習より最大 1.9 倍速く同じ性能に到達し、同じ予算では非同期学習より最大 2.47 ポイント上回った。
papers.why: 方針の古さを生まずにロールアウトと学習を重ねるという、非同期 RL の速度と正確さを両立する新しい実装方式を示した点が重要。
papers.summary_en: In agentic reinforcement learning, synchronous training leaves learner engines idle until rollout and verification finish, while asynchronous overlap incurs policy staleness. ThunderSyncRL starts gradient computation as soon as required inputs are fixed—per-trajectory for GRPO as rewards arrive, and per completed agentic turn for on-policy distillation while tool calls run in the sandbox—provably producing the same updates as batch-synchronous training. On SWE-bench Verified and Terminal Bench 4.0 it reaches the same performance up to 1.9x faster than synchronous training, and outperforms asynchronous training at a fixed budget by up to 2.47 percentage points.
