papers.why_en: It presents a gradient-streaming implementation that removes pipeline bubbles without introducing any policy staleness, provably matching synchronous updates while beating both synchronous and asynchronous RL training in speed/quality trade-off.

papers.title: Transfer-Stratified On-Policy Distillation for RL-Improved Reasoning Teachers
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning can substantially improve a reasoning teacher, but it is unclear which of those improvements survive when the teacher supervises a smaller on-policy student. We study this question in mathematical reasoning by comparing teacher lineages before and after GRPO, multiple student scales, direct GRPO, and several on-policy distillation objectives. The central finding is that transfer is structured rather than scalar: teacher strength alone does not make dense distillation competitive, while an RL-improved teacher creates useful but metric-dependent student gains. This motivates Transfer-Stratified On-Policy Distillation (TS-OPD), which screens training problems by the joint sampled success of the student and teacher, routes acquisition problems to gated forward KL, routes consolidation problems to gated reverse KL, and adds an entropy brake to protect sampled coverage. Across the main comparison, TS-OPD is the strongest student objective for macro average correctness with the GRPO-improved teacher, while pass@K remains more mixed. Ablations show that the gains come from routing and token gating rather than skipping problems. These results support a transfer-aware view of OPD: stronger teachers help when the supervision direction and token budget match the student's observed ability, not merely because the teacher endpoint is stronger.
papers.ja_title: RL で強くした教師モデルの知識は生徒モデルにどう伝わるか: TS-OPD
papers.summary: 強い教師モデル(先生モデル)を強化学習 (RL) でさらに強くしても、そのまま弱い生徒モデル(学生モデル)への蒸留(知識の移し替え)がうまくいくとは限らない、という問題を数学推論で調べた。研究チームは生徒と教師が両方正解できる問題を選び、新しく学ぶ問題には前方向の KL ダイバージェンス(確率分布の差)を、定着させる問題には逆方向をかける Transfer-Stratified On-Policy Distillation (TS-OPD) を提案した。RL で改善した教師を使った場合、TS-OPD は平均正解率で最も強い生徒向け学習目的になったが、pass@K(複数回のうち正解を含む割合)では結果が混在した。
papers.why: RL 後の教師から生徒への知識蒸留で、教師の強さだけでなく「どの問題をどちらの KL 方向で学ばせるか」を選ぶ設計指針を示している。
papers.summary_en: The paper studies whether RL-driven improvements in a reasoning teacher transfer when that teacher supervises a smaller on-policy student, finding transfer is "structured rather than scalar." The authors propose Transfer-Stratified On-Policy Distillation (TS-OPD), which screens problems by joint teacher-student success, routes acquisition problems to gated forward KL and consolidation problems to gated reverse KL, with an entropy brake. TS-OPD is the strongest student objective for macro average correctness with the GRPO-improved teacher, while pass@K results remain more mixed.
papers.why_en: It gives a transfer-aware recipe for distilling an RL-improved teacher into a student, showing routing and token gating—not teacher strength alone—drive the gains, directly usable for RL post-training pipelines.

papers.title: StagQ: Constraint-Driven Multi-Precision Weight Quantization for LLMs
papers.abstract: Serving a large language model (LLM) across a fleet of deployments requires several weight-precision operating points. Multi-precision formats serve them all from one stream whose prefixes are valid lower-precision codes, instead of storing multiple copies. We present StagQ, a multi-precision weight format whose main stream is a 2-bit group-wise affine base followed by a configurable number of 1-bit refinement planes on a dyadic step schedule. Every supported precision is a readable prefix, decoded by an affine map derived from metadata shared across all precisions, with no per-weight lookup. A sparse side record, filled both before and after the grid is fitted, holds out the few weights the grid serves worst. We report two configurations of the encoder. At two bits the cheaper one leads the strongest multi-precision baseline on Llama-3.1-8B, Phi-4, and OLMo-2-7B by 3.1 to 7.0 MMLU points, at a slightly lower logical rate. At three bits it leads on Llama-3.1-8B, leads on Phi-4 at a higher rate, and ties on OLMo-2-7B. At four bits it ties on all three, at a higher rate. In a batch-one matrix-vector product on an NVIDIA A100 GPU, timed on synthetic weights, our kernel is faster than the two baseline kernels in most shape-precision cases.
papers.ja_title: 1 本のデータで複数精度を配れる LLM 重み量子化フォーマット StagQ
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデル (LLM) を複数の精度 (ビット数) で配布するには、これまで精度ごとに別の重みファイルを用意する必要があった。StagQ は 2 ビットの基本データに 1 ビット単位の追加データを重ねることで、先頭部分を読むだけで低精度版にもなる多精度フォーマットを実現した。2 ビット設定では Llama-3.1-8B・Phi-4・OLMo-2-7B で既存最強手法より MMLU (知識問題のテスト) が 3.1〜7.0 ポイント向上し、A100 GPU 上の行列ベクトル積でも大半の形状・精度で既存カーネルより速かった。
papers.why: 1 つのストリームから複数精度を取り出せるため、複数精度でモデルを配布・提供する推論基盤の重複保存やカーネル実装を簡略化できる実用的な量子化フォーマットを示している。
papers.summary_en: Serving an LLM at multiple weight precisions normally requires storing a separate copy per precision; StagQ instead builds one stream with a 2-bit group-wise affine base plus configurable 1-bit refinement planes, where every supported precision is a readable, decodable prefix. The cheaper 2-bit configuration beats the strongest multi-precision baseline by 3.1-7.0 MMLU points on Llama-3.1-8B, Phi-4, and OLMo-2-7B at a slightly lower rate, and its batch-one matrix-vector kernel on an A100 GPU is faster than both baseline kernels in most shape-precision cases.
papers.why_en: It offers a practical multi-precision weight format and kernel letting a serving fleet derive many precisions from one stored stream, reducing duplication and kernel complexity for low-precision inference infrastructure.

papers.title: D-Loop: Looped Diffusion Drafting for Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Block diffusion accelerates speculative decoding by drafting multiple tokens in one forward pass. However, each position predicts a marginal distribution without observing earlier proposed tokens, limiting draft quality and acceptance length. We identify a concrete failure, the \emph{repetition trap}, in which neighboring positions produce redundant copies of the same token. We explain this tendency theoretically and empirically examine its association with shorter accepted drafts. Recent methods refine marginal predictions with an additional causal head or a separately trained drafter, increasing parameter storage and introducing separate training objectives. We instead propose D-Loop, which introduces \emph{intra-block causal conditioning} within the original diffusion drafter without additional model components. Inspired by semi-autoregressive generation and parameter sharing, D-Loop reuses the same backbone across looped passes. The first pass proposes a block, and the second conditions on a selected prefix to regenerate the suffix in parallel. A complementary prefix--suffix objective trains the shared drafter for both anchor-only prefix prediction and prefix-conditioned suffix prediction. Across eight math, code, and chat benchmarks, D-Loop can beat DFlash and DSpark on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with obvious gains.
papers.ja_title: 拡散モデル投機的デコーディングの「同じトークンを繰り返す罠」を直す D-Loop
papers.summary: 投機的デコーディング(先に候補トークンをまとめて作り後で確認する高速化手法)でブロック拡散モデルを使うと、隣接する位置が同じトークンを繰り返す「repetition trap」という失敗が起き、採用される長さが短くなる問題がある。D-Loop は追加のモデル部品を増やさず、同じ拡散モデルを 2 回ループさせ、1 回目で作った接頭部分を条件にして 2 回目で残りを並列に作り直す手法を提案した。数学・コード・対話の 8 個のベンチマークで、Qwen3-4B と Qwen3-8B の両方で既存手法 DFlash・DSpark を明確に上回った。
papers.why: 追加パラメータなしでドラフト品質を改善する投機的デコーディングの設計手法として、推論サービングの高速化に直接応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Block-diffusion speculative decoding drafts several tokens per forward pass but suffers from a "repetition trap," where neighboring positions collapse into redundant copies, shortening accepted draft length. D-Loop adds intra-block causal conditioning by looping the same diffusion drafter twice—proposing a block, then regenerating the suffix conditioned on a selected prefix—without extra model components, trained with a complementary prefix-suffix objective. Across eight math, code, and chat benchmarks, D-Loop can beat DFlash and DSpark on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with obvious gains.
papers.why_en: It shows a parameter-free way to fix a concrete drafting failure mode in diffusion-based speculative decoding, directly useful for speeding up LLM serving.

papers.title: Flash-OPD: Fast On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories, but generating and evaluating long rollouts incurs substantial training cost. Existing acceleration methods reduce this cost through open-loop rollout schedules or closed-loop horizon adaptation. However, supervision compatibility can vary substantially across trajectories, making a single rollout horizon difficult to match their heterogeneous reliable lengths: an overly short horizon may truncate useful supervision, while an overly long one wastes computation beyond reliable regions. Our key insight is that the trajectory-specific reliability boundary need not be predicted before generation. By viewing reliability as the first-passage of accumulated low teacher--student compatibility events, the boundary is inherently unknown before sampling, yet whether it has been reached can be determined exactly from the observed prefix. Building on this insight, we propose *Flash-OPD*, which shifts from rollout-horizon control to adaptive trajectory-level boundary verification. *Flash-OPD* interleaves cached generation with teacher verification and independently stops each trajectory according to its observed compatibility events. To reduce verification overhead, the recent event rate is used only to schedule the next verification point, while the actual stopping decision always relies on the exact cumulative count. This separation prevents estimation errors from causing premature termination while enabling efficient verification during generation. Extensive experiments across diverse datasets and teacher--student settings show that *Flash-OPD* achieves $2.2\times$--$7.5\times$ speedups over standard OPD while maintaining or improving accuracy.
papers.ja_title: ロールアウトを個別に見極めて止める Flash-OPD で蒸留を高速化
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留(生徒が自分で作った文章に教師が指導を与える学習法)は、長いロールアウト(生成と評価)に時間がかかるのが問題だった。Flash-OPD は、どこまで教師の指導が信頼できるかを事前に予測せず、生成しながら教師と生徒の一致度を観察して各ロールアウトごとに個別に打ち切るタイミングを決める手法を提案した。多様なデータセットと教師・生徒の組み合わせで、標準的なオンポリシー蒸留に比べて 2.2〜7.5 倍の高速化を精度を保ったまま達成した。
papers.why: RL 後学習で計算コストの大きいロールアウト生成を精度を落とさず大幅に短縮する実装上の工夫として、学習基盤の効率化に直結する。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) gives dense teacher supervision on student-generated rollouts, but long rollouts are costly to generate and evaluate. Flash-OPD reframes this as adaptive trajectory-level boundary verification: it interleaves cached generation with teacher verification and stops each trajectory independently based on observed teacher-student compatibility events rather than a predicted horizon. Across diverse datasets and teacher-student settings, Flash-OPD achieves 2.2x-7.5x speedups over standard OPD while maintaining or improving accuracy.
papers.why_en: It offers a concrete way to cut the dominant rollout cost of on-policy distillation without sacrificing accuracy, directly relevant to making RL post-training pipelines cheaper.

papers.title: ORCA: The Annealed Spectral Conditioning Optimizer for Faster, Better LLM Training
papers.abstract: Modern LLM optimizers such as Muon often produce weight matrices with higher effective rank than Adam, yet further spectral control has delivered only modest gains. We identify a tension behind this result: concentrated spectra can suppress gradient directions in coupled weight matrices and slow optimization, while constraints maintained throughout training can limit task-specific adaptation and raise the attainable loss floor. We introduce ORCA (Orthogonal Regularization, Cooled After), a minimal optimizer intervention that applies strong but temporary soft orthogonality regularization early in training, then removes it. This allows the weights to benefit from a broader spectrum early on and adapt freely afterward. Across LLaMA, Qwen3, and fine-grained mixture-of-experts models ranging from 130M to 8B parameters, ORCA achieves lower final validation loss than Muon. Its loss reduction relative to Muon matches or exceeds Muon's reduction relative to Adam. Ablations support the early-shaping, later-release design. Further, ORCA requires no architectural changes and adds minimal overhead.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 最初だけ直交化して後で外す最適化手法 ORCA
papers.summary: Muon など最近の最適化手法は Adam より重み行列の有効ランク(情報の広がり)を高くするが、それ以上スペクトル(行列の形)を制御しても効果は小さかった。ORCA は学習の初期だけ強い直交性の正則化(行列の形をそろえる仕組み)をかけ、その後取り除くという単純な工夫で、重みが最初は広いスペクトルから利益を得て後で自由に適応できるようにした。130M から 8B パラメータの LLaMA・Qwen3・混合専門家 (MoE) モデルで、ORCA は Muon より最終的な検証損失が低く、その改善幅は Muon が Adam に対して出した改善幅と同等以上だった。
papers.why: 学習の初期だけ制約をかけるという設計で、アーキテクチャ変更やオーバーヘッドをほぼ増やさずに大規模 LLM 学習の最終性能を上げる実用的な最適化手法を示している。
papers.summary_en: Optimizers like Muon raise the effective rank of weight matrices relative to Adam, but further spectral control has so far given only modest gains. ORCA (Orthogonal Regularization, Cooled After) applies strong soft orthogonality regularization only early in training, then removes it, letting weights exploit a broad spectrum early and adapt freely later. Across LLaMA, Qwen3, and fine-grained MoE models from 130M to 8B parameters, ORCA reaches lower final validation loss than Muon, with its improvement over Muon matching or exceeding Muon's improvement over Adam, while adding no architectural change and minimal overhead.
papers.why_en: It gives a minimal, time-limited optimizer intervention that measurably lowers final training loss for large LLMs without architecture changes, a low-cost lever for training-efficiency work.

papers.title: SO(3)-RoPE for Spherical Transformers
papers.abstract: Spherical data arise in many scientific applications. Often spherical transformers disregard the geometry of the underlying spherical domain, causing distortions and coordinate singularities near the poles. We introduce SO(3)-RoPE, a relative positional embedding that incorporates spherical geometry into transformer attention through unitary SO(3) representations. Our formulation is SO(3)-equivariant and compatible with FlashAttention, retaining efficiency of vanilla transformers. On shallow water dynamics prediction over a rotating sphere, our SO3ViT outperforms an S2Transformer baseline with lower errors and reduced runtime.

papers.title: CentriQ: Calibration-Free Quantization of Diffusion Transformers via Exact Mean Centering
papers.abstract: Diffusion transformers (DiTs) achieve state-of-the-art image generation, but their sampling cost limits deployment. Quantizing both weights and activations to 4 bits reduces this cost, yet existing methods fall short in one of two ways. Calibration-based methods are tied to a specific checkpoint and prompt distribution, whereas data-free Hadamard rotation, effective for LLMs, loses quality on DiTs. We show that this loss has a structural cause. Adaptive layer-norm conditioning adds a per-token mean to the activations, and at the widths of the evaluated DiTs, the Hadamard rotations used by data-free methods cannot spread this mean uniformly across coordinates. A single dominant direction therefore survives the rotation and sets the quantization range. We introduce CentriQ, a calibration-free quantizer that centers each token before rotation and restores the mean exactly through a rank-1 full-precision branch, so that per-token scales follow in closed form without data. Weights are fitted under a robust $\ell_p$ objective that tracks the dense mode of each group and discounts heavy tails. Across three DiTs, CentriQ matches the quality of calibrated SVDQuant at 4 bits, whereas calibration-free weight quantizers with plain per-token activation quantization collapse or degrade substantially. CentriQ outperforms the strongest calibration-free method reported to date at 2-bit weights. It is also the first calibration-free method to retain usable image quality at 2-bit activations.
papers.ja_title: データなしで拡散トランスフォーマーを低ビット量子化する CentriQ
papers.summary: 画像生成を担う拡散トランスフォーマー (DiT) を重みと活性化の両方を 4 ビットに量子化すると生成コストを下げられるが、キャリブレーション(事前データでの調整)が必要な手法はチェックポイントやプロンプトに縛られ、キャリブレーション不要な Hadamard 回転は DiT では品質が落ちる問題があった。CentriQ はトークンごとの平均を回転前に取り除き、ランク 1 の高精度な補正枝で平均を正確に戻すことで、データなしでもトークンごとの量子化範囲を求められるようにした。3 種類の DiT で CentriQ は 4 ビットでキャリブレーション付き手法 SVDQuant と同等の品質を達成し、2 ビット重みでは従来最強のキャリブレーション不要手法を上回り、2 ビット活性化でも使える画質を保てた初めての手法となった。
papers.why: キャリブレーションデータなしで拡散モデルを低ビット量子化できる手法を示し、推論サービングでの前処理不要な量子化パイプラインの設計に役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Quantizing diffusion transformers (DiTs) to 4-bit weights and activations cuts sampling cost, but calibration-based methods are tied to a specific checkpoint/prompt distribution while calibration-free Hadamard rotation loses quality on DiTs because adaptive layer-norm conditioning injects a per-token mean the rotation cannot spread uniformly. CentriQ centers each token before rotation and restores the mean exactly via a rank-1 full-precision branch, deriving per-token scales in closed form without any data, plus a robust l_p weight-fitting objective. Across three DiTs, CentriQ matches calibrated SVDQuant at 4 bits, outperforms the strongest prior calibration-free method at 2-bit weights, and is the first calibration-free method to retain usable image quality at 2-bit activations.
papers.why_en: It provides a data-free quantization recipe for diffusion transformers that reaches calibration-level quality, useful for building calibration-free low-precision inference pipelines.

papers.title: Evolving in Thought Space: Training a Small Model at Test Time Unlocks Better Discoveries
papers.abstract: Open-ended scientific discovery often requires repeatedly proposing and evaluating candidate solutions. LLM-based systems can support this process by generating and refining executable solutions from verifier feedback. Methods such as TTT-Discover use test-time training (TTT) to update the solution-generating LLM from verifier feedback, adapting its generation policy to improve subsequent proposals on the target problem. However, this becomes expensive when reliable execution requires a large model, since training must maintain gradients, optimizer states, and policy statistics while repeatedly generating long, structured outputs. It also complicates credit assignment: outcome-level verifier feedback must jointly evaluate the high-level strategy and its low-level implementation. In this work, we introduce Guidance-TTT, which separates these roles. A compact guidance model is trained at test time to propose high-level strategic changes, while a frozen execution model implements them as complete executable solutions. At each step, the system selects a promising previously discovered solution, proposes a change, executes and verifies it, and updates only the guidance model using an adaptive group-relative RL objective. This concentrates test-time learning on short strategic decisions while retaining the implementation capability of a substantially stronger model without adapting it. Without web access, Guidance-TTT produces strong solutions across four distinct domains: combinatorial optimization (Polyomino Packing), heuristic programming (AHC058), machine learning (Lasso), and GPU kernel optimization (TriMul). Across these tasks, it outperforms the best solutions reported in prior work while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art results on public online leaderboards. Code is available at https://github.com/Human-Agent-Society/reef/tree/guidance-ttt-support.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 小さな誘導モデルだけをテスト時に RL で学習する Guidance-TTT
papers.summary: 大きな実行モデル全体をテスト時に直接学習(テスト時訓練)させると、勾配や最適化の状態を保ちながら長い出力を繰り返し生成する必要があり、計算コストが高くつく問題がある。Guidance-TTT は、戦略の変更だけを提案する小さな「ガイド役」モデルをテスト時に強化学習で更新し、固定されたまま使う大きな「実行役」モデルがその戦略を実際のコードに落とし込む、という役割分担を導入した。組合せ最適化・ヒューリスティックプログラミング・機械学習・GPU カーネル最適化の 4 分野で、ウェブ検索なしでも先行研究の最良解を上回る結果を得た。
papers.why: テスト時に大モデル全体を学習し直す代わりに小さな誘導モデルだけを RL で更新する設計は、計算コストを抑えた RL 後学習・テスト時適応の基盤として使える。
papers.summary_en: Updating a large execution model directly via test-time training (TTT) is expensive because it requires maintaining gradients, optimizer state, and policy statistics while repeatedly generating long structured outputs. Guidance-TTT instead trains only a compact guidance model at test time—using an adaptive group-relative RL objective—to propose high-level strategic changes, while a frozen, substantially stronger execution model implements and the system verifies them. Without web access, it outperforms the best solutions reported in prior work across combinatorial optimization, heuristic programming, machine learning, and GPU kernel optimization, while remaining competitive with state-of-the-art leaderboard results.
papers.why_en: It shows a compute-efficient way to do RL-based test-time adaptation by updating only a small guidance model rather than a large execution model, a useful pattern for scaling RL post-training/test-time compute.

papers.title: Acceleration of Data Analytics on Heterogeneous Supercloud Systems
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous Supercloud systems are transforming data analytics by enabling scalable and efficient task distribution across diverse resources. This paper presents computational models and performance estimation techniques tailored for accelerating Dense Cholesky (CH) Decomposition and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)-based analytics on Heterogeneous Superclouds. Our ReDSEa tool-chain automates mapping, load balancing, scheduling, parallelism, and computation overlap. Implemented on a heterogeneous system with a Huawei Kunpeng 920 ARM CPU and an Ascend 910 AI accelerator, our LLVM compiler tool-chain employs novel performance models for recursive, iterative, and blocked computations, achieving up to 17x speedup for CH and 88x for SVD over fully optimized 48-core CPU implementations.
papers.ja_title: ヘテロジニアス・スーパークラウドでの密行列分解の高速化
papers.summary: 異種ハードウェア(ARM CPU と AI アクセラレータなど)を組み合わせたスーパークラウドでは、密コレスキー分解や SVD(特異値分解)のようなデータ解析処理を効率よく配置・高速化するのが難しいという困りごとがあった。研究チームは ReDSEa という LLVM ベースのツールチェーンを作り、再帰・反復・ブロック計算向けの性能モデルでマッピング・負荷分散・スケジューリング・並列化・計算の重ね合わせを自動化した。Huawei Kunpeng 920 ARM CPU と Ascend 910 AI アクセラレータ上で、最適化済みの 48 コア CPU 実装と比べ、コレスキー分解で最大 17 倍、SVD で最大 88 倍の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: 異種アクセラレータ混在環境でのカーネル性能モデリングとスケジューリング自動化の具体例であり、分散学習・推論基盤のカーネル最適化設計に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Heterogeneous Supercloud systems combine diverse resources like ARM CPUs and AI accelerators, but efficiently mapping dense linear algebra workloads such as Cholesky decomposition and SVD across them remains hard. The authors built the ReDSEa LLVM compiler tool-chain with performance models for recursive, iterative, and blocked computations to automate mapping, load balancing, scheduling, parallelism, and computation overlap. On a Huawei Kunpeng 920 ARM CPU + Ascend 910 AI accelerator system, they achieve up to 17x speedup for Cholesky decomposition and up to 88x for SVD over fully optimized 48-core CPU implementations.
papers.why_en: Gives a concrete example of performance modeling and automated scheduling for kernel-level work across heterogeneous CPU/accelerator systems, relevant to kernel optimization in distributed training/inference infrastructure.

papers.title: Efficient Secure Federated Learning via Information-Theoretically Secure Key Distribution: A Medical Imaging Case Study
papers.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of models across institutions without centralizing sensitive data, making it well-suited for privacy-concerned applications, such as medical imaging. To protect FL model updates during secure aggregation, additive masking is commonly employed. However, its underlying classical key establishment is only computationally secure. On the other hand, physics-based Information-Theoretically Secure (ITS) key exchange introduces practical constraints: finite key generation rates and time-limited storage severely limit throughput and sustained training of uncompressed models. In this work, we address this bottleneck by developing an FL framework that integrates frozen backbones, knowledge distillation, and quantization. These techniques reduce communication payload and, consequently, key material consumption. Moving beyond simulation, we benchmark this framework on a real physics-based key distribution testbed involving a chest X-ray classification application. Our results show that key usage can be reduced by $\sim$35$\times$ while maintaining predictive accuracy. This prevents buffer depletion and key expiration, enabling sustainable FL training under physical key generation constraints.
papers.ja_title: 物理的な鍵共有を使う連合学習の鍵消費を抑える圧縮手法
papers.summary: 連合学習(複数施設がデータを集めずにモデルを学習する方法)の安全な集約には鍵が必要だが、物理法則に基づく情報理論的安全(ITS)な鍵交換は生成速度と保存期間に限りがあり、大きなモデルの継続学習を続けられないという困りごとがあった。研究チームは凍結したバックボーン、知識蒸留(大きいモデルの知識を小さいモデルに移す手法)、量子化を組み合わせて通信量(=鍵消費量)を減らす連合学習の枠組みを作り、胸部 X 線分類という実物の物理鍵配布テストベッドで検証した。結果、予測精度を保ったまま鍵の使用量を約 35 倍減らすことができ、鍵の枯渇や失効を防いで持続的な学習が可能になった。
papers.why: 通信量削減とセキュアな鍵管理を両立させる設計は、分散・連合学習における通信効率化とセキュリティのトレードオフを考える上で直接役に立つ。
papers.summary_en: Federated learning's secure aggregation typically relies on additive masking with classical key establishment that is only computationally secure, while physics-based information-theoretically secure (ITS) key exchange has limited key generation rate and storage, bottlenecking sustained training of uncompressed models. The authors integrate frozen backbones, knowledge distillation, and quantization into an FL framework to cut communication payload and key consumption, benchmarked on a real physics-based key distribution testbed with chest X-ray classification. Results show key usage can be reduced by ~35x while maintaining predictive accuracy, preventing buffer depletion and key expiration.
papers.why_en: Shows a concrete way to co-design communication-efficient model compression with physically-constrained secure key distribution, directly relevant to communication/security trade-offs in distributed/federated learning infrastructure.

papers.title: The Assistance Dilemma: Learning to Teach via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) trained to answer questions are natively poor at teaching. Reinforcement Learning (RL) against a simulated student is a promising approach to improve their pedagogy, but existing RL-trained tutors reward the student's success on the tutored problem with the tutor's words still in context. The reward is then easiest to raise by telling the student the answer, and a tuned penalty is needed to reduce telling. Drawing on learning sciences, we introduce a masked near-transfer post-test: the student is tested on an unseen variant of the tutored problem with the tutor's utterances masked, so the reward can rise only through what the student wrote in its own turns. This discourages cognitive offloading by the student and allows the continuous penalty to be replaced by two binary reward gates (factual correctness of tutor response, no solution handover). A leave-one-out ablation shows that the learning-gain reward on its own does not separate teaching from telling: the gates reduce solution handover while the near-transfer post-test improves out-of-domain transfer. Using these reward designs we develop Eduardo, a multi-turn RL recipe for training LLM tutors, and use it to train 4B, 9B, 14B and 27B models from two distinct LLM architectures. Our post-trained Eduardo-27B model matches Gemini-3.1-Pro on MathTutorBench and Claude Opus 4.8 on TutorMoments at 2.4-6.2x fewer thinking tokens than frontier models, which matters for interactive tutoring. Without being named in the reward, the model more than doubles its use of the push-for-justification teacher move while support fading (e.g., assigning independent work), whose payoff lies beyond a single-problem dialog episode, is trained out. We open-source our training environment, an 8,671-problem near-transfer dataset, and trained models for further development.

papers.title: Behavior-Preserving KV Cache Compression
papers.abstract: KV caches are a major bottleneck in long-context inference and long-form generation with large language models. Existing training-free eviction policies largely rely on proxy importance signals, such as attention mass, to decide which past tokens to retain. We argue that cache compression should instead preserve the predictive behavior of the full-cache model, retaining entries whose removal would substantially change the model's output distribution. We propose Behavior-Preserving KV Cache Compression, a training-free framework that scores candidate evictions by estimating the compressed-cache logits induced by their removal and evaluating the resulting KL to the full-cache next-token distribution. Using pre-eviction forward statistics, the method avoids running separate masked forward passes for each candidate. Across diverse architectures and both prefill-time and generation-time compression, our method delivers substantial gains in downstream task quality over lightweight attention-based heuristics at matched retained-KV budgets, with the largest gains under aggressive compression. It achieves these gains with additional compression-time computation while retaining an end-to-end speedup over full-cache inference in our evaluated settings.
papers.ja_title: 出力分布を変えない KV キャッシュ圧縮
papers.summary: 長い文章を扱う LLM 推論では KV キャッシュ(文脈情報の保存領域)が大きくなりすぎる一方、既存の削減手法は注意の大きさなどの代理指標に頼り、本来の出力まで変えてしまうという困りごとがあった。研究チームは、ある記憶を消したときに出力分布がどれだけ変わるかを KL ダイバージェンス(分布の差を測る指標)で推定し、影響が小さい記憶だけを削除する学習不要の手法を提案した。さまざまなモデル構成や事前計算・生成時の両方の圧縮で、同じ保持量の軽量な注意ベース手法に比べて下流タスクの精度を大きく改善し、特に強く圧縮したときほど効果が大きく、圧縮なし推論より高速な状態も保てた。
papers.why: KV キャッシュ圧縮を「出力分布を保つ」という原理で設計し直す発想は、推論サービングにおけるキャッシュ管理アルゴリズムの改良に直接応用できる。
papers.summary_en: KV caches bottleneck long-context inference and long-form generation, and existing training-free eviction policies rely on proxy signals like attention mass to decide which tokens to keep. The authors propose Behavior-Preserving KV Cache Compression, which scores eviction candidates by estimating the KL divergence between the compressed-cache next-token distribution and the full-cache distribution, using pre-eviction forward statistics to avoid extra forward passes. Across architectures and both prefill-time and generation-time compression, the method delivers substantial downstream task quality gains over attention-based heuristics at matched KV budgets, with the largest gains under aggressive compression, while still retaining an end-to-end speedup over full-cache inference.
papers.why_en: Reframes KV cache eviction around preserving the full model's output distribution rather than proxy attention signals, offering a principled design direction for inference-serving cache management.

papers.title: Symmetry and AI-assisted discovery of magic-state factories
papers.abstract: Magic-state distillation is a major resource cost in fault-tolerant quantum computing. The cost of a magic-state factory depends strongly on its failure rate, which grows with the number of input magic states. Although symmetry-restricted methods have recently made distance two searches tractable, distance three and above have remained elusive at moderate input counts. We develop symmetry- and AI-assisted methods to search this regime. We present a unified binary-matrix formulation encompassing both triorthogonal-code and direct circuit searches. We show that distance at least three is equivalent to nonzero, pairwise distinct syndromes, separating the choice of syndromes from the search for compatible output gates. We restrict the syndrome search using group symmetry and language-model agents, followed by deterministic solving and independent verification. Our searches yield 699 factory classes, including 564 new ones. These include factories for pure-T states and factories with entangled outputs comprising combinations of T, CS, and CCZ magic states. The pure-T factories [[63, 11, 3]] and [[850, 128, 6]] achieve the lowest overhead exponents we know among protocols with at most 100 and 1000 inputs, respectively, with $γ= 1.589$ and $γ= 1.057$. Our [[1715, 287, 6]] factory, with $γ= 0.998$, is the smallest known pure-T factory with $γ< 1$. We also provide a context directory of search briefs and campaign notes with which readers can train their own agents and tailor the search to their requirements. With these results, we begin constructing an active, open-source repository of magic-state distillation protocols for the quantum community, supplemented by our methods and data, for the practical fault-tolerant quantum computing regime.

papers.title: LoGRA: Scaling LLM Reinforcement Learning with Low-Rank Gradient Sketches
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning has greatly advanced the capabilities of large language models, but its memory demands remain a barrier to broader adoption. We introduce LoGRA, an approach to RL post-training that reduces memory by retaining useful learning signals in low-rank gradient sketches. These compact representations support both model updates and efficient policy synchronization. To prevent overly large updates from disrupting learning, we complement gradient compression with predicted-KL step control, which estimates policy changes before applying each update and adjusts its magnitude accordingly. With all techniques combined, LoGRA reduces average training memory usage by up to 45.7% across reasoning tasks without compromising performance. It also enables stable training of a 27B-parameter model for over 1,100 steps on a single eight-GPU node, where dense Adam runs out of memory, making previously memory-infeasible RL training practical. Code is available in the \href{https://github.com/skzhang1/labs-molt/tree/logra/examples/scripts/logra}{Molt library}.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 低ランク勾配スケッチで LLM の RL 学習メモリを削減する LoGRA
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルの強化学習(RL)による後学習はメモリ消費が大きく、限られた GPU では大きなモデルを学習しにくいという困りごとがあった。研究チームは勾配を低ランクに圧縮した「スケッチ」として保持し、モデル更新とポリシー同期の両方に使う LoGRA を提案し、更新前にポリシーの変化量を予測して更新の大きさを調整する仕組み(predicted-KL step control)も組み合わせた。結果、推論タスクで性能を落とさずに学習メモリ使用量を最大 45.7% 削減し、通常の Adam ではメモリ不足になる 27B パラメータモデルを 8 GPU の 1 ノードで 1,100 ステップ以上安定して学習できるようにした。
papers.why: RL 後学習のメモリ制約を解く具体的な圧縮・安定化レシピであり、大規模モデルの RL 学習基盤を構築する人に直接使える知見。
papers.summary_en: RL post-training for LLMs is memory-hungry, limiting which model sizes can be trained on given hardware. LoGRA reduces memory by keeping gradients as compact low-rank sketches used for both model updates and policy synchronization, paired with predicted-KL step control that estimates policy change before applying updates to prevent destabilizing large steps. Combining these techniques cuts average training memory by up to 45.7% across reasoning tasks without hurting performance, and enables stable training of a 27B model for over 1,100 steps on a single eight-GPU node where dense Adam runs out of memory.
papers.why_en: Provides a concrete memory-compression-plus-stability recipe that makes RL post-training of large models feasible on modest hardware, directly useful for building RL post-training infrastructure.

papers.title: Learning What to Imitate: Entropy-Aware Distribution Mixing
papers.abstract: Small language models are often post-trained as students on reasoning traces from stronger teacher models to efficiently learn new skills. However, token-level imitation on traces that lie far outside the student's expected distribution often produces \textit{confident conflicts}, whereby the student is required to imitate a continuation that it deems unlikely (i.e., low-probability) despite being confident in a different continuation (i.e., in a low-entropy state). To mitigate the degradation in generalisation and catastrophic forgetting caused by these conflicts, we propose \textbf{Entropy-Aware Mixing}: a dynamic per-token interpolation of the student and teacher distributions, gated by the student's predictive entropy. We implement both convex and geometric interpolations for both offline trace generation (via speculative decoding, then SFT) and on-policy forward-KL distillation. Our results show that entropy-aware mixing stabilises distillation, improving in-distribution and out-of-distribution math reasoning while better preserving general capabilities than fixed-teacher supervision. Nonetheless, the optimal entropy schedule depends on the training source, with offline-generated traces favouring concave schedules (greater overall teacher influence) and on-policy training favouring linear or convex schedules (teacher concentrated in high-entropy states).
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 生徒モデルの自信度に応じて教師分布を混ぜる蒸留手法
papers.summary: 小さい言語モデルを強い教師モデルの推論過程(トレース)で模倣学習(蒸留)させると、生徒が別の答えに自信を持っているのに低確率な続きを無理に真似させられる「自信の衝突」が起き、汎化性能が落ちたり元の能力を忘れたりするという困りごとがあった。研究チームは、生徒の予測エントロピー(自信の低さ)に応じて生徒分布と教師分布をトークンごとに動的に混ぜ合わせる Entropy-Aware Mixing を提案し、オフラインの SFT とオンポリシーの蒸留の両方に適用した。固定的に教師へ従わせる手法に比べ、分布内・分布外の数学推論の性能を上げつつ元の汎用能力の劣化を抑えられ、オフライン生成トレースは教師寄りの配分、オンポリシー学習は高エントロピー時に教師寄りの配分が最適であることが分かった。
papers.why: 蒸留時の「模倣と生徒自身の自信の衝突」を定量的に扱う発想は、忘却を抑えた効率的な後学習レシピを設計する際に役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Distilling small student LLMs on reasoning traces from stronger teachers token-by-token can create 'confident conflicts,' where the student is forced to imitate a low-probability continuation despite being confident in a different one, hurting generalization and causing catastrophic forgetting. Entropy-Aware Mixing dynamically interpolates student and teacher distributions per token, gated by the student's predictive entropy, applied to both offline SFT traces (via speculative decoding) and on-policy forward-KL distillation. The method stabilizes distillation, improving in- and out-of-distribution math reasoning while better preserving general capabilities than fixed-teacher supervision, with offline traces favoring concave (more teacher-weighted) schedules and on-policy training favoring linear/convex schedules.
papers.why_en: Offers a principled way to balance imitation against the student's own confidence during distillation, useful for designing stable, forgetting-resistant post-training recipes.

papers.title: BRANCH-MoE: Balance-Aware Tree Routing for Large Embedding Models
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) layers increase model capacity without a proportional increase in per-example computation. However, conventional flat routers can yield imbalanced expert utilization and treat experts as an unstructured collection, whose indices carry no topological meaning. We introduce {\bf BRANCH-MoE}, a routing architecture that places \(E\) experts at the leaves of a binary decision tree of depth \(\log_2 E\). At each internal node the branching probability is centered on the arrival-weighted mean score of the traffic reaching that node. This mean is estimated using an exponential moving average, which promotes utilization of both child subtrees without an auxiliary load-balancing loss. We show that this moving-average estimate admits an explicit noise-lag trade-off. We prove that for linear node maps and log-concave arrival distributions, this mechanism prevents routing-mass collapse. We further establish that, under a frozen router, an expert's execution frequency controls its stochastic-gradient convergence rate, and that confident decisions near the root bound cross-device communication when experts are assigned to devices by tree prefix. We evaluate BRANCH-MoE against Switch softmax, DeepSeek-V3 dynamic-bias, Skywork logit-normalized, and deterministic hash routing on Criteo click-through-rate prediction, Forest Covertype, HIGGS, and YearPredictionMSD, using \(E=16\), top-\(4\) routing, and five random seeds. Our results show that hierarchical routing can preserve task quality and balanced utilization while inducing a topology that supports localized expert co-activation and reduced communication.
papers.ja_title: 二分木構造でルーティングする BRANCH-MoE
papers.summary: Mixture-of-Experts(専門家混合、MoE)層は専門家の利用が偏ったり、専門家の番号自体には意味がなく通信や負荷分散が難しいという困りごとがあった。研究チームは E 個の専門家を深さ log2(E) の二分木の葉に配置し、各分岐点の確率をその枝に届いたトラフィックの加重平均スコア(指数移動平均で推定)を中心に決める BRANCH-MoE を提案し、補助的な負荷分散損失なしでも偏りを防げることと、根に近い確信度の高い判断が木の接頭辞でデバイスを割り当てた場合の通信量を抑えることを理論的に示した。Criteo の CTR 予測や Forest Covertype など 4 つのデータで E=16・top-4 ルーティング・5 つの乱数シードで評価し、既存の Switch softmax や DeepSeek-V3 動的バイアスなどと同等の精度・利用バランスを保ちながら、専門家の近接配置による通信削減につながるトポロジーを実現できた。
papers.why: 専門家の配置に木構造の意味を持たせてデバイス間通信を減らすという着想は、大規模 MoE の分散配置設計に直接関係する。
papers.summary_en: Flat MoE routers can produce imbalanced expert utilization and treat expert indices as unstructured, with no topological meaning for placement or communication. BRANCH-MoE places E experts at the leaves of a depth-log2(E) binary tree, with each node's branching probability centered on an exponential-moving-average of arrival-weighted scores, which the authors prove prevents routing-mass collapse without an auxiliary load-balancing loss and show that confident near-root decisions bound cross-device communication when experts are assigned by tree prefix. Across Criteo CTR, Forest Covertype, HIGGS, and YearPredictionMSD with E=16, top-4 routing, and five seeds, hierarchical routing matches task quality and balanced utilization of existing routers (Switch softmax, DeepSeek-V3 dynamic-bias, Skywork logit-normalized, hash routing) while inducing a topology supporting localized expert co-activation and reduced communication.
papers.why_en: Gives experts a meaningful tree topology that can be mapped onto device placement, directly relevant to reducing cross-device communication in large-scale MoE deployment.

papers.title: Decoupling Time and Space: A Temporally Conditioned Refinement for EEG Source Imaging
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) offers millisecond temporal resolution, but inferring underlying neural sources is a severely ill-posed spatial inverse problem. While deep learning has advanced spatial reconstruction, current architectures face a critical dilemma: frame-by-frame models discard vital temporal context, whereas full 4D spatiotemporal networks introduce an architectural trade-off between reconstruction accuracy and inference cost. We propose a novel two-stream framework that explicitly decouples global temporal representation learning from per-time-point spatial refinement. A Transformer-based Temporal Condition Encoder processes the entire EEG sequence via factorized spatiotemporal attention, retaining sensor-resolved features. A fixed inverse then maps these features into source-indexed conditioning for a per-timestep Source-Space Transformer or volumetric convolutional refiner. Extensive evaluations on realistic synthetic data demonstrate that this temporal prior dramatically improves spatial localization, outperforming classical and spatiotemporal baselines, particularly in high-noise and multi-source regimes. Training across diverse leadfields and explicit operator mismatches improves transfer to unseen head geometries and brings template-based reconstruction closer to subject-specific inversion. Furthermore, we apply the model trained only on synthetic EEG data to real-world EEG. A logistic regressor fit on source power differences in eyes-open, eyes-closed conditions successfully decodes age groups.

papers.title: Balancing Memory Pathways: Analyzing and Improving Memory Utilization in Hybrid LMs
papers.abstract: Recurrent-attention hybrid language models (LMs), which interleave attention and recurrent layers, are increasingly used to combine the efficiency of the recurrent layers with the strong performance of attention layers. Prior work suggests that attention and recurrent layers offer complementary pathways to use past information: attention supports precise memory recall from earlier tokens, while recurrent layers support consolidation of disparate information over long contexts. However, we observe that simply having access to both pathways does not mean that hybrid LMs are effectively using them. We find that they rely substantially more on attention than on the recurrent state. Standard supervised fine-tuning improves overall performance but does not improve how the two memory pathways are coordinated: the model becomes more reliant on information propagated by attention layers, while its use of information propagated by recurrent layers remains limited. To encourage better coordination between the two memory pathways, we add an auxiliary loss that limits attention's access to earlier context while the recurrent state propagates through the full sequence. This objective encourages the model to retain and use information through the recurrent pathway alongside attention. It improves overall performance, with particularly strong gains on tasks involving longer contexts or requiring information aggregation, consistent with the strengths of recurrent layers observed in analysis. Crucially, this imbalance and the benefit of our auxiliary loss generalize: they apply to multiple recurrent-attention LMs in question-answering and agentic tasks, as well as to attention-based LMs that combine different forms of memory. Together, our findings show that simply providing multiple memory pathways does not ensure their effective use, and that targeted supervision is needed to better coordinate them.
papers.ja_title: ハイブリッド言語モデルの Attention と再帰、使い分けのズレを直す補助損失
papers.summary: Attention 層と再帰層を組み合わせたハイブリッド言語モデル (LM) は、2 つの記憶経路を持っているのに実際には Attention にばかり頼ってしまう問題がある。研究者は、Attention が参照できる過去の情報を制限しつつ再帰状態には全系列の情報を伝える補助損失を追加し、再帰経路の利用を促した。この学習法は通常のファインチューニングより総合性能を上げ、長い文脈や情報集約を要するタスクで特に効果が大きく、複数のハイブリッド LM や質問応答・エージェントタスクでも効果が確認された。
papers.why: ハイブリッドアーキテクチャを設計・学習させる人にとって、記憶経路のバランスを取るための具体的な補助損失と診断手法を与える。
papers.summary_en: Hybrid LMs that interleave attention and recurrent layers have access to two complementary memory pathways, but the authors find they rely substantially more on attention than on the recurrent state, and standard supervised fine-tuning does not fix this imbalance. They introduce an auxiliary loss that limits attention's access to earlier context while letting the recurrent state propagate through the full sequence, encouraging the model to use the recurrent pathway alongside attention. This improves overall performance, with particularly strong gains on long-context and aggregation tasks, and the effect generalizes across multiple hybrid LMs, QA/agentic tasks, and attention-based LMs with multiple memory forms.
papers.why_en: Gives builders of hybrid attention-recurrent architectures a concrete auxiliary loss and diagnostic for coordinating memory pathways rather than assuming both are used effectively.

papers.title: How to scale your HEP ML models: A recipe for robust architecture comparisons at scale
papers.abstract: Much of the recent progress in machine learning domains such as language models has come from scaling laws that predict performance as a function of training effort. In high-energy physics (HEP) similar behavior has now been observed. To aid further study, we present a systematic procedure to derive robust scaling laws and compare design choices on the relevant budget axes for HEP tasks. We first validate the full scaling trajectory on toy problems and then apply the procedure to multi-task transformers on the ~11 billion-jet ATLAS JetSet2 dataset, in both the compute- and data-constrained regimes. For the latter, we predict, to the best of our knowledge for the first time, the jointly optimal model size, training horizon, learning rate and batch size under early stopping. At compute-optimal scaling, we recover a near-equal $\sqrt{C}$ dependence of model and dataset size, and find that auxiliary objectives lower the primary jet-classification loss at equal compute budget. Expanding the inputs toward lower-level data systematically lowers the loss while leaving the scaling exponent nearly unchanged. The onset of the power-law regime is itself set by scale: below a threshold in dataset size the loss carries little information about high-compute scaling, underscoring the value of large, high-quality full-simulation datasets as a foundation for scaling studies and the development of foundation models in HEP.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 高エネルギー物理 ML でもスケーリング則を安全に測る手順
papers.summary: 高エネルギー物理学 (HEP) のジェット分類モデルでも、学習量を増やすと性能が上がる「スケーリング則」が見られるが、これまで比較の仕方が曖昧だった。研究者は約 110 億個のジェットを含む ATLAS JetSet2 データセットを使い、計算量制約下とデータ制約下の両方で、モデルサイズ・学習時間・学習率・バッチサイズを同時に最適化する手順を示した。計算最適の条件ではモデルサイズとデータサイズがほぼ同じ比率 (√C) で増え、補助タスクを加えると同じ計算量でも主タスクの損失が下がることが分かった。さらに、データセットが小さすぎるとスケーリング則の情報自体が得られないことも示された。
papers.why: スケーリング則を測って設計判断に使う人にとって、モデルサイズ・学習率・バッチサイズを同時最適化する再現可能な手順と、小規模実験で陥りやすい落とし穴 (データ不足でスケーリングが見えない) を示す点が参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Scaling laws that predict performance from training effort have driven progress in language models, and the authors show similar behavior holds in high-energy physics (HEP). They present a systematic procedure to derive robust scaling laws and apply it to multi-task transformers on the ~11-billion-jet ATLAS JetSet2 dataset in both compute- and data-constrained regimes, jointly predicting optimal model size, training horizon, learning rate, and batch size under early stopping for the first time (to their knowledge) in the data-constrained setting. At compute-optimal scaling they recover a near-equal √C dependence of model and dataset size, find auxiliary objectives lower the primary loss at equal compute, and show that below a dataset-size threshold the loss carries little information about high-compute scaling.
papers.why_en: Offers anyone deriving scaling laws for design decisions a reproducible recipe for jointly optimizing model size, learning rate, and batch size, plus a cautionary finding that too-small datasets give scaling curves that are uninformative about high-compute behavior.

review.note: スケーリング則を測る際、小さいデータセットでは曲線がべき乗則領域に達せず高計算量での挙動について誤った結論を導きうるという落とし穴を示す。
review.note_en: Shows a pitfall in measuring scaling laws: below a dataset-size threshold, the observed curve carries little information about high-compute scaling and can mislead conclusions.

papers.title: MC-Sparse: Deconstructing and Closing the Dense-Sparse Attention Gap in Diffusion Transformers
papers.abstract: Sparse attention is a primary approach to reducing the latency of diffusion transformers in long-sequence generation tasks, such as video and high-resolution 3D asset generation. However, existing methods can degrade generation quality and fidelity at high sparsity levels. Through controlled oracle comparisons, we trace this degradation to three sources: constraints imposed by token grouping, inaccurate interaction selection, and the attention contributions lost when tokens are discarded. Guided by this analysis, we propose Meta-Cached Sparse Attention (MC-Sparse), a training-free framework that selects individual key-value (KV) tokens while organizing similar queries into tile-aligned groups for efficient GPU execution. MC-Sparse caches metadata comprising query groups, KV indices selected using exact attention probabilities, and residuals between dense and sparse attention outputs, and reuses them across subsequent denoising steps. Across video and 3D generation models, MC-Sparse achieves higher fidelity to dense-attention outputs and larger denoising speedups than existing sparse-attention baselines, without visible quality degradation. Relative to dense attention, it delivers a $1.80\times$ denoising speedup on Minimax-H3-Base and a $2.32\times$ speedup on 3D asset generation, both with negligible quality loss.
papers.ja_title: 疎な注意機構で動画・3D 生成の拡散モデルを高速化しつつ品質を保つ
papers.summary: 動画や高解像度 3D 生成を行う拡散トランスフォーマー (Diffusion Transformer) は系列が長く遅いため、注意機構を疎 (スパース) にして速くする手法があるが、疎度を上げると品質が落ちる問題があった。研究者はオラクル比較で劣化原因を「トークンのグループ化による制約」「相互作用選択の不正確さ」「捨てたトークンの寄与の消失」の 3 つに分解し、個々のキー・バリュートークンを選びつつクエリはタイル単位でまとめる学習不要の手法 MC-Sparse を提案した。Minimax-H3-Base で密な注意に対し 1.80 倍、3D 資産生成で 2.32 倍の高速化を、見た目の品質劣化なしに達成した。
papers.why: 長い系列を扱う生成モデルの推論を高速化したい人にとって、疎な注意の品質劣化要因を分解した分析と、GPU 実行に適した具体的な実装が参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Sparse attention is a key way to cut latency in diffusion transformers for long-sequence generation (e.g., video, high-resolution 3D assets), but existing methods degrade quality at high sparsity. Through controlled oracle comparisons the authors trace this to three sources—token-grouping constraints, inaccurate interaction selection, and lost attention contributions from discarded tokens—and propose MC-Sparse, a training-free framework that selects individual KV tokens while grouping queries into tile-aligned groups and caching/reusing metadata across denoising steps. It achieves a 1.80x denoising speedup on Minimax-H3-Base and 2.32x on 3D asset generation relative to dense attention, with negligible quality loss.
papers.why_en: Gives anyone speeding up inference for long-sequence generative models a decomposition of why sparse attention degrades quality plus a concrete, GPU-friendly, training-free implementation that closes the gap to dense attention.

papers.title: Sharpen Without Search: On-Policy Distillation of Sequence-Level Power Distribution
papers.abstract: A language model can give a correct answer more probability than any single incorrect answer and still usually sample an incorrect one, because the incorrect answers together hold more probability. The power distribution raises each complete answer's probability to a power above one and renormalizes, shifting probability toward answers the model finds most likely (sharpening). Sampling from it improves reasoning without changing parameters, but needs many scored candidates per query. We show that a model can instead be trained to produce such answers in one generation. On-policy power distillation (OPPD) runs a sequential Monte Carlo sampler in which the model being trained generates candidates and a frozen teacher's power distribution weights them; the same probabilities weight each answer in a maximum-likelihood update. Training raises single-generation accuracy by up to 23.0 points on MATH500 and 27.3 on GSM8K over the untrained model at the same temperature, and one generation scores 2.4 and 3.5 points above published power sampling with 64 candidates, recovering 94 percent of the gain that 16 candidates give the untrained model. For context, against GRPO trained with verified rewards from the same checkpoint and budget, OPPD scores 3.8, 4.0 and 5.4 points higher on MATH500, GSM8K and AIME using no reference answers; the two are complementary, and OPPD applied after GRPO adds up to 9.3 points. Trained only on mathematics, OPPD raises HumanEval accuracy by up to 5.3 points. One loss coefficient moves the sharpening exponent the model absorbs between 1.19 and 2.02, against 1.14 for ordinary on-policy distillation, and it rises mostly on the model's own answers. Gains hold across model families and sizes, including a model already trained with verified rewards, where lowering the temperature gives nothing and OPPD adds 4.4 points on MATH500. Code: https://github.com/ArminAzizi98/OPPD.
papers.ja_title: 探索なしでサンプリングを鋭くする：on-policy 蒸留で推論精度を上げる
papers.summary: 言語モデルは正解に最も高い確率を割り当てていても、誤答全体の確率の合計が大きいためサンプリングで誤りやすいという問題がある。研究者は、各完全な答えの確率をべき乗して鋭くした「べき乗分布」を 1 回の生成だけで再現できるように学習する手法 OPPD (on-policy power distillation) を提案した。MATH500 で学習前のモデルより最大 23.0 点、GSM8K で 27.3 点精度が上がり、64 個の候補を使う従来のべき乗サンプリングより 1 回生成でそれぞれ 2.4 点・3.5 点高い結果を得た。検証済み報酬で学習する GRPO と比べても MATH500 で 3.8 点、GSM8K で 4.0 点、AIME で 5.4 点高く、両者を組み合わせるとさらに最大 9.3 点改善した。
papers.why: 検証用の正解ラベルを使わずに、複数サンプリングにかかる計算コストを 1 回の生成に圧縮してサンプリング品質を高める学習法として、RL 後学習や推論時サンプリングのコストを下げたい人に使える。
papers.summary_en: A language model can give a correct answer higher probability than any single wrong answer yet still usually sample a wrong one, because incorrect answers collectively hold more probability mass; sharpening via a "power distribution" fixes this at sampling time but needs many scored candidates per query. The authors propose on-policy power distillation (OPPD), training a model to produce such sharpened answers in a single generation via a sequential Monte Carlo sampler weighted by a frozen teacher's power distribution. OPPD raises single-generation accuracy by up to 23.0 points on MATH500 and 27.3 on GSM8K over the untrained model, beats published power sampling with 64 candidates by 2.4 and 3.5 points in one generation, and outperforms GRPO trained with verified rewards by 3.8-5.4 points on MATH500/GSM8K/AIME while using no reference answers; combining OPPD with GRPO adds up to 9.3 points further.
papers.why_en: Offers anyone building RL post-training or inference-time sampling pipelines a way to compress the cost of many-candidate sampling into a single generation without needing verified reward labels.

papers.title: FluidPD: In-Place Elasticity for SLO-Aware Prefill-Decode Disaggregated LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Prefill-decode disaggregation is becoming a common architecture for LLM serving because it separates two phases with distinct execution patterns and SLO objectives. Existing systems typically combine a fixed prefill/decode worker ratio with request routing across workers. However, real-world workloads exhibit both short bursts and sustained shifts in the prefill-to-decode demand ratio. As a result, a configuration that is well provisioned at one time may quickly become mismatched, causing latency SLO violations even when idle capacity exists elsewhere. Existing autoscaling mechanisms can add capacity, but they react slowly, require spare GPUs, and do not directly address short-timescale phase imbalance. We present FluidPD, a P/D-disaggregated serving system that provides SLO-aware in-place elasticity. FluidPD introduces two complementary mechanisms. FluidToken handles transient imbalance by offloading a bounded portion of prefill computation to decode workers when decode-side slack is available. FluidRole handles sustained imbalance by reassigning running workers between prefill and decode roles in place, avoiding model reload and engine restart. Both mechanisms are guided by lightweight pressure indices that expose prefill and decode-side resource pressure before they appear as SLO violations. Across production Azure trace workloads, FluidPD improves overall SLO attainment over static SGLang by up to 94.6 percentage points, demonstrating that SLO-aware in-place P/D elasticity improves service quality without provisioning additional workers.
papers.ja_title: Prefill と Decode の役割を動かさず入れ替えて SLO を守る LLM サービング
papers.summary: Prefill と Decode を別ワーカーに分けて LLM を提供する方式では、ワーカー比率を固定しがちだが、実際の負荷は Prefill 対 Decode の需要比が短時間でも長期でも変動し、片方が過負荷になって遅延の目標 (SLO) を破ることがある。研究者は FluidPD というシステムを作り、短時間の不均衡には Decode 側に余力がある時だけ Prefill 計算の一部を肩代わりする「FluidToken」、長期的な不均衡にはモデル再読込なしでワーカーの役割自体を Prefill/Decode 間で入れ替える「FluidRole」を組み合わせて対応した。Azure の実運用トレースを使った評価で、静的な SGLang 構成に比べ SLO 達成率を最大 94.6 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: Prefill/Decode を分離したサービング基盤を運用する人にとって、追加 GPU なしで短期・長期の負荷変動に即応する具体的な仕組みを示す点が使える。
papers.summary_en: Prefill-decode disaggregated LLM serving systems typically fix the prefill/decode worker ratio, but real workloads shift the prefill-to-decode demand ratio both in short bursts and over sustained periods, causing SLO violations even when idle capacity exists elsewhere. FluidPD introduces FluidToken, which offloads a bounded portion of prefill computation to decode workers during transient imbalance when decode-side slack exists, and FluidRole, which reassigns running workers between prefill and decode roles in place for sustained imbalance without model reload or engine restart. Across production Azure trace workloads, FluidPD improves overall SLO attainment over static SGLang by up to 94.6 percentage points.
papers.why_en: Gives operators of prefill-decode disaggregated serving infrastructure a concrete mechanism to absorb both short-timescale and sustained load imbalance without provisioning extra GPUs.

papers.title: AttSVD:Prompt-Adaptive Low-Rank KV Cache Compression via Attention-Guided SVD
papers.abstract: The key-value (KV) cache of autoregressive transformers grows linearly with context length and dominates memory at long context. Most training-free remedies evict low-importance tokens, an irreversible choice along the sequence axis. We instead keep every token and store it more cheaply along the "feature" axis. We therefore propose AttSVD, a new "interpretable" low-rank compression whose basis is derived from each prompt's own attention geometry: an online, per-prompt truncated SVD that keeps only the directions attention actually reads, cutting persistent per-head KV memory in proportion to the retained rank. We propose two decode-time caching strategies, accumulating and streaming, for short and long generation regimes. Furthermore, we propose two refinements that make compression adaptive. A per-matrix energy rule sizes the logit space and the attention mass independently. An attention-aware basis truncates only in the spaces attention actually reads, preserving both the attention logits and the attention output. The same factors also provide free, per-head interpretability insights into the effective rank and the geometry attention consumes. Across multiple models, on both an agentic benchmark and the full LongBench suite AttSVD stays on par with the dense cache while using up to 50% of the KV-cache memory.
papers.ja_title: 注意が実際に読む方向だけを残す、プロンプト適応型 KV キャッシュ圧縮
papers.summary: 長い文脈を扱う自己回帰トランスフォーマーでは KV キャッシュ (過去の key/value を保存する領域) がメモリを大きく消費し、既存の多くの手法はトークンを間引いて戻せなくしてしまう。研究者は AttSVD という手法で、トークンは全て残しつつ、各プロンプトの Attention パターンから得た特徴方向だけに低ランク圧縮する、オンラインの特異値分解 (SVD) を提案した。複数モデルでエージェント系ベンチマークや LongBench 全体を評価した結果、KV キャッシュのメモリを最大 50% まで削減しても密なキャッシュと同等の性能を保った。
papers.why: 長文コンテキストを扱う推論基盤で KV キャッシュのメモリを削りたい人にとって、トークンを捨てずに特徴軸を圧縮する代替アプローチと、各ヘッドの実効ランクを可視化できる点が参考になる。
papers.summary_en: The KV cache of autoregressive transformers grows linearly with context length and dominates memory at long context, and most training-free remedies evict tokens irreversibly along the sequence axis. AttSVD instead keeps every token and compresses along the feature axis via an online, per-prompt truncated SVD whose basis is derived from each prompt's own attention geometry, retaining only the directions attention actually reads. Across multiple models on an agentic benchmark and the full LongBench suite, AttSVD stays on par with the dense cache while using up to 50% of the KV-cache memory.
papers.why_en: Gives builders of long-context serving infrastructure an alternative to token eviction that compresses along the feature axis instead, plus per-head interpretability of the effective rank attention actually uses.

papers.title: WavePrune: One period is often enough for RoPE
papers.abstract: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) encodes token positions by rotating each two-dimensional channel of the query and key vectors at a channel-specific frequency, making the attention logits invariant to a common shift of positions. However, this rotation is periodic, and it leads to position aliasing where relative positions separated by a full rotation period become hard to tell apart. To address this, we propose WavePrune, which restricts each channel to its first rotation period. We show that it removes the distractions in attention maps created by position aliasing and improves overall long-context performance. Specifically, WavePrune raises the HELMET score on four of five models we test without any extra tuning (e.g., 35.7 -> 40.0 on Qwen3-8B). When pretraining models from scratch, WavePrune also achieves lower validation loss at extrapolated lengths than pretraining without it. Because WavePrune restricts each channel to a sliding window, it induces a fine-grained sparsity that our hardware-aligned CUDA kernels exploit for 1.15x prefill and 1.24x decoding speedups over FlashAttention-2 at 32K context. Together, these results show that RoPE's periodic structure, widely regarded as essential, is largely redundant beyond the first rotation period.
papers.ja_title: RoPE は 1 周期分だけで十分、位置エンコーディングの冗長性を刈り込む
papers.summary: 回転位置埋め込み (RoPE) はクエリ・キーを周波数ごとに回転させて位置情報を与えるが、この回転は周期的なため、1 周期ずれた位置同士が区別しにくくなる「位置エイリアシング」が起きる。研究者は各チャンネルを最初の 1 周期だけに絞る WavePrune を提案し、追加の学習なしで 5 モデル中 4 モデルの長文ベンチマーク HELMET を改善した (例: Qwen3-8B で 35.7 から 40.0)。スクラッチから事前学習する場合も外挿した長さでの検証損失が下がり、1 周期に絞ったことで生まれる疎構造を使う CUDA カーネルで FlashAttention-2 に対し 32K コンテキストで Prefill 1.15 倍・Decode 1.24 倍の高速化も得た。
papers.why: 長文脈を扱うモデルの位置エンコーディングを見直したい人にとって、RoPE の周期構造の多くが不要であるという知見と、それをそのままハードウェア向け高速化に繋げられる点が使える。
papers.summary_en: Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) rotates each two-dimensional channel of query/key vectors at a channel-specific frequency, but because this rotation is periodic it causes "position aliasing" where positions separated by a full rotation period become hard to distinguish. WavePrune restricts each channel to its first rotation period, removing these aliasing-induced distractions and improving long-context performance without extra tuning (e.g., HELMET 35.7 -> 40.0 on Qwen3-8B, improving four of five tested models); pretraining from scratch with WavePrune also yields lower validation loss at extrapolated lengths. Because it restricts each channel to a sliding window, the induced fine-grained sparsity is exploited by hardware-aligned CUDA kernels for 1.15x prefill and 1.24x decoding speedups over FlashAttention-2 at 32K context.
papers.why_en: Shows builders of long-context models that RoPE's periodic structure is largely redundant beyond the first rotation period, giving both a performance improvement and a direct path to kernel-level speedups.

papers.title: JIVEAdapter: A Multi-Task Additive Low-Rank Adapter via Joint and Individual Variation Explained (JIVE)
papers.abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning adapts pretrained models at a fraction of the cost of full fine-tuning, yet most low-rank adapters are single-task and represent each weight update multiplicatively, leaving no explicit account of what is shared across tasks and what is task-specific. We introduce JIVEAdapter, a multi-task "additive" low-rank adapter inspired by statistical Joint and Individual Variation Explained (JIVE). JIVEAdapter decomposes every weight update into a Joint structure shared across all tasks plus a per-task Individual structure, penalizes the Individual structures to be near-orthogonal to the Joint so shared and task-specific signal stay "interpretable" and separated, and allocates rank adaptively across a shared Joint pool and a per-task Individual pool. The Joint is learned once, jointly over a task group or incrementally, one task at a time, then frozen and reused as a prior for new tasks without retraining the shared part. On GLUE and SuperGLUE with DeBERTaV3-base, JIVEAdapter is competitive with strong single-task and multi-task low-rank baselines at a matched per-task effective rank, without extra modules such as MoE, and when a related held-in task exists its frozen Joint serves a held-out task by reusing that task's Individual with only a cheap per-direction scale, otherwise training a small new one.
papers.ja_title: JIVEAdapter: 共通部分と個別部分を分けるマルチタスク LoRA
papers.summary: 低ランクアダプタ (LoRA) は普通 1 タスクずつ学習し、タスク間で何が共通で何が専用かを区別できない。この論文は、重みの更新を全タスク共通の「共同」成分とタスクごとの「個別」成分に分け、両者がほぼ直交するように罰則をかける JIVEAdapter を提案した。GLUE と SuperGLUE で DeBERTaV3-base に適用すると、同じ有効ランクで比較した強いシングルタスク・マルチタスク手法と同等の性能を、MoE のような追加モジュールなしで達成した。
papers.why: 新しいタスクを追加する際に共同部分を再学習せず、個別部分だけ安く学習して使い回せる設計は、継続的にタスクを増やすマルチタスク PEFT 運用に使える発想。
papers.summary_en: Most low-rank adapters are single-task and give no explicit account of what is shared versus task-specific. JIVEAdapter decomposes each weight update into a Joint structure shared across tasks and per-task Individual structures penalized to be near-orthogonal to the Joint, with adaptive rank allocation. On GLUE and SuperGLUE with DeBERTaV3-base, it is competitive with strong single-task and multi-task low-rank baselines at matched per-task effective rank, without extra modules such as MoE.
papers.why_en: The ability to freeze and reuse the Joint as a prior for new tasks while training only a cheap Individual component is a useful pattern for continually growing multi-task PEFT deployments.

papers.title: Exact Unlearning via Quantized Sufficient Statistics
papers.abstract: Exact unlearning requires a deployed predictor to match one rebuilt without the information named by a deletion request. Existing general-purpose exact methods localize retraining through disjoint shards, but every request still invalidates a model, and smaller shards reduce the data available to each constituent predictor. We introduce Quantized Sufficient Statistics (QSS), which separates a small frozen schema from mutable, sum-decomposable content. The schema learns global structure; the content stores local prediction corrections as additive statistics indexed by quantized regions. Deleting content is therefore exact subtraction rather than optimization. We distinguish two guarantees: QSS-L exactly removes a label while retaining the unlabelled input, whereas QSS-E exactly removes both input and label by learning the schema without deletable examples. A deletion takes the arithmetic fast path with probability $1-ρ$ and triggers a full rebuild with probability $ρ$; all reported expected latencies include both events. Across 15 vision, text, and tabular datasets at $ρ=0.5\%$, QSS-L is within 2 percentage points of SISA on 11 tasks and provides 4--483$\times$ lower expected deletion latency on the low-class-count tasks where a compact schema is effective. QSS-E quantifies the additional accuracy cost of removing every trace of an input.

papers.title: Cascadia: Resident 975B MoE Inference on Eleven AI PCs
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-experts models make nearly trillion-parameter capacity accessible with sparse per-token computation, provided that the serving system can distribute the weights and coordinate their execution. We present Cascadia's resident execution of Inkling, a 975B-total/41B-active-parameter model, on eleven Intel Core Ultra X7 358H AI PCs, each with 64 GB of memory, Arc B390 integrated graphics and gigabit Ethernet. We contribute a custom resident MoE engine that preserves Inkling's routing rules, constructs compressed graphs for OpenVINO's fused iGPU primitives, and coordinates FP16 expert computation with FP32 output restoration. The engine fits six consecutive decoder layers per machine and represents dense feed-forward blocks as all-active expert slices, reducing measured dense-layer call time from approximately 8.1 to 4.5 ms. A streaming pipeline coordinates concurrent generation, while captured-state draft evaluation measures agreement with the deployed numerical path. Paired measurements at fifteen concurrency levels from 1 to 176 streams reach 60.29 aggregate decode tokens/s at 88 streams, with 46.87 tokens/s over the complete serving phases. At fifteen streams, median first-token latency is 6.05 s. Raising the context budget from the 1,024-position default, real prompts of 1k to 64k tokens recover the embedded code in all 19 measured answers, with first-token time growing as $aN+bN^2$ and decode latency growing approximately linearly, both bounded by a single-threaded CPU attention loop rather than by memory, which holds 512k positions per stream. Evaluation on captured fleet states separates the effects of vocabulary selection and weight quantization on draft agreement. Together, these contributions establish an execution and evaluation approach for large sparse models on distributed client systems with shared CPU-GPU memory.
papers.ja_title: Cascadia: 11台の AI PC で動かす 975B パラメータ MoE 推論
papers.summary: ほぼ1兆パラメータの疎な MoE (混合専門家) モデルを動かすには、重みの分配と実行調整が課題になる。この論文は、975B 総パラメータ・41B 活性パラメータのモデル Inkling を、メモリ 64GB の Intel Core Ultra 搭載 PC 11台に常駐させて動かす Cascadia エンジンを作り、密な層の呼び出し時間を約 8.1ms から 4.5ms に短縮した。88ストリームの同時実行で合計デコード速度 60.29 トークン/秒、15ストリームでの初トークン応答は中央値 6.05秒となり、1k〜64k トークンの長文プロンプトでも埋め込まれたコードを全19件の回答で正しく復元できた。
papers.why: 共有 CPU-GPU メモリを持つ複数台の民生 PC に巨大 MoE を分散常駐させる実行方式と評価手法は、分散推論基盤を小規模ハードウェアで作る人に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Serving near-trillion-parameter sparse MoE models requires distributing weights and coordinating execution. Cascadia runs Inkling, a 975B-total/41B-active model, resident across eleven Intel AI PCs with 64GB memory each, reducing measured dense-layer call time from approximately 8.1 to 4.5 ms and reaching 60.29 aggregate decode tokens/s at 88 streams, with median first-token latency 6.05 s at fifteen streams, and recovering embedded code in all 19 measured answers for prompts from 1k to 64k tokens.
papers.why_en: The resident execution approach and evaluation methodology for running a huge sparse model across distributed client machines with shared CPU-GPU memory is directly relevant to anyone building distributed inference on commodity hardware.

papers.title: Ofan: Optimal Load Balancing for AI Training
papers.abstract: The extreme collective completion time (CCT) demands of AI workloads challenge existing packet spraying algorithms, which can have trouble efficiently load-balancing workloads that are sent at full line rates. We trace this to a structural cause: on a fat tree, once a packet picks its upward path, the downward path to its destination is unique, so destination-oblivious schemes cannot undo the imbalance it creates. We prove that such schemes can suffer from $Θ(\sqrt{m})$ queueing for messages of size $m$, thus eventually triggering rate reductions by the congestion control. Instead, we suggest Ofan, a switch-based destination-aware LB scheme that can reach $O(1)$ queueing. We also present its pOfan variant that fits the pipe-based architecture of current switches. Our P4 implementation shows that it consumes modest resources. An end-to-end FSDP2 evaluation with Llama-3 405B-parameter models shows that Ofan cuts CCT inflation by $16$--$39\times$ when compared to existing algorithms.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: Ofan: AI 学習向けの最適負荷分散で通信完了時間を大幅短縮
papers.summary: ファットツリー構造のネットワークでは、パケットが上り経路を選んだ時点で下り経路が一意に決まるため、送信先を見ない従来の負荷分散方式では不均衡を直せず、メッセージサイズ m に対して Θ(√m) のキュー待ちが起こることを示した。これに対し、スイッチが送信先を認識して分散する Ofan という方式を提案し、O(1) のキュー待ちを実現した。Llama-3 405B パラメータモデルの FSDP2 実験で、既存手法に比べて通信完了時間の膨張を 16〜39 倍削減した。
papers.why: スイッチ側で送信先を考慮した負荷分散を行うという設計は、GPU クラスタの集団通信を実装・最適化する人にとって直接使える新しいアプローチ。
papers.summary_en: On a fat tree, once a packet picks its upward path the downward path is unique, so destination-oblivious load-balancing schemes cannot undo the imbalance they create, suffering Θ(√m) queueing for messages of size m. Ofan is a switch-based destination-aware load-balancing scheme that can reach O(1) queueing, with a P4 implementation consuming modest resources; an end-to-end FSDP2 evaluation with Llama-3 405B-parameter models shows Ofan cuts CCT inflation by 16-39x compared to existing algorithms.
papers.why_en: A switch-based, destination-aware load-balancing design that provably bounds queueing is directly applicable to anyone building or tuning collective communication for GPU clusters.

papers.title: Stepped MoE: Segment-Level Routing with Configurable Inference Complexity
papers.abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) is resource-intensive, and adapting them for diverse deployment scenarios with varying computational constraints remains challenging. While elastic architectures enable flexible model deployment and sparsely activated models allow input-adaptive computation, existing approaches treat these dimensions independently. Moreover, models catered towards on-device edge inference need to conform to the memory and compute limitations of the serving devices. In this paper, we introduce a unified framework that combines elastic structures with sparsely gated architectures to create models that adapt simultaneously to both deployment constraints and task requirements. Our approach employs a model backbone that conditions on both the context and target efficiency specifications, enabling fine-grained control over the accuracy-efficiency trade-off at inference time. The model learns to activate task-relevant parameters within elastically-nested sub-networks, allowing a single model to span multiple capacity points while maintaining input-adaptive routing. Through experiments we demonstrate that we can create a model that allows the flexibility to use 1,2,3,4 billion parameters while being more accurate than their dense counter-parts (2-5\% on knowledge-intensive benchmarks) and at par with their static versions while delivering similar latency metrics as dense models. Overall, we save on device disk space by sharing the model parameters, allow flexibility of serving based on DRAM and compute available while delivering more accurate results.
papers.ja_title: Stepped MoE: 推論時に規模を切り替えられるエラスティック MoE
papers.summary: LLM を様々な計算制約のデバイスに配備するには、弾力的な構造 (エラスティック) と入力に応じて計算量を変える疎なゲート構造の両方が必要だが、従来は別々に扱われていた。この論文は、文脈と目標とする効率条件の両方を条件づけるバックボーンで両者を統合したモデルを提案し、1台のモデルが 1, 2, 3, 4B パラメータの規模を切り替えられるようにした。知識集約型ベンチマークで密なモデルより 2〜5% 高精度でありながら、静的な専用モデルと同等の精度・レイテンシを達成した。
papers.why: 1つのモデルを複数の容量・精度点に跨って共有パラメータで運用できる設計は、端末のメモリや計算資源に応じて配信モデルを切り替えるオンデバイス推論の運用コスト削減に使える。
papers.summary_en: Elastic architectures and sparsely activated models have been treated independently, yet on-device deployment needs both flexible capacity and input-adaptive computation under memory/compute limits. This paper introduces a backbone that conditions on both context and target efficiency specifications, letting a single model span 1, 2, 3, 4 billion parameter points while being more accurate than dense counterparts (2-5% on knowledge-intensive benchmarks) and on par with static versions at similar latency to dense models.
papers.why_en: A single model that shares parameters across multiple capacity points and adapts its computation to both the task and the serving device's memory/compute budget offers a new lever for reducing on-device deployment cost.

papers.title: MARS: Multi-resolution Adaptive Routing for Sequential Recommendation
papers.abstract: Long-history recommenders often compress each user's history into a compact, candidate-independent memory that is cached and reused to score large candidate pools. We show that real user histories exhibit multi-scale semantic structure, with short-lived intent, medium-term interests, and long-term preferences coexisting in one sequence, and that monolithic cached memories preserve these scales unevenly: linear probes recover recent and mid-range content far worse than long-range content. We call this failure mode \textit{temporal aliasing}. We propose \textbf{MARS}, a multi-resolution user memory that writes the full history into recurrent state tracks anchored to different half-lives, and a sparse routing reader that materializes compact seed memories by selecting the relevant temporal resolutions for each seed, preserving fixed-size candidate scoring. MARS outperforms strong baselines on three public datasets, with gains that grow with history length. Component-matched ablations with paired tests show that temporal diversity and selective routing each contribute beyond what hard-window memories or added capacity provide. The advantage of MARS over its interface-matched baseline also widens after within-user behavioral shifts, at about $1.02\times$ that baseline's warm-cache serving latency for $1{,}000$ candidates per user.
papers.ja_title: MARS: 時間スケールの混在に対応する推薦システムの多重解像度メモリ
papers.summary: 長い利用履歴を持つ推薦システムは、各ユーザーの履歴を1つの固定サイズのキャッシュメモリに圧縮して候補採点に使うが、実際の履歴には短期・中期・長期の意図が混在し、1つのメモリでは最近や中期の情報が長期の情報より読み取りにくくなる「時間的エイリアシング」が起きていることを示した。これに対し MARS は、異なる半減期を持つ複数の記憶トラックに履歴を書き込み、タスクに関係する時間スケールを選んで候補採点用の小さなメモリを作るスパースルーティング読み出し器を提案した。3つの公開データセットで強いベースラインを上回り、1000候補あたりのサービング遅延はベースラインの約 1.02 倍にとどめた。
papers.why: 長期履歴を扱う大規模推薦基盤で、計算量を増やさずに複数の時間スケールを使い分けるキャッシュメモリ設計は、サービング基盤の効率と精度のトレードオフを考える人に参考になる。
