papers.summary_en: Long-history recommenders cache each user's history into a single candidate-independent memory, but real histories have multi-scale structure, and monolithic cached memories recover recent and mid-range content far worse than long-range content, a failure mode the authors call temporal aliasing. MARS writes the full history into recurrent state tracks anchored to different half-lives and uses a sparse routing reader to materialize compact seed memories by selecting relevant temporal resolutions, outperforming strong baselines on three public datasets with gains growing with history length, at about 1.02x the interface-matched baseline's warm-cache serving latency for 1,000 candidates per user.
papers.why_en: A multi-resolution cached-memory design that handles mixed short/medium/long-term signal without increasing candidate-scoring cost is a useful pattern for anyone designing large-scale recommendation serving infrastructure.

papers.title: NCCL M2N: A Layout- and Topology-Aware Collective for Distributed Tensor Resharding
papers.abstract: Distributed training and rollout generation often use different tensor layouts, requiring model weights to be resharded across distinct process groups. This M-to-N redistribution is not directly expressed by standard collectives. Flat direct sends duplicate traffic across destination replicas, while gather-then-broadcast concentrates network injection at one root and transfers data that destinations do not need. For DeepSeek-V3 on 256 GPUs, legacy all-gather plus broadcast accounts for 29.4% of the reported reinforcement-learning step time. We present NCCL M2N, a layout- and topology-aware collective primitive for distributed tensor resharding. Given source and destination meshes and placements, it derives the required transfer regions and a global communication schedule. Its hierarchical route balances source contributions across eligible destination ranks, forwards one copy between destination NVLink domains, and completes local replication over NVLink. Network transfer and local replication overlap, avoiding replica-multiplied source egress. An aggregate data-movement model captures the limits of both stages. We evaluate NCCL M2N on up to 256 GB200 GPUs in an NVL72 cluster with NDR InfiniBand. A single FFN-MoE layer transfer achieves up to 7.9x speedup over flat direct sends (9.8 ms versus 77.3 ms). In a separate 256-GPU DeepSeek-V3 NeMo-RL experiment, NCCL M2N reduces reported weight-sync time from 5.78 s to 2.77 s, a 2.09x speedup over legacy all-gather plus broadcast, and reduces step time by 12.7%.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: NCCL M2N: レイアウトとトポロジを考慮したテンソル再分配の集団通信
papers.summary: 学習とロールアウト生成で異なるテンソルの配置を使う場合、重みを別々のプロセスグループ間で再分配 (M対N変換) する必要があるが、既存の集団通信では直接表現できない。DeepSeek-V3 を 256 GPU で動かすと、従来の all-gather + broadcast が報告された強化学習ステップ時間の 29.4% を占めていた。NCCL M2N は送信元・送信先のメッシュと配置から転送範囲と通信スケジュールを導出し、1つの FFN-MoE 層の転送で直接送信方式より最大 7.9 倍 (9.8ms 対 77.3ms) 高速化し、256 GPU の DeepSeek-V3 NeMo-RL 実験では重み同期時間を 5.78秒から 2.77秒 (2.09倍高速化) に短縮し、ステップ時間を 12.7% 削減した。
papers.why: 分散学習と強化学習のロールアウト生成でテンソルレイアウトが異なるときの重み再配布を高速化する新しい collective primitive は、MoE 学習や RL 基盤の通信最適化に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Distributed training and rollout generation often use different tensor layouts, requiring M-to-N weight resharding across process groups that standard collectives cannot directly express; for DeepSeek-V3 on 256 GPUs, legacy all-gather plus broadcast accounts for 29.4% of the reported RL step time. NCCL M2N derives transfer regions and a global schedule from source/destination meshes and placements, achieving up to 7.9x speedup over flat direct sends (9.8 ms versus 77.3 ms) for a single FFN-MoE layer transfer, and in a 256-GPU DeepSeek-V3 NeMo-RL experiment reduces weight-sync time from 5.78 s to 2.77 s (2.09x speedup), reducing step time by 12.7%.
papers.why_en: A new topology- and layout-aware collective primitive for M-to-N weight resharding is directly usable for speeding up communication in MoE training and RL post-training infrastructure.

papers.title: Activation Denoising: A Robustness View on Parallel vs Sequential LLM Quantization
papers.abstract: Post-training quantization is a powerful tool for compressing large language models. The most scalable methods quantize every layer in parallel, but quantization errors then compound through the residual stream, as no layer corrects for the errors of the layers before it. Sequential quantization accounts for this error compounding by re-calibrating each layer on the already-quantized outputs of its predecessors, yielding stronger results but at the cost of a serial schedule that becomes a bottleneck at scale. As a solution, we propose parallel quantization with activation denoising, which recovers much of the sequential benefit while keeping quantization fully parallel. Rather than re-calibrating layer-by-layer, we take a robustness perspective and model the upstream error as noise, regularizing to be robust to it through a preprocessing step followed by metric-weighted rounding. Applied at every layer, this regularization forms a depth-compounding smoothness penalty that dampens how strongly quantization errors amplify through the model. Unlike orthogonal rotations commonly used in quantization, which must preserve the model's function, we multiply the weights by a more general linear transformation. We find that the two are complementary and their effects compound. Empirically, our robustness regularization recovers a significant part of sequential quantization's benefit in a single parallel pass, at a fraction of its time. Overall, by treating compounding quantization errors as a robustness problem, we offer a principled foundation for more efficient and accurate LLM quantization at scale.
papers.ja_title: 活性化デノイジング: 並列量子化でも逐次量子化に近い精度を得る手法
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルの量子化は、各層を並列に処理する方式だと誤差が残差ストリームを通じて積み重なり、逐次方式 (前の層の量子化済み出力で再調整) なら誤差を抑えられるが処理が直列になり規模が大きいと遅くなる。この論文は、上流の誤差をノイズとみなし、前処理とメトリック重み付き丸め込みでそのノイズに頑健になるよう正則化する「活性化デノイジング」を使った並列量子化を提案した。実験では、この手法は並列処理のまま逐次量子化の利点を大きく回復しつつ、処理時間は逐次方式のごく一部に収まった。
papers.why: 量子化誤差の層をまたいだ増幅をロバスト性の問題として扱う視点は、大規模モデルの量子化パイプラインを速く正確にする設計指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Parallel post-training quantization lets errors compound through the residual stream since no layer corrects for earlier ones, while sequential quantization fixes this by re-calibrating each layer on already-quantized predecessor outputs at the cost of a serial, bottlenecked schedule. The authors propose parallel quantization with activation denoising, modeling upstream error as noise and regularizing robustness to it via a preprocessing step plus metric-weighted rounding, complementary to orthogonal rotations. Empirically, this robustness regularization recovers a significant part of sequential quantization's benefit in a single parallel pass, at a fraction of its time.
papers.why_en: Treating compounding quantization errors as a robustness problem offers a principled, efficient path to improving parallel quantization pipelines for large-scale LLM deployment.

papers.title: TRANSIT: Transparent Scale-in for Multi-Node LLM Training
papers.abstract: TRANSIT is a transparent scale-in framework to enable multi-node model training on fewer GPUs while maintaining training efficiency by transparently leveraging CPU DRAM as an extension of GPU memory during distributed training. It achieves this through a user-space interposition layer, requiring no modifications to the application, training framework, cluster scheduler, device driver, or operating system. Furthermore, TRANSIT achieves higher efficiency by leveraging a zero-copy data path for CPU-GPU transfers. We evaluate TRANSIT on dense and MoE models across scales up to 64 NVIDIA H100 GPUs and multiple parallelism configurations over a RoCE network. Our evaluation shows that TRANSIT can: (a) outperform state-of-the-art framework-managed offloading techniques, achieving up to 68%, 59%, and 42% higher per-GPU throughput than TorchTitan, ZeRO-Offload, and ZeRO-Infinity, respectively, (b) enables training with 50% fewer GPUs while maintaining over 90% of baseline per-GPU throughput, (c) lower per-node network traffic by up to 33%, and (d) improve per-GPU throughput by up to 35% in communication-bound settings.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: CPU メモリを GPU 拡張に使う透過的スケールイン分散学習フレームワーク
papers.summary: 多くの GPU ノードを使う LLM の分散学習は、GPU メモリ(VRAM)が足りないと動かせないという困りごとがある。TRANSIT はユーザー空間の差し込み層(インターポジションレイヤー)だけで CPU の DRAM を GPU メモリの拡張として使い、アプリや学習枠組みを書き換えずに少ない GPU 台数でも学習できるようにした。H100 64 基までの検証で、既存の ZeRO-Offload などより最大 68% 高いスループットを達成し、GPU 台数を 50% 減らしても基準の 90% 以上の性能を保てた。
papers.why: 既存のオフロード手法を書き換え不要で上回り、通信量も最大 33% 減らせるため、GPU 不足時の分散学習基盤をそのまま改善できる実用的な手法。
papers.summary_en: Multi-node LLM training is often constrained by limited GPU memory across nodes. TRANSIT uses a user-space interposition layer to transparently extend GPU memory with CPU DRAM via a zero-copy data path, requiring no changes to the application, framework, scheduler, driver, or OS. On up to 64 H100 GPUs, it outperforms TorchTitan, ZeRO-Offload, and ZeRO-Infinity by up to 68%, 59%, and 42% per-GPU throughput respectively, and enables training with 50% fewer GPUs while retaining over 90% of baseline per-GPU throughput.
papers.why_en: It beats state-of-the-art framework-managed offloading without any code changes and cuts per-node network traffic by up to 33%, making it a practical drop-in improvement for distributed training infrastructure under GPU scarcity.

papers.title: Monte Carlo Estimation for KV Cache Eviction
papers.abstract: Most KV-cache eviction methods ask, in effect, which memory appeared important while reading the prompt? We instead ask which memory will matter while answering? Since decoding queries are unavailable at eviction time, prior future-aware methods rely on pseudo-responses or synthetic future-query estimates. We cast fixed-budget future-aware eviction as distributional estimation over plausible model-conditional query trajectories and introduce LORE-KV (Lookahead Output-perturbation with Reliability-weighted Ensembles for Key-Value caches), a training-free method that samples short autoregressive continuations from the frozen target model and uses their response-side query states to estimate prompt-token utility. Tokens are scored by projected leave-one-out attention-output deletion cost and aggregated across sampled futures with optional trajectory weighting. The temporary continuations are discarded before final decoding, requiring no auxiliary model or training. Ablations isolate the mechanism: at B=128, a single response-side continuation recovers about 89% of the gain over the prompt-window control, while additional futures provide smaller improvements. At B=128, LORE-KV raises the LongBench average on Qwen2.5-14B from 45.49 to 48.24 (+2.75) and the 16K RULER average on Mistral-7B from 45.20 to 51.05 (+5.85); on Llama-3.1-8B, the RULER margin over AnDPro widens to +8.13 and +11.65 points at 64K and 128K contexts. Gains diminish at larger cache budgets and coexist with task-level regressions. LORE-KV incurs 1.46-2.77x AnDPro's per-sample wall-clock time as a one-time compression overhead across six dense and hybrid-attention backbones. Project webpage: https://ahsanbilal7.github.io/train_free_kv/
papers.ja_title: これから使われる記憶を予測して削る KV キャッシュ圧縮
papers.summary: LLM の推論で使う KV キャッシュ(過去の計算結果の記憶)を減らす既存手法は、プロンプトを読む時に重要だった記憶を残すだけで、これから答えを作るときに本当に必要な記憶を見ていないという困りごとがある。LORE-KV は、学習済みモデル自身に短い続き(仮の答え)を何通りも生成させ、その「これからの質問」を使って各トークンの重要度を見積もる、追加学習なしの手法である。キャッシュ容量 128 の設定で、Qwen2.5-14B の LongBench 平均を 45.49 から 48.24 に、Mistral-7B の 16K RULER 平均を 45.20 から 51.05 に上げ、Llama-3.1-8B では既存手法 AnDPro より 64K・128K 文脈でそれぞれ 8.13 点、11.65 点高い結果を得た。
papers.why: 将来のクエリを明示的にサンプリングして重要度推定に使うという発想は、推論サービングの KV キャッシュ圧縮基盤に組み込める新しい将来予測アプローチ。
papers.summary_en: Most KV-cache eviction methods keep tokens that looked important while reading the prompt, not tokens that will matter while answering — since decoding queries aren't available at eviction time. LORE-KV is a training-free method that samples short autoregressive continuations from the frozen target model and uses their response-side query states to estimate prompt-token utility via leave-one-out attention-output deletion cost. At cache budget B=128, it raises the LongBench average on Qwen2.5-14B from 45.49 to 48.24 and the 16K RULER average on Mistral-7B from 45.20 to 51.05, and widens the RULER margin over AnDPro on Llama-3.1-8B by +8.13 and +11.65 points at 64K and 128K contexts, though gains diminish at larger budgets.
papers.why_en: Explicitly sampling plausible future queries to estimate token utility is a new angle for future-aware KV-cache compression that could be built into existing serving-side eviction pipelines.

papers.title: Does On-Policy Distillation for Safety Pose Backdoor Risks?
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) has attracted growing attention as an effective way to transfer capabilities from teacher models to student models. Recent studies further explore OPD as a tool for improving large language model safety with promising results. However, these approaches typically assume that the teacher and training data are trustworthy. In this paper, we uncover an overlooked threat to OPD for safety: a safety-aligned but backdoored teacher can propagate its hidden malicious behavior to an initially clean student. Under our threat model, a poisoning rate as low as 3% results in an attack success rate (ASR) of up to 70% on the distilled student. We further identify two training choices that can amplify this risk. First, increasing the number of training epochs can lead to high ASR even at low poisoning rates. With only 10 poisoned samples, ASR reaches 67% after 16 epochs. Second, the commonly used top-k KL can accelerate backdoor transfer, causing trigger-conditioned harmful behavior to emerge earlier than sampled-token KL in most settings. Alongside these findings, we explore a simple mitigation, Lazy Defense, which clips KL rewards to make student updates less aggressive, limiting aggressive updates and slowing backdoor learning. Experiments show that Lazy Defense delays backdoor transfer in low poisoning rate settings. Together, our findings reveal that OPD can propagate backdoors, highlighting the need to address the safety risks of OPD.
papers.ja_title: 安全性のためのオンポリシー蒸留が裏口を広めてしまう危険
papers.summary: 教師モデルの振る舞いを生徒モデルに写す「オンポリシー蒸留」は LLM の安全性向上に使われているが、教師モデルに裏口(バックドア)が仕込まれていると、それをきれいな生徒モデルに伝えてしまうという困りごとを明らかにした。実験では、学習データのわずか 3% を汚染するだけで、攻撃成功率(ASR)が最大 70% まで上がることを示した。さらに学習エポック数を増やすと汚染サンプルが 10 個だけでも 16 エポック後に ASR が 67% に達し、簡易な対策(Lazy Defense、KL 報酬を切り詰める)で裏口の伝播を遅らせられることも示した。
papers.why: 安全性向上を狙う蒸留パイプラインにも供給網リスクがあることを定量的に示し、RL 後学習や蒸留基盤のセキュリティ検証に使える観点を与える。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) is increasingly used to improve LLM safety by transferring a teacher's behavior to a student, but this paper shows that a safety-aligned yet backdoored teacher can propagate hidden malicious behavior to an initially clean student. A poisoning rate as low as 3% yields an attack success rate (ASR) up to 70% on the distilled student, and with only 10 poisoned samples, ASR reaches 67% after 16 training epochs; a simple mitigation (Lazy Defense, clipping KL rewards) delays backdoor transfer at low poisoning rates.
papers.why_en: It quantifies a supply-chain-style risk in safety-oriented distillation pipelines, giving a concrete, measured threat model and mitigation that's useful for security-testing RL post-training and distillation infrastructure.

papers.title: Cleave: Scaling Tensor Program Optimization via Decoupled Algebraic Search and Operator Scheduling
papers.abstract: Optimized kernels such as FlashAttention and FlashDecoding are crucial for accelerating today's large models. Most of them are handwritten by experts because existing ML compilers cannot match their efficiency. Producing such kernels requires fusing computations with multiple reductions, which requires both algebraic transformation of the computation graph and operator scheduling of the transformed graph. Unfortunately, searching the two jointly yields a space too large to navigate. We propose Cleave, an ML compiler built on symbolic decoupling: Cleave discovers transformations by performing superoptimization on a graph with symbolic shapes, and then schedules each resulting graph on concrete shapes. Representing shapes as symbols makes equivalence checking cheap and lets a new Split operator, with a symbolic split count, parallelize along a reduction dimension. Cleave's scheduler fuses graphs with multiple reductions through iterative tiling and horizontal fusion. Evaluation on common LLM subgraphs shows that Cleave generates kernels up to 2.8x faster than the best baseline (1.6x on average) and reduces compilation time by 5.9x on average compared to Mirage. For dynamic workloads captured from production serving traces, Cleave compiles each operator once and achieves geometric mean speedups of 1.4x and 1.7x over FlashInfer's handwritten FA2 and FA3 backends. Cleave's code is available at: https://github.com/nyu-systems/cleave
papers.ja_title: 代数変換と演算スケジューリングを分離して探索するカーネル生成コンパイラ Cleave
papers.summary: FlashAttention のような高速カーネルは専門家が手で書くしかなく、既存の ML コンパイラでは追いつけないという困りごとがある。Cleave は計算グラフの形(シェイプ)を記号のまま扱うことで、代数変換の探索と、具体的な形に対する演算スケジューリングの探索を分離し、探索空間を小さくした。LLM の代表的な部分グラフで、最良の既存手法より最大 2.8 倍(平均 1.6 倍)速いカーネルを生成し、コンパイル時間は Mirage より平均 5.9 倍短縮、実運用トレースでは手書きの FlashInfer FA2/FA3 より平均 1.4 倍・1.7 倍速かった。
papers.why: 記号的シェイプによる探索分離という考え方は、手書きカーネルに依存しない自動カーネル生成基盤の設計に直接応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Hand-written kernels like FlashAttention are needed because existing ML compilers can't match their efficiency, largely because jointly searching algebraic transformations and operator scheduling creates too large a space. Cleave decouples the two by performing superoptimization on a graph with symbolic shapes before scheduling each resulting graph on concrete shapes, generating kernels up to 2.8x faster (1.6x on average) than the best baseline while cutting compilation time by 5.9x on average versus Mirage, and beating FlashInfer's handwritten FA2/FA3 backends by geometric mean speedups of 1.4x and 1.7x on production serving traces.
papers.why_en: The idea of decoupling search via symbolic shapes is directly applicable to building automatic kernel-generation infrastructure that doesn't rely on hand-written kernels.

papers.title: Later Is Better: Token Reduction for ViTs Under Distribution Shift
papers.abstract: Training-free token reduction accelerates vision transformers by removing redundant tokens across layers, recovering most of the original accuracy at a fraction of the compute. These methods, however, are designed and evaluated primarily on clean data, and under real-world distribution shift their accuracy gap to the uncompressed model widens with the removal rate. We show that this gap is governed by the reduction schedule, the depth profile of removal, usually left fixed as an implementation detail. Concretely, we introduce a one-parameter late-concentrated power-law schedule that consistently improves out-of-distribution accuracy over flat at no extra inference cost. On ImageNet-C with DeiT-S, the late schedule closes 83% of that gap at a 26% compute reduction (+1.17pp), and 99% of it at a lighter 7% reduction (+0.26pp). The gain cannot be attributed to retaining more tokens or using extra compute: held to flat's compute, the late schedule removes more tokens in total and leaves fewer tokens at the end, yet still wins. Single-layer probes point to a mechanism: earlier reductions perturb features that pass through more remaining layers, front-loading reduction error in depth. The effect is broad, holding across five token-reduction methods (ToMe, EViT, ATS, ATC, PiToMe), nine backbones, all ImageNet-C corruption types, eight further shift suites, and two further modalities, video and vision-language QA. It is also specific to shift, still positive on clean and rising monotonically to ~4x that at the highest severity 5. The schedule keeps its gain under six test-time adaptation methods, and needs no per-input or per-domain tuning.
papers.ja_title: 視覚変換器のトークン削減は後の層でやるほど分布変化に強い
papers.summary: 画像認識の視覚変換器(ViT)を速くするトークン削減は、きれいなデータでは精度を保てるが、現実のノイズ画像(分布のずれ)では削除率を上げるほど精度差が広がるという困りごとがある。この論文は、どの層でどれだけトークンを削るかという「削減スケジュール」が原因だと見抜き、後の層ほど多く削る 1 パラメータのスケジュールを提案した。ImageNet-C と DeiT-S の実験で、計算量を 26% 減らしながら精度差の 83% を取り戻し(+1.17 ポイント)、7% の軽い削減では差の 99% を取り戻した(+0.26 ポイント)。
papers.why: 既存のトークン削減手法に追加コストなしで差し込める改善であり、推論サービング時のロバスト性評価の観点としても使える。
papers.summary_en: Training-free token reduction speeds up vision transformers on clean data, but under real-world distribution shift, the accuracy gap to the uncompressed model widens as more tokens are removed. The paper traces this to the reduction schedule — which layer removes how many tokens — and introduces a one-parameter late-concentrated schedule that removes more tokens later. On ImageNet-C with DeiT-S, the late schedule closes 83% of the gap at a 26% compute reduction (+1.17pp) and 99% of it at a lighter 7% reduction (+0.26pp), with the effect holding across five methods, nine backbones, and multiple modalities.
papers.why_en: It's a zero-extra-cost drop-in improvement for existing token-reduction methods and offers a robustness-evaluation lens useful for assessing serving-time efficiency techniques under distribution shift.

review.note: トークン削減などの効率化手法をきれいなデータだけで評価すると、分布のずれで性能差が広がる落とし穴を見逃す、という評価設計の観点。
review.note_en: Evaluating efficiency techniques like token reduction only on clean data can hide a widening accuracy gap under distribution shift, a pitfall in benchmark design.

papers.title: TRACE: Rollout-Guided Quantization-Aware Training for FP4 Reinforcement Learning of MoE Language Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for post-training large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial computation and memory overhead during rollout generation, which motivates low-precision rollout for efficient RL training. However, existing FP4 RL methods suffer from a key limitation: they primarily optimize quantization accuracy on the training and rollout paths independently rather than directly reducing the discrepancy between the two quantized execution paths. In this work, we propose TRACE (Train-Rollout Quantization Alignment via Compact GuidancE), an FP4 quantization framework for RL training of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models that addresses the limitation of existing FP4 RL methods. TRACE incorporates rollout-guided quantization-aware training that uses rollout-side quantization outcomes to guide training-side FP4 rounding decisions, directly reducing train-rollout discrepancy. Moreover, TRACE adopts an efficient quantization-information caching scheme that selectively retains mantissa and scale information from deeper layers to reduce the storage and communication overhead introduced by rollout guidance. We evaluate TRACE on four large-scale MoE language models across reasoning, coding, and long-horizon RL tasks. Our results demonstrate that TRACE enables joint FP4 weight/activation and FP4 KV-cache rollout with RL performance comparable to BF16 rollout, while achieving up to 5.4xrollout speedup and strong final FP4 performance compared with post-hoc FP4 quantization of BF16-trained policies.
papers.ja_title: 学習と推論の量子化のずれを直接合わせる FP4 強化学習手法 TRACE
papers.summary: LLM の強化学習(RL)による後学習では、答えを生成する「ロールアウト」の計算と記憶(メモリ)の負担が大きく、精度を落とした FP4 計算で速くしたいが、既存手法は学習側と推論側の量子化をそれぞれ別々に最適化するだけで、両者のずれ自体を減らせていないという困りごとがある。TRACE は推論側の量子化結果を使って学習側の FP4 丸め方を導く手法を導入し、深い層だけ情報を残すキャッシュでオーバーヘッドも抑えた。4 つの大規模 MoE(専門家混合)モデルでの評価では、FP4 の重み・活性・KV キャッシュを使ったロールアウトで BF16 相当の RL 性能を保ちながら、最大 5.4 倍のロールアウト高速化を達成した。
papers.why: RL 後学習のロールアウトと学習の量子化を整合させる発想は、低精度計算を使う RL 基盤の実装に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: RL post-training of LLMs is bottlenecked by the computation and memory cost of rollout generation, motivating low-precision (FP4) rollout, but existing FP4 RL methods optimize quantization accuracy on the training and rollout paths independently rather than reducing the discrepancy between them. TRACE introduces rollout-guided quantization-aware training, using rollout-side quantization outcomes to guide training-side FP4 rounding, plus a selective caching scheme to limit overhead. Across four large-scale MoE language models, TRACE enables joint FP4 weight/activation/KV-cache rollout with RL performance comparable to BF16 rollout while achieving up to 5.4x rollout speedup.
papers.why_en: Aligning train-side and rollout-side quantization decisions directly addresses a key gap for building low-precision RL post-training infrastructure for MoE models.

papers.title: Reading, Not Manipulating: Leveraging Router Logits for Multimodal Safety in MoE Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) face compositional safety risks where harmful intent emerges from the interaction between visual and textual inputs. As mixture-of-experts (MoE) VLMs become increasingly common, recent work has explored various safety interventions, including prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and routing-based expert steering. However, these methods show inconsistent improvements across models and evaluation distributions, and the intervention into model behavior or internal states introduce safety-utility tradeoffs by over-refusal. Rather than manipulating internal states to steer model behavior, we instead ask whether routing states can serve as diagnostic signals for multimodal safety. We find that router logits indeed provide highly predictive signals of whether a multimodal input is safe or not. Motivated by this observation, we introduce a lightweight router-logit safety detector that reads out routing signals during prompt prefill and identifies unsafe requests before generation, without modifying model parameters or expert routing. Across Qwen3-VL and Kimi-VL, the proposed detector substantially reduces safety errors on the HoliSafe benchmark and resoundingly generalizes to out-of-distribution safety benchmarks featuring different safety patterns, including MISHard and MM-SafetyBench. The success of the proposed router-logit detector also suggests a broader perspective on model internals: rather than focusing only on manipulating internal components to steer behavior, simply reading naturally emerging signals and linking them to an external safety mechanism can provide a simple, effective, and non-intrusive complement to existing safety interventions.
papers.ja_title: ルーター信号を読むだけで分かるマルチモーダル VLM の安全性診断
papers.summary: 画像と文章を両方使うモデル(VLM)では、画像と文章の組み合わせで初めて危険になる入力があるが、既存の安全対策は内部状態を操作するため精度と安全性のトレードオフが生まれるという困りごとがある。この研究は、専門家混合(MoE)モデルの「どの専門家を使うか」を決めるルーター信号(ロジット)が、入力が危険かどうかをよく予測することを発見し、モデルを一切変えずにルーター信号だけを読んで危険を検出する軽量な検出器を作った。Qwen3-VL と Kimi-VL で、HoliSafe ベンチマークの安全性エラーを大きく減らし、学習に使っていない別の安全性ベンチマーク(MISHard、MM-SafetyBench)にもよく汎化した。
papers.why: モデルを改造せず自然に出る内部信号を読むだけで安全性診断ができるという考え方は、推論時の安全フィルタ基盤に低コストで組み込める。
papers.summary_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) face compositional safety risks where harm emerges from the interaction of image and text, and existing interventions that manipulate internal states introduce safety-utility tradeoffs via over-refusal. This work finds that router logits in mixture-of-experts (MoE) VLMs are highly predictive of whether a multimodal input is unsafe, and builds a lightweight detector that reads these routing signals during prefill without modifying model parameters or routing. Across Qwen3-VL and Kimi-VL, the detector substantially reduces safety errors on HoliSafe and generalizes well to out-of-distribution benchmarks like MISHard and MM-SafetyBench.
papers.why_en: Reading naturally emerging router signals rather than intervening on internals offers a cheap, non-intrusive safety-detection mechanism that could be added to inference-time safety pipelines at low cost.

papers.title: APEX: Speculate smarter, not deeper
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding reduces large language model inference latency by drafting multiple tokens before target-model verification, but its effectiveness depends on both the proposal mechanism and draft depth. Fixed configurations cannot respond to changes in predictability, repetition, and acceptance during generation, so deeper drafting can increase wasted computation without proportional speedup. We introduce APEX, a learned controller that balances decoding speed and draft-token waste through request-level expert selection and block-level depth adaptation. APEX-Router selects among EAGLE-3, n-gram, and draft-model speculation for each request, while APEX-Depth adjusts draft length at each verification block using causal decoding signals and recent verifier feedback. APEX models accepted draft length as censored survival feedback, learning position-wise rejection hazards, block execution costs, and an action utility that balances throughput, accepted progress, and wasted tokens. This allows the controller to adapt speculation while retaining the target model's verification procedure. We integrate APEX into vLLM and evaluate it with Qwen3-8B across six workloads, achieving up to 5.24X speedup over autoregressive decoding. Across the aggregate evaluation, APEX-S achieves 4.27X speedup, while APEX-B achieves 3.27X speedup with a 41.0% relative reduction in wasted-token percentage compared with fixed n-gram speculation at k=16, providing distinct operating points for balancing acceleration and draft-token utilization.
papers.ja_title: 投機的デコードの深さと方式を状況に応じて切り替える学習型コントローラ APEX
papers.summary: LLM の推論を速くする投機的デコード(先に複数トークンを予想してまとめて検証する手法)は、予想の方式や深さを固定すると、予測しにくい場面で無駄な計算が増えてしまうという困りごとがある。APEX は、リクエストごとに EAGLE-3・n-gram・ドラフトモデルのどれを使うか選ぶ「ルーター」と、検証のたびにドラフトの長さを調整する「深さ」部分からなる学習型コントローラで、採用されたドラフト長を生存時間分析のような枠組みで扱って学習する。vLLM に組み込んで Qwen3-8B・6 種類の作業で評価したところ、通常の自己回帰デコードより最大 5.24 倍、全体平均で 4.27 倍の高速化を達成し、固定の n-gram 投機(深さ 16)と比べて無駄トークン率を 41.0% 減らしながら 3.27 倍の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: 投機的デコードの方式と深さを実行時に動的に選ぶという設計は、既存の推論サービング基盤にそのまま載せられる速度・無駄のトレードオフ改善策。
papers.summary_en: Speculative decoding speeds up LLM inference by drafting tokens before verification, but fixed proposal mechanisms and draft depths can't adapt to changing predictability and acceptance during generation, wasting computation. APEX is a learned controller combining request-level expert selection among EAGLE-3, n-gram, and draft-model speculation with block-level depth adaptation, modeling accepted draft length as censored survival feedback. Integrated into vLLM and evaluated with Qwen3-8B across six workloads, it achieves up to 5.24x speedup over autoregressive decoding, with APEX-S reaching 4.27x average speedup and APEX-B reaching 3.27x with a 41.0% relative reduction in wasted-token percentage versus fixed n-gram speculation at k=16.
papers.why_en: Dynamically choosing both the speculation method and draft depth at runtime is a drop-in improvement for the speed/waste tradeoff in existing inference-serving infrastructure.

papers.title: Adaptive Mean Estimation by In-Context Learning: A Gradient-Flow Analysis
papers.abstract: Prior Fitted Networks (PFNs) such as TabPFN now rival established statistical procedures across prediction and estimation tasks. A natural explanation is that PFNs have the property of statistical adaptivity, that is, they perform nearly as well as a method tailored to the true data-generating model for a heterogeneous set of models, while not being told which model the data comes from. We study how such adaptivity is learned in a controlled location-estimation problem. Each task is an unlabeled sample whose family is hidden: Gaussian data call for averaging, with error of order $n^{-1}$, whereas uniform data are best estimated from their extremes, at the faster rate $n^{-2}$. We also provide the example of a symmetric Gaussian mixture, for which a rate of $σ^2_n/n$ can be attained. On scalar inputs, softmax attention computes the derivative of the empirical cumulant-generating function. A single primitive therefore both supplies features that distinguish the families and forms estimators interpolating between the sample mean and the mid-range. We combine attention experts through either a softmax mixture of experts or a gated linear unit (GLU), and analyze stagewise gradient flow. With $\widetildeΩ(n^{1+ε})$ pretraining tasks, the learned estimator is asymptotically efficient on Gaussian tasks, within a factor $n^ε$ of the minimax rate on uniform tasks, and order-optimal on mixtures in a shrinking-variance regime. These guarantees extend to new locations and longer contexts. A risk decomposition separates expert error, routing error and normalization error, which clarifies the architectural contrast. Softmax gating enforces normalization and exact translation equivariance, whereas the GLU must learn it: its dynamics separate into fast bias removal followed by slow expert selection. End-to-end experiments recover the predicted specialization.
papers.ja_title: 文脈内学習による適応的平均推定の仕組みを勾配流で解明
papers.summary: TabPFN のような事前学習済みネットワーク (PFN) は、データがどの分布から来たか知らされなくても、その分布に合わせた統計手法とほぼ同じ性能を出す。本研究は、ソフトマックス注意(アテンション)が標本の累積生成関数の微分を計算していることを示し、これが標本平均と中点を補間する推定器を自然に作り出す仕組みであることを明らかにした。Ω(n^{1+ε}) 個の事前学習タスクがあれば、ガウス分布データでは漸近的に最適、一様分布データでも最適解の n^ε 倍以内、混合分布でも最適な順序の推定精度を達成できることを理論と実験の両方で示した。
papers.why: 注意機構がどのように統計的な適応推定を内部で実装しているかを数学的に説明し、LLM の構造や文脈内学習の仕組みを理解する基盤になる。
papers.summary_en: Prior-fitted networks (PFNs) like TabPFN achieve near-tailored statistical performance without being told the data's generating family. The authors show that softmax attention computes the derivative of the empirical cumulant-generating function, a single primitive that both distinguishes families and interpolates between the sample mean and mid-range. With Ω̃(n^{1+ε}) pretraining tasks, the learned estimator is asymptotically efficient on Gaussian tasks, within a factor n^ε of minimax on uniform tasks, and order-optimal on mixtures in a shrinking-variance regime.
papers.why_en: This gives a rigorous explanation of how attention internally implements adaptive statistical estimation, useful for understanding LLM architecture and in-context learning mechanisms.

papers.title: Harness Engineering for Software Engineering via Modular Executable Dev-Primitives
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) equipped with terminal access have demonstrated strong capabilities in automating software engineering tasks. However, existing agents remain brittle on long-horizon workflows, where they must repeatedly reconstruct program state scattered across source files, configurations, tests, dependencies, and runtime behavior, leading to increasingly long interaction histories, context explosion, and semantic drift. Large repositories further complicate the identification of task-relevant components. To address these challenges, we introduce \textbf{Dev-Primitives} (\emph{Development Primitives}), a modular and executable abstraction that transforms repository components from passive software artifacts into active participants in software engineering. Each Dev-Primitive pairs a repository artifact with a resident LLM, which gives the artifact an agent-native interface grounded in its own implementation and dependencies, enabling natural-language reasoning, inter-component communication, and localized self-modification. Building on Dev-Primitives, we propose \textbf{HERMES}, a Harness Engineering framework for software engineeRing via Modular Executable Dev-PrimitiveS, which instantiates these primitives at repository scale through a dependency-aware dynamic activation mechanism and a bug diagnosis mechanism that maps execution evidence back to the components that must be revised. Extensive experiments on four software engineering benchmarks demonstrate that HERMES outperforms matched baseline harnesses by 12.4\% on average. Moreover, when paired with strong activation and diagnosis models, HERMES, even with Qwen3-8B Dev-Primitives, remains within 4.5\% of the homogeneous GPT-5.6 Sol configuration across all four benchmarks, while reducing inference cost by 26.2\% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, highlighting the importance of harness design in software engineering agents.

papers.title: Lost in the bf16 Cast: Exporting Ternary Language Models Can Revert Most Low-Learning-Rate Code Changes
papers.abstract: Ternary language models such as BitNet b1.58, Falcon-E and BitCPM are fine-tuned through higher-precision latents and deployed as ternary codes by an export that, in the labs' documented pipelines, first casts latents to bf16. We audit releases from three labs. In released checkpoints, fp32 quantization of the shipped latents disagrees with deployed codes on 0.83-1.77% of codes (Falcon-E, BitCPM) and 1.530% (2B-4T); most Falcon-E and BitCPM disagreements are bf16 products exactly on the threshold, which ties-to-even maps to zero, and the unmodified onebitllms exporter reproduces all four Falcon-E releases byte for byte. At fine-tuned endpoints with ULP-matched rates, the documented export lowers greedy GSM8K strict accuracy from 58.79% to 0.78% (Falcon-E-1B-Base) and 36.13% to 0.39% (BitCPM-CANN-0.5B), and a bf16 save and reload lowers 2B-4T's by 27.54 points while its last-number accuracy rises at that endpoint. The strict decrease recurs at each of three new seeds in all three models and has the same direction on 607 reserve test rows, but it is recipe-dependent: at Falcon-E's online-loss-selected rate the export was non-inferior, and after a longer recipe no difference was detected. Two remedies, writing the trained codes directly or adjusting bf16 inputs so unchanged tools emit them, met an inherited 4-point strict-accuracy non-inferiority criterion in all three models, also for the pooled mean over three fixed new trajectories per model and, separately, on the reserve rows. In a frozen study of bf16 latents in fine-tuning (one task, one trajectory per arm), native bf16 writes left 2B-4T's endpoint codes unchanged and changed one Falcon-E code; emulated stochastic-rounding and compensated writers changed codes and were non-inferior to fp32 training at that margin. In two model families, randomized threshold-distance interventions support distance-dependent selection of changed codes.
papers.ja_title: 三値 LLM の bf16 書き出しでコード変更が消える問題
papers.summary: BitNet b1.58 など、重みを -1・0・1 の三値(三つの値)に圧縮する言語モデルは、学習時の高精度な重みを bf16(16 ビット浮動小数点)に変換した後に三値コードへ書き出すが、この変換で低い学習率で加えた変更の大半が元に戻ってしまうことが分かった。3 社の公開モデルを調べたところ、公開済みコードは 0.83〜1.77%(Falcon-E、BitCPM)や 1.530%(2B-4T)が本来の fp32 量子化と一致せず、ファインチューニング後の GSM8K 正解率は Falcon-E-1B で 58.79% から 0.78% へ、BitCPM-CANN-0.5B で 36.13% から 0.39% へ急落した。重みを直接書き出す、または bf16 への入力を調整するという 2 つの対策で、この劣化を防げることも確認した。
papers.why: 低精度・量子化パイプラインの丸め誤差が実際の学習成果を消してしまう具体例を定量的に示し、カーネル・低精度分野の検証や公開手順を見直す材料になる。
papers.summary_en: Ternary LLMs such as BitNet b1.58 are fine-tuned in higher precision but exported by first casting latents to bf16, which the authors show can revert most low-learning-rate code changes. Across three labs' released checkpoints, fp32 quantization disagrees with deployed codes on 0.83-1.77% (Falcon-E, BitCPM) and 1.530% (2B-4T) of codes, and the documented export drops greedy GSM8K strict accuracy from 58.79% to 0.78% (Falcon-E-1B-Base) and 36.13% to 0.39% (BitCPM-CANN-0.5B). Two remedies -- writing trained codes directly or adjusting bf16 inputs -- met a 4-point non-inferiority criterion across all three models.
papers.why_en: This provides a quantified case where rounding behavior in a low-precision export pipeline silently erases real training effects, informing how low-precision/quantization pipelines should be audited and released.

review.note: 公開済みモデルの重み書き出しパイプラインを、学習成果が実際に反映されているかという観点で丸め誤差まで追って検証する測り方の例。
review.note_en: An example of auditing a released model's export pipeline down to rounding behavior, to check whether training effects actually survive deployment.

papers.title: ReFold: Training-Free Reversible Inter-Turn Context Folding for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents act on an append-only interaction history that is re-sent to the model at every step, so the context and its cost grow with steps until the sessions exceed the context window. Existing methods manage the context through context requirement prediction, relying on additional model calls, heuristic rules, or trained policies. However, these predictive approaches introduce runtime overhead, invalidate prefix caches, and permanently discard content with no guarantee of recovery. To overcome these limitations, we introduce ReFold: a training-free rendering layer that preserves the underlying interaction history while compressing only the model's rendered context. It removes two kinds of inter-turn redundancy without an auxiliary predictor: content an earlier turn already displayed, replaced by a stub, and turns the agent itself reports finished, folded into a one-line note. Both operators use chunked rendering, rewriting the cached prefix once every few steps rather than at every step. Every removal is strictly reversible, a wrong removal costs one restore from the history rather than permanent content loss. Because it operates at the rendering layer, ReFold is plug-and-play across standard ReAct-style harnesses. Evaluations across five long-horizon benchmarks and two frontier LLMs demonstrate that ReFold reduces token consumption by up to 2.5x and halves the KV-cache memory per session without degrading task success rates. Under capped context budgets, it avoids up to 92% of forced compactions. Under concurrent serving workloads, it reduces request queuing delays by up to 100%, accelerating inference by up to 1.7x, while cutting inference costs by up to 3.4x.
papers.ja_title: ReFold: 学習不要で可逆な文脈折り畳みによる長期エージェントの効率化
papers.summary: 長時間動くLLMエージェントは、やり取りの履歴をそのまま毎回モデルに送り直すため、文脈(コンテキスト)がステップを重ねるごとに膨らみ、やがて文脈窓の上限を超えてしまう。ReFold は追加学習なしで履歴そのものは保持したまま、モデルに見せる表示だけを圧縮し、既に表示済みの内容をスタブに置き換え、完了したやり取りを1行の要約に折り畳む仕組みを導入した。5つの長期ベンチマークと2つの最先端LLMで、トークン消費を最大 2.5 倍削減、KVキャッシュ(推論中の中間データ)のメモリ使用量を半減させながらタスク成功率を落とさず、同時サービング環境ではキュー待ち時間を最大 100% 削減、推論を最大 1.7 倍高速化、コストを最大 3.4 倍削減した。
papers.why: 文脈を破棄せず可逆に圧縮するという設計は、推論サービングの運用コスト削減とキャッシュ効率向上に直接使える手法である。
papers.summary_en: Long-horizon LLM agents re-send an ever-growing append-only history at every step until it exceeds the context window. ReFold is a training-free rendering layer that preserves the full history while compressing only what's rendered to the model, via reversible stubbing of already-shown content and folding of finished turns into one-line notes. Across five long-horizon benchmarks and two frontier LLMs, it cuts token consumption by up to 2.5x and halves KV-cache memory per session without degrading task success, and under concurrent serving it reduces queuing delays by up to 100%, speeds inference by up to 1.7x, and cuts cost by up to 3.4x.
papers.why_en: A strictly reversible context-compression design that directly reduces serving cost and improves cache efficiency, applicable to any ReAct-style agent harness.

papers.title: FC-SWE: Failure-Conditioned RL for Long-Horizon Software Engineering Agents
papers.abstract: Repository-level software engineering (SWE) is a challenging long-horizon setting: agents must reason over extended interactions, use tools, and adapt to stateful environments. Recent work trains SWE agents with reinforcement learning methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), which independently sample multiple trajectories per issue, test the resulting patches, and compare terminal rewards within a fixed group. However, this training setup does not reuse verifier feedback from failed patches as context for subsequent attempts, even though this feedback contains valuable diagnostic information about what went wrong. Training on recovery trajectories is challenging because the preceding outcome determines whether the next trajectory is generated, while the failed execution determines its conditioning context. We introduce FC-SWE, a failure-conditioned RL framework that incorporates recovery attempts into policy training. After a patch fails verification, FC-SWE restores the repository to its original task state and uses the failed patch and verifier feedback as context for a recovery trajectory. FC-SWE adapts GRPO to these chains of complete, multi-turn tool-use trajectories through two mechanisms. Trajectory-local rewards preserve each attempt's verifier outcome, preventing recovery success from rewarding an earlier failed patch. Active-set advantage estimation forms a comparison group from all initial and recovery trajectories actually executed for the same issue, so failed attempts remain in the group while unexecuted attempts are excluded. On all 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks under a verifier-assisted protocol, FC-SWE with Qwen3.5-4B and SWE-agent achieves 41.7% Resolved@1 and 52.8% Resolved@2, compared with 38.9% and 48.5% for GRPO. Although trained with at most two attempts per chain, FC-SWE reaches 70.7% Resolved@11 under an eleven-attempt test-time budget.
papers.ja_title: 失敗を文脈に活かすFC-SWE: 長期ソフトウェア工学エージェントの強化学習
papers.summary: GRPO(グループ相対方策最適化)を使ったソフトウェア工学エージェントの強化学習は、複数の試行を独立にサンプリングして評価するだけで、失敗したパッチの検証結果という有用な手がかりを次の試行に活かせていなかった。FC-SWE は、パッチが検証に失敗した時点でリポジトリを元の状態に戻し、失敗内容と検証結果を文脈として次の「回復」試行を生成し、各試行の検証結果を保ったまま報酬を割り当てる仕組みを取り入れた。SWE-bench Verified の全 500 件で、FC-SWE は Resolved@1 で 41.7%、Resolved@2 で 52.8% を達成し、通常の GRPO の 38.9%、48.5% を上回り、学習時は最大2回の試行連鎖だったがテスト時に11回まで試行を許すと Resolved@11 で 70.7% に達した。
papers.why: 検証失敗からのフィードバックを明示的に学習信号として取り込む GRPO 拡張であり、長期タスクの RL 後学習基盤を設計する際の新しい視点を提供する。
papers.summary_en: RL training for SWE agents with GRPO samples trajectories independently per issue and never reuses verifier feedback from failed patches as context for later attempts. FC-SWE restores the repository after a failed verification and conditions a recovery trajectory on the failed patch and verifier feedback, using trajectory-local rewards and an active-set advantage estimator over executed attempts. On all 500 SWE-bench Verified tasks, FC-SWE with Qwen3.5-4B and SWE-agent achieves 41.7% Resolved@1 and 52.8% Resolved@2 versus 38.9%/48.5% for GRPO, and reaches 70.7% Resolved@11 at test time despite training with at most two attempts per chain.
papers.why_en: A GRPO extension that explicitly folds verifier failure feedback into the training signal, offering a new angle for designing RL post-training infrastructure for long-horizon tasks.

papers.title: Continuous Memory Machines
papers.abstract: Recurrent neural networks typically compress information into a single vector-valued recurrent state, forcing short-term computation and long-term retention to share the same representation. Past extensions alleviate this bottleneck by increasing the memory capacity or separating timescales, but lack the combination of rapid neuron-level processing and longer-term retention found in biology. To that end, we introduce the Continuous Memory Machine (CMM), a recurrent architecture with matrix-valued short- and long-term memory states serving distinct functional roles. Building on the Continuous Thought Machine (CTM), the CMM's short-term memory tracks recent neural activity, with uniquely parameterized neuron-level models learning to use these activity patterns for computation. A persistent long-term memory stores information for later use, with a Transformer jointly updating both memory stores, providing an expressive bidirectional read--write mechanism such that each store can reorganize its own contents and both read from and write to the other. Across algorithmic, in-context learning, and recurrent reasoning tasks, the CMM outperforms a broad suite of baselines, exhibiting stronger generalization than prior memory-augmented networks while preserving the CTM's interpretable attention patterns. Code is available at https://github.com/SakanaAI/continuous-memory-machines.
papers.ja_title: 短期・長期記憶を分離した新しい再帰構造 Continuous Memory Machine
papers.summary: 従来の再帰型ニューラルネットワーク(RNN)は、短い時間の計算と長期の記憶保持を1つのベクトル状態に押し込めていたため、両者が互いに干渉してしまう問題があった。Continuous Memory Machine (CMM) は、短期記憶と長期記憶をそれぞれ行列の形で持つ新しい再帰構造で、Transformer が両方の記憶を双方向に読み書きして整理する仕組みを備える。アルゴリズム課題、文脈内学習、再帰的推論のタスクで、既存の記憶拡張ネットワークより広い汎化性能を示した。
papers.why: 短期・長期記憶を明確に分離した設計は、LLM のアーキテクチャに新しい記憶管理の選択肢を与える。
papers.summary_en: Standard RNNs compress short-term computation and long-term retention into a single vector state, forcing them to share representation. The Continuous Memory Machine (CMM) uses matrix-valued short- and long-term memory states with distinct roles, jointly updated by a Transformer with bidirectional read-write access between the two stores. Across algorithmic, in-context learning, and recurrent reasoning tasks, CMM outperforms a broad suite of baselines, exhibiting stronger generalization than prior memory-augmented networks.
papers.why_en: Separating short- and long-term memory into distinct matrix states gives LLM/recurrent architecture designers a new memory-management primitive.

papers.title: VisionWeave: Weaving Elastic Visual Representations as a Native Capability of MLLMs
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models have become the dominant paradigm for visual understanding, but incur substantial costs by encoding inputs into dense, fixed-size patch tokens. However, visual information is unevenly distributed: some regions require fine-grained detail, while others admit compact representations. Downsampling sacrifices this detail, while existing token pruning and adaptive approaches remain limited in content-adaptive granularity, task generalization, and integration with modern MLLMs and serving infrastructure. Overcoming these limitations calls for foundation models that learn, end to end, where-and at what granularity-to allocate visual representations, a native capability we term elastic visual representation weaving. We introduce VisionWeave, establishing this capability in frontier-level MLLMs through large-scale training. It combines two components: a gated spatial pooler constructs coarse-grained representations alongside native fine-grained representations within a shared MRoPE coordinate, while a granularity router learns their content-adaptive allocation. Through self-distillation alone, we validate this capability on Qwen3.5-4B and scale to Qwen3.8-27B with over 30K A100 GPU-hours. Based on Qwen3.8-27B, VisionWeave adaptively adjusts token savings to visual content, saving 43.0% tokens on average while retaining 98.9% native performance across eight benchmarks, versus only 88% performance preserved for token pruning baselines with a fixed 50% savings target. Extensive evaluations confirm robust efficiency-quality trade-offs across diverse tasks, resolutions and video frames. When deployed on SGLang serving engine, our method achieves a 2.3x throughput gain while reducing mean TTFT by 54.4% and mean TPOT by 60.6%. Together, we believe these results position elastic visual weaving as a promising capability for next-generation multimodal models.
papers.ja_title: VisionWeave: 内容に応じて視覚トークンの粒度を変えるマルチモーダル LLM
papers.summary: マルチモーダル大規模言語モデル(MLLM)は画像を固定サイズのトークン(パッチ)に変換するため、細部が不要な領域にも同じコストがかかってしまう。VisionWeave は、粗い表現と細かい表現を共有の座標系の中で同時に作り、内容に応じてどちらをどれだけ使うかを学習するルーターを導入した。Qwen3.8-27B で検証したところ、平均 43.0% のトークンを削減しながら 8 つのベンチマークで性能を 98.9% 維持し、固定 50% 削減の既存トークン刈り込み手法の性能維持率 88% を上回った。推論サービング基盤 SGLang に組み込むと、スループットが 2.3 倍、平均初回応答時間(TTFT)が 54.4%、平均トークン生成間隔(TPOT)が 60.6% 改善した。
papers.why: 視覚トークンの粒度を内容に応じて動的に割り当てる手法を実サービング基盤 (SGLang) で検証しており、MLLM の推論コスト削減に直結する知見を与える。
papers.summary_en: MLLMs encode images into dense fixed-size patch tokens even where visual content needs little detail. VisionWeave combines a gated spatial pooler producing coarse- and fine-grained representations in a shared MRoPE coordinate with a granularity router that learns content-adaptive allocation. On Qwen3.8-27B, it saves 43.0% tokens on average while retaining 98.9% native performance across eight benchmarks, versus only 88% performance preserved by fixed-50%-savings token pruning baselines; deployed on the SGLang serving engine it achieves a 2.3x throughput gain while reducing mean TTFT by 54.4% and mean TPOT by 60.6%.
papers.why_en: A content-adaptive visual token granularity method validated directly on a production serving engine (SGLang), offering a concrete path to cutting MLLM inference cost.

papers.title: TICDA: Tabular In-Context Data Attribution
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) achieve strong predictive performance by conditioning on labeled demonstrations provided in context, without any parameter update. Yet how individual demonstrations shape a given prediction remains poorly understood. This gap matters in practice: the context is often assembled from whatever labeled data is available, potentially leading to the inclusion of mislabeled, redundant, or low-quality examples that degrade performance. Standard data attribution methods do not transfer to the TFM setting: resampling-based approaches such as DemoShapley require a combinatorial number of forward passes, and gradient-based estimators such as influence functions require computing training point's effect on the model parameters, which in-context learning never updates. We introduce TICDA, a method that measures the influence of every demonstration in the context directly from linear surrogates trained on TFM latent embeddings, in a single forward pass and at negligible cost. We show that TICDA offers the best compromise against competitors across four tasks: detecting labeling errors, curating context to preserve predictive accuracy while lowering inference cost, producing attribution scores that transfer across TFMs, and supporting an acquisition strategy for efficient active learning.

papers.title: Enhancing Diffusion Language Models with Autoregressive Post-Training Weights
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models (dLLMs) have emerged as a promising alternative to autoregressive (AR) language models, offering flexible token-update orders and parallel decoding. Recent dLLMs are often initialized from pretrained AR models before diffusion conversion in order to inherit their learned representations. After the conversion, however, they typically ignore the extensive post-training ecosystem of their AR ancestors. In this work, we show that these existing AR post-training weight updates can instead be effectively recycled to enhance diffusion models. Despite the changes by AR-to-diffusion conversion, directly adding an AR post-training weight update to a diffusion base model remains effective, bringing its performance close to that achieved by direct diffusion post-training. Notably, AR and diffusion post-training updates are nearly orthogonal in weight space, yet induce substantially more aligned representation changes in the diffusion model. Their distinct updates are also complementary: composing their weights can retain gains from both regimes and further improve the post-trained diffusion model. Based on these findings, we propose A2D, a simple training-free framework for enhancing diffusion models with existing AR post-training resources. A2D can transfer capabilities from AR post-trained models to diffusion base models, and further improve already post-trained diffusion models by composing AR and diffusion post-training updates. Across various dLLMs, including Dream, DreamReasoner, DiffuCoder, Dream-Coder, Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion, and DiffusionGemma, A2D reliably improves instruction following, mathematical reasoning, and coding with both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning updates, without additional training, or inference-time computation.
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 自己回帰モデルの事後学習をそのまま拡散言語モデルに移植する A2D
papers.summary: 拡散言語モデル (dLLM) は自己回帰 (AR) モデルから初期化されるが、変換後は AR モデル向けの指示調整や強化学習などの事後学習資産を使えなくなるという課題があった。本研究は、AR モデルの事後学習による重みの差分をそのまま拡散モデルに加えるだけで、拡散モデルを直接事後学習した場合に近い性能が得られることを示した。AR と拡散の更新は重み空間ではほぼ直交するが、表現の変化としては強く揃っているため両者を合成するとさらに性能が上がり、追加学習も推論時計算も増やさない A2D という手法として、Dream や DiffuCoder など複数の拡散モデルで指示追従・数学推論・コーディングの性能を一貫して改善した。
papers.why: 拡散言語モデルの学習基盤を作る人にとって、既存の AR 事後学習資産 (SFT・RL の重み更新) を無駄にせず再利用できる具体的な方法を示している。
papers.summary_en: Diffusion language models (dLLMs) are often initialized from pretrained autoregressive (AR) models but then lose access to the extensive AR post-training ecosystem after conversion. This work shows that simply adding an AR post-training weight update to a diffusion base model brings performance close to that of direct diffusion post-training, and that AR and diffusion updates, while nearly orthogonal in weight space, induce aligned representation changes that make them complementary when composed. The resulting training-free framework, A2D, reliably improves instruction following, math reasoning, and coding across dLLMs such as Dream, DiffuCoder, and DiffusionGemma, without additional training or inference-time compute.
papers.why_en: For people building diffusion LLM training pipelines, this gives a concrete, training-free way to reuse existing AR post-training assets (SFT and RL weight updates) rather than discarding them after AR-to-diffusion conversion.

papers.title: Learn2Play Bench: How Well Do LLM Agents Learn from Experience in Unfamiliar Environments?
papers.abstract: Learning from experience is essential for LLM agents to adapt to unfamiliar and dynmaic environments. Evaluating this ability is therefore important for understanding how effectively agents acquire and use new knowledge. Existing benchmarks have sought to evaluate this ability, but they primarily evaluate tasks whose rules are provided in the instructions or already familiar to pretrained models, making it difficult to distinguish learning from interactions from reasoning with existing knowledge. To address this, we introduce Learn2Play Bench, a benchmark of newly designed text-based games, whose rules are novel or counterintuitive, requiring agents to acquire knowledge through interaction rather than rely solely on pretrained knowledge. These games provide reproducible feedback and automatic scoring, enabling controlled evaluation of learning across repeated attempts. We also vary game instances to test whether agents can apply what they have learned to new situations. Therefore, we evaluate how backbone models, self-evolving methods, and agent harnesses affect agents' learning ability, revealing three findings: (1) Experience retention: Retaining complete records of actions and feedback can support more effective learning than summarizing these experiences into rules or strategies. (2) Human agent gap: Top-performing human players achieve higher peak scores than the evaluated agents. Human explore more varied strategies, and repeat actions less. (3) Harness matters: With the backbone fixed, changing the harness can improve performance while reducing estimated inference cost. Together, these findings provide insights into how LLM agents learn from experience and suggest directions for future work to improve their learning ability. Project website: https://liushiliushi.github.io/learn2play-bench-website/

papers.title: GPU Acceleration of Awkward Arrays: Using Python cuda.compute
papers.abstract: Awkward Array is a widely used library in high-energy physics (HEP) for representing and manipulating nested, variable-length data in Python. Previous CHEP contributions have explored GPU acceleration for Awkward Array, demonstrating the feasibility and performance benefits of CUDA-based backend while also identifying limitations related to irregular data access, fine-grained kernel launches, and composability of operations. In this contribution, we present recent developments that build directly on these earlier efforts by introducing a CUDA execution model for Awkward Array based on the Python CUDA Core Compute Libraries (CCCL). Using CCCL, we eliminate the need for custom CUDA kernels and can instead use a high-level Python interface. The CCCL-based approach also enables fusion of multiple Awkward operations into a reduced number of CUDA kernels, addressing kernel launch overhead observed in earlier GPU implementations. Lazy execution allows expression graphs to be constructed and optimized prior to kernel generation, improving performance for analysis workflows involving jagged arrays, combinatorial operations, and reductions. In contrast to earlier approaches, this design also emphasizes extensibility, allowing user-defined Python code to be incorporated into GPU execution paths with minimal boilerplate and without breaking existing analysis semantics. We present performance studies that demonstrate improvements over previously reported eager GPU execution strategies for representative HEP analysis patterns. These developments extend the GPU capabilities of Awkward Array toward a more composable and sustainable backend, aligned with the needs of Python-based analysis at the HL-LHC and beyond.
papers.ja_title: Python の cuda.compute で高エネルギー物理データ構造を GPU 加速
papers.summary: 高エネルギー物理 (HEP) で広く使われる Awkward Array は長さが揃わない入れ子データを扱うライブラリだが、従来の CUDA 実装は細かいカーネル起動を多数要し、演算同士の組み合わせにも弱かった。本研究は Python の CUDA Core Compute Libraries (CCCL) を使い、個別の CUDA カーネルを書かずに高水準な Python インタフェースで複数の演算を少数のカーネルに融合する仕組みを導入した。遅延実行によりカーネル生成前に計算グラフを最適化でき、ジャグ配列や組み合わせ演算、縮約を含む代表的な HEP 解析パターンで、従来の即時実行型 GPU 実装より性能が向上したことを示した。
papers.why: LLM 分野に限らず、カーネル融合や遅延実行によってカーネル起動オーバーヘッドを減らす設計は、分散学習・推論基盤のカーネル最適化を考える人にも参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Awkward Array, a widely used library for nested, variable-length data in high-energy physics (HEP), previously had GPU implementations hampered by fine-grained kernel launches and poor composability of operations. This work introduces a CUDA execution model built on Python's CUDA Core Compute Libraries (CCCL), eliminating custom CUDA kernels in favor of a high-level Python interface that fuses multiple Awkward operations into fewer CUDA kernels, with lazy execution allowing the expression graph to be optimized before kernel generation. Performance studies show improvements over previously reported eager GPU execution strategies for representative HEP analysis patterns involving jagged arrays, combinatorial operations, and reductions.
papers.why_en: Even outside LLM workloads, the kernel-fusion and lazy-execution design for reducing kernel-launch overhead is a useful reference for anyone optimizing kernels in distributed training/inference systems.

papers.title: Test-Time Adaptation of Quantized ViTs via Single-Pass Quantizer-Aligned Recalibration
papers.abstract: Post-training quantization is a standard route to fitting vision transformers (ViTs) into edge compute and memory budgets, yet quantized models become especially brittle under distribution shift. Test-time adaptation (TTA) addresses such shifts without labels, but most existing approaches are poorly aligned with the constraints of quantized inference. Prevailing TTA methods recover accuracy through backpropagation, while backprop-free methods often still incur overhead from extra forward passes or parameter updates, and lightweight feature- or logit-level methods recover only part of the loss. Across these approaches, a quantization-specific failure mode that amplifies the drop is not directly targeted: under shift, activations occupy frozen quantizers' calibrated ranges differently, distorting their code distribution. We propose Quantizer-Aligned Recalibration (QuAR), a single-pass TTA method tailored to quantized ViTs that neither backpropagates nor updates any model parameters. QuAR recalibrates activations at the input to a frozen quantizer, mapping the test stream's running per-channel statistics back toward the source calibration. On ImageNet-C with ViT-B, QuAR achieves the highest mean accuracy among state-of-the-art backprop-free TTA methods at 3-, 4-, 6- and 8-bit weight/activation precision, outperforming the strongest baseline by 2.28 points at 8 bits and 4.00 at 3 bits, with 46% lower latency and a memory overhead of only 0.17 MB (0.01% of peak inference memory). Analysis and diagnostics trace the gain to a reduced per-channel mismatch at these quantizers, which restores the code distribution the baselines leave unchanged or distort further. A single fixed configuration remains ahead across continual streams, non-i.i.d. label shift, seven out-of-distribution suites, and three other backbones.
papers.ja_title: 量子化済み ViT を推論時に 1 回だけ調整するテスト時適応手法 QuAR
papers.summary: 量子化したビジョン Transformer (ViT) はエッジ環境向けに軽量化できる一方、入力データの分布が変わると性能が大きく落ちやすい。既存のテスト時適応 (TTA) 手法は逆伝播や追加の順伝播でコストがかかり、量子化特有の問題 (活性値が固定された量子化範囲からずれて符号分布が歪む現象) に直接対処していなかった。本研究は逆伝播もパラメータ更新もせず 1 回の順伝播だけで量子化器への入力統計を元の校正状態に戻す QuAR を提案し、ImageNet-C で ViT-B の 8 bit 設定で最強のベースラインより 2.28 点、3 bit 設定では 4.00 点精度を改善し、レイテンシも 46% 低く、メモリ増加はピーク推論メモリの 0.01% にとどまった。
papers.why: 量子化推論の運用で分布シフトに対処する軽量な手法であり、カーネル・低精度最適化や推論サービング基盤を作る人に実用的な指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: Quantized vision transformers (ViTs) are efficient for edge deployment but become especially brittle under distribution shift, and existing test-time adaptation (TTA) methods either rely on backpropagation or extra forward passes, without directly targeting the quantization-specific failure where activations drift out of a frozen quantizer's calibrated range. The authors propose QuAR, a single-pass, backprop-free TTA method that recalibrates per-channel activation statistics back toward the source calibration, which on ImageNet-C with ViT-B outperforms the strongest backprop-free baseline by 2.28 points at 8-bit and 4.00 points at 3-bit precision, with 46% lower latency and only 0.17 MB (0.01% of peak inference memory) overhead.
papers.why_en: This offers a lightweight way to handle distribution shift in quantized inference deployments, giving practical guidance to people building kernel/low-precision optimizations and inference-serving infrastructure.

papers.title: ECO: Energy-Oriented Configuration Optimization for Attention FFN Disaggregated LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Energy-efficient LLM serving requires minimizing serving GPU energy while meeting latency and throughput service-level objectives (SLOs). Attention--FFN disaggregation (AFD) enables separate resource allocation and operating controls for attention and expert computation, but their energy effects remain coupled through the execution pipeline. Realizing its energy-saving potential therefore requires navigating a hierarchical configuration space in which deployment structures constrain admissible controls and shape their end-to-end effects. Finding low-energy configurations that meet SLOs is challenging because physical evaluations are costly and only a small fraction of candidates can be measured. We present Energy-Oriented Configuration Optimization (ECO), which jointly searches deployment structures and their admissible operating controls under a limited measurement budget. ECO constructs a structure-aware energy prior from calibrated stage behavior and pipeline dependencies, then learns residual prediction errors with a Gaussian process. Its cost-aware constrained Bayesian optimization prioritizes measurements according to expected energy improvement while accounting for SLO feasibility, execution success, and evaluation cost, and returns the lowest-energy measured feasible configuration. Across all 16 scenarios on A6000 and A100 with Qwen and DeepSeek, ECO's frozen configurations, evaluated on disjoint requests, reduce serving energy by 40.5\% and increase output token rate by 20.7\% on average relative to baselines while meeting target SLOs. Across the 8 A6000 scenarios, its selected feasible energy averages 33.1\% below generic constrained Bayesian optimization and 25.8\% below genetic search.
papers.ja_title: 注意機構と FFN を分離した LLM サービングの省エネ構成探索 ECO
papers.summary: Attention と FFN (フィードフォワード層) を別々の資源に分離配置する AFD 構成では、消費電力を抑えつつ遅延やスループットの目標 (SLO) を満たす設定を探すのが難しく、実機での計測コストが高いため候補のごく一部しか試せない。本研究は、段階ごとの挙動とパイプラインの依存関係から構成した省エネ事前知識とガウス過程による残差予測を組み合わせ、SLO 達成可能性や計測コストも考慮したベイズ最適化で低消費電力な構成を探す ECO を提案した。A6000 と A100 上で Qwen と DeepSeek を使った 16 通りの設定で、ECO が選んだ構成はベースラインに比べ消費電力を平均 40.5% 削減し、出力トークン速度を平均 20.7% 向上させた。
papers.why: 推論サービング基盤の省エネ設計において、限られた実機計測回数で構成探索する具体的な最適化手法を示している。
papers.summary_en: Attention-FFN disaggregation (AFD) lets attention and expert computation be allocated separately, but finding low-energy configurations that still meet latency/throughput SLOs is hard because physical measurements are costly and only a small fraction of candidates can be tested. The authors propose ECO, which builds a structure-aware energy prior from calibrated stage behavior and pipeline dependencies, learns residual errors with a Gaussian process, and runs cost-aware constrained Bayesian optimization; across 16 scenarios on A6000 and A100 with Qwen and DeepSeek, ECO's frozen configurations reduce serving energy by 40.5% and increase output token rate by 20.7% on average relative to baselines while meeting target SLOs.
papers.why_en: This gives a concrete optimization method for exploring configuration spaces under a limited measurement budget, directly useful for energy-aware inference-serving infrastructure design.

papers.title: Lachesis: Lifetime-Aware KV Cache Placement for Agent Serving across HBM and High-Bandwidth Flash
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) serving is increasingly dominated by agentic workloads, in which agents and their sub-agents accumulate context as KV cache across many requests, consuming substantial memory. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) is a promising solution, providing an order of magnitude greater capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth, but its finite write endurance is the key limiting factor. Our key insight is that KV cache should be placed across HBM and HBF by its lifetime. Placing shorter-lived data in HBM lets HBM absorb more of an agent run's writes and sends less of them to HBF. As the lifetime of KV cache in agentic serving is dictated by the harness, the program that orchestrates the agents, we analyze its behavior and identify three axes along which lifetime diverges, temporal, structural, and inter-worker. Guided by these observations, we present Lachesis, a lifetime-aware KV cache placement layer between the agent harness and the serving engine. At write time, it places each segment in HBM or HBF according to its lifetime, and frees its blocks once the segment is no longer read. In trace-driven simulation, Lachesis extends HBF lifetime by 1.19-3.13x over HBM-first placement, reaching 3.3-12.2 device-years. Even under continuous 24x7 operation at the full load a tight SLO admits, HBF outlasts its five-year warranty on the multi-agent trace.
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュの寿命に応じて HBM と高帯幅フラッシュに配置する Lachesis
papers.summary: エージェント型の LLM サービングでは、多数の要求にわたって KV キャッシュ (文脈の中間結果) が積み重なり大量のメモリを消費する。高帯幅フラッシュ (HBF) は HBM と同等の読み出し帯幅で 1 桁大きい容量を持つが書き込み耐久性に制約があるため、短命なデータを HBM に残して HBF への書き込みを減らす必要がある。本研究はエージェントの実行を制御するハーネスの挙動を時間・構造・ワーカー間の 3 軸で分析し、KV キャッシュの寿命に応じて HBM と HBF に配置する Lachesis を提案した。トレース駆動のシミュレーションで、HBM 優先配置に比べて HBF の寿命を 1.19〜3.13 倍 (3.3〜12.2 デバイス年) に延ばし、継続稼働条件下でも 5 年保証を超えることを示した。
papers.why: 分散推論基盤でメモリ階層の書き込み耐久性を考慮した KV キャッシュ配置の設計指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Agentic LLM serving accumulates KV cache across many requests, consuming substantial memory; high-bandwidth flash (HBF) offers an order of magnitude more capacity at HBM-class read bandwidth but is limited by finite write endurance. The authors analyze agent-harness behavior along temporal, structural, and inter-worker axes and present Lachesis, a lifetime-aware KV cache placement layer that keeps shorter-lived data in HBM to reduce writes to HBF; in trace-driven simulation, Lachesis extends HBF lifetime by 1.19-3.13x over HBM-first placement, reaching 3.3-12.2 device-years, and HBF outlasts its five-year warranty even under continuous full-load operation.
papers.why_en: This gives concrete design guidance for KV cache placement across memory tiers with write-endurance constraints in distributed inference-serving systems.

papers.title: SSR: Sparse Segment Reduction for Ternary GEMM Acceleration
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) require substantial computational resources, limiting their deployment on resource-constrained hardware. Ternary LLMs mitigate these demands through weight quantization via ternary values, achieving significant compression often with 50-90% sparsity. However, existing approaches have limitations: methods optimized for ternary weights, such as BitNet, redundant segment reduction (RSR), and its improved version RSR++, do not exploit sparsity structures, while conventional sparse formats neglect ternary characteristics, foregoing dual optimization opportunities. In this paper, we introduce Sparse Segment Reduction (SSR), a ternary matrix multiplication method designed to accelerate the inference of ternary LLMs and general Ternary Weight Networks (TWNs). SSR has a dedicated optimized ternary data format and an algorithm that systematically exploits sparsity patterns through computation trees that scale with the sparsity. SSR provides theoretical gains with asymptotically faster inference than RSR++ for sparsity above 50%, while practical evaluations reveal performance improvements across all sparsity levels. Evaluation results show that SSR achieves 2.1-11.3x speedup over RSR++ on ternary GEMM with 45-95% sparsity. Furthermore, SSR achieves 3.5-6.3x end-to-end speedup and 4.9% of memory saving over RSR++ on the Llama-3 1B model inference.
papers.ja_title: 三値量子化 GEMM を疎性構造に合わせて高速化する SSR
papers.summary: LLM を三値 (-1, 0, 1) に量子化すると計算量とメモリを大きく削減できるが、既存手法 (BitNet や RSR/RSR++) は三値専用に最適化されている一方で疎性 (重みの 50〜90% がゼロ) をうまく活かせず、逆に汎用の疎行列形式は三値特有の性質を無視していた。本研究は三値専用のデータ形式と、疎性の度合いに応じて計算木をスケールさせるアルゴリズムを組み合わせた Sparse Segment Reduction (SSR) を提案し、疎性 45〜95% の三値 GEMM で RSR++ より 2.1〜11.3 倍、Llama-3 1B モデルの推論全体では 3.5〜6.3 倍の高速化と 4.9% のメモリ削減を達成した。
papers.why: カーネル・低精度最適化に携わる人に、三値量子化モデルの疎性を活用した具体的な GEMM 高速化の設計を示している。
papers.summary_en: Ternary weight quantization (-1, 0, 1) greatly reduces LLM compute and memory, often reaching 50-90% sparsity, but existing ternary-optimized methods (BitNet, RSR, RSR++) do not exploit sparsity structure while generic sparse formats ignore ternary-specific properties. The authors introduce Sparse Segment Reduction (SSR), a dedicated ternary data format with a computation-tree algorithm that scales with sparsity, achieving 2.1-11.3x speedup over RSR++ on ternary GEMM at 45-95% sparsity and 3.5-6.3x end-to-end speedup with 4.9% memory saving on Llama-3 1B inference.
papers.why_en: This gives kernel/low-precision engineers a concrete GEMM design that jointly exploits ternary quantization and sparsity structure for inference speedups.

papers.title: NeMo-DCR: Bit-Exact Delta-Compressed Refit for Scalable Agentic RL at Trillion-Parameter Scale
papers.abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) disaggregates training from rollout, so each policy update must reach the rollout clusters before the next batch. Transferring a full 1T checkpoint for such weight synchronization (refit) takes 87.5 min between two AWS regions. Measurements of BF16 training show that about 1% of weights change their stored values per step. Recent systems exploit this sparsity but fall short on placement, exactness, or efficiency: they reimplement placement rules, assemble full tensors, rebuild values arithmetically, or use a cross-cluster collective, and none fully recovers from mid-refit failures. We present NeMo-DCR (Delta-Compressed Refit), which sends only changes yet is bit-exact: receivers obtain the same parameter and buffer bits as a dense refit. For placement, fixed affine mappings project changes from training shards into the checkpoint's canonical coordinates, residual conversion covers the other changes, and the serving runtime's native loader places all changes in receiver storage. For exactness, compressible XOR masks carry affine changes whose projection and loader preserve stored bits, and overwrites carry the others. Receivers apply both in place, retries overwrite partial writes, and a joint commit binds the policy to the baseline for the next delta. For efficiency, object storage or a relay tree streams payloads during delta construction, without a cross-cluster collective. Even at 3% and 5% change rates, NeMo-DCR refits of 30B-1T models are 12-40$\times$ faster than a transport-only full-checkpoint reference. A 1T relay-tree refit at 3% takes 150 s instead of 87.5 min, making refits practical for cross-cluster agentic RL at trillion-parameter scale.
papers.ja_title: 兆パラメータ規模のエージェント RL を支える差分圧縮リフィット NeMo-DCR
papers.summary: エージェント型の強化学習 (RL) では学習とロールアウトが別クラスタに分かれており、次のバッチが来る前に更新した方針 (ポリシー) をロールアウトクラスタへ届ける「リフィット」が必要になるが、1 兆パラメータのチェックポイント全体を転送すると AWS の 2 リージョン間で 87.5 分もかかる。実測では BF16 学習で 1 ステップごとに値が変わる重みは全体の約 1% にすぎないことが分かっており、本研究はこの差分だけを送りつつ受信側が完全なチェックポイントと同一のビット列を得られる NeMo-DCR を提案した。固定アフィン写像による配置、圧縮可能な XOR マスクと上書きによる厳密な一致、オブジェクトストレージやリレーツリーによる転送を組み合わせ、変化率 3% の 1 兆パラメータモデルのリフィットを 87.5 分からわずか 150 秒に短縮し、30B〜1T のモデルで既存の転送のみの方式より 12〜40 倍高速化した。
papers.why: 兆パラメータ級のエージェント RL を分散クラスタ間で運用する際の、ビット精度を保ったまま高速に方針を同期する具体的な実装を示している。
papers.summary_en: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) disaggregates training from rollout, requiring each policy update ("refit") to reach rollout clusters before the next batch, but transferring a full 1T-parameter checkpoint takes 87.5 minutes between two AWS regions; measurements show only about 1% of BF16 weights change per step. NeMo-DCR sends only these changes while remaining bit-exact with a dense refit, combining fixed affine mappings for placement, compressible XOR masks plus overwrites for exactness, and object storage or relay-tree streaming for transport; even at 3-5% change rates, it refits 30B-1T models 12-40x faster than a transport-only baseline, cutting a 1T relay-tree refit at 3% from 87.5 minutes to 150 seconds.
papers.why_en: This provides a concrete, bit-exact implementation for fast cross-cluster policy synchronization needed for trillion-parameter-scale agentic RL serving.

papers.title: ActTune: Action-Aware Precision and GPU Operating-Point Adaptation for Energy-Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference
papers.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies repeatedly invoke inference to control robots, making graphics processing unit (GPU) energy a recurring cost of task execution. Reducing energy per inference call, however, may not reduce energy per successful task if numerical errors increase failures or slower inference prolongs execution. We therefore target GPU energy per successful task while preserving task success and keeping the inference-latency increase within 10\%. Our approach builds on two observations: quantization sensitivity varies across action classes, model layers, and weights versus activations; and numerical precision changes the workload, shifting favorable GPU operating points. We introduce ActTune, an action-aware framework that connects layer-wise precision allocation with workload-dependent GPU operating-point selection over requested frequency--power-cap pairs. A lightweight decision tree learns its splits and leaf precision configurations directly from configuration action errors, then selects precision before each policy call. The controller forecasts the next workload and applies the selected GPU operating point asynchronously using a lookup table calibrated under a latency budget. A shared resident quantized weight bank enables configuration switching without weight reconstruction or additional policy evaluations. On LIBERO, a benchmark for lifelong robot learning, ActTune improves mean task success by up to 2.3\% relative to state of the art. Relative to the original BF16 implementations, it delivers up to $2.02\times$ faster inference and, with GPU operating-point adaptation, reduces energy per successful task by up to 76.8\%.
papers.ja_title: ActTune: 行動に応じた精度とGPU動作点の調整で省エネなロボット推論
