papers.summary: ロボットを動かす VLA(視覚言語行動)方針は推論を繰り返し呼ぶため、GPU(画像処理装置)の消費電力が実行コストとして重くのしかかる。本研究は、行動の種類や層ごとに量子化(数値を低精度化すること)への感度が違うこと、精度を変えると得意な GPU 動作点(周波数と電力上限の組)も変わることに着目し、軽量な決定木で行動ごとに層別の精度配分と GPU 動作点を選ぶ ActTune を提案した。LIBERO ベンチマークで、タスク成功率を最先端より最大 2.3 ポイント改善しつつ、元の BF16 実装に比べ最大 2.02 倍速い推論を実現し、成功した 1 タスクあたりの消費電力を最大 76.8% 削減した。
papers.why: 推論速度や電力だけでなく「成功したタスクあたりの電力」という実務指標を軸に精度とハードウェア設定を同時に最適化する手法で、エッジでの省エネ推論設計の指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies repeatedly call inference to control robots, making GPU energy a recurring cost, and reducing energy per call alone can backfire if numerical errors raise failures or latency grows. The authors observe that quantization sensitivity differs across action classes, layers, and weights vs. activations, and that precision shifts favor different GPU operating points, leading to ActTune, a lightweight decision-tree controller that jointly selects layer-wise precision and GPU frequency-power-cap settings. On LIBERO, ActTune improves mean task success by up to 2.3% over state of the art, delivers up to 2.02x faster inference than the original BF16 implementation, and reduces energy per successful task by up to 76.8%.
papers.why_en: It optimizes precision and GPU operating points jointly around the practical metric of energy per successful task rather than raw speed/energy alone, offering a design pattern for energy-efficient edge inference of VLA-like policies.

papers.title: Rethinking Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation: From Alignment Coverage to Supervision Reliability
papers.abstract: On-Policy Distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own generations using teacher feedback. With different tokenizers, comparing teacher and student predictions requires alignment at both sequence and vocabulary levels. In this paper, we examine whether expanding this alignment coverage improves learning. Across three heterogeneous teacher--student pairs on mathematical reasoning and code generation, strict 1:1 groups already cover most student-generated tokens despite substantial vocabulary mismatch. On responses sampled from the students before distillation, the shared vocabulary retains nearly all teacher and student probability mass at strictly aligned positions on average. Restricting reverse KL to a student-selected top-16 subset of the shared vocabulary at each strict position achieves accuracy comparable to full shared-vocabulary OPD, outperforming the evaluated cross-tokenizer baselines. Adding mean squared error supervision on span log-probabilities in mismatch groups gives complete supervision coverage, yet reduces accuracy. At checkpoints from training with only the strict loss, the span gradients show weak or negative directional agreement with the strict gradients and grow in magnitude relative to them. These diagnostics may help explain the accuracy drop from adding span supervision. Our findings motivate a shift from maximizing alignment coverage to prioritizing supervision reliability: compact supervision at strict positions can be more effective than broader coverage that introduces weakly aligned or conflicting training signals.
papers.ja_title: トークナイザーが違う教師生徒の蒸留、対応範囲より信頼性を優先すべき
papers.summary: 教師モデルと生徒モデルのトークナイザー(文字の分け方の規則)が異なると、生成文を比べるために語彙を細かく対応付ける必要がある。本研究は数学推論とコード生成で 3 種類の教師生徒組を調べ、厳密な 1 対 1 対応だけでも生成トークンの大部分をすでにカバーしており、共有語彙の上位 16 件に絞った KL(カルバック・ライブラー)蒸留で、完全な共有語彙版と同等の精度を達成できることを示した。一方、対応が緩い区間に MSE(平均二乗誤差)監督を追加すると対応範囲は完全になるが、勾配の向きが厳密対応と合わず、精度は逆に下がることも確認した。
papers.why: 蒸留で「どこまで対応させるか」より「対応の信頼性」を優先すべきという知見は、異なるトークナイザー間でのオンポリシー蒸留を設計する際の具体的な指針になる。
papers.summary_en: When teacher and student use different tokenizers, on-policy distillation requires aligning sequences and vocabularies; across three heterogeneous teacher-student pairs on math reasoning and code generation, the authors find strict 1:1 alignment already covers most student-generated tokens, and restricting reverse KL to a student-selected top-16 shared-vocabulary subset matches full shared-vocabulary OPD accuracy, outperforming cross-tokenizer baselines. Adding MSE supervision on mismatched spans gives complete coverage but reduces accuracy, with span gradients showing weak or negative directional agreement with the strict gradients.
papers.why_en: The result that compact, reliable supervision beats broader but weakly-aligned coverage gives concrete guidance for designing cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation pipelines.

papers.title: UNREAL: Unifying Retrieval and Long-Context with a Single Model
papers.abstract: Long-context inference and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) handle evidence selection at vastly different scales, from a single long prompt to an entire corpus. We ask whether a single model-internal mechanism can select evidence across this range. We introduce UNifying REtrieval And Long-Context with a Single Model (UNREAL), a model-native evidence selection framework to span corpus retrieval and long-context inference. UNREAL encodes chunks and derives retrieval queries directly from the frozen LLM's internal representations. It adds fewer than 500K trainable parameters and leaves the backbone unchanged. On a 3B-token, 21M-chunk Wikipedia index, all four dense and hybrid UNREAL backbones outperform state-of-the-art retriever-reranker systems. The best model raises recall from 49.1% to 73.2% on HotpotQA, from 31.7% to 60.1% on 2WikiMultiHopQA, and from 8.8% to 14.4% on MuSiQue. Applied to long-context tasks, the same selection mechanism removes distractors before generation, raising NoLiMa accuracy from 1.0% to 24.83% at its maximum context length of 128K tokens, and LV-Eval's F1 score from 49.97% to 54.66% at 256K. UNREAL also reduces FLOPs and time-to-first-token relative to full-context inference from roughly 32K tokens onward, with larger gains as context grows. Together, these results establish model-internal evidence selection as a common foundation for corpus retrieval and evidence-sparse long-context inference.
papers.ja_title: UNREAL: 検索と長文脈処理を1つのモデル内機構で統一
papers.summary: 検索拡張生成(RAG)は巨大な文書集合から、長文脈推論は 1 つの長い入力から、それぞれ別々の方法で根拠を選んでいる。本研究は、凍結した LLM(大規模言語モデル)の内部表現から直接クエリとチャンク表現を作る軽量な機構 UNREAL を提案し、50 万未満のパラメータ追加だけで両方の根拠選択を 1 つのモデルで行えるようにした。3B トークン・2100 万チャンクの Wikipedia 索引で、最良モデルは HotpotQA の再現率を 49.1% から 73.2%、2WikiMultiHopQA を 31.7% から 60.1% に上げ、長文脈タスクでは NoLiMa の精度を 128K トークンで 1.0% から 24.83% に、LV-Eval の F1 を 256K トークンで 49.97% から 54.66% に改善した。
papers.why: 検索と長文脈処理という別物として扱われてきた仕組みを、LLM 内部の表現のみで統一して扱える可能性を示し、検索付き推論システムの構造を見直す材料になる。
papers.summary_en: Retrieval-augmented generation and long-context inference select evidence at very different scales using different mechanisms; UNREAL derives retrieval queries and chunk encodings directly from a frozen LLM's internal representations, adding fewer than 500K trainable parameters. On a 3B-token, 21M-chunk Wikipedia index, the best UNREAL backbone raises recall from 49.1% to 73.2% on HotpotQA and 31.7% to 60.1% on 2WikiMultiHopQA over state-of-the-art retriever-rerankers, and on long-context tasks raises NoLiMa accuracy from 1.0% to 24.83% at 128K tokens and LV-Eval F1 from 49.97% to 54.66% at 256K, while also reducing FLOPs and time-to-first-token versus full-context inference.
papers.why_en: It suggests a single model-internal evidence-selection mechanism can unify corpus retrieval and long-context evidence filtering, relevant to rethinking the architecture of retrieval-augmented inference systems.

papers.title: How Bregman Divergences Shape Shampoo
papers.abstract: Understanding the principles behind Shampoo has recently guided the development of more effective neural network optimizers. These methods learn a preconditioner by optimizing the Frobenius or Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence against the gradient second moment. In this work, we investigate how the choice of divergence shapes preconditioning, which remains unclear and blocks further improvements. To do so, we develop a unified Bregman divergence framework that connects all popular divergences, allowing us to study them jointly. Through empirical spectral analysis of gradient second moments, we examine how divergence choice shapes Kronecker approximation and interacts with finite-sample error in preconditioning. We find that some divergences can better compensate for finite-sample underestimation of the empirical second moment, helping explain the differing behavior of their corresponding Shampoo variants. We further validate this explanation through GPT-2 pretraining experiments. By connecting divergence choice to practical training behavior, we believe our framework provides principled guidance for understanding the foundations of, and further improving, Shampoo.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: Bregman 発散の選び方が Shampoo の前処理をどう決めるか
papers.summary: Shampoo のような二次モーメント前処理オプティマイザは、勾配の二次モーメントに対する Frobenius または KL(カルバック・ライブラー)発散の最小化として前処理行列を学習するが、どの発散を選ぶべきかは不明だった。本研究は様々な発散をまとめて扱える統一 Bregman 発散の枠組みを作り、スペクトル解析によって発散の選択が Kronecker 近似の精度や、サンプル数不足による誤差への耐性をどう変えるかを調べた。GPT-2 の事前学習実験でこの説明を検証し、発散の選択が Shampoo 系手法の挙動の違いを裏付けることを確認した。
papers.why: オプティマイザの設計を「発散の選択」という統一視点で理解できるようにし、Shampoo 系の前処理手法をさらに改善するための理論的指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: Shampoo-like preconditioned optimizers learn a preconditioner by minimizing Frobenius or KL divergence against the gradient second moment, but how divergence choice shapes preconditioning was unclear. The authors build a unified Bregman divergence framework covering popular divergences and use empirical spectral analysis to show how divergence choice affects Kronecker approximation quality and robustness to finite-sample underestimation of the second moment, validating the explanation with GPT-2 pretraining experiments.
papers.why_en: It reframes optimizer design around the choice of divergence, giving principled guidance for understanding and further improving Shampoo-family preconditioning methods.

papers.title: A Systematic Study of Small Language Models on Abstract Reasoning Tasks
papers.abstract: Endpoint accuracy on abstract-reasoning benchmarks does not reveal whether a language model has acquired a transferable rule or fit distribution-specific regularities. We study this distinction in small language models on the ARC-TGI benchmark, which organizes abstract grid transformations into controllable task families and supports resampling, spatial shifts, and cross-benchmark transfer. Across more than 1,000 runs, we profile decoder-only, encoder--decoder, and mixture-of-experts model families under supervised fine-tuning. We examine the efficiency and stability of skill acquisition, robustness beyond the training distribution, interactions with model family and task formulation, and layer-wise attention signatures that accompany behavioral differences. Substantial in-distribution accuracy is attainable, but acquisition is sensitive to optimization and unevenly distributed across task families. Performance deteriorates sharply outside the training distribution, including when the rule is retained but grid scale changes. Greater training-set depth and breadth yield uneven gains, while the effect of additional in-context examples depends on model family. Executable-rule induction also yields correct solutions not observed under direct grid generation. On selected tasks, attention diagnostics show distinct concentration and context-dependence profiles, but do not establish general causal mechanisms. Overall, abstract-reasoning scores are conditional on the model, adaptation regime, evaluation distribution, and response format.
papers.ja_title: 小型言語モデルは抽象推論の「ルール」を本当に学べているか
papers.summary: ARC のような抽象的なグリッド変換ベンチマークで正解率が高くても、それが転移可能な規則を覚えたのか、見た分布に特化しただけなのかは分からない。本研究は再サンプリングや空間シフト、別ベンチマークへの転移を測れる ARC-TGI を使い、デコーダのみ・エンコーダデコーダ・混合エキスパートの小型モデルを 1,000 回超の実験で比較した。学習分布内では高い正解率に達するものの、グリッドの大きさが変わるなど分布外では成績が急落し、学習データの量やモデル形式によって得られる効果も一様でないことが分かった。
papers.why: ベンチマークの見かけの正解率と、モデルが実際に汎用ルールを学んだかどうかを区別する評価設計の落とし穴を具体的に示している。
papers.summary_en: High accuracy on abstract grid-transformation benchmarks like ARC does not reveal whether a model learned a transferable rule or merely fit distribution-specific regularities. Using ARC-TGI, which supports resampling, spatial shifts, and cross-benchmark transfer, the authors profile decoder-only, encoder-decoder, and mixture-of-experts small models across more than 1,000 runs, finding substantial in-distribution accuracy but a sharp drop out-of-distribution—including when the rule is retained but grid scale changes—with uneven effects from training-set depth/breadth and model family.
papers.why_en: It concretely illustrates a benchmarking pitfall: endpoint accuracy on abstract-reasoning benchmarks can mask whether a model actually acquired a transferable rule versus distribution-specific shortcuts.

review.note: 見かけの正解率だけでなく、再サンプリングや分布外評価で「規則獲得かどうか」を切り分ける測り方の観点を示している。
review.note_en: Illustrates a measurement approach that separates genuine rule acquisition from distribution-specific fitting using resampling and out-of-distribution evaluation, beyond raw endpoint accuracy.

papers.title: When Forgetting is not Catastrophic: On the Mechanics of Spurious Forgetting
papers.abstract: Knowledge that a language model appears to forget during finetuning often remains stored and can be recovered, a phenomenon called spurious forgetting. Finetuning on new facts can even produce forgetting that undoes itself: recall of the old facts collapses, recovers as training continues on new facts alone, and only then erodes for good. We seek to understand when such forgetting is not catastrophic. A minimal associative memory reproduces these dynamics with three ingredients: keys with shared structure, concentrated new values, and normalization in the network. Finetuning moves all old representations along a common direction, hiding the old facts while preserving their relative geometry; normalization withdraws this shift once the new facts are learned, whereas fact-specific changes accumulate and cause the erosion. Moreover, subtracting the common shift eliminates the collapse in a Transformer trained on synthetic data, and removing a single direction from each weight update restores old facts in a pretrained language model. Forgetting thus combines a shared, reversible loss of access with a slow erosion of individual facts, and only the second is catastrophic. Which one dominates depends on whether the new data move old memories together or apart.
papers.ja_title: 忘れたように見える知識はなぜ戻るのか: 見かけ上の忘却の仕組み
papers.summary: ファインチューニング(追加学習)で言語モデルが古い知識を忘れたように見えても、実は保存されたままで取り出せることがある「見かけ上の忘却」という現象がある。本研究は、共有構造を持つキーと集中した新しい値、そしてネットワークの正規化という 3 要素だけでこの動きを再現する最小モデルを作り、追加学習が古い表現をまとめて一方向にずらして隠すだけであり、正規化が新事実を学ぶとその移動を打ち消すのに対し、個別の事実ごとの変化は蓄積して本当の侵食を起こすことを示した。さらに、Transformer から共通の移動方向を 1 つ差し引くだけで崩壊が解消し、事前学習済みモデルでも重み更新から 1 方向を除くだけで古い事実を復元できることを確認した。
papers.why: モデルの忘却を「共有的で可逆な隠れ」と「個別で不可逆な侵食」に分けて説明する枠組みで、継続学習や追加学習で知識を守る実装の手がかりになる。
papers.summary_en: Knowledge that a language model appears to forget during finetuning often remains stored and can be recovered — so-called spurious forgetting, where recall can even collapse, recover, and only later erode for good. A minimal associative-memory model with shared-structure keys, concentrated new values, and normalization reproduces this dynamic: finetuning shifts old representations along a shared direction that normalization later withdraws once new facts are learned, while fact-specific drift accumulates and causes the real erosion. Subtracting the common shift eliminates the collapse in a synthetic Transformer, and removing a single direction from each weight update restores old facts in a pretrained language model.
papers.why_en: It offers a mechanistic framework separating a shared, reversible hiding of knowledge from a slow, catastrophic erosion, giving a concrete handle for protecting knowledge during continual/finetuning updates.

papers.title: Sherpa: Teaching LLMs to Teach Adaptively
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have become increasingly capable problem solvers, but being able to solve a problem is not the same as being able to teach it. Existing approaches to training LLMs as teachers rely on demonstrations, preference data, or predefined pedagogical criteria that specify what good teaching looks like. However, these signals are often not grounded in individual student learning outcomes, where effective teaching strategies can vary substantially across learners. To address this, we introduce Sherpa, a multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that instantiates multiple student archetypes with LLMs conditioned on distinct learning preferences and trains a teacher model to adapt its instruction by directly maximizing their learning outcomes. Teacher LLMs trained with Sherpa improve instructed students' performance across all archetypes by an average of 20.5 percentage points. Under MathTutorBench's evaluation, Sherpa raises the overall pedagogy score from 52.5% to 79.2%, indicating better teaching responses. Our human studies show that the trained teacher is preferred over the base model in 79.6% of pairwise comparisons. Together, Sherpa trains LLM teachers to adapt to diverse simulated students and become better aligned with human teachers, paving the road towards AI tutors teaching real students.

papers.title: On KL-Regularized Policy Optimization
papers.abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) for large language model (LLM) agents trains one policy on trajectories generated by another: rollouts come from stale checkpoints, and the inference engine's probabilities differ from the trainer's even at identical parameters. Standard remedies either clip importance ratios, which biases the update, or, as in GRPO, sample a group of responses per prompt, which is costly when episodes are long. We propose KL-Regularized Policy Optimization (KLPO), a framework that anchors the KL regularizer at the sampler. The regularized improvement step then has a closed-form Gibbs solution, and KLPO fits its log-ratio optimality condition by least squares on the sampler's own trajectories, so the sampler probability enters through a log-ratio and no importance weights are needed. Profiling out the regression intercept replaces the intractable log-partition function with the signal's sampler mean plus a sampler-to-trainer KL divergence. For token-level policy mirror descent targets, we show that the resulting gradient can be computed from terminal returns without a critic, via sampler-centered scores or a single trajectory residual, even under stochastic tool outputs. We further prove that independent Monte Carlo estimates of the KL term keep these gradients unbiased, derive the exact KL gap of cheaper top-$K$ and binary approximations, and show that SPPO, GPO, REBEL, and BPO arise as special cases of KLPO. The result is a critic-free update that uses one rollout per prompt and requires neither a learned normalizer nor a group of responses.
papers.ja_title: サンプラー基準のKL正則化で非同期RLのインポータンス重みを不要にする
papers.summary: LLM(大規模言語モデル)エージェントの非同期強化学習では、古いチェックポイントで生成した軌跡を新しい方針が学習するため、推論エンジンの確率と学習側の確率がずれてしまう。既存手法はインポータンス比をクリップして偏りを生むか、GRPO のようにプロンプトごとに複数の応答を集めてコストをかけるしかなかった。本研究は KL 正則化をサンプラー側に固定した KL-Regularized Policy Optimization(KLPO)を提案し、クリティック(価値関数)なし・プロンプト 1 件につき 1 回のロールアウトだけで勾定を最小二乗で求められることを示し、SPPO・GPO・REBEL・BPO はこの枠組みの特殊な場合になることを示した。
papers.why: インポータンス重みや学習済み正規化項、グループサンプリングを必要としない RL 更新則は、非同期・長エピソードな LLM エージェント学習の計算コストを下げる実装の土台になる。
papers.summary_en: Asynchronous RL for LLM agents trains one policy on trajectories from stale checkpoints, so sampler and trainer probabilities diverge even at identical parameters; existing fixes either bias updates via importance-ratio clipping or incur the cost of GRPO-style group sampling per prompt. The authors propose KL-Regularized Policy Optimization (KLPO), which anchors the KL regularizer at the sampler, yielding a closed-form Gibbs solution fit by least squares on the sampler's own trajectories without importance weights, with a critic-free gradient computable from terminal returns using one rollout per prompt; SPPO, GPO, REBEL, and BPO arise as special cases of this framework.
papers.why_en: A critic-free RL update that needs neither importance weights, a learned normalizer, nor grouped sampling lowers the computational cost of asynchronous, long-episode LLM agent training, serving as a practical building block for RL post-training infrastructure.

papers.title: Socio-Foundation: A Model for Generalizable Individual Behavior Simulation via Hierarchical Capability Distillation
papers.abstract: Simulating individual behavior requires large language models (LLMs) to preserve persona traits while adapting to dynamic social contexts. However, general-purpose LLMs often flatten distinct personas, while task-specific tuning suffers from fragmentation and generalization. To overcome these challenges, we organize individual simulation into the \textbf{FONTS Taxonomy}, comprising five complementary capability dimensions: \emph{persona fidelity} (\textbf{F}), \emph{outcome realization} (\textbf{O}), \emph{behavioral naturalness} (\textbf{N}), \emph{trajectory coherence} (\textbf{T}), and \emph{social grounding} (\textbf{S}). Grounded in this taxonomy, we curate a standardized training corpus library of approximately 10 million instances across 14 representative datasets and present \textbf{Socio-Foundation}. Socio-Foundation decouples specialization from integration via a three-stage pipeline: learning task experts via DAPO, consolidating them into capability experts via off-policy distillation, and unifying them via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). We also establish \textbf{IndiEval}, consolidating 29 metrics across the FONTS dimensions. Experiments show that Socio-Foundation outperforms its \textit{Qwen3-8B} base by 11.0 points and approaches frontier models such as \textit{GLM-5.2}, with ablations and out-of-distribution evaluations further demonstrating the effectiveness and generalization of our model.

papers.title: The Best Optimizer Depends on Batch Size
papers.abstract: A plethora of new adaptive optimizers are designed to efficiently estimate and use minibatch gradient statistics to shape parameter updates, but they are typically benchmarked at a single batch size. Hyperparameter scaling rules promise to preserve performance as batch size and gradient noise change, suggesting that the best optimizer at one batch size should remain the best at another. We challenge this approach to developing and evaluating optimizers by showing: (1) no principled scaling rule for Muon works consistently across training settings, and (2) the best optimizer for language model pretraining changes with batch size even after extensive hyperparameter tuning. To understand these failures, we analyze a noisy quadratic model and show that the batch-size scaling rule that preserves performance is direction-dependent, shifting from square-root to linear as a direction's curvature-to-noise ratio rises. We further prove that gradient noise drives a bias-variance tradeoff in preconditioning that can reverse optimizer rankings across batch sizes, even under optimal learning rate and momentum tuning. Consistent with this, when we increase the batch size $16\times$ partway through language model pretraining, keeping small-batch updates in only the sharpest $0.001\%$ of directions removes up to $59.5\%$ of the resulting loss gap over the next $8\%$ of training, while a random subspace of the same size barely helps. Taken together, our results show that principled optimizer design must account for batch size and empirical benchmarking should be performed across batch sizes.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 最適なオプティマイザはバッチサイズで変わる
papers.summary: バッチサイズが変わると、どの最適化アルゴリズム（オプティマイザ）が一番良いかも変わってしまうという問題を調べた。著者らは Muon など新しいオプティマイザのバッチサイズ拡大則（スケーリングルール）が一貫して成立しないことを示し、言語モデルの事前学習で最良のオプティマイザがバッチサイズごとに入れ替わることを確認した。ノイズ付き二次モデルで分析すると、性能を保つスケーリング則は方向ごとに異なり、曲率とノイズの比が高い方向では平方根則から線形則へ移ることを示した。バッチサイズを学習途中で 16 倍にした実験では、最も尖った 0.001% の方向だけ小バッチ時の更新を残すと、その後の学習の 8% で生じる損失差の最大 59.5% を解消できたが、同サイズのランダムな部分空間ではほとんど効果がなかった。
papers.why: オプティマイザの比較やハイパーパラメータのスケーリング則を設計する際、バッチサイズを固定したベンチマークでは結論が誤る可能性があることを示し、分散学習で大バッチ訓練を行う際の最適化アルゴリズム選定に直接関わる知見。
papers.summary_en: The paper studies how batch size changes which optimizer performs best for language model pretraining. The authors show that no principled scaling rule for Muon works consistently across training settings, and that the best optimizer for pretraining changes with batch size even after extensive hyperparameter tuning. Using a noisy quadratic model, they prove that the batch-size scaling rule that preserves performance is direction-dependent, shifting from square-root to linear as curvature-to-noise ratio rises, and that gradient noise drives a bias-variance tradeoff that can reverse optimizer rankings across batch sizes. When batch size is increased 16x partway through pretraining, keeping small-batch updates in only the sharpest 0.001% of directions removes up to 59.5% of the resulting loss gap over the next 8% of training, while a random subspace of the same size barely helps.
papers.why_en: Shows that optimizer benchmarking and hyperparameter scaling rules must account for batch size, directly relevant to anyone choosing optimizers for large-batch distributed pretraining.

review.note: オプティマイザの優劣を一つのバッチサイズだけで比較するベンチマークは誤った結論を導く恐れがあるという、測り方自体を問う観点。
review.note_en: Shows that benchmarking optimizers at a single batch size can yield misleading rankings, a methodology point for how to measure and compare optimizers.

papers.title: PhysEvo: Astra Can Act, Let It
papers.abstract: Astra can act, yet reliable manipulation depends on the system through which it observes and controls the world. We introduce PhysEvo, a framework for physical recursive self-improvement (RSI) around a single frozen model. A task agent executes robot tasks; a meta-agent uses the resulting trajectories to diagnose failures, revise tools and skills, and test corrections. The meta-agent can also improve its own diagnostic tools, so retained revisions support both later action and later self-improvement. This process develops joint-level control, evidence-seeking observation, and reusable manipulation skills without model-weight updates or a separately trained action policy. Across 42 RoboDojo tasks, held-out-layout evaluation of retained task-specific deployment versions yields a five-dimension average score of 68.14/100 and 62.00% success, compared with 47.17% for RoboDawn's one-shot Astra agent, the strongest published reference in our comparison. On eight manipulation tasks challenging direct Astra, PhysEvo achieves 55.00% success, compared with 1.25% for the direct-Astra reference. Deploying the simulation-evolved harness on AgileX PiPER and continuing skill revision yields 90.60/100 average score and 84.00% success across 25 trials on five real-world tasks. PhysEvo turns the consequences of action into persistent, testable changes to how a frozen model acts and improves.

papers.title: A Self-Pruning Transformer: Extreme KV-Cache Compression with Universal Attention
papers.abstract: The large KV-cache size of modern LLMs creates a barrier to efficient deployment. Recent work has explored replacing attention layers' RoPE positional embeddings with alternative decay-based mechanisms, which can then be used to prune KV-cache during inference. However, these decay functions have limited expressivity, and in practice devolve into sliding-window-like eviction patterns. In this work, we propose a unifying framework for complementary and novel decay mechanisms, capturing complex key statistics and interactions while preserving expressive RoPE embeddings and Softmax attention. The resulting Universal Attention is a highly expressive and end-to-end trainable architecture, whose composite decay mechanism acts as a natural, $\textit{adaptive}$ pruning criterion, removing tokens that contribute least to attention computation. Experimentally, Universal Attention achieves state-of-the-art $10\times$ compression on natural language and synthetic task data, while $\textit{improving}$ downstream performance compared to both state-of-the-art baselines and unpruned oracles. It further demonstrates superior long-context generalization with unprecedented $25\times$ compression at length 16k.
papers.ja_title: 普遍アテンションで KV キャッシュを最大 25 倍圧縮
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルの推論を遅くする KV キャッシュ（過去の計算結果を保存するメモリ）の肥大化が課題。本研究は位置情報の埋め込み（RoPE）や通常の Softmax アテンションを保ったまま、キーの統計情報を柔軟に捉える減衰機構を導入した「普遍アテンション」を提案し、アテンション計算への寄与が少ないトークンを適応的に刈り取る。自然言語タスクと合成タスクで 10 倍の圧縮を達成しつつ既存の最良手法や刈り取りをしていないモデルより性能が上回り、長さ 16k の長文脈では前例のない 25 倍圧縮も実現した。
papers.why: RoPE の表現力を損なわずに学習ベースの適応的な KV キャッシュ刈り取りを実現しており、長文脈推論のメモリ削減を狙う推論基盤の設計に直結する成果。
papers.summary_en: Large KV-cache size is a major barrier to efficient LLM deployment, and prior decay-based alternatives to RoPE tend to collapse into sliding-window-like eviction. The authors propose Universal Attention, a unifying, end-to-end trainable framework of decay mechanisms that preserves expressive RoPE embeddings and Softmax attention while acting as an adaptive pruning criterion. It achieves state-of-the-art 10x compression on natural language and synthetic tasks while improving downstream performance over both state-of-the-art baselines and unpruned oracles, and demonstrates unprecedented 25x compression at 16k context length.
papers.why_en: Offers a learned, adaptive KV-cache pruning mechanism that keeps RoPE's expressivity, directly useful for building memory-efficient long-context inference serving.

papers.title: What Bloats Your Floats? Right-Sizing Numerical Precision for Scientific Computing
papers.abstract: While FP64 (binary64) remains the standard representation of real numbers in scientific computing, hardware trends increasingly favor low-precision formats optimized for AI workloads. This shift prioritizes throughput and energy efficiency over full-precision capabilities. We challenge the necessity of high-precision arithmetic in PDE-governed simulations, where spatial and temporal discretization errors introduce a physical noise floor that masks the lower-order bits of the FP64 format, rendering them irrelevant. We propose a criterion based on the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) with respect to spatial and temporal refinements to evaluate the impact of safe precision reduction on scientific computations. Finally, we present an automated dataflow-centric workflow for targeted lowering within mixed-precision subgraphs in complex scientific applications. Large-scale evaluations of weather and climate applications show that strategic precision reduction on GPUs achieves up to 1.8x speedup without compromising physical fidelity.
papers.ja_title: 科学計算の浮動小数点精度は本当に FP64 が必要か
papers.summary: 天気予報や気候シミュレーションなどの科学計算では現在も FP64（64 ビット浮動小数点数）が標準だが、AI 向けの低精度演算の方が処理速度や省エネに優れる。本研究は、偏微分方程式を離散化する際に生じる誤差（物理的なノイズ）が FP64 の下位ビットをどうせかき消してしまうことに着目し、信号対雑音比（SNR）を基準に精度をどこまで落とせるか判定する基準を提案した。さらに混合精度のサブグラフを自動で見つけて精度を下げる自動化ワークフローを作り、気象・気候の大規模計算に適用したところ、物理的な正確さを損なわずに GPU 上で最大 1.8 倍の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: LLM に限らず科学計算全般での低精度化の判定基準と自動混合精度ワークフローを示しており、カーネル・低精度最適化の設計パターンとして参考になる。
papers.summary_en: FP64 remains the standard in scientific computing even as hardware increasingly favors low-precision formats built for AI workloads. The authors argue that in PDE-governed simulations, spatial and temporal discretization errors create a physical noise floor that masks FP64's lower-order bits, and propose a Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) criterion to judge how far precision can be safely reduced. They present an automated dataflow-centric workflow for targeted precision lowering within mixed-precision subgraphs, and large-scale evaluations on weather and climate applications show up to 1.8x GPU speedup without compromising physical fidelity.
papers.why_en: Provides a principled criterion and automated workflow for mixed-precision lowering beyond LLMs, useful as a design pattern for kernel/low-precision optimization work generally.

papers.title: MaRK: Markov-adapted Recurrent Kernels for Dynamic Operator Conditioning in State Space Models
papers.abstract: State Space Models (SSMs) offer an efficient alternative to Transformers for sequence modeling, yet conditioning pre-trained SSMs for iterative generation typically operates outside the recurrent operator, through input injection or activation modulation. While such mechanisms expose the model to conditioning information, they leave the underlying temporal dynamics fixed. We introduce MaRK (Markov-adapted Recurrent Kernels), a dynamic operator-conditioning framework that maps context vectors directly into bounded modulations of a frozen SSM's recurrence ($A$), read-in ($B$), read-out ($C$), skip ($D$), and discretization ($Δ$) parameters. Viewed through the lens of LPV-SSM systems, MaRK induces a context-indexed family of Markov parameter sequences, allowing each diffusion timestep to reshape the model's input-output memory kernel. We instantiate MaRK on a frozen 111M-parameter Hydra SSM backbone and study three adapter geometries: Hypernet, Chebyshev polynomial, and Discrete Cosine Transform kernels. Since these adapters modify the Markov parameter sequence through low-rank auxiliary maps on the frozen backbone, parameter-efficient fine-tuning arises as a structural consequence of the adaptation mechanism itself, requiring only 6.3--11M trainable auxiliary parameters to transition from a bidirectional objective to an iterative diffusion regime. The bounded recurrence parameterization further yields an analytic Affine Quadratic Stability certificate for the modulated recurrence. Through synthetic LPV recovery experiments and Markov-operator diagnostics, we show that MaRK recovers coordinate-invariant temporal operators under matched assumptions and produces distinct, stable timestep-conditioned memory profiles. Empirically, the Chebyshev variant yields the strongest performance, achieving an average validation loss of 2.55, followed by the DCT (2.59) and Hypernet (3.77) geometries.
papers.ja_title: MaRK: 状態空間モデルの再帰演算子をコンテキストで直接変調
papers.summary: 状態空間モデル（SSM）は Transformer より効率的な系列モデルだが、事前学習済みの SSM を条件付けする従来手法は再帰の外側（入力の加算や活性の調整）に留まり、時間方向の力学自体は固定されたままという課題があった。本研究の MaRK は、コンテキスト情報を SSM の再帰パラメータ（A, B, C, D, Δ）に直接かつ有界に変調する仕組みを導入し、拡散モデルの各タイムステップごとにモデルの記憶の仕方を変えられるようにした。111M パラメータの凍結 SSM（Hydra）上で検証し、学習が必要な追加パラメータはわずか 6.3〜11M で双方向の目的から反復的な拡散処理へ切り替えられ、最良の Chebyshev 型アダプタは検証損失 2.55（DCT は 2.59、Hypernet は 3.77）を達成した。
papers.why: 事前学習済み SSM のバックボーンを凍結したまま再帰演算子そのものを低ランクに適応させる手法で、パラメータ効率の良いファインチューニングやモデル構造の拡張設計に新しい視点を与える。
papers.summary_en: State Space Models offer an efficient alternative to Transformers, but existing methods for conditioning pre-trained SSMs operate outside the recurrent operator via input injection or activation modulation, leaving the underlying temporal dynamics fixed. MaRK instead maps context vectors directly into bounded modulations of a frozen SSM's recurrence (A), read-in (B), read-out (C), skip (D), and discretization (Δ) parameters, letting each diffusion timestep reshape the model's memory kernel. Instantiated on a frozen 111M-parameter Hydra backbone, MaRK requires only 6.3-11M trainable auxiliary parameters to move from a bidirectional objective to an iterative diffusion regime, with the Chebyshev adapter variant achieving the strongest average validation loss of 2.55, versus 2.59 for DCT and 3.77 for Hypernet.
papers.why_en: Proposes adapting the recurrent operator itself of a frozen pretrained SSM backbone through low-rank auxiliary maps, offering a new angle on parameter-efficient fine-tuning and architectural extension for SSM-based models.

papers.title: Same Text, Different Prediction: Serving-Context Nondeterminism in Text Classifiers
papers.abstract: Deterministic inference is essential for reliable and trustworthy machine learning. Prior studies of text generation have shown that changing factors such as batch size, batch composition, hardware, or inference engine can alter the generated text, even when the prompt, model parameters, and sampling randomness are fixed. These differences have been attributed in part to floating-point non-associativity, shape-dependent kernel selection, and other implementation-level differences in numerical execution. However, it remains unclear whether, when, and to what extent the same factors affect text classification. We present a systematic study of serving-context non-invariance in text classifiers, which prior work has measured only through generated text. We train 180 models spanning discriminative, pseudo-generative, and fully generative classifier formulations and evaluate each across four categories of serving contexts, holding the checkpoint and the text fixed. Label stability does not imply score stability. Changing only the batch shape changes no labels across fp32 comparisons, yet under bf16 it moves up to 56.7 percentage points of predicted probability mass, with label changes concentrated at small margins. Fully generative classifiers change more labels than their discriminative counterparts under the same serving changes. We derive sufficient conditions for label stability under each serving change and give a separate mitigation for each mechanism. Our results identify and quantify the serving conditions that must be fixed for reproducible text classification.
papers.ja_title: 同じ文章でも推論環境が違うと分類結果が変わる問題
papers.summary: 同じプロンプトやモデルの重みを固定しても、バッチサイズや計算順序などの違いで生成される文章が変わることは知られていたが、文章分類（テキストクラシファイア）でも同じことが起きるかは分かっていなかった。著者らは識別型・疑似生成型・完全生成型の 180 個のモデルを学習し、チェックポイントと入力文章を固定したまま 4 種類の推論環境（サービングコンテキスト）で比較した。ラベル（分類結果）が安定していても確信度のスコアは安定とは言えず、バッチの形だけを変えると fp32 ではラベルは変わらないが bf16 では予測確率の最大 56.7 ポイント分が移動し、完全生成型の分類器は識別型より多くのラベルが変わった。著者らはラベルが安定するための十分条件と、それぞれの原因に対する対処法を示した。
papers.why: 推論サービングの実装差（バッチ形状、ハードウェア、浮動小数点の非結合性など）が分類結果の再現性を壊すことを定量的に示し、推論基盤を再現可能に作るための具体的な検証観点を与える。
papers.summary_en: Prior work showed that serving-context factors like batch size, batch composition, hardware, or inference engine can change generated text even with fixed prompts and weights; it was unclear whether the same holds for text classification. The authors train 180 models spanning discriminative, pseudo-generative, and fully generative classifier formulations and evaluate each across four categories of serving contexts with the checkpoint and text held fixed. They find label stability does not imply score stability: changing only batch shape changes no labels under fp32, yet under bf16 it shifts up to 56.7 percentage points of predicted probability mass, and fully generative classifiers change more labels than discriminative ones under the same serving changes. They derive sufficient conditions for label stability under each serving change and give a mitigation for each mechanism.
papers.why_en: Quantifies how serving implementation differences (batch shape, precision, hardware, floating-point non-associativity) break reproducibility in text classification, giving concrete conditions to check when building reproducible inference serving.

review.note: 推論サービングの違い（バッチ形状・精度・ハードウェア）がラベルやスコアの再現性に与える影響を、条件を一つずつ固定して切り分ける検証手法。
review.note_en: A methodology for isolating which serving-context factors (batch shape, precision, hardware) break label/score reproducibility by holding other conditions fixed.

papers.title: GeoNatureAgent (GNA): A Framework and Benchmark for Pre-Production Evaluation of Tool-Using Agents on Geospatial and Environmental Tasks
papers.abstract: Before tool-using LLM agents are deployed in environmental and geospatial workflows, teams need evidence that an agent reliably selects the right operations against real APIs. We introduce GeoNatureAgent (GNA), a framework for pre-production evaluation of tool-using agents: a fixed sixteen-tool geospatial interface published as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, so the agent under test is the only variable, scored against an identical tool layer, task suite, and deterministic scorer. Its flagship instance is a 103-task benchmark (a 93-task main suite across 18 categories plus a ten-task comparison expansion) evaluated against an open, self-hostable geospatial API serving three environmental indicators across Spain and Portugal. We evaluate nine LLMs under three temperature-1.0 seeds, reporting capability and per-case cost as orthogonal axes. (1) Claude Sonnet 4 achieves the highest capability (61.7% +/- 0.7% on all 103 tasks; 60.8% on the main suite), followed closely by DeepSeek V3.2 (57.9%), while no other model exceeds 53%; (2) the cost-accuracy Pareto frontier is mostly open-weight, with DeepSeek V3.2 offering 93% of Claude's capability at 11.3x lower list-price cost; (3) under strict all-checks scoring the best model sits 24-36 points below the 85-97% reported on general-purpose GIS benchmarks, whereas per-check partial credit for the top four models (86-90%) is comparable, so much of that gap reflects scoring strictness rather than task difficulty alone. The MCP server, evaluation harness, benchmark, and API are publicly available; swapping the tool executors and task suite instantiates an equivalent benchmark for any geospatial domain.

papers.title: Compiling Semi-Ring Dynamic Programming to Tier-Aware 3D-DRAM Processing-in-Memory
papers.abstract: Processing-in-Memory (PIM) on monolithic 3D (M3D) DRAM is a promising answer to the memory wall for data-intensive dynamic programming (DP), yet extracting its performance today demands hand-written kernels: the programmer must pick a tile size, place data across non-uniform-latency memory tiers, partition work between heterogeneous processing units, and insert the right broadcasts and queues by hand. We present GenMLIR, an MLIR compiler that automates this mapping for tier-aware 3D PIM. GenMLIR encodes the semi-ring generalized grid update, the algebraic form shared by all-pairs shortest path (APSP) and sequence alignment, as a first-class IR abstraction, and lowers it through four GenDRAM-aware pass groups that derive blocked tiling, tier-aware placement, tile-to-PU assignment, and explicit communication. We also characterize precisely which DP recurrences the abstraction admits and which it does not. On the GenDRAM architecture, GenMLIR-generated code runs up to 5.8 (APSP) and 16.7 (alignment) faster than a lowering without compiler support, and 1.2-1.4 faster than a standard affine-tiling PIM compiler we also implement, reaching 90-100% of an achievable-performance bound. It expresses these workloads in 4-9 lines instead of 300-500 and compiles in a negligible fraction of runtime.
papers.ja_title: 3D DRAM 内処理向けに動的計画法カーネルを自動生成するコンパイラ GenMLIR
papers.summary: 3D 積層 DRAM 内で計算を行う PIM(メモリ内処理)向けに、最短路計算や配列アライメントなどの動的計画法カーネルは今まで手書きでタイルサイズや階層配置、処理ユニット割当を調整する必要があった。著者らはこれを半環の一般化グリッド更新として中間表現に落とし込み、自動でタイル分割・階層配置・通信挿入を行う MLIR コンパイラ GenMLIR を作った。全対最短路で最大 5.8 倍、配列アライメントで最大 16.7 倍速くなり、達成可能性能の 90〜100% に達し、コードは 300〜500 行から 4〜9 行に減った。
papers.why: メモリ階層を意識したカーネル自動生成の仕組みとして、PIM やメモリ内蔵アクセラレータ向けのコンパイラ基盤設計に直接参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Dynamic-programming kernels (shortest path, sequence alignment) on monolithic 3D PIM DRAM today require hand-tuned tiling, tier placement, PU assignment, and communication insertion. The authors encode the semi-ring generalized grid update as a first-class IR abstraction and build GenMLIR, an MLIR compiler that automates this mapping through four tier-aware pass groups. GenMLIR-generated code runs up to 5.8x (APSP) and 16.7x (alignment) faster than an unoptimized lowering, reaching 90-100% of an achievable-performance bound, while shrinking code from 300-500 lines to 4-9 lines.
papers.why_en: Offers a concrete compiler abstraction and pass pipeline for tier-aware memory placement and PU assignment, directly useful for anyone building compilers for PIM or memory-centric accelerators.

papers.title: Q-PACE: Dynamic Precision Allocation for Quantization-Aware Training
papers.abstract: Quantization-aware training (QAT) leverages lower-precision arithmetic to reduce the cost of LLM deployment, but aggressive quantization degrades final model performance. A common remedy is mixed-precision training, in which high precision is assigned to some of the layers to maintain performance while keeping the cost constrained. This approach then requires precision assignments for model layers during training. We provide a new approach, called Q-PACE, consisting of a second-order sensitivity model that predicts the loss increase as a sum of quantization noise MSE weighted by per-layer curvature coefficients. During training, we periodically re-compute these coefficients using perturbations across layers, and re-assign precision. Pretraining and supervised fine-tuning experiments on LLMs of up to 4B parameters show that Q-PACE consistently improves over existing mixed-precision training recipes, and achieves comparable loss at substantially lower total memory budgets. We further find that quantization sensitivity is highly predictable by depth and layer type, and its stability during training allows for infrequent, cheap recalibration.
papers.ja_title: 層ごとの量子化感度を推定して精度配分を動的に決める Q-PACE
papers.summary: 量子化対応学習(QAT)で混合精度を使う際、どの層に高精度を割り振るかを決めるのが難しい。著者らは各層の曲率(感度)から損失増加を予測する二次モデルを作り、学習中に時々再計算して精度配分を更新する Q-PACE を提案した。最大 4B パラメータの LLM の事前学習・ファインチューニングで、既存の混合精度 QAT 手法より同じメモリ予算でより良い損失を達成し、感度は層の深さや種類で予測しやすく安定しているため低頻度な再計算で十分だと分かった。
papers.why: 混合精度の割り当てを静的な直感ではなく感度モデルで動的に決める実用的な方法として、QAT パイプラインを設計する人にすぐ適用できる。
papers.summary_en: Mixed-precision QAT needs a way to decide which layers get higher precision, but this assignment is usually hand-tuned. The authors propose Q-PACE, a second-order sensitivity model predicting loss increase from per-layer curvature-weighted quantization noise, periodically recalibrated during training to reassign precision. On LLMs up to 4B parameters, Q-PACE consistently beats existing mixed-precision training recipes and reaches comparable loss at substantially lower memory budgets, while sensitivity proves highly predictable by depth/layer type and stable enough for infrequent, cheap recalibration.
papers.why_en: Gives a concrete, learned sensitivity model for dynamic mixed-precision assignment that practitioners building QAT pipelines can plug in directly.

papers.title: Few Bits, One Law: Toward W2A4KV2
papers.abstract: Extreme low-bit LLM compression is most challenging when weights, activations, and KV caches are quantized together: their distributions differ, and quantization errors interact throughout the network. We introduce CanonQ, a unified quantization-aware training framework that addresses these challenges by separating source canonicalization from task-aware adaptation. Fixed rotations and energy normalization map heterogeneous tensor sources to canonical coordinates, enabling frozen Gaussian-reference codebooks to be reused across layers and models. Joint training then adapts the network to the coupled errors of weight, activation, and cache quantization within a common scalar/vector interface. We bound frozen-codebook transfer error and local task loss, and derive an exact normalization-aware straight-through Jacobian that links quantization distortion to gradient bias. The strongest gains arise under joint W2A4KV2 compression: across LLaMA3-1B/3B/8B, CanonQ-Omni achieves up to 14.28x lower WikiText-2 perplexity and up to 57.9% higher mean zero-shot accuracy than prior state-of-the-art and representative quantization baselines. The benefits extend to Qwen3-1.7B, code generation, and mathematical reasoning: on instruction-tuned MobileLLM-Pro-1B at W2A16KV16, CanonQ achieves relative improvements of 41.7% in HumanEval pass@1 and 39.1% in GSM8K exact match over the strongest evaluated quantization baseline.
papers.ja_title: 重み・活性化・KV キャッシュを同時に極低ビット化する CanonQ
papers.summary: 重み・活性化・KV キャッシュを同時に極低ビット(例えば 2 ビット)に量子化すると、分布の違いと誤差の相互作用で性能が落ちやすい問題がある。著者らは固定の回転とエネルギー正規化で異なる種類の値を共通の座標に揃え、固定のガウス参照コードブックを層やモデル間で再利用できるようにした統合 QAT 手法 CanonQ を提案した。W2A4KV2 の設定で LLaMA3 系モデルにおいて、既存最良手法より WikiText-2 のパープレキシティを最大 14.28 倍低く、ゼロショット精度を最大 57.9% 高くし、命令チューニング済みモデルでも HumanEval と GSM8K で大きく改善した。
papers.why: 重み・活性化・KV キャッシュの同時極低ビット化という最も難しい設定で誤差の相互作用を抑える具体的な設計(正準座標化+共有コードブック)を示しており、推論コスト削減を目指す量子化設計者に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Jointly quantizing weights, activations, and KV caches to extreme low bit-widths is especially hard because their distributions differ and quantization errors interact. The authors introduce CanonQ, which maps heterogeneous tensor sources to canonical coordinates via fixed rotations and energy normalization, letting frozen Gaussian-reference codebooks be reused across layers and models, then jointly trains to adapt to coupled errors. Under W2A4KV2, CanonQ-Omni achieves up to 14.28x lower WikiText-2 perplexity and up to 57.9% higher mean zero-shot accuracy than prior state-of-the-art on LLaMA3-1B/3B/8B, with large relative gains on HumanEval and GSM8K for instruction-tuned models.
papers.why_en: Provides a concrete recipe (canonicalization + shared codebooks) for taming error interaction in the hardest joint weight/activation/KV-cache extreme quantization setting, directly useful to anyone designing low-bit inference systems.

papers.title: SearchWorld: Spatial Value-Grounded Imagination for UAV Object Search via World Models
papers.abstract: Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) object search involves a closed loop of perception, decision-making, and action under partial observability. Urban environments pose several challenges: large search areas and narrow egocentric views limit coverage, dense 3D geometry constrains safe motion, and open-world instructions require identifying a specific target among distractors. Many existing methods mitigate partial observability through explicit maps or memory representations, yet remain largely reactive, reasoning over past observations without explicitly predicting future states. World models enable prospective reasoning through imagined rollouts. However, image-generating world models can incur high inference latency, while spatially grounded planning remains challenging for latent world models. We propose SearchWorld, a recurrent state-space world model that connects explicit spatial memory with value-guided imagination. The model maintains BEV exploration and obstacle memory and decodes a task-aware spatial value layer to guide search. A cognition-action network uses this learned spatial value prior to improve the policy through imagined rollouts, without training a separate scalar critic. Training progresses from world-model learning to expert imitation and imagination-based exploration refinement. On UAV-ON, SearchWorld improves the success rate to 23.8% (19.5% for the strongest published agent) and raises oracle success to 35.5%, while remaining robust on unseen scenes (19.9% success rate). By grounding imagination in explicit spatial representations, SearchWorld enables UAV agents to plan prospectively rather than react.

papers.title: Shared Low-rank Basis Factorization for Data-free Mixture-of-Experts Compression
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models decouple capacity from compute through sparse routing, but their large parameter count creates storage and serving challenges. We analyze three MoE compression families: expert pruning, expert merging, and weight reconstruction, and derive structural error bounds showing that pruning and merging can incur non-vanishing errors tied to routing and expert heterogeneity. In contrast, weight reconstruction avoids these structural costs by preserving expert structure and routing. Motivated by the analysis, we propose Shared Low-rank Basis Factorization (SLBF), a data-free weight reconstruction method that uses rank-$k$ bases shared among experts, enabling richer cross-expert sharing, faster convergence, and lower reconstruction error. A post-hoc gauge fixing removes redundant parameters at no representational cost. Across five MoE architectures spanning 16B to 122B parameters, SLBF consistently outperforms methods from all three compression families.
papers.ja_title: 専門家間で低ランク基底を共有して MoE をデータなしで圧縮する SLBF
papers.summary: 専門家混合(MoE)モデルはパラメータ数が多く保存や配信が大変だが、専門家を枝刈りしたり統合したりすると経路選択の違いや専門家の異質性に起因する誤差がなくならないことを理論的に示した。著者らは専門家構造と経路選択をそのまま保つ「重み再構成」の一種として、専門家間で低ランクの基底を共有する Shared Low-rank Basis Factorization (SLBF) を提案し、学習データなしで適用できるようにした。16B から 122B パラメータまでの 5 種類の MoE アーキテクチャで、枝刈り・統合・重み再構成のすべての既存手法を一貫して上回った。
papers.why: MoE 圧縮の 3 系統(枝刈り・統合・重み再構成)を誤差境界で比較した分析と、データなしで適用できる具体的な再構成手法を示しており、大規模 MoE の配信コストを下げたい人にすぐ使える。
papers.summary_en: MoE LLMs decouple capacity from compute but their huge parameter counts make storage and serving costly; the authors show theoretically that expert pruning and merging incur non-vanishing errors tied to routing and expert heterogeneity. They propose Shared Low-rank Basis Factorization (SLBF), a data-free weight-reconstruction method using rank-k bases shared among experts, which preserves expert structure and routing. Across five MoE architectures from 16B to 122B parameters, SLBF consistently outperforms methods from all three compression families (pruning, merging, reconstruction).
papers.why_en: Offers both a structural error-bound analysis comparing three MoE compression families and a concrete data-free reconstruction method, directly useful to anyone trying to cut serving cost for large MoE models.

papers.title: Democratizing MoE inference on commodity GPUs with CoMoE
papers.abstract: Deploying Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models relies heavily on Expert Parallelism, which generates intense inter-GPU communication. Consequently, state-of-the-art inference systems require high-bandwidth, P2P interconnects (e.g., NVLink) in datacenter GPUs to handle massive token routing, making deployment prohibitively expensive. Consumer GPUs offer comparable compute power at significantly lower cost, promising to democratize MoE inference for individuals and enable privacy-preserving local deployments. However, their bandwidth-limited (only weak PCIe bus bandwidth) and host-mediated interconnects (no P2P support) introduce severe communication bottlenecks. We present CoMoE, a communication-efficient MoE inference system that resolves this mismatch through novel host-centric routing. Our key insight is that the unique communication topology provides the opportunity to elevate the host to an active routing hub, which can fundamentally reduce communication volume and eliminate global synchronization-induced stalls. Specifically, for token dispatch, we introduce host-backed token multicast to write shared tokens to the host exactly once, eliminating outbound transmission redundancy. For token combine, we propose a fine-grained, token-level aggregation mechanism using host staging buffers, which replaces rigid global synchronization and mitigates straggler effects. Evaluation on RTX 5090 GPUs shows that CoMoE improves inference throughput by up to 1.46x, approaching the performance of NVLink-capable A800 GPUs at only 23.4% of the hardware cost.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: ホストを通信ハブにして安価な GPU 上で MoE 推論を高速化する CoMoE
papers.summary: 専門家混合(MoE)モデルの推論は専門家並列で GPU 間通信が激しく、NVLink のような高速な P2P 接続を持つ高価なデータセンター GPU が必要になる。著者らは PCIe のみで P2P 非対応の安価な GPU 向けに、CPU 側のホストを能動的な中継ハブとして使う CoMoE を提案し、共有トークンを一度だけホストに書き込むマルチキャストと、ホスト上のバッファでトークンごとに集約する仕組みで全体同期を省いた。RTX 5090 での評価では、ハードウェアコストが NVLink 搭載 A800 のわずか 23.4% でありながらスループットを最大 1.46 倍改善し、A800 に近い性能に達した。
papers.why: コモディティ GPU(PCIe・P2P 非対応)でも MoE の通信ボトルネックを解消できることを示しており、分散推論のコスト構造を変えうる具体的な設計を提供する。
papers.summary_en: MoE inference relies on Expert Parallelism, generating intense inter-GPU communication that typically demands expensive datacenter GPUs with NVLink-class P2P interconnects. The authors target bandwidth-limited, host-mediated consumer GPUs (PCIe, no P2P) and propose CoMoE, which elevates the host to an active routing hub: host-backed multicast writes shared tokens once for dispatch, and fine-grained host-staged aggregation replaces rigid global synchronization for combine. On RTX 5090 GPUs, CoMoE improves throughput by up to 1.46x, approaching NVLink-capable A800 performance at only 23.4% of the hardware cost.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates that MoE communication bottlenecks can be resolved on commodity, P2P-less GPUs, offering a concrete host-centric routing design relevant to anyone rethinking distributed inference cost structures.

papers.title: GeoPrior-Mamba: Structured Process Priors with Mamba for Fine-Resolution XCO2 Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Reconstructing fine-resolution column-averaged dry-air CO2 (XCO2) fields from sparse satellite observations requires models to infer spatial structure that is only weakly constrained by direct measurements. Existing learning-based methods typically treat environmental covariates as ordinary numerical inputs and must therefore learn heterogeneous source-sink relationships largely from sparse supervision. We introduce GeoPrior-Mamba, a multi-directional Mamba framework augmented with offline language-model-induced structured process priors. Rather than using a language model to predict XCO2, we use it before training to organize relative process knowledge for biospheric uptake, ecosystem respiration, and anthropogenic emissions into deterministic prior tables. These priors are spatially instantiated using geographic, ecological, emission-related, and seasonal information and are adaptively injected into the reconstruction backbone through a lightweight knowledge adapter. Using OCO-2 observations from 2018-2020, GeoPrior-Mamba achieves an RMSE of 0.81 ppm and an R2 of 0.93 on held-out observations, reducing RMSE by 48.2% relative to CAMS background interpolation and by 3.1% relative to Trans-XCO2 under the same evaluation protocol. Ablation experiments show a measurable contribution from the knowledge-prior branch and substantially faster convergence than the knowledge-free Mamba backbone. Independent TCCON evaluation further supports the consistency of the reconstructed fields with ground-based column CO2 measurements. These results suggest that language models can provide a practical mechanism for constructing structured process priors when globally consistent process-response representations are difficult to obtain directly, while remaining outside the numerical prediction loop.

papers.title: Lightweight and Versatile Learned Optimization by Recombination of Gradient History
papers.abstract: This paper presents a lightweight and versatile learned optimizer that dynamically recombines gradient history, represented as averages over disjoint time spans. The optimizer reduces the prediction space to one scalar coefficient per gradient average, shared by multiple parameters. Progressively averaging older gradients minimizes memory cost of long history, while keeping their contributions independently accessible. A 37k-parameter network trained in 0.87 GPU-hours generalizes zero-shot to unseen tasks, lowering validation loss by 9.1% and 0.4% on BERT-Tiny and GPT-Tiny, and improving test accuracy over Adam by 3.5 %p on a Vision Transformer and by 2.7 %p on average across nine graph models, with FLOPs overhead as low as 0.3%.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 勾配履歴を時間区間ごとに平均化して再結合する軽量な学習型オプティマイザ
papers.summary: 学習によって最適化手法そのものを作る「学習型オプティマイザ」は多くの場合パラメータ数が多く汎用性に欠けるという課題がある。著者らは勾配の履歴を互い違いの時間区間ごとの平均として表し、各平均につき 1 つのスカラー係数だけを予測する軽量な方式を提案し、古い勾配ほど粗く平均化してメモリ消費を抑えた。パラメータ数 37,000 のネットワークを GPU 時間わずか 0.87 時間で学習させるだけで未知タスクにゼロショットで汎化し、BERT-Tiny と GPT-Tiny で検証損失を 9.1% と 0.4% 下げ、Vision Transformer のテスト精度を Adam より 3.5 ポイント、9 種のグラフモデル平均で 2.7 ポイント改善し、計算量の増加はわずか 0.3% だった。
papers.why: 巨大なメタ学習コストをかけずに Adam 相当以上の性能を出す軽量な学習型オプティマイザとして、学習効率を上げたい実務者がすぐ試せる具体的な改善幅を示している。
papers.summary_en: Learned optimizers often suffer from large parameter counts and limited generality. The authors present a lightweight learned optimizer that dynamically recombines gradient history represented as averages over disjoint time spans, reducing the prediction space to one scalar coefficient per average while progressively coarsening older averages to limit memory cost. A 37k-parameter network trained in just 0.87 GPU-hours generalizes zero-shot to unseen tasks, lowering validation loss by 9.1% and 0.4% on BERT-Tiny and GPT-Tiny, improving test accuracy over Adam by 3.5 %p on a Vision Transformer and 2.7 %p on average across nine graph models, with FLOPs overhead as low as 0.3%.
papers.why_en: Shows a cheap-to-train learned optimizer that matches or beats Adam across varied architectures, giving practitioners a concrete, low-overhead option to try for improving training efficiency.

papers.title: Reproducible LLM Inference Benchmarking: A Sequential Isolation Protocol for Regression Testing
papers.abstract: Reproducible benchmarking of Large Language Model (LLM) inference is challenging because repeated measurements can vary with execution and system state. We present the Sequential Isolation Methodology, a controlled benchmarking and regression-testing protocol designed to reduce between-run measurement variance while deliberately varying workload concurrency. We evaluate three representative open-source LLMs on an NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU using vLLM 0.9.1 across six context sizes and eight concurrency levels, with five repetitions per configuration. The final protocol reduces average coefficient of variation (CV) from 15.2% in the least controlled methodology stage to 2.2% under the final protocol; using CV computed across the five repetition-level median (P50) TTFT values per configuration, 113 of 144 configurations (78.5%) achieve CV below 3%. The measurements also show a marked latency transition between 200 and 500 concurrent users on the tested stack and descriptive differences in P99 latency across the three models. We additionally provide an explicit cost break-even model with sensitivity to API pricing. The protocol is intended to provide a stable reference for reproducible comparison and regression testing rather than to predict absolute behavior under uncontrolled production traffic. Infrastructure-as-Code and benchmark scripts support replication of the experimental environment.
papers.ja_title: LLM 推論ベンチマークを再現可能にする逐次分離プロトコル
papers.summary: LLM 推論の速度測定は実行環境のばらつきで結果が安定しない(ばらつく)という問題がある。筆者らは「逐次分離手法」という計測手順を作り、A100 GPU 上で vLLM を使い 3 つのモデル・6 種類の文脈長・8 段階の同時接続数を 5 回ずつ測定した。この手順により、測定のばらつきを示す変動係数 (CV) が最も粗い手法の 15.2% から最終手法で 2.2% まで下がり、144 設定中 113 件 (78.5%) が CV 3% 未満になった。また、同時利用者数が 200〜500 の間で遅延が急に変わる点も見つかった。
papers.why: 推論ベンチマークの再現性を担保する具体的な手順と、インフラのコード化(IaC)まで公開している点が、回帰テストの基盤として使える。
papers.summary_en: Repeated LLM inference latency measurements vary with execution and system state, making benchmarking unreliable. The authors introduce the Sequential Isolation Methodology, tested on an A100 80GB GPU with vLLM 0.9.1 across three models, six context sizes, and eight concurrency levels with five repetitions each. The protocol reduces the average coefficient of variation (CV) from 15.2% in the least controlled stage to 2.2% in the final protocol, with 113 of 144 configurations (78.5%) reaching CV below 3%, and reveals a latency transition between 200 and 500 concurrent users.
papers.why_en: Provides a concrete, reproducible measurement protocol plus Infrastructure-as-Code for regression testing of inference serving stacks.

review.note: ベンチマークの変動係数(CV)を測り、手順を段階的に絞り込んで再現性を検証する測り方の例。
review.note_en: Shows how to measure and reduce benchmark variance (CV) stage by stage to validate reproducibility.

papers.title: Judging in Latent Space: Efficient Generative Reward Modeling via Semantics-Preserving Compression
papers.abstract: Reward modeling often requires jointly representing and reasoning over multiple evaluation criteria, yet verbalizing this process token by token can incur substantial inference cost. Recent work on latent reasoning suggests that continuous states may support this computation more compactly. We introduce LatentGRM, a latent evaluation framework built on semantic chunking, compression, and reconstruction. By using the structure of rubric-guided evaluations to guide compression, LatentGRM learns compact continuous trajectories that support autonomous pairwise judgments without generating textual assessments. A separate interpreter reconstructs evaluation text from these trajectories, providing an offline view of the information retained under compression. Under matched training data and backbones, LatentGRM achieves competitive aggregate preference accuracy relative to explicit Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) judges at both 4B and 8B scales. Across four benchmark domains, LatentGRM-8B compresses evaluation trajectories by 8.9--9.2x and reduces total judge inference time by 6.1--7.0x at vote@5. Controlled rubric interventions show that criterion-dependent preference information is carried through the latent sequence. Together, these results demonstrate that continuous latent evaluation can substantially reduce inference cost while preserving competitive judgment quality.
papers.ja_title: 潜在空間で審判する: 圧縮した連続表現による報酬モデルの高速化
papers.summary: LLM の出力を複数の評価基準で判定する報酬モデル(採点役のモデル)は、評価文をトークンごとに生成すると推論コストが大きいという課題がある。LatentGRM は評価過程を意味のまとまり(セマンティックチャンク)で圧縮し、文章化せずに連続した潜在表現のまま優劣判定を行う。4B と 8B のモデルで、同じ学習データ条件下で通常の教師ありファインチューニング判定器と同等の精度を保ちながら、8B モデルでは評価の軌跡を 8.9〜9.2 倍圧縮し、判定全体の推論時間を 6.1〜7.0 倍 (vote@5 条件) 短縮した。
papers.why: 報酬モデル・審判モデルの推論コストを大きく下げる圧縮手法で、RLHF やサービング時の判定コスト削減に直結する。
papers.summary_en: Reward modeling that verbalizes multi-criteria judgments token by token incurs substantial inference cost. LatentGRM compresses rubric-guided evaluation into compact continuous latent trajectories and performs pairwise judgments without generating text. Under matched training data and backbones, LatentGRM-8B achieves competitive aggregate preference accuracy versus explicit SFT judges while compressing evaluation trajectories by 8.9-9.2x and reducing total judge inference time by 6.1-7.0x at vote@5.
papers.why_en: A compression approach that substantially cuts inference cost for judge/reward models, directly relevant to reducing serving cost in RLHF-style pipelines.

papers.title: Dual-QK: Sharp Queries and Flat Keys for Prunable 2-bit KV Caches
papers.abstract: Long inputs and extended generation increase the storage and access costs of the key-value (KV) cache. Low-bit quantization reduces storage and memory traffic, while query-channel pruning can further reduce key-cache reads. Rotation-based quantization redistributes the energy of key outliers across channels. To maintain computational invariance, the same orthogonal transform must be applied to queries, preserving query-key dot products. However, this rotation can disperse query energy, weakening the separation between a few large components to retain and many small ones to prune. We introduce Dual-QK, which uses paired non-orthogonal query and key transforms to address this conflict. Using calibrated query and key statistics, Dual-QK combines partial key whitening with a query-aligned basis to balance key scales for INT2 quantization and concentrate query energy for dynamic channel pruning. Channel-0 protection and bucket-relative RoPE support low-bit accuracy over long contexts. Experiments on four models across five generative benchmarks and long-context retrieval tasks show improved accuracy over OSCAR on most tasks at 40% query-channel sparsity. At a 128K context, Dual-QK provides $6.8\times$ KV-cache compression and an estimated $8.3\times$ reduction in KV read volume relative to unpruned BF16. Under the evaluated configurations, our SGLang implementation achieves up to $3.75\times$ the decoding throughput of unpruned BF16.
papers.ja_title: Dual-QK: クエリとキーを別の変換で整える 2 bit KV キャッシュ圧縮
papers.summary: 長い文脈を扱う LLM では KV キャッシュ(過去の計算結果の保存)の容量とメモリ転送が問題になる。回転変換を使った低ビット量子化はキーの外れ値を抑えられるが、同じ変換をクエリにも使うとクエリのエネルギーが分散し、枝刈り(プルーニング)に必要な「重要な成分と不要な成分の差」が弱まってしまう。Dual-QK はキーとクエリに別々の変換を組み合わせることでこの矛盾を解き、40% のクエリチャネル枝刈りで既存手法 OSCAR より精度が上がり、128K 文脈で KV キャッシュを 6.8 倍、読み込み量を推定 8.3 倍圧縮し、SGLang 実装でデコード速度を最大 3.75 倍にした。
papers.why: KV キャッシュの低ビット量子化とチャネル枝刈りを両立させる具体的なトリックで、長文脈サービングのスループット向上に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Long-context LLM serving suffers from growing KV-cache storage and memory traffic. Rotation-based quantization reduces key outliers but, when the same orthogonal transform is applied to queries, disperses query energy and weakens channel-pruning separability. Dual-QK uses paired non-orthogonal query and key transforms to resolve this conflict, improving accuracy over OSCAR at 40% query-channel sparsity, achieving 6.8x KV-cache compression and an estimated 8.3x reduction in KV read volume at 128K context, with up to 3.75x higher decoding throughput in SGLang versus unpruned BF16.
papers.why_en: A concrete technique that reconciles low-bit KV quantization with channel pruning, directly useful for improving long-context serving throughput.

papers.title: Learning to Accumulate Knowledge with Mutual Information
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can improve their performance by reusing knowledge distilled from past interactions. However, curating new experiences into a knowledge bank that becomes more useful as it grows remains challenging. Effective knowledge accumulation should limit redundant overlap among entries and ensure that new knowledge contributes beyond what the bank already provides. Yet training a curator with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on standalone task success can reinforce general guidance even when it duplicates existing knowledge. Therefore, we propose Knowledge Weaver, a reinforcement learning framework that trains a language model to curate reusable knowledge from agent trajectories. We couple feedback inspired by token-wise mutual information (MI) with marginal success rewards to guide knowledge accumulation. Together, these signals encourage the curator to preserve distinct information from experience and produce entries that improve task success when added to existing knowledge. Standalone success rewards also favor entries that are useful on their own. On ALFWorld and WebShop, Knowledge Weaver achieves mean success rates of 54.0\% and 42.0\% with k=10 retrieved entries, exceeding GRPO by 16.9 and 18.7 percentage points, respectively. Its knowledge banks also outperform the evaluated prompt-based and established banks, including human-written banks, in overall ALFWorld success rate and WebShop score with the executor frozen. Our codebase is available at https://github.com/LaoKuiZe/Knowledge-Weaver.
papers.ja_title: 相互情報量で知識バンクを育てる LLM エージェントの経験蓄積法
papers.summary: LLM エージェントは過去の経験から学んだ知識を蓄積して使い回すと性能が上がるが、重複した知識ばかり増えると知識バンクの質が上がらないという課題がある。Knowledge Weaver は、トークン単位の相互情報量(どれだけ新しい情報が含まれるか)を使った信号と、タスク成功率を組み合わせて GRPO で知識の取捨選択モデルを学習する。ALFWorld と WebShop で、取得件数 10 件の設定で成功率 54.0% と 42.0% を達成し、通常の GRPO を 16.9 ポイントと 18.7 ポイント上回った。
papers.why: 知識バンクの重複を減らす強化学習の報酬設計で、エージェントの経験蓄積・継続学習の基盤として使える。
papers.summary_en: LLM agents can reuse distilled knowledge from past interactions, but curating entries that avoid redundancy while remaining useful is hard; training a curator on task success alone can reinforce duplicated guidance. Knowledge Weaver trains a curator with GRPO combining token-wise mutual-information feedback with marginal success rewards. On ALFWorld and WebShop with k=10 retrieved entries, it reaches mean success rates of 54.0% and 42.0%, exceeding plain GRPO by 16.9 and 18.7 percentage points respectively.
papers.why_en: A reward design that reduces redundancy in accumulated knowledge banks, useful as a foundation for agent experience accumulation and continual learning via RL.

papers.title: Cache the Encoder Within:Compact, Reusable Memory across LLM Queries
papers.abstract: Repeated queries over shared documents incur redundant encoding, while caching model states introduces persistent storage costs. Building on CoMem's intermediate-state interface, EncBank treats a pretrained LLM's lower layers as a reusable document encoder and compactly stores their outputs for an adapted upper-layer reader. A self-distilled suffix adapter is shared across storage precisions within each backbone, without quantization-specific retraining. Across five benchmark suites on three Qwen backbones spanning different sizes and full-attention and hybrid architectures, 4-bit storage keeps each reported benchmark aggregate within one score point of native-precision EncBank. In a fixed Qwen3-8B workload, it retains 28.1% of the native-precision persistent GPU store. Separate native-precision controls yield a 1.40x selected-pack prefill speedup over same-evidence, same-adapter text replay, at a 3.12-point RULER accuracy cost. A native-precision Qwen3.8-27B configuration also passes 70 of 89 Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks. EncBank thus combines reusable computation with compact memory, while task fidelity and end-to-end benefits remain dependent on the workload, preparation costs, and reuse frequency.
papers.ja_title: EncBank: LLM の下位層をエンコーダとして再利用する圧縮メモリ
papers.summary: 同じ文書に対する繰り返し質問は毎回エンコード(符号化)し直すのが無駄で、一方で計算結果をそのまま保存すると保存コストが大きいという問題がある。EncBank は事前学習済み LLM の下位層を再利用可能な文書エンコーダとして使い、その出力を圧縮して保存し、専用の読み取り用アダプタで上位層に読ませる。Qwen の 3 つのバックボーンで、4 bit 保存にしてもベンチマーク平均は元の精度から 1 点以内にとどまり、Qwen3-8B では GPU に常駐させる保存量を元の 28.1% まで減らせた。
papers.why: 文書エンコード結果を低ビットで圧縮保存し再利用する仕組みで、繰り返しクエリの多いサービングでの計算とメモリの両方を削減できる点が使える。
papers.summary_en: Repeated queries over shared documents cause redundant encoding, while caching model states introduces persistent storage costs. EncBank reuses a pretrained LLM's lower layers as a document encoder and compactly stores their outputs for an adapted upper-layer reader, with a shared self-distilled adapter across storage precisions. Across three Qwen backbones, 4-bit storage keeps each benchmark aggregate within one score point of native precision, and for Qwen3-8B it retains only 28.1% of the native-precision persistent GPU store.
papers.why_en: A scheme for compactly caching and reusing document encodings at low bit-width, useful for reducing both compute and memory in serving workloads with repeated queries.

papers.title: EdgeRock: Strong Reasoning at Constant Memory
papers.abstract: We present EdgeRock, a family of multimodal models that deliver strong reasoning at constant memory. Most models keep reasoning history in a key-value (KV) cache that grows with every token, consuming accelerator memory, limiting concurrent requests, and competing with perception and control on edge devices. With fixed history, memory is allocated once and never runs out, however long the model reasons. Constant memory alone is not new: bounded-state models (recurrent, state-space, and sliding-window) already achieve it, but often at the cost of reasoning, because they cannot keep the distant details that later reasoning needs. We therefore introduce Rock Memory Anchors (RMA): the model learns what is worth remembering and stores it as KV records in a fixed-size bank, directly readable however far back the source lies. EdgeRock-4B, our first open-source release, supports text and image reasoning and reaches 82.9% mean pass@1 on AIME 2024-2026, while the bounded-state models we evaluate reach at most 18.8%, even at 14B scale. This result is on par with leading compact models whose memory grows with reasoning. Compared with its source model, EdgeRock-4B uses up to 99.1% less KV cache and delivers up to 6.42$\times$ higher end-to-end batch throughput.
papers.ja_title: EdgeRock: メモリを一定に保ったまま強く推論するエッジ向けモデル
papers.summary: LLM の推論は長く思考するほど KV キャッシュが増え続け、エッジデバイスでのメモリ確保や同時処理数を圧迫するという問題がある。EdgeRock は「Rock Memory Anchors」という、思考の中で覚えておくべき情報だけを固定サイズの保存領域に残す仕組みを導入し、遠くの詳細も直接読み出せるようにした。EdgeRock-4B は AIME 2024-2026 で平均 pass@1 82.9% を達成し、既存の有限状態モデル(最大 14B でも 18.8%)を大きく上回りつつ、元のモデルに比べ KV キャッシュを最大 99.1% 削減、バッチ処理のスループットを最大 6.42 倍にした。
papers.why: メモリ量を固定しながら長い推論性能を落とさない仕組みで、エッジ・サービング両方で同時リクエスト数を増やせる点が実用的な新しさ。
papers.summary_en: LLM reasoning history is kept in a KV cache that grows with every token, straining accelerator memory and concurrency on edge devices; bounded-state models achieve constant memory but typically sacrifice reasoning quality. EdgeRock introduces Rock Memory Anchors, letting the model learn what to keep in a fixed-size, directly-readable KV bank regardless of distance. EdgeRock-4B reaches 82.9% mean pass@1 on AIME 2024-2026, far above the bounded-state models evaluated (at most 18.8%, even at 14B scale), while using up to 99.1% less KV cache and delivering up to 6.42x higher end-to-end batch throughput than its source model.
papers.why_en: A mechanism that keeps memory constant without sacrificing long-reasoning quality, offering a practical way to raise concurrency on both edge and server deployments.

papers.title: From Prompts to Trees: Effective LLM-Guided Tree Generation for Few-Shot Tabular Classification
papers.abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) possess rich world knowledge and impressive generalization capabilities, their direct application to tabular data classification is hindered by high inference costs and limited interpretability. In contrast, decision trees are fast and transparent but often underperform in low-data regimes. In this work, we propose a novel framework that bridges these paradigms by distilling LLM knowledge into interpretable decision trees under a few-shot learning setting. Instead of directly prompting the LLM to generate full trees, which is often unstable and inefficient, we develop a three-stage paradigm that prompts the LLM to generate rules and organize the rules into a tree. Experiments on multiple real-world tabular datasets demonstrate that our method achieves superior accuracy and interpretability with significantly lower prompting overhead compared to existing baselines.

papers.title: Stale, Misattributed, or Late: Where Personal Memory Fails Before Generation
papers.abstract: Personal memory for language agents is usually judged by whether the final an- swer is correct. That score hides errors that arise before generation: the memory block may contain an obsolete value, a fact about the wrong person, or no use- ful fact before the serving deadline. We measure these failures directly. Using Personal Fact Memory (PFM) as a reference layer, we find that temporal validity is primarily a property of memory construction in our setting. On a controlled revision benchmark, serving only the active value of each correctly keyed slot eliminates observed stale exposure; without update resolution, 70.3% of prompts expose a superseded value. Once retrievers share the same active store and par- ticipant information, participant-aware BM25 is equivalent to the reference ranker within a prespecified 0.02 margin. The harder problem is assigning revisions to the right slot. Missed merges leave stale values active, whereas false merges silently remove current values; four LLM key assigners achieve higher key re- call than a rule extractor yet produce lower clean-retrieval rates, and open-domain merge recall on LongMemEval never exceeds 0.062. Misattribution survives va- lidity filtering: an entity posterior reduces same-name exposure on controlled data but cannot distinguish identically named speakers in LoCoMo. Two frozen lan- guage models reproduce prompt errors in generated text. Retrieval latency varies across rankers, but prompt prefill dominates turn-level latency on our hardware. These results argue for evaluating agent memory before generation, separating stored-state validity, identity resolution, abstention, and serving latency.
papers.ja_title: 生成前に壊れる個人メモリ: 古い情報・誤帰属・遅延の実態
