papers.summary: 言語エージェント向けの個人用メモリ機能は、最終的な回答が正しいかどうかでしか評価されず、生成前の段階で起きる誤り(古い値の提示、別人の事実の混在、締め切りまでに有用な事実がない)が見えにくいという問題がある。筆者らは Personal Fact Memory (PFM) という基準層を使い、更新を正しく解決しないと 70.3% のプロンプトで古い値が提示されてしまうことを示し、同じ検索ストアと参加者情報を共有すれば参加者を考慮した BM25 検索は基準ランカーと誤差 0.02 の範囲で同等になることを確かめた。一方、改訂情報を正しいスロットに割り当てる作業はより難しく、4 つの LLM によるキー割り当て器はルールベース抽出器より再現率は高いのに検索の清潔さは下がり、LongMemEval での結合再現率は 0.062 を超えなかった。
papers.why: 回答の正誤だけでなく、記憶の有効期限・人物の取り違え・検索遅延を分けて測る評価設計を示しており、RAG やエージェントメモリの検証観点として使える。
papers.summary_en: Personal memory for language agents is usually judged only by final-answer correctness, which hides pre-generation errors such as serving an obsolete value, attributing a fact to the wrong person, or lacking a useful fact before the deadline. Using Personal Fact Memory (PFM) as a reference layer, the authors show that without update resolution 70.3% of prompts expose a superseded value, while once retrievers share the same active store and participant information, participant-aware BM25 matches the reference ranker within a prespecified 0.02 margin. Assigning revisions to the correct slot proves harder: four LLM key assigners achieve higher key recall than a rule extractor yet yield lower clean-retrieval rates, and open-domain merge recall on LongMemEval never exceeds 0.062.
papers.why_en: Offers an evaluation design that separates stored-state validity, identity resolution, and retrieval latency rather than relying on final-answer correctness, useful as a verification lens for RAG and agent-memory systems.

review.note: 最終回答の正解率だけでなく、記憶の有効期限・人物誤帰属・遅延を切り分けて測る評価観点の例。
review.note_en: An example of evaluating separately for memory validity, identity misattribution, and retrieval latency rather than only final-answer accuracy.

papers.title: Continual Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: In Continual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CMARL), agents learn cooperative policies across sequences of tasks, aiming to adapt effectively to new tasks while preserving the ability to solve previously encountered ones. In many applications, tasks differ in their underlying structure, which can represent, for example, distinct operational conditions or target configurations (e.g., different network topologies in power grids or arrangements in formation control). Existing CMARL methods lack dedicated mechanisms to leverage this structural information when learning new tasks, failing to promote transfer and mitigate forgetting. To fill this gap, we propose Continual Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CGMARL), a novel framework for CMARL problems in which task sequences are mapped into a series of attributed graphs, each modeling a task-specific structure. In CGMARL, each graph determines the environment dynamics (next states and/or rewards) and the number of agents for the corresponding task. Then, we present Graph-based Formation (GRAFO), the first CGMARL benchmark, and show how forgetting arises in this setting. Finally, to address this limitation, we propose Frozen Graph Encoder (FROG), a method that relies on a frozen graph backbone to preserve past structural information in graph-based CMARL policies. Experiments on GRAFO show that pairing FROG with existing CL methods substantially improves performance on multiple CGMARL scenarios.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク

papers.title: Fault-tolerant foundation models
papers.abstract: Emerging computer hardware often trades reliability for energy efficiency; here we show that large-language models (LLMs) can be trained to tolerate this unreliability, and that rather than degrading, their error resilience actually increases as they grow. Modified neural scaling laws inferred from 40,000 GPU-hours of training runs on simulated faulty digital hardware quantify this trend and suggest that models learn to compute within "good" error-correcting codes, whose relative overhead remains finite no matter how large the model gets. This finding leads us to conjecture that appropriately trained LLMs may be formally fault-tolerant; if true, running AI inference on low energy, faulty hardware may be a path to substantial energy savings over the status quo.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 故障に強いハードウェアで育てる大規模言語モデルの耐障害性スケーリング則
papers.summary: 新しい省電力な計算機ハードウェアは、省エネの代わりに計算の信頼性を落とすことがある。研究チームは意図的に誤りが起きるシミュレーション上の故障ハードウェアで大規模言語モデル (LLM) を学習させ、40,000 GPU 時間規模の実験からスケーリング則を測定した。モデルが大きくなるほど誤りへの耐性がむしろ増し、誤り訂正符号に似た仕組みを自ら学習することで、オーバーヘッドがモデルサイズに関わらず有限に収まる傾向を見つけた。
papers.why: 分散学習基盤を低電力・低信頼性ハードウェアに移す際の省エネ経路を示し、耐障害性を前提にした学習設計の理論的な裏付けを与える。
papers.summary_en: Emerging computer hardware often trades reliability for energy efficiency, but this work shows LLMs can be trained to tolerate that unreliability. From 40,000 GPU-hours of training on simulated faulty digital hardware, the authors derive modified neural scaling laws showing that error resilience increases, not degrades, as models grow, suggesting models learn to compute within 'good' error-correcting codes whose relative overhead stays finite at any scale.
papers.why_en: This offers distributed-training infrastructure builders a theoretical basis and evidence for running training/inference on low-energy, faulty hardware as a path to energy savings.

papers.title: Open-MMUnlearning: Unifying Methods and Evaluation for MLLM Unlearning
papers.abstract: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become more capable and widely deployed, concerns about privacy and safety have become increasingly pressing. Machine unlearning offers one approach to addressing these concerns by removing designated information from trained models while preserving unrelated capabilities. However, fragmented implementations and evaluation protocols, incomplete robustness testing, and limited understanding of metric reliability make progress in MLLM unlearning difficult to assess systematically. We introduce Open-MMUnlearning, an open-source, extensible framework that integrates target-model preparation, multimodal data processing, unlearning, and evaluation through shared interfaces and structured configurations. The framework supports five benchmarks spanning privacy, safety, and copyright, eight MLLMs from four model families, and twelve unlearning methods. Its evaluation suite jointly assesses forgetting effectiveness, retained utility, and robustness to model interventions, adversarial inputs, and membership inference attacks. Using a common evaluation protocol, we compare ten representative unlearning methods. In this comparison, GD and MIP-Editor tie for the highest overall score: GD achieves the highest Forget Quality, while MIP-Editor preserves more Model Utility. We further introduce a metric meta-evaluation protocol that tests faithfulness using models with controlled exposure to target knowledge and robustness under quantization and relearning. Among the thirteen evaluated metrics, BLEU achieves the highest aggregate reliability score. KS-Test attains the highest faithfulness AUC but performs less well on robustness. Together, the framework and these findings support reproducible comparison of MLLM unlearning methods and systematic assessment of evaluation reliability.

papers.title: ResidualQuant: KV Cache Quantization for Looped Transformers with 2-Bit Residuals
papers.abstract: Looped Transformers improve parameter efficiency by applying shared Transformer blocks over recurrent loops, increasing computational depth without increasing the parameter count. However, KV cache memory still scales with loop count, becoming a key memory bottleneck that limits batch size and inference throughput. KV cache quantization can alleviate this bottleneck, but existing methods often suffer substantial accuracy degradation at aggressive low-precision regimes. We observe that looped Transformers offer a unique opportunity: KV states across loops are highly similar. Based on this observation, we propose ResidualQuant, which uses the final-loop KV states as a reference and represents the remaining loops with low-precision residuals. Our method further combines least-square scaling and rotation-based quantization, as well as loop-wise mixed precision, to enable accurate quantization down to INT2 while retaining efficient reconstruction. Across multiple looped Transformer models and mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks, ResidualQuant consistently improves the accuracy-memory tradeoff over state-of-the-art rotation-based KV quantization. In particular, our method retains accuracy close to BF16 under mixed-precision settings while reducing theoretical KV storage by 80.7%, achieving up to 13.0% higher accuracy than the rotation-based baseline at nearly the same memory budget. On an RTX 5090, reduced KV memory traffic improves fixed-batch decode throughput by up to 3.66x, while the smaller memory footprint enables up to 8x larger batches, improving peak throughput by up to 5.38x.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: ループ型Transformerの KV キャッシュを 2bit 残差で圧縮する ResidualQuant
papers.summary: 同じブロックを繰り返し使うループ型 Transformer は、ループ回数に比例して KV キャッシュ (注意計算の中間結果を保存するメモリ) が膨らみ、バッチサイズと推論スループットを制限してしまう。研究チームは最終ループの KV 状態を基準に、他のループを低精度の残差として表すResidualQuantを提案し、理論上の KV ストレージを 80.7% 削減しつつ既存の回転量子化手法より最大 13.0% 高い精度を達成した。RTX 5090 上では固定バッチでのデコードスループットを最大 3.66 倍、バッチサイズ拡大も合わせたピークスループットを最大 5.38 倍に改善した。
papers.why: 推論サービング基盤でメモリがボトルネックになるループ型モデルに対し、INT2 まで精度を保って圧縮する具体的な量子化手法と実測の高速化効果を示している。
papers.summary_en: Looped Transformers reuse shared blocks across recurrent loops, but their KV cache still scales with loop count, becoming a key memory bottleneck for batch size and throughput. ResidualQuant represents final-loop KV states as a reference and encodes remaining loops as low-precision residuals, cutting theoretical KV storage by 80.7% while achieving up to 13.0% higher accuracy than rotation-based baselines at similar memory budget, and on an RTX 5090 improving fixed-batch decode throughput by up to 3.66x and peak throughput by up to 5.38x via larger batches.
papers.why_en: It gives serving-infrastructure builders a concrete INT2-capable KV quantization method tailored to looped Transformers, with measured throughput gains from reduced memory traffic and larger batches.

papers.title: A Good Self-Teacher Meets the Student Where They Are: Joint On-Policy Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) from outcome rewards suffers from sparse supervision, particularly on difficult, long-horizon tasks where successful trajectories are rare and costly to generate. On-Policy Distillation (OPD) offers an attractive alternative by providing dense token-level supervision from a stronger teacher along the student's own generations. Self-distillation methods further remove the need for a separate teacher model by conditioning the same policy on privileged information to serve as its own teacher. However, privileged conditioning alone does not guarantee that the resulting distillation update improves the student. Indeed, privileged information can lead the teacher to solve tasks through shortcuts unavailable to the student, producing supervision poorly matched to the student's current behavior. Consequently, even a higher-performing teacher can provide guidance that degrades student performance. To address this, we analyze how the choice of privileged teacher affects the student's update. We derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the teacher's local distillation update to be a positive multiple of the student's reward gradient. Our analysis suggests that the teacher should not only perform well on the task, but also provide guidance suited to the student's current capabilities. This characterization motivates a practical teacher-training surrogate that combines outcome rewards with token-level Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization toward the student. Based on this result, we propose Joint On-Policy Learning and Teaching (JOLT), which jointly trains a single policy in two roles: a privileged teacher using a KL-regularized objective, and an unprivileged student using dense on-policy distillation. Across mathematical reasoning, coding, tool use, and terminal use, JOLT improves training efficiency and performance, with further gains from student rewards.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 教師も生徒も同じポリシーで育てる JOLT: 自己蒸留の落とし穴を理論で詰める
papers.summary: 強化学習は成功例が少ない難しいタスクでは報酬が疎になり学習が進みにくい。オンポリシー蒸留は強い教師モデルから密な手本を与える手法だが、特権情報を使う自己蒸留では教師が生徒には使えない近道で答えを出してしまい、手本がかえって生徒の性能を下げることがあった。研究チームは教師の更新が生徒の報酬勾配と正しく一致する必要十分条件を導き、それに基づき同じポリシーを教師役と生徒役の両方で同時学習する JOLT を提案し、数学推論やコーディング、ツール使用などで学習効率と性能を改善した。
papers.why: RL 後学習で自己蒸留の教師設計を誤ると生徒の性能が下がる条件を理論的に明らかにし、実用的な教師訓練法を示した点が新しい。
papers.summary_en: RL from outcome rewards suffers from sparse supervision on hard, long-horizon tasks. On-policy distillation provides denser guidance from a stronger teacher, but self-distillation using privileged information can let the teacher solve tasks via shortcuts unavailable to the student, so even a higher-performing teacher can degrade student performance. The authors derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the teacher's distillation update to be a positive multiple of the student's reward gradient, and propose JOLT, which jointly trains one policy as both a KL-regularized privileged teacher and an on-policy distillation student, improving training efficiency and performance across math reasoning, coding, tool use, and terminal use.
papers.why_en: It gives RL post-training infrastructure builders a theoretical account of when self-distillation teacher guidance helps or hurts, plus a practical joint-training recipe.

papers.title: Composing What Each Teacher Learned: Delta Distillation for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Learning
papers.abstract: Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) is used in two settings. In common-domain composition, several teachers score each student rollout from one prompt domain and their signals form a single target; in routed-domain distillation, prompts from different domains are assigned to the corresponding specialist. Both settings usually transfer each teacher's endpoint policy, which mixes what post-training changed with preferences inherited from the teacher's base. We introduce $Δ$-MOPD, which transfers each teacher's teacher-minus-base logit shift re-anchored at the student's frozen initialization, and compare it with endpoint supervision in both settings while holding teacher selection fixed. We first expose the mechanism that impedes endpoint transfer: inherited base pull can exceed the post-training shift. Removing it reduces the teacher-term norm ratio and target--student KL. Across our experiments, the results suggest that shift targets are particularly useful when teacher signals are combined at a state. With three composed teachers, $Δ$-MOPD exceeds endpoint composition by $4.11$ Math and $1.95$ five-benchmark points; with two, it matches endpoint accuracy. Under phased routing, it achieves higher mean performance in both phase orders and reduces the observed order gap from $10.50$ to $6.42$ points. Under interleaved routing, where each update involves one teacher, the two targets perform comparably. The phased results provide supporting evidence that the benefit may extend to signals accumulated across training phases. Target construction is thus an independent design axis in MOPD, complementary to teacher selection. The experiment repo could be find at https://github.com/HJSang/Delta-MOPD
papers.ja_title: 教師の「差分」だけを転送する Δ-MOPD: 複数教師オンポリシー蒸留の設計軸
papers.summary: 複数の教師モデルから生徒モデルを蒸留する際、通常は教師の最終的な出来上がったポリシーをそのまま使うため、事後学習で変化した部分と元のベースモデルから引き継いだ好みが混ざってしまう。研究チームはΔ-MOPDを提案し、教師の「ベースからの変化分」だけを生徒の初期状態を基準に転送したところ、3 人の教師を組み合わせた設定で従来方式より数学ベンチマークで 4.11 点、5 ベンチマーク平均で 1.95 点上回り、フェーズ切り替え型ルーティングでは学習順序による性能差を 10.50 点から 6.42 点に縮小した。
papers.why: 複数教師蒸留で何を転送するかを教師選択とは独立した設計軸として整理し、具体的な改善量とメカニズムを示した点が実装者に役立つ。
papers.summary_en: In multi-teacher on-policy distillation, transferring each teacher's full endpoint policy mixes post-training changes with preferences inherited from the teacher's base model. The authors introduce Δ-MOPD, which transfers only each teacher's teacher-minus-base logit shift re-anchored at the student's initialization; with three composed teachers it exceeds endpoint composition by 4.11 Math and 1.95 five-benchmark points, and under phased routing it reduces the observed order gap from 10.50 to 6.42 points.
papers.why_en: It frames target construction as an independent design axis in multi-teacher distillation, complementary to teacher selection, with concrete measured gains useful for practitioners building RL post-training pipelines.

papers.title: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly applied to tasks grounded in long, heterogeneous information sources. Conventional Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) relies on fixed similarity-based retrieval, while agentic variants adapt queries and tool use but remain largely retrieval-centric. However, in many tasks, the evidence required for a solution is not explicitly present in any single source item. Instead, it must be derived through filtering, aggregation, or computation across multiple source items. In this work, we introduce RECAST (Routing Evidence through Computation, Access, and Synthesized Tools), a learned framework that formulates evidence construction as a sequential decision process over heterogeneous retrieval and computation operations, allowing evidence to be actively derived rather than merely retrieved. A lightweight RouterLM iteratively selects and formulates primitive operations or specifies customized operations for a frozen CompilerLM to translate into executable code. Once it judges the evidence sufficient, RouterLM passes the accepted evidence to a frozen AnswerLM to produce the final solution. We train RouterLM with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) followed by group relative policy optimization (GRPO). Across six heterogeneous benchmark families, RECAST achieves a mean success rate of 75.6%, outperforming the strongest large-model baseline by 15.9%. Moreover, training enables the Qwen3.5-9B RouterLM to outperform a training-free Gemini 3.5 Flash RouterLM by 5.0%. On three held-out benchmarks, RECAST improves over the strongest baseline by 15.0% on average, demonstrating strong zero-shot generalization across tasks and heterogeneous source representations.

papers.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Latent world models have shown a remarkable ability to predict future states and to plan in the real world. In practice, however, we lack a principled way to estimate how their capabilities scale with model size, data, and compute, an open problem that slows progress in the field. In this work we present RoboJEPA, a world model based on the Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) and trained on a large-scale dataset spanning 12 robotic embodiments. We show that RoboJEPA's imagination error, the error of its latent rollouts, follows a second-order power law in compute, allowing us to predict model quality well beyond the scale at which the law is fit. We further show that downstream robotic planning performance improves predictably with compute, and that imagination error is strongly correlated with it, making it a reliable proxy for real-robot evaluation. Finally, we demonstrate that latent world models can be deployed zero-shot as robotic agents, planning toward a single goal image to solve tasks requiring long-horizon planning on real hardware. We release all model checkpoints together with our training and robot deployment code. To our knowledge, this is the first work to establish scaling laws for multi-embodiment robotic world models trained on real robot data, and RoboJEPA, at 8B parameters, is the largest JEPA predictor model trained to date.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 実機ロボットデータで初めて確立した世界モデルのスケーリング則 RoboJEPA
papers.summary: ロボットの未来を予測する潜在世界モデル (観測を圧縮した表現の中で未来を予測するモデル) は、モデルサイズやデータ量を増やすとどれだけ性能が上がるのか、これまで体系的に分かっていなかった。研究チームは 12 種類のロボットの身体構成のデータで学習した JEPA ベースの世界モデルRoboJEPAを作り、潜在空間での予測誤差 (想像誤差) が計算量に対して二次のべき乗則に従うことを示し、少ない計算量のデータから大規模域の性能を予測できるようにした。8B パラメータのRoboJEPAは現時点で最大の JEPA 予測器モデルであり、実機での長期計画タスクにもゼロショットで適用できた。
papers.why: 実機ロボットデータに基づくマルチ身体世界モデルのスケーリング則を初めて確立し、計算量投資の判断に使える代理指標 (想像誤差) を提供した。
papers.summary_en: It was previously unclear how latent world models for robotics scale with model size, data, and compute. RoboJEPA, a JEPA-based world model trained on a large-scale dataset spanning 12 robotic embodiments, shows that its imagination error (latent rollout error) follows a second-order power law in compute, enabling prediction of model quality beyond the fitted scale, with downstream planning performance improving predictably and correlating strongly with imagination error. At 8B parameters, RoboJEPA is reported as the largest JEPA predictor trained to date and is deployed zero-shot for long-horizon real-robot planning.
papers.why_en: This is, to the authors' knowledge, the first work establishing scaling laws for multi-embodiment robotic world models trained on real robot data, giving a reliable compute-scaling proxy for guiding future model investment.

papers.title: SLVR: Structured Latent Visual Reasoning via Human-like Reasoning Flows
papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often answer visual reasoning questions by relying on linguistic priors rather than task-relevant visual evidence. Textual chain-of-thought reasoning can partially mitigate this issue by encouraging models to decompose visual questions into intermediate evidence-seeking steps, but generating these steps autoregressively increases inference cost. Latent reasoning avoids explicit rationale generation, but existing approaches provide limited control over what intermediate states encode, making it difficult to impose separate supervision for planning, grounding, and evidence selection. We propose Structured Latent Visual Reasoning (SLVR), a training framework that bridges explicit chain-of-thought and latent reasoning by organizing multimodal reasoning into typed latent stages for planning, grounding, evidence selection, and reasoning integration. SLVR first trains the model to rely on the image by masking answer-revealing text and contrasting the correct answer with visually plausible distractors. It then organizes reasoning into latent stages for planning, grounding, evidence selection, and integration, supervising each stage with the corresponding signal: plans, boxes, visual evidence, and final rationales. This gives latent reasoning an explicit functional structure while avoiding generated textual chains at inference time. Built on Qwen2.5-VL-7B, SLVR improves consistently across multimodal reasoning benchmarks, with absolute gains of +9.4 on MMVP and +14.2 on BLINK Relation, as well as improvements on V*, MathVista, and ChartQA. These results suggest that structured latent supervision can improve fine-grained visual reasoning without the decoding overhead of textual CoT. Project page is available \href{https://bogao-code.github.io/SLVR/}{here}.
papers.ja_title: 視覚推論を型付き潜在ステージに分解して鍛える SLVR
papers.summary: 多モーダル大規模言語モデル (MLLM) は画像問題を解くとき、本当は画像を見るべきなのに言語の思い込み (言語的事前知識) に頼ってしまうことが困りごと。文章で段階的に考える手法 (CoT) は改善するが推論時の計算が増えるため、著者らは答えを隠した学習と計画・画像位置特定・証拠選択・統合という型付きの潜在段 (目に見えない内部ステージ) を個別に教える SLVR を提案した。Qwen2.5-VL-7B 上で MMVP は +9.4 ポイント、BLINK Relation は +14.2 ポイント改善し、V*、MathVista、ChartQA でも向上した。
papers.why: 推論時に文章を生成しない潜在推論でも、段ごとに教師信号を与えれば視覚推論の精度を保てることを示しており、低遅延な多モーダル推論の作り方に使える。
papers.summary_en: MLLMs often answer visual questions using linguistic priors instead of real visual evidence, and textual chain-of-thought mitigates this but adds inference cost. SLVR trains the model with answer-masking and organizes latent reasoning into typed stages for planning, grounding, evidence selection, and integration, each supervised by a corresponding signal. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B, SLVR gives absolute gains of +9.4 on MMVP and +14.2 on BLINK Relation, plus improvements on V*, MathVista, and ChartQA.
papers.why_en: It shows structured latent supervision can improve fine-grained visual reasoning without the decoding overhead of textual CoT, which is directly useful for designing low-latency multimodal reasoning systems.

papers.title: Code Understanding is a Bottleneck for Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Repository benchmarks (e.g., SWE-bench) for coding agents often assume that lines of code edited can predict task difficulty, but such datasets' poor control over code and task types makes it hard to know which abilities truly drive agent errors. We present CABRA: a Coding Ability Blueprint for Rigorous Agent evaluation. CABRA builds tasks from scratch as call graph transformations and scales difficulty via a task size parameter on four axes: function traversal, search, runtime resolution, and instruction following. We run eight LLMs and six coding agents on 6,840 CABRA tasks to show: 1) LLM accuracy falls as task size~grows, but agents stay near-perfect by offloading work to tools (e.g., grep); 2) Larger CABRA tasks elicit more tool calls for reading and analysis, while a separate study on SWE-bench Verified shows these tool call counts predict agents' accuracy better than lines of code edited, suggesting task difficulty for agents can lie in understanding code to edit, not just in making edits; 3) Extending CABRA to an intense understanding task where models analyze divergent logic across two classes backs this finding, as agent accuracy finally falls. More broadly, we argue for synthetic evaluations like CABRA to unmask LLM weaknesses trivialized by tools (e.g., needle-in-a-haystack) and abilities beyond just editing (e.g., understanding) that coding agents still find difficult, pairing SWE-bench-style tasks with controlled diagnosis.
papers.ja_title: コーディングエージェントの弱点は「編集」より「理解」にある CABRA
papers.summary: SWE-bench のようなベンチマークは編集した行数で難しさを測るが、それがエージェントの本当の失敗原因を説明できているか分からないという困りごとがあった。著者らはコールグラフの変換からタスクを作り、関数巡回・検索・実行時解決・指示追従の4軸でサイズを調節できる CABRA を作り、8つの LLM と6つのコーディングエージェントに 6,840 件のタスクを実行させた。その結果、LLM 単体はタスクが大きくなると精度が落ちるがエージェントは grep などのツール呼び出しでほぼ満点を保ち、SWE-bench Verified でもツール呼び出し回数の方が編集行数より精度をよく予測できることが分かった。
papers.why: ベンチマークの難易度指標 (編集行数) が本当の能力差を捉えていないことを実測で示しており、評価設計や落とし穴を考えるうえで参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Repository benchmarks like SWE-bench assume lines of code edited predict task difficulty, but it's unclear what abilities actually drive agent errors. CABRA builds tasks from call graph transformations, scaling difficulty across function traversal, search, runtime resolution, and instruction following, and running 6,840 tasks on 8 LLMs and 6 coding agents shows LLM accuracy falls with task size while agents stay near-perfect by offloading to tools like grep; on SWE-bench Verified, tool-call counts predict agent accuracy better than lines edited.
papers.why_en: It demonstrates with real counts that a commonly used difficulty proxy (lines edited) poorly reflects what actually drives agent errors, offering a concrete lens on benchmark design pitfalls.

review.note: ベンチマークの難易度指標が実際の失敗原因と一致するかを、実測の呼び出し回数などで検証する観点。
review.note_en: A review lens for checking whether a benchmark's difficulty proxy actually matches real failure causes, using measured counts like tool calls.

papers.title: Recurrent Self-Improvement: Dynamic Cross-Loop On-Policy Distillation for Looped Language Models
papers.abstract: Looped Language Models (LoopLMs) offer a parameter efficient approach to scaling reasoning by reusing shared parameters across recurrent computation steps. Despite their promise, effective post-training of LoopLMs remains challenging. Existing approaches either provide reward based supervision that is sparse or costly to extend across loops, or rely on external teachers or privileged information, leading to limited teacher availability or teacher-student context mismatch. To address these limitations, we introduce LoopOPD, a cross-loop on-policy distillation framework that uses additional recurrent computation within a LoopLM as its own source of supervision. LoopOPD uses a frozen terminal loop policy as a compute privileged teacher for an intermediate loop student on student generated rollouts, providing dense supervision without an external teacher or privileged information. We further propose Dynamic LoopOPD (D-LoopOPD), which continually refreshes the terminal loop teacher as the shared model parameters are updated, enabling recurrent self-improvement. We characterize how distillation updates propagate across loop depths and derive sufficient conditions under which a single update yields simultaneous local improvement at both loop depths. Experiments on Ouro-Thinking models show that LoopOPD improves mathematical reasoning, while D-LoopOPD yields further gains through dynamic teacher updates. Despite being trained only on mathematical data, the resulting models also improve on general reasoning and code generation benchmarks, demonstrating that recurrent computation can serve as an effective source of supervision for LoopLMs. Our code and model checkpoints will be released upon acceptance.
papers.ja_title: ループ型言語モデルを自分の深い思考で鍛える LoopOPD
papers.summary: ループ型言語モデル (LoopLM、同じパラメータを繰り返し使って推論する仕組み) は学習後の調整 (post-training) が難しく、既存法は報酬信号が疎か外部の教師モデルが必要だった。著者らは、ループを多く回した自分自身を教師とし、少ないループの自分を生徒として蒸留する LoopOPD を提案し、教師を更新し続ける D-LoopOPD も作った。Ouro-Thinking モデルでの実験で数学推論が改善し、数学データのみで学習したのに一般推論やコード生成のベンチマークでも向上した。
papers.why: 外部教師なしでモデル自身の深いループを教師にする自己蒸留の仕組みは、省パラメータな推論強化モデルの学習効率を上げる方法として使える。
papers.summary_en: LoopLMs are hard to post-train effectively: reward supervision is sparse and costly across loops, while external-teacher methods suffer from limited availability or context mismatch. LoopOPD uses a frozen terminal-loop policy of the same model as a compute-privileged teacher for an intermediate-loop student on student-generated rollouts, and D-LoopOPD continually refreshes this teacher as parameters update. On Ouro-Thinking models, LoopOPD improves mathematical reasoning and D-LoopOPD yields further gains, with the resulting models also improving on general reasoning and code generation despite training only on math data.
papers.why_en: Using the model's own deeper-loop computation as a dense, teacher-free self-distillation signal is a concrete way to make post-training of parameter-efficient recurrent reasoning models more efficient.

papers.title: Nullify: Null-Space Activation Steering for Training-Free LLM Unlearning
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) inevitably internalize substantial amounts of sensitive or private information during pre-training, while LLM unlearning aims to selectively erase specific knowledge to prevent privacy leakage with minimal loss of model utility. However, existing methods struggle to balance forget quality with utility, and typically incur substantial computational costs due to parameter fine-tuning. To address this, we propose Nullify, a training-free, non-destructive activation steering method for LLM unlearning. Nullify employs steering vectors during inference to redirect privacy-related activations away from their memorized answers, while satisfying a null-space constraint that leaves retained-query activations essentially unaffected to maintain utility. Evaluations on TOFU and MUSE show that Nullify matches or surpasses established baselines in forget quality while achieving near-lossless preservation of model utility. By avoiding weight updates entirely, Nullify serves as an efficient, plug-and-play inference-time intervention framework.
papers.ja_title: 重み更新なしで忘れさせる Nullify
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルは学習時に機密情報を覚えてしまい、特定の知識だけ忘れさせる「アンラーニング」が必要だが、既存法はパラメータの再学習にコストがかかり、忘れさせる質と使い勝手のバランスが難しかった。著者らは重みを一切更新せず、推論時に活性 (モデル内部の値) を操作して私的情報に関する出力の方向をずらし、残したい知識への影響を抑える制約 (null-space 制約) を満たす Nullify を提案した。TOFU と MUSE での評価で、既存手法と同等以上の忘却質を保ちながらほぼ性能を落とさないことを確認した。
papers.why: 重み更新なしの推論時介入でアンラーニングを実現する手法は、学習コストをかけずにモデル運用後の情報漏えい対策を行う方法として使える。
papers.summary_en: LLMs inevitably internalize sensitive information during pre-training, and unlearning methods must erase specific knowledge while preserving utility, but existing approaches struggle to balance this and incur substantial fine-tuning cost. Nullify is training-free: it steers inference-time activations away from memorized private-related answers while satisfying a null-space constraint that leaves retained-query activations essentially unaffected. On TOFU and MUSE, Nullify matches or surpasses established baselines in forget quality while achieving near-lossless preservation of utility, without any weight updates.
papers.why_en: An inference-time, weight-free unlearning intervention offers a way to address post-deployment privacy leakage without the cost of fine-tuning.

papers.title: Lossy Compressive Text Autoencoders
papers.abstract: Our work explores learning a compressed latent representation of text, at the intersection of data compression and representation learning. We propose an autoencoder architecture that performs residual downscaling and upscaling of hidden representations along the time axis, with a residual low-dimension discrete bottleneck. We analyze our approach for different quantization methods, training objectives, and datasets. For different levels of compression, we evaluate the similarity between the original and reconstructed text both at the surface-level (BLEU) and at the semantic-level (LLM-based judge). Additionally, we evaluate our models on downstream question-answering and semantic text similarity benchmarks. Our approach results in compressed representations which are on par with lossless text compression algorithms at 2.24 bits per byte on web text data, while having good reconstruction and downstream task performance.
papers.ja_title: 文章をロスレス圧縮並みの短さに詰め込む潜在オートエンコーダ
papers.summary: 文章を小さい表現に圧縮しつつ、意味を保つのが困りごとで、データ圧縮と表現学習の境界を狙った研究。時間方向に残差で縮小・拡大し、低次元の離散ボトルネック (情報を限られた選択肢に押し込む仕組み) を持つオートエンコーダを提案し、量子化手法や学習目的、データセットを変えて比較した。ウェブテキストで 1 バイトあたり 2.24 ビットという、既存のロスレス圧縮アルゴリズムと同等の圧縮率を実現しつつ、元文章の再現性と質問応答・文類似度といった下流タスクの性能も良好だった。
papers.why: 文章を少数の離散トークンに圧縮しても下流タスク性能を保てることを示し、長文コンテキストを圧縮してモデルに入れる設計の手がかりになる。
papers.summary_en: The work sits at the intersection of data compression and representation learning: it proposes an autoencoder that performs residual downscaling/upscaling along the time axis with a residual low-dimension discrete bottleneck, comparing quantization methods, training objectives, and datasets. The approach yields compressed text representations on par with lossless text compression algorithms at 2.24 bits per byte on web text, while maintaining good reconstruction (BLEU, LLM-judge) and downstream QA/semantic similarity performance.
papers.why_en: Showing that text can be compressed to near-lossless bit rates in a discrete latent while keeping downstream task performance offers a useful reference point for designing context-compressing representations for LLMs.

papers.title: What can linear attention learn from nonlinear teachers in-context?
papers.abstract: Linear attention is a tractable model for understanding the mechanisms governing in-context learning in transformers. For linear regression tasks, recent asymptotic analyses have characterised its learning and generalisation behaviour. We extend this theory to nonlinear single-index targets, $y=f(x^\top w)+\varepsilon $. Our main result establishes a nonlinearity-noise equivalence: linear attention extracts only the linear Hermite component of $f$, while the remaining nonlinear structure contributes to the generalisation error as effective noise. This reduction allows results from the corresponding linear theory to be transferred to nonlinear tasks. We illustrate its implications for finite pretraining data and for the transition from task memorisation to task generalisation as task diversity increases. These results identify a limitation of the reduced linear-attention model and provide a tractable starting point for studying nonlinear in-context learning.
papers.ja_title: 線形アテンションは非線形の先生から線形成分しか学べない
papers.summary: 文脈内学習 (手本を見て新しい問題を解く仕組み) の仕掛けを理解する手がかりとして、線形アテンションというモデルがこれまで線形回帰課題で理論解析されてきたが、著者らは y=f(x^⊤w)+雑音 という非線形の目標関数にこの理論を拡張した。主結果は「非線形性・雑音等価性」で、線形アテンションは f のうち線形なエルミート成分だけを取り出し、残りの非線形な部分は実質的な雑音として一般化誤差に乗ってくることを示した。これにより、有限の事前学習データの影響や、タスクの多様性が増えるにつれて記憶から一般化へ移る様子についての既存の線形理論の結果を、非線形タスクにそのまま持ち込めることを示した。
papers.why: 線形アテンションの理論限界を明確にし、非線形な文脈内学習を扱いやすい形で分析するための出発点を与える。
papers.summary_en: Linear attention is a tractable model for understanding in-context learning, previously characterised asymptotically for linear regression; this work extends the theory to nonlinear single-index targets y=f(x^Tw)+noise. The main result is a nonlinearity-noise equivalence: linear attention extracts only the linear Hermite component of f, while the remaining nonlinear structure acts as effective noise in the generalisation error, letting results from finite-data and memorisation-to-generalisation transitions in the linear theory transfer to nonlinear tasks.
papers.why_en: It clarifies a concrete limitation of reduced linear-attention models and offers a tractable starting point for analyzing nonlinear in-context learning.

papers.title: Large Language Models for Machine Translation Quality Annotation: Humans and Models Are Both Challenged
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are considered to be a more efficient and cost-effective alternative to human judgment for Machine Translation (MT) evaluation. With MT evaluation spanning a large number of language pairs, domains and levels of annotation granularity, LLMs must be thoroughly evaluated across these dimensions before being reliably used as alternatives to human evaluation. In this paper, we evaluate the performance of LLMs for two prominent MT quality evaluation schemes: Multidimensional Quality Metrics (MQM) and Error Span Annotation (ESA) by comparing their agreement with human annotators. We present results on a long-context test set of 70 language pairs and the publicly available WMT23 and WMT25 data, investigating both score and error span annotation agreement across a variety of language pairs and domains. Our results show that while LLM agreement with human annotators exceeds agreement between human annotators for some evaluation tasks, both vary substantially across annotation schemes, language pairs and domains and remain unreliable for most settings. Furthermore, we identify challenges facing both human and LLM annotators: humans are particularly challenged by fine-grained MQM annotations and low-resource language pairs, while LLMs struggle with minor errors, wrong language variants and error span annotation. Our results highlight the potential for improvement for both human and LLM annotation performance, possibly through human-LLM collaborative annotation pipelines that address the reliability issues identified in this work.

papers.title: The Missing Fourth Term for the Emulation Tensor Memory Equilibrium (TME) Model: The Residue Deconstruction Cost
papers.abstract: The Tensor-Memory Equilibrium (TME) model of "FP8 is All You Need (Part 1)" calculates the execution time of Ozaki Scheme II emulation of fp64 as the maximum of a tensor-core term and a High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) traffic term, plus a per-output reconstruction term. However, it omits the per-input deconstruction cost: every streamed fp64 operand must be scaled, rounded, and reduced modulo each of the $r$ moduli on SIMT pipes before any matrix multiply can issue. In this note we add this fourth term, calibrate its constant from the cuBLAS emulation path, and derive a closed-form operational-intensity threshold $\mathrm{OI}^{*} = c_q r P_{\mathrm{fp64}}/(8P_{\mathrm{int}})$ below which emulation cannot match native fp64 regardless of tensor-core throughput. On the NVIDIA B300 GPU the threshold is $\mathrm{OI}^{*}\approx 0.56$ FLOP/B. As a result, GEMV, SpMV, and low-batch GEMV, which are the memory-bound kernels the original paper claims to accelerate, are limited to 0.3-0.9x of native performance, and the 7-point stencil to 1.8x rather than the claimed 3.1x. Dense GEMM is unaffected as expected. We also show that precomputing and storing the residues moves the same cost into the bandwidth term, and we state the instruction count that an implementation would have to achieve to invalidate the bound.
papers.ja_title: FP8 で fp64 を再現する計算の見落とされたコスト項
papers.summary: 「FP8 is All You Need」の TME モデルは、fp64 を fp8 でエミュレーションする実行時間をテンソルコア項と HBM 帯域項の最大値に出力の再構成項を足して計算していたが、入力の各 fp64 オペランドをスケーリング・丸め・剰余演算する「分解コスト」を見落としていた。著者らはこの第4項を追加し、cuBLAS の実測から定数を校正して、エミュレーションが素の fp64 に勝てなくなる演算強度のしきい値 OI* を導出した。NVIDIA B300 GPU ではこのしきい値は約 0.56 FLOP/B で、元論文がメモリ帯域制約カーネルとして高速化を主張していた GEMV・SpMV・低バッチ GEMV は実際には素の fp64 の 0.3〜0.9 倍にしかならず、7 点ステンシルも主張の 3.1 倍ではなく 1.8 倍にとどまることを示した。密な GEMM には影響しない。
papers.why: 低精度エミュレーションの速度向上の主張を、見落とされたコスト項を加えた閾値モデルで再検証する手法として使える。
papers.summary_en: The TME model from "FP8 is All You Need (Part 1)" computes the execution time of fp8-emulated fp64 (Ozaki Scheme II) as the max of a tensor-core term and an HBM-traffic term plus a per-output reconstruction term, but omits the per-input deconstruction cost of scaling, rounding, and reducing each fp64 operand modulo r moduli. This note adds that fourth term, calibrates its constant from the cuBLAS emulation path, and derives a closed-form operational-intensity threshold OI* below which emulation cannot match native fp64; on an NVIDIA B300 GPU this threshold is about 0.56 FLOP/B, so GEMV, SpMV, and low-batch GEMV (the memory-bound kernels the original paper claims to accelerate) are limited to 0.3-0.9x of native performance, and the 7-point stencil reaches 1.8x rather than the claimed 3.1x, while dense GEMM is unaffected.
papers.why_en: It demonstrates how to re-check low-precision emulation speedup claims by adding a previously omitted cost term into a closed-form threshold model.

review.note: 既存の高速化の主張を、見落とされたコスト項を加えた閾値モデルで再計算し、実際の倍率を修正する検証のやり方。
review.note_en: A research-practice lens: recompute an existing speedup claim by adding a previously omitted cost term into a closed-form threshold model, revealing the corrected real-world ratio.

papers.title: Spectrally Targeted Muon
papers.abstract: The Muon optimizer orthogonalizes each update matrix, setting all of its singular values to one, and has proven highly effective for training large language models. It remains unclear, however, whether this success comes from amplifying small singular directions that gradient descent neglects or from suppressing large, degenerate directions that disrupt training. We introduce Spectrally Targeted Muon, which orthogonalizes only the singular values above or below a threshold $τ$, so that varying $τ$ interpolates between normalized SGD and Muon. It isolates the relevant singular subspaces with projections computed by Newton-Schulz iteration on a shifted Gram matrix, so no SVD is needed. We evaluate these variants on the CIFAR-10 and NanoGPT speedruns, tracking the effective rank of gradient, update, and weight matrices and a new metric, the alignment of updates with the tangent space of the weight matrix's isospectral manifold. We find three things. First, the small singular values of the momentum are not noise. Orthogonalizing everything except the few largest singular values of each matrix nearly matches Muon while touching only a small fraction of the momentum, whereas orthogonalizing only the top falls well short even though it holds almost all of it. On language models every momentum singular value is far below one, so targeted orthogonalization can only amplify, and Muon wins by making directions that are too small to train on at their raw scale trainable. Second, shrinking the largest singular values is what keeps the parameter spectrum flat; this is cheap, and it is not what drives the loss. Third, AdamW differs from Muon mainly in how slowly it builds structure, which explains its slower start and why warmup helps AdamW but only hurts Muon.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: Muon 最適化手法はなぜ効くのか：特異値のしきい値で切り分けて検証する
papers.summary: Muon という最適化手法(行列の更新量をすべて同じ大きさの特異値に揃える手法)が LLM の学習で効く理由が、小さい方向を増幅しているのか大きい方向を抑えているのか分かっていなかった。しきい値 τ を境に特異値の上側か下側だけを直交化する Spectrally Targeted Muon を作り、CIFAR-10 と NanoGPT の学習速度競争で検証した。モーメンタムの小さい特異値を残して大きい側だけ直交化すると性能が大きく劣る一方、最大のいくつかを除いてほぼ全部を直交化すると Muon とほぼ同じ性能になることが分かり、言語モデルでは Muon の効果は小さすぎて学習できない方向を増幅することにあると示された。
papers.why: Muon 系最適化手法の効果を特異値スペクトルの観点で切り分けて検証する方法を示し、今後の最適化手法設計やチューニングの指針になる。
papers.summary_en: It was unclear whether Muon's success (orthogonalizing every singular value of the update matrix to one) comes from amplifying small neglected directions or suppressing large degenerate ones. The authors build Spectrally Targeted Muon, which orthogonalizes only singular values above or below a threshold τ, and test it on CIFAR-10 and NanoGPT speedruns. Orthogonalizing everything except the few largest singular values nearly matches Muon, while orthogonalizing only the top falls well short; since every momentum singular value in LLMs is far below one, they conclude Muon wins mainly by making otherwise-too-small directions trainable.
papers.why_en: It gives a way to disentangle which part of Muon's spectral normalization actually drives the gains, useful guidance for designing and tuning future matrix-based optimizers.

papers.title: Optimizing Large Language Models with Chained LMOs
papers.abstract: Muon has motivated a growing family of optimizers that compose multiple matrix normalizations, but these methods remain fragmented and lack a unified perspective. We introduce chained linear minimization oracles (chained LMOs), which cast these methods as compositions of LMOs. Despite their empirical success, many chains fall outside the standard LMO framework and can diverge on smooth convex objectives. To explain why composition can nevertheless help, we turn to linear associative memory and show that chaining can improve over Muon under anisotropic embeddings. Empirically, we propose TensorChain, a novel optimizer within the framework that stacks compatible weight matrices across different layers and normalizes the 3d tensor across its axes. In Qwen3 0.6B and 1.7B pretraining, TensorChain outperforms all chained baselines in average token efficiency, with average token savings of 9.6% over Muon at matched validation loss.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: Muon 系の最適化手法を統一的に見る枠組みと、層をまとめて正規化する新手法
papers.summary: Muon をきっかけに複数の行列正規化を組み合わせる最適化手法が次々に出てきたが、それらを比べる共通の見方がなかった。この論文では、これらを「連結した線形最小化オラクル(chained LMOs)」という共通の枠組みで整理し、違う層の重み行列を束ねて 3 次元のまとまりとして正規化する新しい手法 TensorChain を提案した。Qwen3 の 0.6B と 1.7B モデルの事前学習実験で、TensorChain は既存の連結型手法をすべて上回り、同じ検証損失に到達するまでに Muon より平均 9.6% 少ないトークン数で済んだ。
papers.why: 行列正規化系の最適化手法を一つの枠組みで整理し、層をまとめた正規化という新しい設計方向とトークン効率の改善を具体的な数値で示している。
papers.summary_en: Muon has spawned a growing but fragmented family of optimizers composing multiple matrix normalizations, with no unified perspective. The authors cast these as chained linear minimization oracles (chained LMOs) and propose TensorChain, which stacks compatible weight matrices across layers and normalizes the resulting 3D tensor. In Qwen3 0.6B and 1.7B pretraining, TensorChain outperforms all chained baselines, saving an average of 9.6% of tokens over Muon at matched validation loss.
papers.why_en: It unifies Muon-style matrix-normalization optimizers under one framework and demonstrates a concrete new design (cross-layer tensor normalization) with measured token-efficiency gains.

papers.title: Omni-Diffusion-Distill: Few-Step Distillation of Unified Multimodal Diffusion Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Unified multimodal diffusion large language models (dLLMs) offer a single architecture for both image generation and multimodal understanding, but their iterative decoding requires tens to hundreds of forward passes. Existing few-step distillation methods largely focus on either image generation or text generation, making it unclear how to compress a fully discrete multimodal dLLM into a single efficient student while preserving both generation and understanding. We introduce Omni-Diffusion-Distill, a unified two-stage distillation framework that retains strong generation and understanding capabilities while substantially reducing the inference cost of a unified multimodal dLLM. Omni-Diffusion-Distill aligns the distillation of both generation and understanding, for both images and text, in the discrete token space. In the first stage, the student is trained to skip decoding steps by replaying cached teacher trajectories, and in the second stage the student is refined on intermediate states along its own rollouts. We further remedy two sources of degradation in unified distillation with a pairwise collision penalty that reduces repetition under parallel text decoding, and entropy-matched guidance that prevents entropy collapse caused by fitting the sharpened teacher distribution in image generation. Omni-Diffusion-Distill achieves state-of-the-art trade-offs between decoding efficiency and generation and understanding performance for multimodal dLLMs, reducing image generation from 128 to 8 decoding steps and multimodal understanding from 512 to 64, giving 18.2x and 21.2x wall-clock speedups. Under these budgets, it scores 0.828 on GenEval and 83.0 on DPG-Bench for text-to-image generation, while reaching GPT judge scores of 20.0 on MM-Vet and 57.2 on COCO captioning (twice the teacher's 28.4 at the same steps) for multimodal understanding.
papers.ja_title: 画像生成とマルチモーダル理解を両方できる拡散 LLM を、少ないステップに蒸留する
papers.summary: 画像生成と画像理解を 1 つのモデルで行う統一マルチモーダル拡散 LLM は、出力を作るのに数十〜数百回もモデルを繰り返し動かす必要があり遅かった。この論文では、教師モデルの軌跡を再生して生徒モデルにステップを飛ばさせる第 1 段階と、生徒自身の生成過程で微調整する第 2 段階からなる蒸留手法 Omni-Diffusion-Distill を作り、繰り返し回数を画像生成で 128 回から 8 回、理解で 512 回から 64 回に減らした。これにより実行時間が 18.2 倍・21.2 倍速くなり、同じステップ数での画像キャプション採点(COCO)は教師モデルの 2 倍の性能を達成した。
papers.why: 画像生成と理解を両方扱う拡散 LLM の推論コストを大きく下げる蒸留設計を示しており、マルチモーダルサービングの効率化に直接応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Unified multimodal diffusion LLMs that do both image generation and understanding need tens to hundreds of iterative forward passes, which is slow. Omni-Diffusion-Distill distills such a model with a two-stage approach (replaying cached teacher trajectories, then refining on the student's own rollouts), cutting decoding steps from 128 to 8 for image generation and from 512 to 64 for understanding, giving 18.2x and 21.2x wall-clock speedups, and reaching twice the teacher's COCO captioning score (57.2 vs. 28.4) at the same step budget.
papers.why_en: It offers a concrete distillation recipe that substantially cuts inference cost for unified multimodal diffusion LLMs while preserving both generation and understanding quality, directly useful for multimodal serving.

papers.title: CORAL-KV: Compact Cross-Layer Prediction and Residual Coding for Autoregressive Video KV Caches
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models maintain a growing attention key-value (KV) cache, making memory a key bottleneck for long video generation. Recently, clustering-based quantization has emerged as an effective method to compress video KV caches by grouping similar key and value vectors then quantizing residual errors. However, when later frames attend to the compressed history, small reconstruction errors can compound as the video grows. Beyond the within-layer similarity exploited by clustering, we find strong dependencies across cache layers in video models. This motivates Coral-KV - Calibrated Offline, Residual-coded, and Adapted Locally - a KV-cache compression framework that uses cache states in each layer to predict keys and values in subsequent layers, then quantizes the remaining prediction residuals. We construct compact block-diagonal-plus-low-rank (block-DPLR) predictors: block-diagonal components model channel relationships within each attention head, while a global low-rank term models dependencies between heads. Coral-KV exposes a flexible fidelity-memory trade-off: it can reuse its predictors across videos or refit lightweight block-diagonal predictors to the current video for higher fidelity. Across extensive evaluations on both HY-WorldPlay and MAGI-1, our reusable configuration improves PSNR over QVG-4 by 0.32 dB and 4.95 dB, respectively, while using 48% and 37% less cache memory. Against QVG-Pro, our video-adapted configuration improves MAGI-1 PSNR by 3.77 dB while using 33.7% less cache memory. Coral-KV also maintains higher reconstruction fidelity over extended generation and reduces temporal discontinuities while retaining comparable generation latency.
papers.ja_title: 層をまたいだ予測で動画生成の KV キャッシュをさらに小さくする Coral-KV
papers.summary: 自己回帰の動画拡散モデルは、フレームを増やすたびに注意機構の KV キャッシュ(過去の情報の記憶)が膨らみ、メモリがボトルネックになる。既存のクラスタリング量子化は層の中の似た情報しか使っていなかったが、この論文では層をまたいだ強い依存関係を見つけ、ある層のキャッシュから次の層のキー・値を予測して残差だけを量子化する Coral-KV を作った。HY-WorldPlay と MAGI-1 での実験で、既存手法 QVG-4 に比べて画質(PSNR)を 0.32 dB・4.95 dB 改善しながらキャッシュメモリを 48%・37% 削減した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュ圧縮で層間の依存関係を使うという新しい着眼点を示し、長尺動画生成のメモリ効率と画質の両立に具体的な改善をもたらす。
papers.summary_en: Autoregressive video diffusion models' attention KV cache grows with video length, making memory the bottleneck, and reconstruction errors from existing clustering-based quantization compound over time. Coral-KV exploits strong cross-layer dependencies (beyond within-layer similarity) by predicting one layer's keys/values from another's cache state and quantizing only the residual, using compact block-diagonal-plus-low-rank predictors. On HY-WorldPlay and MAGI-1, its reusable configuration improves PSNR over QVG-4 by 0.32 dB and 4.95 dB respectively while using 48% and 37% less cache memory.
papers.why_en: It introduces cross-layer prediction as a new axis for KV-cache compression and shows concrete gains in both fidelity and memory footprint for long autoregressive video generation.

papers.title: Token Utility for On-Policy Distillation via Local Trust-Region Optimization
papers.abstract: Token-selection methods for on-policy distillation (OPD) prioritize student-visited positions using diverse signals, including uncertainty, teacher-student disagreement, and mismatch direction. We instead derive token importance from the distillation objective itself: how much can each position's loss decrease under an equal local KL budget on the student's predictive distribution? The answer is the utility $s_t=g_t^\top F_t^\dagger g_t$, where $g_t$ is the logit gradient and $F_t$ is the categorical Fisher matrix. For reverse-KL it equals the student-weighted variance of the student-teacher log-probability ratio, and for forward-KL it equals the Pearson $χ^2$ divergence, so the appropriate utility follows from the choice of objective. On shared training checkpoints, several independently motivated criteria, including student entropy, KL disagreement, and TIP, concentrate their importance on nearly the same positions as the derived utility at a 50\% selection fraction, while diverging at stricter fractions and for direction-specific criteria. We instantiate the utility as Fisher Utility Weighting (FUW), a continuous, mean-normalized token weighting. Across seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks and three Qwen3 student-teacher pairs, FUW improves over matched uniform OPD under both reverse-KL (1.35-4.0 macro points) and forward-KL (1.08-2.71 macro points), and is competitive with existing selective methods using a single closed-form score derived from the training objective.
papers.ja_title: 蒸留の目的関数そのものからトークンの重要度を導く Fisher Utility Weighting
papers.summary: On-policy distillation(生徒モデルが自分で生成した位置に絞って教師から学ぶ手法)では、不確実性や教師生徒の不一致など色々な基準でトークンを選んでいたが、どれが本来の目的関数に対応するのか不明だった。この論文は、各位置での損失をどれだけ減らせるかを示す量 s_t を目的関数から直接導き、Fisher Utility Weighting (FUW) というシンプルな重み付けとして実装した。7 つの数学ベンチマークと 3 組の Qwen3 生徒・教師で、FUW は均等に学ぶ従来法より reverse-KL で 1.35〜4.0 ポイント、forward-KL で 1.08〜2.71 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: 複数ある既存のトークン選択ヒューリスティックを 1 本の理論的な指標に統一し、RL 後学習・蒸留パイプラインに組み込みやすい重み付け手法を示している。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation token-selection methods relied on various heuristics (uncertainty, teacher-student disagreement, etc.) without clarity on which aligns with the actual distillation objective. The authors derive token utility directly from the objective as s_t = g_t^T F_t^† g_t, matching student-weighted variance for reverse-KL and Pearson χ² divergence for forward-KL, and implement it as Fisher Utility Weighting (FUW). Across seven math reasoning benchmarks and three Qwen3 student-teacher pairs, FUW improves over matched uniform OPD by 1.35-4.0 macro points (reverse-KL) and 1.08-2.71 macro points (forward-KL).
papers.why_en: It unifies several independently motivated token-selection heuristics for on-policy distillation into one theoretically grounded score, giving a practical, closed-form weighting usable in RL post-training/distillation pipelines.

papers.title: AbridgeKV: Compressing Long Reasoning into the KV Cache of Learned Pause Tokens
papers.abstract: Long chain-of-thought decoding is memory-bound: the KV cache of the generated tokens grows linearly with the test-time compute being spent. Evicting cache entries does not fix this, because a model never trained on a cache with entries removed generates longer, often up to the length limit. We instead train the model to compress its own output. AbridgeKV compresses each completed block of generated text into the KV entries of a few learned pause tokens. These are extra input tokens with trained embeddings that produce no output. Once the pause tokens have encoded the block, AbridgeKV frees the block's original cache; subsequent tokens attend to the pause tokens' KV entries in its place. Three novel choices make this work: the pause tokens' KV entries take positions inside the block they replace, the cache budget is allocated across layers according to the measured value of each layer's entries, and compression operates on relatively large blocks. On 446 competition problems from AIME, HMMT, AMC, BRUMO, CMIMC and SMT with 32K-token generations, keeping a quarter of the generated cache matches an identically trained full-KV model in accuracy and output length; the strongest published evictor at a matched budget writes far longer, and the closest trained compressor, retrained on the same data, loses 10 points. Served in vLLM, the cache is 3.5x smaller per sequence and a saturated H100 finishes a problem 3.2x faster than with full KV.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 学習済みの「ポーズトークン」に推論過程を圧縮して KV キャッシュを縮める AbridgeKV
papers.summary: 長い連鎖思考で答えを出す LLM は、生成が長くなるほど KV キャッシュ(過去の計算結果の記憶)が線形に膨らみメモリを食う。単純にキャッシュを削除すると、削除に慣れていないモデルがさらに長く生成してしまい解決にならない。この論文は、完成したブロックの情報を学習済みの「ポーズトークン」数個の KV に圧縮し、元のキャッシュを捨てる AbridgeKV を作った。32K トークン生成の競技数学 446 問で、生成キャッシュを 4 分の 1 に減らしても完全な KV を使うモデルと同じ精度・出力長を保ち、vLLM 上でキャッシュを 3.5 倍小さく、H100 で解答を 3.2 倍速く終わらせた。
papers.why: キャッシュの削除ではなくモデル自身に出力を圧縮させる訓練という発想で、長い推論チェーンのメモリとレイテンシを同時に改善する具体策を示している。
papers.summary_en: Long chain-of-thought decoding is memory-bound because the KV cache grows linearly with generated length, and simply evicting entries backfires since a model never trained without them just generates even longer. AbridgeKV instead trains the model to compress each completed block into the KV entries of a few learned pause tokens, freeing the original block's cache. On 446 competition-math problems with 32K-token generations, keeping just a quarter of the generated cache matches a full-KV model's accuracy and output length, while served in vLLM the cache is 3.5x smaller and a saturated H100 finishes 3.2x faster.
papers.why_en: Rather than evicting cache entries, it trains the model itself to compress its output, offering a concrete way to simultaneously cut memory and latency for long reasoning chains in serving.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Tabular Learning via Hypergraph Reasoning with LLMs
papers.abstract: Tabular data are prevalent across diverse domains such as healthcare and finance. Zero-shot tabular learning aims to make predictions without labeled data. However, existing LLM-based approaches rely on row-wise prompting, resulting in high inference cost and limited use of inter-row dependencies. In this work, we propose TABHGR+, an efficient relation-aware zero-shot framework for tabular data that leverages LLM-generated rules to label and group rows. Specifically, based on column and task descriptions, we use LLMs to generate rules that assign weak labels to all rows. To refine these noisy weak labels, we construct a hypergraph by grouping semantically related rows using LLM-generated rules and perform hypergraph-based label propagation. Lastly, we further enhance the LLM-generated hypergraph for propagation, which is potentially sub-optimal, by assigning label-adaptive weights to hyperedges. By requiring only a constant number of LLM calls independent of dataset size, TABHGR+ substantially reduces inference cost while achieving higher classification accuracy than zero-shot and strong few-shot baselines.

papers.title: miniTE: Diagnosing and Bridging the Execution Gap in Native NVFP4 Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Native NVFP4 promises to accelerate reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models (LLMs), but achieving stable learning across separate training and sampling engines remains challenging. We show that matching model weights and numerical formats is insufficient to ensure consistent policy evaluation, highlighting the importance of cross-engine numerical execution. We introduce miniTE, a lightweight framework that combines execution diagnostics, cross-engine numerical alignment, and efficient native W4A4 (4-bit weights and activations) GEMM computation for LLM RL. It improves numerical execution consistency without modifying the RL objective, while reducing implementation overhead to realize the benefits of native low-bit computation. Long-horizon RL experiments on Qwen3-30B-A3B demonstrate stable training and benchmark performance close to BF16, outperforming naive Transformer Engine (TE) NVFP4 in evaluation quality. On single NVIDIA B300 GPU node, the optimized learner reaches 33,540 tokens/s, yielding 1.39x and 1.47x the throughput of BF16 and TE NVFP4, respectively, for complete learner updates. We released the framework, kernels, diagnostics, and training configurations to make native low-bit RL easier.
papers.ja_title: 4bit 演算で LLM の強化学習を安定させる miniTE
papers.summary: 重みと活性化を 4bit にする NVFP4 という低精度形式は LLM の強化学習(RL)を速くできるはずだが、学習エンジンとサンプリングエンジンが別々だと、重みと数値形式を合わせるだけでは方策の評価が一致せず学習が不安定になることが分かった。この論文は、実行診断・エンジン間の数値整合・効率的な W4A4(重み 4bit・活性化 4bit)の GEMM 計算をまとめた軽量フレームワーク miniTE を作った。Qwen3-30B-A3B での長期 RL 実験で BF16 に近い性能を保ちつつ安定学習を達成し、単一の NVIDIA B300 GPU ノードで BF16 の 1.39 倍、素朴な NVFP4 実装の 1.47 倍のスループット(33,540 tokens/s)を得た。
papers.why: 低精度演算を RL 学習に組み込む際の数値的な落とし穴とその診断・対処法、および実際のカーネル実装を示し、分散 RL 基盤の低精度化を進める上で直接使える知見になる。
papers.summary_en: Native NVFP4 (4-bit weights and activations) promises to speed up LLM RL, but the authors find that matching weights and numerical formats across separate training and sampling engines is insufficient for consistent policy evaluation, due to cross-engine numerical execution gaps. miniTE combines execution diagnostics, cross-engine numerical alignment, and efficient native W4A4 GEMM to fix this without changing the RL objective. On Qwen3-30B-A3B, long-horizon RL training is stable and close to BF16 in quality, and on a single NVIDIA B300 GPU node the optimized learner reaches 33,540 tokens/s, 1.39x and 1.47x the throughput of BF16 and naive TE NVFP4 respectively.
papers.why_en: It surfaces a concrete numerical-execution pitfall in deploying native low-bit computation for RL and provides diagnostics plus kernel-level fixes, directly useful for building low-precision distributed RL infrastructure.

review.note: 重みと数値形式を揃えただけでは学習・サンプリング用エンジン間で方策評価が一致しないことがある、という分散実装のクロスエンジン整合性を確かめる観点。
review.note_en: A development-time check: matching weights and numeric formats across separate training/sampling engines does not guarantee consistent policy evaluation, so cross-engine numerical execution must be explicitly verified.

papers.title: Factorization-Guided Training and Inference for Diffusion-Drafted Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference through parallel verification of tokens proposed by a drafter. Diffusion drafters further parallelize proposal generation, but greater proposal capacity or higher mean accepted tokens (MAT) need not yield higher throughput. Because verification accepts only a consecutive prefix, early rejections can render later correct predictions ineffective, limiting MAT gains, while even higher MAT may not improve throughput if per-round latency increases. We introduce DScout, which uses two complementary factorizations to guide diffusion drafter training and inference for higher throughput. For training, DScout factorizes position-wise loss into inclusion, weighting, and prediction loss. This guides the design and combination of mixed-horizon training, intra-block unmasking, and acceptance-weighted loss to align supervision with prefix acceptance and improve MAT. For inference, DScout factorizes throughput as the ratio of MAT to per-round latency, guiding target-conditioning depth, drafter depth, and inference block size selection to identify a high-throughput configuration for each workload. Across six benchmarks, DScout achieves $3.84\times$ and $4.14\times$ mean speedups over autoregressive decoding on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, respectively, improving mean speedup over the state-of-the-art baseline by 9.1% and 7.1%. Across models and concurrency settings, our inference configuration policy provides up to 9.75% additional mean speedup over DScout's fixed configuration.
papers.ja_title: 分解に基づく学習・推論設計で拡散ドラフタ型投機的デコーディングを高速化
papers.summary: LLM 推論を速める投機的デコーディング (候補トークンを下書き役が出し本体が検証する手法) では、拡散モデルをドラフタ (下書き役) にすると並列に多くの候補を出せるが、検証で採用できるのは先頭から連続した部分だけなので、平均採用トークン数 (MAT) が増えても必ずしも速くならない問題があった。DScout は学習時の損失を「含めるか・重みづけ・予測」の 3 つに分解して学習方法を設計し、推論時はスループットを「MAT ÷ 1 ラウンドの遅延」に分解して設定を選ぶ。6 個のベンチマークで自己回帰デコーディングに比べ Qwen3-4B で 3.84 倍、Qwen3-8B で 4.14 倍の高速化を達成し、既存最強手法より 9.1%、7.1% 速く、設定の自動選択でさらに最大 9.75% 速くなった。
papers.why: 拡散ドラフタを使う投機的デコーディングで「採用トークン数を増やす」だけでは速度向上に直結しないことを示し、学習と推論設定を体系的に分解して最適化する枠組みを提示している点が、推論高速化の基盤設計に役立つ。
papers.summary_en: In speculative decoding, diffusion drafters can parallelize proposal generation, but higher proposal capacity or mean accepted tokens (MAT) need not yield higher throughput, since verification accepts only a consecutive prefix and per-round latency can offset MAT gains. DScout factorizes the position-wise training loss into inclusion, weighting, and prediction components to design mixed-horizon training, intra-block unmasking, and acceptance-weighted loss, and factorizes inference throughput as MAT divided by per-round latency to select target-conditioning depth, drafter depth, and block size. Across six benchmarks, DScout achieves 3.84x and 4.14x mean speedups over autoregressive decoding on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B respectively, improving over the state-of-the-art baseline by 9.1% and 7.1%, with the inference configuration policy adding up to 9.75% further speedup.
papers.why_en: The work shows that simply raising accepted-token counts for diffusion drafters does not guarantee throughput gains, and offers a systematic factorization-based framework for both training and inference configuration that is useful for anyone building speculative decoding systems.

papers.title: TraceQuery: learning what to recompute from full-denoising trajectory in diffusion language models
papers.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) enable flexible generation through iterative masked denoising, but incur substantial inference cost because token representations are repeatedly recomputed across denoising steps. Existing cache-based methods reduce this cost by reusing intermediate results across denoising steps and recomputing only a subset of positions at each step, chosen either on a fixed schedule or by heuristic signals of change. Our trajectory experiments instead point to decoding trajectory as the more relevant quantity. Cached generation remains accurate when it stays close to the full-denoising trajectory, with errors concentrated around unmask-order deviations and reduced as longer reference prefixes are recovered. This suggests a more direct principle: limiting representation error helps, but keeping generation on the full-denoising trajectory is a more direct route to accurate decoding. We therefore formulate efficient dLLM inference as trajectory-guided querying. Rather than broadly repairing representation error, we use full-denoising trajectories to supervise which unresolved positions should receive limited fresh computation. Based on this formulation, we introduce TRACEQUERY, a lightweight sparse decoding framework that predicts a small set of near-future trajectory-relevant positions, queries only those candidates, and lets the backbone select which one to commit from their fresh predictions. TRACEQUERY delivers the strongest quality-computation trade-off among cache-based approaches, sustaining high accuracy with substantially fewer fresh token computations, and generalizes across tasks, model variants, and families. Code: https://github.com/fish1928/tracequery.git
papers.ja_title: 完全デノイズ軌跡に沿わせて拡散言語モデル推論を間引く TraceQuery
papers.summary: 拡散言語モデル (dLLM) はマスクを繰り返し外して文章を作る仕組みだが、各ステップでトークンの中間表現を何度も計算し直すため推論コストが大きいという問題があった。この研究は、キャッシュで再計算を省く既存手法が「完全にデノイズした場合の生成経路 (trajectory)」に近いほど正確になることを実験で確かめ、どの位置を新しく計算すべきかを、表現誤差ではなくこの軌跡に基づいて予測する軽量な手法 TraceQuery を提案した。少数の軌跡関連位置だけを新規計算することで、既存のキャッシュ手法より良い精度と計算量のバランスを達成し、タスクやモデルの種類・系列を超えて同じ傾向が見られたという。
papers.why: dLLM 推論の高速化で「表現誤差を抑える」よりも「完全デノイズ軌跡に沿わせる」ことが精度に直結するという着眼点は、キャッシュやスパース計算を設計する際の新しい判断基準になる。
papers.summary_en: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) generate via iterative masked denoising but incur high inference cost because token representations are repeatedly recomputed across steps. The authors' trajectory experiments show that cached generation stays accurate when it remains close to the full-denoising trajectory, with errors concentrated around unmask-order deviations, leading them to propose TRACEQUERY, a lightweight sparse decoding framework that predicts a small set of near-future trajectory-relevant positions and queries only those. TRACEQUERY delivers the strongest quality-computation trade-off among cache-based approaches, sustaining high accuracy with substantially fewer fresh token computations, and generalizes across tasks, model variants, and families.
papers.why_en: The finding that staying on the full-denoising trajectory is a more direct route to accurate decoding than merely limiting representation error gives a new design principle for cache and sparse-computation schemes in dLLM inference.

blogs.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on vLLM: 5x Agentic Throughput Since Day 0
blogs.excerpt: Within three weeks of release, vLLM made DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 1.9x faster at low concurrency and lifted its throughput 5x on SemiAnalysis AgentX, with SWA bounded replay, CUDA graphs, DeepSeek's new kernels, and vLLM kernel fusions.
blogs.ja_title: vLLM が DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash を3週間で低並行時1.9倍・エージェント向けスループット5.3倍に高速化
blogs.summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash は decode では16B、prefill では8Bパラメータしか使わない encoder-decoder 構造 (CED) に加え、FP4のKVキャッシュなどでキャッシュを1トークンあたり890バイトまで圧縮したモデルである。公開から3週間、Inferact と vLLM チームはスライディングウィンドウ (直近だけ見る) KVキャッシュを CUDA グラフ付きで再構築する「SWA bounded replay」と、DeepSeek 製の新カーネル (MegaAttention など) の統合、カーネル融合を組み合わせ、低並行時で1.9倍、150TPS (1秒あたりトークン数) という遅延制約下のエージェント向けベンチマーク (SemiAnalysis AgentX) では5.3倍のスループットを達成した。SWA bounded replay 単独でも初回応答までの時間 (TTFT) を約30%短縮した。
blogs.why: 長い会話が続くエージェント用途でのKVキャッシュ管理とカーネル最適化を、公開モデルに対して vLLM 側でどこまで積めるかを示す実例で、サービング基盤の最適化の参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash uses a causal encoder-decoder (CED) architecture that activates 16B parameters per token during decode but only 8B during prefill, and shrinks its KV cache to about 890 bytes per token via Compressed Sparse Attention 2 (CSA2), FP4 KV cache, and inter-layer KV cache sharing. In the three weeks after release, Inferact and the vLLM community combined SWA bounded replay (rebuilding the sliding-window KV cache with CUDA graphs on a cache hit, skipping most prefill on a hit) with DeepSeek's newly released kernels (MegaAttention, Mega-mHC, Mega-Gate, DeepSelect) and aggressive kernel fusion, achieving a 1.9x speedup at low concurrency and a 5.3x throughput improvement under a 150 TPS constraint on the SemiAnalysis AgentX agentic benchmark; SWA bounded replay alone cut TTFT by about 30%.
blogs.why_en: Shows concretely how a serving framework (vLLM) layers cache-management and kernel-fusion optimizations on top of a model's own architecture to hit day-0-to-week-3 throughput gains for long-horizon agentic serving.

review.note: 単純なスループットでなく、150TPS という遅延制約を固定した上でのスループットを比べることで、エージェント向けサービングの最適化を公平に測っている、という評価設計の観点。
review.note_en: A measurement-design note: comparing throughput under a fixed 150 TPS latency constraint (rather than unconstrained throughput) is what makes the agentic serving optimization numbers comparable.

blogs.title: Fine-tune a search agent with multi-turn RL on Amazon SageMaker AI
blogs.excerpt: Fine-tuning teaches a small search agent your tools and environment, giving it the reliability of a frontier model at lower latency and cost. In this post, we fine-tune an LLM-powered search agent with multi-turn reinforcement learning (MTRL) on Amazon SageMaker AI and share the gains we measured in retrieval quality and reliability.
blogs.ja_title: 検索エージェントを複数ターンの強化学習 (MTRL) でファインチューニングし、小さいモデルで大モデル並みの信頼性を出す
blogs.summary: 検索エージェントは何を検索し、どの検索方法を使い、いつ探索を止めるかを複数ターンにわたって自分で決める必要があるが、小さいモデルにそのまま指示しても安定して動かず、大きいフロンティアモデルだと速度とコストがかさむという困りごとがある。教師あり学習 (SFT) は理想的な複数ターンの手本データを集めるのが大変で、単発の強化学習 (RLVR など) は1回のやり取りだけを採点するためターン間のつながりを見逃す。この記事では複数ターン強化学習 (MTRL) を Amazon SageMaker AI 上で使い、最終的な結果だけに報酬を与えて複数ターン全体の判断を学習させることで、検索の精度と安定性を改善したと報告している。
blogs.why: 単発の強化学習ではエージェントのマルチターンの意思決定を正しく学習できないという問題設定と、その解決としてのMTRLの考え方は、エージェント向けRL後学習基盤を作る人にとって直接参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: A search agent has to decide, across multiple rounds, what to search for, which retrieval strategy to use, and when to stop, but small models don't reliably learn this from prompting alone, while frontier models work but cost more in latency and price. Supervised fine-tuning needs costly multi-turn demonstration data that usually doesn't exist, and single-turn RL such as RLVR scores one response at a time and misses the dependencies across turns. The post describes fine-tuning a search agent with multi-turn reinforcement learning (MTRL) on Amazon SageMaker AI, rewarding only the final outcome across the full trajectory, and reports gains in retrieval quality and reliability from this approach.
blogs.why_en: Lays out why single-turn RLVR under-trains multi-turn agent decisions and offers MTRL as the fix, directly relevant to anyone building RL post-training infrastructure for tool-using agents.

review.note: 単発の強化学習 (1回のやり取りだけを採点) はターンをまたいだ意思決定の依存関係を見逃す、という複数ターンRLの設計上の注意点。
review.note_en: A research-design note: single-turn RL (scoring one response at a time) misses the cross-turn dependencies in an agent's decisions, which is why the reward needs to span the full trajectory.

blogs.ja_title: 推薦システムの埋め込み検索カーネルを CUDA から Triton へ移行 (FBTriton の TBE 実装)
blogs.summary: 何千もの GPU に分散された推薦システムでは、テーブルごとの埋め込み検索 (embedding lookup) をまとめて1回の GPU 呼び出しで行う TBE (Table-Batched Embedding) というカーネルが性能の要になっている。この記事では従来の CUDA 実装を Triton (GPU カーネルを書きやすくする言語) で書き直し、バッグ (まとまり) 単位でまとめて処理する汎用パスと、小さいテーブル向けにヒストグラムと tensor core (行列演算専用回路) を使う高速パスの2種類を用意した。境界チェックの処理だけでも B200 GPU で最大 1.24 倍速くなったと報告している。
blogs.why: 巨大な推薦システムを支える低レベルカーネルを、保守しやすい Triton に移しながら既存の CUDA 実装を上回る性能を出した実例で、カーネル開発・低精度演算の参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: In large recommendation systems, Table-Batched Embedding (TBE) kernels do embedding lookup and pooling across many tables in a single GPU launch, and are central to performance at scale across thousands of sharded GPUs. The post describes rewriting the legacy CUDA TBE kernels in Triton, with a generic gather path for arbitrary shapes and a specialized small-table histogram plus tensor-core path for a narrow, common shape, and reports the Triton implementation outperforms the legacy CUDA kernels; the standalone bounds-check step alone achieves up to a 1.24x speedup on B200.
blogs.why_en: A concrete example of replacing hand-written CUDA with an autotunable Triton kernel for a workload (embedding lookup at massive sharded scale) that's core to recommendation-system serving, useful as a kernel-engineering reference.

blogs.ja_title: 自動チューニング型カーネル DSL「Helion」で vLLM の量子化線形層カーネルを書き直し、スループットを最大10%超改善
blogs.summary: vLLM は FP8 や INT4 などに量子化した線形層 (linear layer) のために CUTLASS や DeepGEMM といった専用カーネルライブラリを使い分けているが、ハードウェアや形状ごとにカーネルを個別に作り込む手間が大きい。この記事では PyTorch 発の高水準カーネル記述言語 (DSL) である Helion を vLLM の線形層バックエンドに統合し、1つの GEMM (行列積) 実装から Standard・Split-K・Swap-AB という複数のアルゴリズムの変種をカバーし、形状ごとの自動チューニング (autotuning) で最適な変種と設定を選ばせた。NVIDIA Hopper GPU では、この Helion バックエンドが vLLM 標準の CUTLASS・DeepGEMM バックエンドを上回り、一部のワークロードでは10%超のスループット向上が一貫して得られたとしている。
blogs.why: 量子化カーネルを手作業で作り分ける代わりに、1つの高水準実装と自動チューニングでハードウェア・形状をまたいで性能を出す手法として、カーネル開発・低精度演算基盤の参考になる。
blogs.summary_en: vLLM's quantized linear layers (FP8, INT8, INT4, NVFP4) rely on hand-specialized kernels from libraries like CUTLASS, DeepGEMM, and FlashInfer for different hardware and formats. The post integrates Helion, a PyTorch-native, hardware-agnostic kernel DSL, into vLLM's linear backend: a single Helion GEMM implementation covers Standard GEMM, Split-K, and Swap-AB variants, with the best variant and config chosen automatically via per-shape autotuning. On NVIDIA Hopper GPUs, the Helion linear backend outperforms vLLM's default CUTLASS and DeepGEMM backends across the evaluated models, delivering consistent end-to-end gains and more than 10% throughput improvement for some workloads.
blogs.why_en: Demonstrates replacing a set of hand-specialized quantized GEMM kernels with one autotuned, hardware-agnostic DSL implementation that still beats the specialized baselines, a useful kernel-engineering pattern for inference serving.

blogs.ja_title: TLX で書いた Jagged Flash Attention が Blackwell で FA4 を上回る
blogs.summary: Meta の広告モデル GEM が使う attention カーネル Jagged Flash Attention を、Triton の拡張である TLX (Triton Low-level Extensions) で書き直した。可変長 (ジャグド) のシーケンスをパディングなしで処理するこのカーネルを、NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell) 上で bfloat16 精度で測定し、最新の手書き CuteDSL カーネルである FlashAttention-4 (FA4、2026 年 5 月版) と比較した。コード量は約 3.2K 行で FA4 の約 10K 行から 3 分の 1 程度に減らしつつ、GEM で使う実際の形 (jagged shapes) では forward が約 13%、backward が約 50% 速くなった。
blogs.why: 分散推論・学習の attention カーネルを、CUDA や CuteDSL の専門家でなくても高水準の Triton で書けて、しかも最先端の手書きカーネルを上回れることを示した例で、カーネル開発の生産性と性能を両立させる手がかりになる。
blogs.summary_en: Meta rewrote the attention kernel behind its Generative Ads Model (GEM), Jagged Flash Attention, using TLX (Triton Low-level Extensions), which adds explicit hardware-aware control (SMEM/TMEM allocation, async warp specialization, barriers, async TMA) on top of Triton's tile-based model. Benchmarked in bfloat16 on NVIDIA B200 (Blackwell) against FlashAttention-4 (FA4, May 2026 version), the TLX kernel is about 3.2K lines of code, roughly 3x less than FA4's ~10K-line CuteDSL implementation, and it outperforms FA4 on the jagged shapes that matter for GEM by about 13% on the forward pass and about 50% on the backward pass.
blogs.why_en: It shows that a high-level, Triton-based kernel approachable to modeling engineers (not only kernel specialists) can both cut development cost and beat a state-of-the-art hand-written CuteDSL kernel on Blackwell, which matters for anyone building or maintaining attention kernels for large-scale training or serving.
